modules.title: p2 · 应用插件

modules.title: AI · 模型与提供商

modules.title: Schema · JSON Schema 构造与校验

modules.title: Durable · 持久任务与文档
modules.description: 提交优先的会话、任务、模型生成、子智能体与存储。

modules.title: Env · 远程执行环境
modules.description: 通过 SSH 与远端 Rust daemon 执行文件和进程操作，Durable 与凭据留在本机。

modules.title: TUI · 终端界面

modules.title: 原生集成 · 平台能力
modules.description: Windows、macOS、Linux 原生剪贴板与平台适配。

modules.title: Chord · 对象与热重载

modules.title: Telemetry · 遥测契约

modules.title: 示例 · 扩展与 SDK

modules.title: 示例 · Durable 能力演练

modules.description: models.dev v2 等来源、逐 provider 定义、模型家族规则与生成顺序。

modules.title: 工程 · 构建与维护
modules.description: 依赖校验、构建发布、模型目录生成和开发统计。

features.title: CLI 启动与模式分派
features.purpose: 解析命令行并创建与当前目录绑定的会话，选择交互、print、JSON 或 RPC。
features.behavior: 启动装配设置、资源与模型运行时；实际模型循环由 Agent 执行。

features.title: 分层设置与配置值解析
features.purpose: 解析用户与项目设置，并提供跨安装形态的资源路径。
features.behavior: 配置作用域和优先级以 settings/configuration 文档为准。

features.title: 项目资源信任决策
features.purpose: 决定是否加载受信任控制的项目配置与可执行资源。
features.behavior: 项目资源信任不是文件系统、网络或进程级通用沙箱。

features.title: Pi 包安装、移除与资源配置
features.purpose: 组织 npm、git 和本地资源包的安装、更新与发现。
features.behavior: 区分 Pi 自身更新、扩展包更新与模型目录更新。

features.title: 资源发现、来源与冲突诊断
features.purpose: 统一发现扩展、技能、模板、主题与项目上下文文件。
features.behavior: 记录来源并处理碰撞；项目资源需遵守信任加载顺序。

features.title: 内置扩展装配与替换
features.purpose: CLI 把 llama.cpp、codemode、tool-search、MCP 作为内置扩展装配；同名用户扩展可替换可替换项。
features.behavior: SDK 默认不加载内置扩展；宿主需要显式加入对应工厂。

features.title: 扩展发现、注册与事件分发
features.purpose: 加载 TS/JS 扩展，注册工具、命令、快捷键、提供商与事件。
features.behavior: 工厂负责注册，runner 提供上下文与分发；原始类型注释可在 API 清单中逐项阅读。

features.title: MCP 分层配置与服务器注册
features.purpose: 合并用户 mcp.json、已信任项目配置与扩展注册，验证服务器及单工具暴露设置。
features.behavior: 同名文件配置优先于扩展；项目仅覆盖开关或暴露时保留用户端连接配置。项目来源受信任控制。

features.title: MCP OAuth 登录与提供商凭据转接
features.purpose: 管理服务器 OAuth 凭据、回调与增量授权；HTTP 服务器也可采用已登录提供商的 token。
features.behavior: 凭据按服务器名和 URL 隔离；项目配置不可使用 auth.provider；配置元数据 URL 与 clientRegistration 影响授权流程。

features.title: MCP 管理命令、UI 与日志
features.purpose: 添加、移除、检查、登录服务器，在交互会话中显示状态、工具与配置来源，并记录服务日志。
features.behavior: login 的 --timeout 限制整个登录流程；Shell 命令不加载扩展；已连接工具暴露和开关可按所属配置文件保存。

features.title: MCP 后台连接、等待与重连
features.purpose: 会话启动时后台连接服务器，按需等待、更新工具目录，并在断连后下一次调用重连。
features.behavior: 首个 prompt 只为 direct 服务器等待；调用工具不会因临时错误盲目重试，资源读取可重试；连接时不再预先枚举资源，由显式列表请求获取。

features.title: MCP 工具命名、暴露与结果适配
features.purpose: 把服务器工具接入 Pi 工具管线，规范化名称，传递 structuredContent、isError 和安全提示。
features.behavior: 规范化后的重名工具带 hash 后缀；模型端大文本截断并保留完整临时文件，脚本可收到完整结果。

features.title: MCP 资源、URI 模板与二进制读取
features.purpose: 注册资源列表、模板列表和读取工具，统一输出文本、图像或二进制临时文件路径。
features.behavior: 仅面向启用且非 hidden 的资源服务器；当前不渲染 MCP Apps 的 ui:// 与 HTML 资源。

features.title: 技能发现与按需说明
features.purpose: 发现技能元数据，把需要的完整说明提供给模型。
features.behavior: 技能主要是说明和资源；可执行扩展是另一种机制。

features.title: 提示模板与参数展开
features.purpose: 复用提示词文件并展开输入参数。
features.behavior: 发生在模型请求组装之前；与系统提示配置分别管理。

features.title: 认证存储与命令行登录退出
features.purpose: 支持 pi auth login/logout，并持久保存刷新凭据。
features.entry: pi auth login / pi auth logout / /login / /logout
features.behavior: 退出等待已开始的 OAuth refresh 保存；离线导览不读取凭据或发起授权。

features.title: 模型选择、目录与提供商组合
features.purpose: 汇总可用模型、解析选择模式，并通过运行时派发请求。
features.behavior: 目录元数据不等同于可调用性；认证与具体提供商能力仍需满足。

features.title: 虚拟模型与请求路由
features.purpose: 允许选择逻辑模型，并将每次请求路由到物理模型。
features.behavior: 虚拟模型不会直接到达提供商；路由状态可跟随会话分支保存。

features.title: llama.cpp 路由器集成
features.purpose: 发现并管理本地模型路由器中的模型。
features.behavior: 与兼容 API 的 models.json 配置路径区分。

features.title: SDK 创建与替换运行时
features.purpose: 让应用在进程内创建、继续或替换编码智能体会话。
features.behavior: SDK 注入流函数、配置、工具与存储；运行时负责会话替换和重新绑定。

features.title: 会话保存、恢复与命名
features.purpose: 保存树形会话记录，并按项目、路径或 ID 恢复。
features.behavior: 当前分支重建下一次模型上下文，内存会话可关闭持久化。

features.title: 系统提示与上下文组装
features.purpose: 把工具、技能、项目说明与对话消息组织成请求内容。
features.behavior: 扩展可变换上下文；模型投影与持久化消息并非完全相同。

features.title: 文件附件、图片与管道输入
features.purpose: 将 @文件、图片和标准输入转成首条用户消息的内容。
features.behavior: 读取与规范化输入后组装消息；RPC 不接受 CLI 的 @file 参数。

features.title: 交互聊天与终端工作流
features.purpose: 接收用户交互并呈现模型消息、工具输出与运行状态。
features.behavior: UI 订阅会话事件；不把 UI 控制逻辑等同于模型执行循环。

features.title: 全屏终端、普通模式与启动显示
features.purpose: 默认全屏呈现聊天，提供 regular 模式保留终端滚动历史，支持安静启动时只显示 header。
features.behavior: fullscreen/regular 是终端呈现选择，不改变底层 Agent 消息循环。

features.title: 一次性文本与 JSON 事件输出
features.purpose: 适配脚本与管道：输出最终文本，或逐条输出 JSONL 事件。
features.behavior: 提交输入，等待会话处理并清理；标准输出背压与协议输出单独处理。

features.title: CLI RPC 与扩展 UI 代理
features.purpose: 让外部程序通过标准输入输出控制会话，并处理支持的扩展交互。
features.behavior: 通过 stdin/stdout 交换 JSONL 命令、响应与事件；外部程序管理进程与协议交互。

features.title: 快捷键与斜杠命令
features.purpose: 集中定义可配置动作与内置命令清单。
features.behavior: 快捷键应复用命名配置；完整命令表在参考文档内。

features.title: 剪贴板与外部编辑器
features.purpose: 支持复制消息、接收剪贴板图片及外部编辑工作流。
features.behavior: 能力取决于操作系统与终端环境。

features.title: 输入处理、排队与任务收尾
features.purpose: 协调扩展命令、输入转换、steering/follow-up、重试与最终通知。
features.behavior: agent_end 后仍可能继续；agent_settled 是完成自动处理后的通知边界。

features.title: 用户与自定义消息的统一运行准备
features.purpose: 用户输入和触发运行的自定义消息统一经过 _startRun、_prepareRun 与 before_agent_start。
features.behavior: 先标记忙碌，再检查压缩、执行扩展、准备工具与系统提示；事件的 messageType 区分 user 和 custom。

features.title: 工具暴露、命名空间与请求 Loadout
features.purpose: 把工具注册、激活、模型声明和脚本可调用性分开管理，扩展可为每次请求准备工具集。
features.behavior: 模型声明不代表所有注册工具；annotations、outputSchema 与 structuredContent 承载额外契约。

features.title: tool_search：BM25 搜索与延迟工具加载
features.purpose: 按名称、描述、参数与命名空间检索未声明工具，激活匹配项供下一次模型请求直接调用。
features.behavior: tool_search 改变工具集合并写入会话；脚本 searchTools 只查找可调用工具，两者职责不同。

features.title: codemode：脚本编排与并行工具
features.purpose: 让模型用 JavaScript 编排工具、并行调用与过滤大结果，仅把脚本输出送回模型。
features.behavior: on 保留直接工具，only 调整模型可见工具；QuickJS 没有文件、网络、Node 或 timer 能力，外部操作通过注入工具。

features.title: codemode 跨调用状态与分支恢复
features.purpose: 成功脚本把 store/load 修改保存为 codemode-store 条目，在继续、分叉和切换分支后恢复各自状态。
features.behavior: 失败脚本不提交 store 写入；工具已经造成的外部效果不会因此回滚，存储有值大小和总量限制。

features.title: 脚本分类模型、图像模型与用量
features.purpose: 向脚本暴露分类与图像模型目录及执行接口，沿会话凭据调用，并汇总用量。
features.behavior: 脚本不能执行对话模型；每脚本最多同时运行四个此类模型调用，需检查返回的 stopReason。

features.title: 脚本图像落盘与完整输出文件
features.purpose: 保存 image() 的图像和被截断的完整文本，让后续工具能用真实文件路径处理结果。
features.behavior: 图像只接受支持格式的 base64 数据，不把远程 URL 当作图像数据；临时文件生命周期由输出文件实现管理。

features.title: 嵌套工具管线、父子事件与用量记录
features.purpose: ctx.executeTool 将脚本发起的子调用交给同一校验、拦截和结果管线，汇总到父工具。
features.behavior: 子调用收到取消信号，串行策略由队列处理；嵌套结果不逐条进入模型上下文，记录有界。

features.title: read：读取文本与图片
features.purpose: 读取指定文件，把文本或支持的图像作为工具结果给模型。
features.behavior: 路径处理、输出限制与图片处理决定返回内容；可注入读取操作。

features.title: grep：内容检索
features.purpose: 搜索文件内容并返回匹配位置。
features.behavior: rg 的 cwd 设为搜索目录或目标文件父目录，相对 glob 基于搜索根匹配；输出上限与上下文行数仍受工具参数限制。

features.title: find：文件路径搜索
features.purpose: 通过路径模式查找文件。
features.behavior: 适合先定位路径，再调用 read；不同于 grep 的文件内容检索。

features.title: ls：目录枚举
features.purpose: 列出目录条目，帮助模型了解文件结构。
features.behavior: 仅列目录不读取全部文件内容。

features.title: edit：保留行尾并在写入前计算差异
features.purpose: 仅替换目标内容，保留未变行的 CRLF/LF。
features.behavior: 差异围绕变动计算并在写文件前完成，避免大文件写完后才因 diff 内存不足报错。

features.title: write：创建或覆写文件
features.purpose: 把模型给定内容写入目标文件。
features.behavior: 与 edit 的精确替换不同，write 可覆写内容；查看文件修改队列边界。

features.title: bash：Shell 执行与输出
features.purpose: 执行 shell 命令并将输出、退出状态和截断信息传回模型。
features.entry: 默认启用工具 bash；用户 ! 命令
features.behavior: 信号、超时、子进程与输出捕获由执行层协作处理。

features.title: powershell：Windows 命令执行
features.purpose: 为 Windows 提供 PowerShell 工具定义与可注入的操作。
features.behavior: 不是所有平台的默认工具；平台、编码与进程行为以实现为准。

features.title: 上下文压缩与分支摘要
features.purpose: 把长历史压缩为摘要，控制下一次请求的上下文规模。
features.behavior: 摘要影响上下文投影，不直接等价于删除原始会话历史。

features.title: 会话树、分叉与克隆
features.purpose: 从历史位置继续，或复制历史创建独立会话。
features.behavior: 区分同文件内的分支和新会话副本；分支敏感扩展状态需要重新恢复。

features.title: 提示缓存预热与用量统计
features.purpose: 管理适用模型的空闲缓存预热并统计请求用量。
features.behavior: 缓存保留时间取决于模型声明；不能把预热当成所有提供商都有的保证。

features.title: 会话导入、导出与分享
features.purpose: 将会话转为 JSONL 或可阅读 HTML，并支撑会话分享流程。
features.behavior: 导出是格式转换；shareDestination 可选 auto/gist/radius，auto 优先可用 Radius，否则使用 GitHub secret gist。上传需要对应认证。

features.title: 选择器、消息与工具 UI 组件
features.purpose: 提供模型/会话/设置选择与不同消息、工具结果的呈现。
features.behavior: 组件清单按源码保留，可从符号和原始注释追踪每个组件。

features.title: 主题、颜色与代码高亮
features.purpose: 加载主题定义并为终端文本、Markdown 与代码提供样式。
features.behavior: 样式属于呈现层；主题资源有独立验证与重载机制。

features.title: 系统主题与终端调色板
features.purpose: 默认从终端调色板派生颜色，并支持独立主题切换与重载。
features.behavior: 主题改变显示颜色；终端能力和调色板读取决定最终效果。

features.title: Radius 登录与 MCP 一步配置
features.purpose: 在登录菜单中提供 Radius 认证，并在完成登录后引导配置其 MCP 服务。
features.behavior: 模型凭据与 MCP 连接属于不同对象，服务采用提供商认证配置复用 token。

features.title: 模型目录刷新与搜索界面
features.purpose: 读取更新目录并在模型选择界面中查找可用模型，维护本地目录与提供商声明的组合。
features.behavior: 目录记录不保证认证有效；查找与刷新和实际发出模型请求分开。

features.title: 网络代理、归因与连接管理
features.purpose: 集中处理请求的代理、连接超时与提供商归因等配置。
features.behavior: 这些是请求基础设施，离线文档不会触发这些网络操作。

features.title: 诊断、错误记录与问题报告
features.purpose: 收集诊断信息、启动耗时与问题报告内容。
features.behavior: 诊断数据可能含运行上下文；报告上传与本地记录分别处理。

features.title: 源码解析器与历史实验资料
features.purpose: 将工作区包导入解析到当前 TypeScript 源码，供本地运行和断点调试。
features.behavior: 实验 CLI 与服务栈已移除；experimental 中遗留中文 README 是历史资料，不能作为可运行应用入口。

features.title: 终端程序状态与取消结果
features.purpose: 向支持 OSC 7501 的终端报告工作、等待交互、完成或失败；agent_settled 的 aborted 区分取消与完成。
features.behavior: 状态协议依赖终端能力；会话最终通知仍在自动重试与压缩处理之后。

features.title: 默认工具的增减选择
features.purpose: 在默认工具集合上添加或排除指定工具，例如 -t +codemode,-write。
features.behavior: 恢复会话先沿用已保存的活动工具，再应用 CLI 增减项；明确替换或 --no-tools 可覆盖。最终工具仍受排除与暴露约束。

features.title: 配置与主题 Schema 校验
features.purpose: 用显式 Schema 校验设置、快捷键与主题。主题拒绝顶层和 colors/export 内未知属性。
features.behavior: 旧主题的自定义颜色应放 vars，更新 $schema 路径并清理不支持的元数据。

features.title: 摘要输出预算与触发阈值分离

features.title: 按插件提供工具与界面
features.purpose: 工具的执行定义与 Web/TUI 呈现由各插件提供。
features.behavior: 包含模型、MCP OAuth、文件、终端、环境与子智能体；具体启用由插件配置决定，目录存在不表示已在本机运行。

features.title: 消息、工具与多轮循环
features.purpose: 维护内存消息、工具批次、steering/follow-up、模型上下文变换与取消。
features.behavior: 当前 Agent 是内存运行循环；持久 Harness 在 pi-durable，CLI 会话由 coding-agent 管理。

features.title: 独立工具管线与前后 Hook
features.purpose: 让宿主通过 runToolCall 复用参数校验、beforeToolCall、执行及 afterToolCall。
features.behavior: 适合嵌套调用；宿主直接调用 tool.execute 会跳过此管线。

features.title: 代理流与状态事件
features.purpose: 将代理返回的响应流映射为 Agent 使用的事件与消息。
features.behavior: 是否使用由宿主注入的流函数决定。

features.title: 根入口与类型 · 支撑实现
features.purpose: Agent · 消息与工具执行的 root 文件尚未单独作语义解读，在此按实现目录完整列出。
features.behavior: 目录归属是索引依据；具体作用请结合原始注释、完整实现与双向引用阅读。

features.title: 统一消息、模型与工具契约
features.purpose: 定义统一请求/响应、模型能力和工具调用数据。
features.behavior: 根入口保持核心能力；具体提供商通过子路径接入。

features.title: 模型目录、缓存与生成数据
features.purpose: 组织模型元数据与目录存储。
features.behavior: 自动生成数据列为资源，不能把每个模型记录当成独立执行功能。

features.title: 凭据存储、解析与 OAuth
features.purpose: 统一凭据来源、登录流程与刷新。
features.entry: 认证上下文 / OAuth 子路径
features.behavior: 认证策略随提供商而异；平台差异通过入口隔离。

features.title: 按凭据个性化 OpenRouter 模型目录
features.purpose: 读取 /models/user，按当前 key 可用模型过滤聊天目录并更新上下文、输出上限与定价。
features.behavior: 无凭据或 401/403/404 时保留输入目录；其他失败抛错。coding-agent 的 ModelRuntime.create 用 withPersonalizedCatalog 接入此函数。

features.title: OpenAI ChatGPT 登录与 OAuth 回调
features.purpose: 让 OpenAI 提供商使用 ChatGPT 登录凭据，并支持浏览器回调处理。
features.behavior: 认证方法选择与模型服务不同；deviceId 和凭据由产品层配置存储。

features.title: 远端浏览器与复制代码登录
features.purpose: 在浏览器不运行于 Pi 所在机器时处理复制代码/回调的授权流程。
features.behavior: 这是认证交互路径，不改变模型消息与工具契约。

features.title: Anthropic 工作负载联合身份
features.purpose: 从提供商支持的环境配置解析身份认证，可使用 API key、OAuth 或联合身份路径。
features.behavior: 是否可用由所选提供商声明与实际凭据决定；文档快照不读取用户认证文件。

features.title: 模型协议适配与惰性加载
features.purpose: 把统一请求映射到各模型协议，再规范化流式结果。
features.behavior: 包含 OpenAI、Anthropic、Google、Bedrock、Mistral、分类/图像等适配；具体清单由文件索引列出。

features.title: Anthropic 严格工具 Schema 适配
features.purpose: 转换统一消息与工具定义，区分支持 strict 的参数 schema，并处理提供商流式结果。
features.behavior: strict 能力取决于 schema 关键词及提供商契约；工具参数最终仍经执行层校验。

features.title: 类型化分类问题、评分与选择
features.purpose: 对 JSON state 提 choice/score/bool 问题，返回答案、概率或评分，而非聊天文本。
features.behavior: 具体可选 ID、支持协议与认证由模型目录和提供商决定。

features.title: 图片模型与注册表
features.purpose: 提供图像生成相关模型与 API 注册机制。
features.behavior: 不等同于对话中的图片输入；两条路径分别有契约。

features.title: 流事件、校验、重试与转录工具
features.purpose: 支持增量 JSON、工具参数验证、消息转换、重试、取消和溢出判断。
features.entry: 工具函数 / Provider 实现
features.behavior: 具体函数、参数与注释由 AST 提取，避免依名字猜契约。

features.title: 兼容入口与 API 别名
features.purpose: 提供旧调用形态与兼容入口。
features.behavior: 兼容层是否使用取决于调用者；与无副作用根入口区分。

features.title: AI 命令行入口
features.purpose: 提供 AI 包的命令行入口。
features.behavior: 与 coding-agent 的 pi 产品入口分开。

features.title: 客户端身份、User-Agent 与归因
features.purpose: 为请求设置客户端身份，统一 User-Agent 与提供商归因头。
features.behavior: 调用级身份覆盖默认值；认证凭据与客户端归因是不同机制。CLI 已通过 pi-ai 传递身份。

features.title: 模型请求与轮询的显式遥测
features.purpose: 提供 AI_TELEMETRY_SCHEMA 与 request/poll span、首事件、用量和指标。
features.behavior: 已替代 telemetryContext，无兼容别名；取消标记与 provider_error 分开，未知费用不推算。

features.title: 脚本格式、选项行与语法契约
features.purpose: 解析原始脚本和首行 @options，保留行号，并提供支持语法约束模型的 Lark grammar。
features.behavior: 解析器不自行执行 timeout/output 选项；宿主决定策略。

features.title: 工具 TypeScript 声明与标识符映射
features.purpose: 从 JSON Schema 生成模型可读工具声明，规范化工具与命名空间标识符。
features.behavior: 声明不是运行时参数校验；递归或远程 schema 引用降为 unknown。

features.title: WASM 编译缓存与打包宿主接入
features.purpose: 加载缓存 QuickJS wasm，允许打包宿主显式传入 wasm 与 Worker 位置。
features.behavior: 包资源路径不一定存在于单文件可执行程序，打包宿主需提供相应入口。

features.title: 沙箱宿主、工具桥接与截止时间
features.purpose: 每次 execute 创建 Worker 和独立 VM，向宿主转发工具消息并管理取消、超时与关闭。
features.behavior: 脚本错误以结果返回；未等待工具在结束时取消，外部操作副作用不自动回滚。

features.title: 确定性启动与有序响应投递
features.purpose: 以固定起始时间、随机种子和 UTC 环境启动脚本，由宿主按顺序投递工具结果。
features.behavior: 响应序号从 1 连续递增，虚拟时间单调；恢复要求相同代码指纹。库只提供执行契约，持久日志由 Durable 管理。

features.title: QuickJS Worker 与能力隔离
features.purpose: 在 WebAssembly 的 QuickJS 实例内执行 async 函数体，注册工具与输出、存储 globals。
features.behavior: 脚本没有 Node、fetch、模块或 timer；宿主注入函数是外部能力边界。

features.title: JSON Store 复制与容量限制
features.purpose: 为脚本提供同步 store/load 与 JSON 值副本，成功结果报告 set/delete 写入。
features.behavior: 库不持久化 store；宿主负责保存，失败执行不提交 storeWrites。

features.title: 文本图像输出、调用状态与错误分类
features.purpose: 收集 text、image、console、return，记录工具完成/错误/取消及脚本失败原因。
features.behavior: 仅支持 base64 图像，存在总输出大小和条数限制；图像落盘由 coding-agent 产品层实现。

features.title: 可移植、同线程与远程沙箱
features.purpose: 用统一 CodemodeSandboxBase 契约支持 Node Worker、同线程 VM 与远程 isolate 三种部署方式。
features.behavior: portable 入口无 Node 导入；远程 VM 执行脚本，工具仍在调用者一侧执行；同线程 interruptBudget 限制不等待工具的计算。

features.title: 根入口与类型 · 支撑实现
features.purpose: Codemode · 脚本沙箱的 root 文件尚未单独作语义解读，在此按实现目录完整列出。
features.behavior: 目录归属是索引依据；具体作用请结合原始注释、完整实现与双向引用阅读。

features.title: MCP 握手、请求关联与取消
features.purpose: 提供传输中立客户端，管理 initialize、请求 ID、取消、超时与通知。
features.behavior: 传输负责 I/O，客户端负责协议；不是 MCP 服务端，当前不支持 batch、sampling 与 tasks。

features.title: stdio 进程传输与进程组关闭
features.purpose: 启动本地 MCP 子进程，用标准输入输出交换 JSON-RPC 消息，捕获 stderr 并关闭整组进程。
features.behavior: 停止时先关 stdin，再使用终止与强制终止步骤；command 与 args 分开，不按 shell 字符串执行。

features.title: Streamable HTTP、SSE 流与断点续接
features.purpose: 通过 HTTP POST 和服务端流传输消息，管理 session、重连和 Last-Event-ID 续接。
features.behavior: 使用 Streamable HTTP 协议中的事件流，不等于旧 HTTP+SSE 传输；调用是否重放要按协议/应用边界判断。

features.title: OAuth 资源与授权服务器发现
features.purpose: 读取受保护资源元数据和授权服务器元数据，为授权选择真实端点。
features.behavior: 这是 MCP OAuth 子路径的能力；配置和 issuer 校验需对照实际返回数据。

features.title: OAuth 回环回调与状态校验
features.purpose: 监听本机回调并等待授权结果，核对 state 和预期 issuer。
features.behavior: 回调 URI、端口与 CIMD 路径受配置约束，授权响应不能只取 code 而跳过校验。

features.title: OAuth PKCE、注册、刷新与升级授权
features.purpose: 实现授权码 PKCE、动态注册或 CIMD、共享刷新和 insufficient_scope 的升级授权。
features.behavior: 凭据持久化由注入 StateStore 完成；库不自行打开浏览器或选择保存目录。

features.title: MCP 内容转为模型消息
features.purpose: 把工具结果中的文本、图像和嵌入资源转为 LLM 内容，纯 structuredContent 转成 JSON。
features.behavior: 音频、资源链接与其他二进制返回短占位；Pi 产品层资源工具还有独立临时文件处理。

features.title: 内存传输与协议测试支撑
features.purpose: 在进程内成对交换 MCP 消息，为客户端与适配器验证提供无需网络的传输。
features.behavior: 用于测试与宿主适配，不是生产外部服务器。

features.behavior: 目录归属是索引依据；具体作用请结合原始注释、完整实现与双向引用阅读。

features.title: 文档、条目、任务与 ID 契约
features.purpose: 定义持久记录类型、文档语义和任务阶段。
features.behavior: 这些记录契约与 CLI JSONL 条目不是同一套 API。

features.title: 会话事务、分叉与观察
features.purpose: 组织持久会话、提交事务、分叉与观察。
features.behavior: 存储事务与观察者通知有专门边界。

features.title: 会话执行、注册表与调度
features.purpose: 组合模型与工具注册、会话配置及任务调度。
features.behavior: 以当前实现为准；设计文档不代表所有计划已经落地。

features.title: 扩展注册、工具覆写与在线替换
features.purpose: 把工具、提示区块、hook、wrapper 与任务定义组成命名扩展，支持同名替换。
features.behavior: 运行中的阶段保留已解析代码，新阶段使用新注册表；会话保存名字而不是代码对象。

features.title: 逐会话模型、工具和工作目录配置
features.purpose: 在 pi.agent 文档保存会话级 agent 选择，继承或修改宿主默认配置。
features.behavior: 请求准备时固定模型和提示；当前 cwd 与扩展在后续工具阶段可重新解析。

features.title: 提示区块、上下文投影与位置化系统条目
features.purpose: 按已选扩展组织 system sections、会话说明、上下文重置与压缩投影。
features.behavior: 提示或工具变化被记录成系统条目；只发变化可保留提供商缓存，历史不会被 reset 物理删除。

features.title: 持久输入队列、幂等提交与撤回
features.purpose: 在忙碌会话中保存 steer、follow-up 和 write，提供可恢复的 Submission 等待/撤回。
features.behavior: 同 requestId 重用原提交；取消等待只取消等待者，不自动终止底层工作。

features.title: 应用自定义输入条目与即时展示写入
features.purpose: 输入可保留应用条目 kind/data，同时向模型投影用户内容；纯展示 write 可在忙碌时直接提交。
features.behavior: 自定义 kind 不可占用 pi.*；带 model、head 或 edits 的写入仍排队到运行边界，排队 reset 也影响写入顺序。

features.title: 持久模型生成、重试与续轮
features.purpose: 将请求意图、流式 partial、模型回答和下一轮工具计划作为任务阶段提交。
features.behavior: 模型调用与可观察状态以提交为边界，重启恢复工作；provider session identity 持久保存。

features.title: 工具任务、重放安全与结果控制
features.purpose: 在执行之前提交工具意图，持久化输出，并运行前后 hook、用量与 terminate/handoff。
features.behavior: 重启只重跑显式安全任务；其他中断调用形成 interrupted 结果，避免重复外部副作用。

features.title: 延迟工具检索与模型工具装载
features.purpose: 以 BM25 检索延迟工具元数据与参数 schema，将命中项加入模型后续请求的工具声明。
features.behavior: 默认最多 8 项；此工具只允许模型调用，且可安全重放。模型声明与工具执行资格分开。

features.title: 持久脚本、日志重放与嵌套工具
features.purpose: 将脚本执行注册为持久工具，先记录外部响应再交付虚拟机，重启时重放日志并重新关联未完成子调用。
features.behavior: 已完成子调用不重复执行；代码指纹、版本或响应顺序不匹配时失败。关闭沙箱不等于确定脚本最终结果。

features.title: 脚本工具声明、按需发现与命名空间
features.purpose: 按命名空间生成脚本可用声明，控制内联预算并提供 searchTools、describeTool 等发现接口。
features.behavior: 默认内联预算 3000 tokens；延迟工具通过查询发现，工具可调用资格与模型直接声明分别管理。

features.title: 持久脚本分类与图像模型
features.purpose: 将模型目录、分类和图像生成接到可恢复的嵌套调用。
features.behavior: 可以禁用模型助手；执行与恢复仍遵循持久任务和提供商契约。

features.title: 脚本结果、调用清单与跨轮存储
features.purpose: 组织脚本、耗时、文本、控制台、图像文件和嵌套调用状态，并维护会话分支中的 store/load。
features.behavior: 完整大文本写临时文件；结构化错误值的返回与抛错由工具 schema 和输出决定。

features.title: 执行环境与输出捕获
features.purpose: 提供文件/进程环境与可截断输出管理。
features.behavior: abort、timeout 与 cleanup 等待所属命令收尾。Windows 使用 IPC supervisor 与 taskkill/MSYS 子树清理；POSIX 使用进程组。执行环境不是操作系统沙箱。

features.title: Durable 编码工具与环境隔离
features.purpose: 提供 read/write/edit/bash/powershell，通过逐调用的 ExecutionEnv 访问文件与进程。
features.behavior: read 支持图像和可选处理器；文件修改按 env.id 与路径串行。bash/powershell 非零退出返回带 exit_code 诊断的错误结果。

features.title: 文件监视、字节解码与大文件扫描
features.purpose: 为执行环境提供可靠监视、分块解码、行扫描、目录分页与字节范围读取。
features.behavior: Windows 监视采用轮询以避免目录句柄阻止重命名；实际平台分支以实现为准。

features.title: 后台压缩、溢出恢复与陈旧摘要处理
features.purpose: 把压缩做成独立任务，允许会话继续，按边界放置摘要并处理过时 cut。
features.behavior: 手动、后台和溢出压缩有不同触发；摘要费用计入用量，旧条目仍保留。

features.title: 阻塞压缩失败与等待环检测
features.purpose: 压缩失败使依赖它的生成停止并公开最近失败；任务调度拒绝形成等待环的等待关系。
features.behavior: 成功摘要清除最近压缩失败；失败期间不继续发送本次模型请求。等待环错误需要修正任务依赖。

features.title: 持久子会话、背景任务与取消传播
features.purpose: 工具在原子提交中创建 task-owned 子会话，由所有权传播终止；背景锚点让子会话独立继续。
features.behavior: 安全重放需复用子会话和 requestId；前台和后台的取消/空闲行为不同。

features.title: 任务所有权、子任务等待与实时任务图
features.purpose: 观察活跃任务状态及 owner/子会话关系，调度 allSettled 或 failFast 等待并收尾。
features.behavior: 后台任务构成取消与空闲边界；任务图显示活跃任务，不替代完整审计历史。

features.title: 文档与任务图观察
features.purpose: 订阅文档、会话和任务图状态，不再从消息事件组装视图。
features.behavior: WatchCall 以 kind 区分 value 与 failed，WatchEnd 以 kind 区分结束原因；文档退休后地址观察仍可等待新文档。

features.title: 会话视图与完整 Transcript
features.purpose: 从有界会话视图合并长历史，按需补齐缺口。
features.behavior: watchEvents 已移除。默认视图从最新 50 条开始，超过 100 条收缩至 50；模型上下文使用 context()，历史使用 entries()。

features.title: 按模型、工具与会话累计用量
features.purpose: 把生成、压缩、嵌套工具的 token 和费用写入 pi.usage，支持会话和整个 Harness 汇总。
features.behavior: 失败或取消但已有用量的尝试也计入；数值依赖提供商实际报告。

features.title: 内存存储
features.purpose: 提供进程内的记录与事务契约实现。
features.behavior: 内存实现不提供进程退出后的磁盘恢复。

features.title: JSONL 存储与 Node 文件适配
features.purpose: 将持久提交写到文件记录和 sidecar。
features.behavior: 单写入者所有权与 fsync 选项影响耐久性。

features.title: SQLite 存储、迁移与 Node 适配
features.purpose: 用 SQLite 保存持久记录并执行有序 schema 迁移。
features.behavior: 当前 portable SQLite 核心使用 Promise 数据库 facade，事务内必须使用事务句柄。

features.title: 存储一致性用例与基准
features.purpose: 让存储实现复用相同契约测试及读写负载。
features.behavior: 基准是比较基础，不是生产容量保证。

features.title: 持久嵌套调用与结构化输出
features.purpose: executeTool 将子调用记录为调用者拥有的 pi.tool 任务，经过校验、hook、输出限制和重放策略；structuredOutput 给程序调用者使用。
features.behavior: 模型结果使用 output；嵌套调用以 key 重新关联，调用者结束前取消遗留子调用。modelTools 与 callers 分开控制模型声明和调用资格。

features.title: 存储故障与有界缓存
features.purpose: 存储异常使 Session 失败关闭并拒绝后续操作；未被观察的文档按 documentRetentionMs 释放，活跃工作决定调度索引保留范围。
features.behavior: 读取时的 StorageRequestError 或调用方取消只使该次读取失败；commit/mintId 的错误没有此豁免，会使 Session 失败。存储重试由后端负责。文档缓存默认十分钟，0 表示使用后释放，再次访问从存储加载。

features.title: 图像读取与可选 WASM 处理器
features.purpose: read 返回模型支持且符合限制的图像，注入 images 处理器可旋转、转换和缩小图片。
features.behavior: Node loader 在 worker 中处理图像，空闲 30 秒后退出；模型无图像输入能力时返回占位诊断。

features.title: 浏览器 IndexedDB 存储
features.purpose: 在浏览器中持久保存会话、文档、条目与任务。
features.behavior: 与 memory、JSONL、SQLite 共用 Storage 契约；使用前核对浏览器 IndexedDB 可用性。

features.title: 只读 Harness 与批量提交接收
features.purpose: 只读查看会话；批量存储逐项确认已耐久的提交。
features.behavior: receive(index, seq) 对每个已存批次调用一次；返回 stored/refused。I/O 失败是结果未知，不是业务拒绝；已收到的回执仍有效。

features.title: 持久睡眠、宿主时钟与唤醒
features.purpose: 任务结束阶段进入 sleeping，到期从持久 checkpoint 继续；wake/onWake 让宿主决定下次运行。
features.behavior: sleepUntil 替代旧 TaskRuntime.sleep；睡眠不持有 invocation。SQLite schema v2 不能由 1.3.0 或更早版本打开。

features.title: 无进展重启上限与运行失败
features.purpose: 重启连续到达 restartLimit 后结束任务，公开失败原因。
features.behavior: 默认上限 5；任务不再停放，旧 retryTask 已移除。工具返回 restart_limit，重新执行需提交新的工作。

features.title: 持久任务与提交遥测
features.purpose: 记录接纳、phase、提交、嵌套重放、指标与固定报告字段，显式传播 span。
features.behavior: 遥测不保存提示正文作为常规属性；业务状态仍以持久提交为准。

features.title: 动态模型设置与失败后队列策略
features.purpose: 在使用时读取宿主提供的 models/settings 函数，并按模型覆盖压缩阈值、处理失败后排队输入。
features.behavior: keep/continue/withdraw 控制失败后输入；热替换不等于自动重跑已经失败的任务。

features.title: 分组提交与延迟进度落盘
features.purpose: 多个会话共享存储往返；partial 可以先展示再合并落盘。
features.behavior: 默认进度最长延迟 1000ms 落盘；崩溃可丢失该窗口的 partial。观察视图不等于耐久回执，observeCommits 只观察已存提交。

features.title: 继续、轮数上限与运行后任务
features.purpose: 提供 continue、turnLimit、事务内 submit、afterRun 与逐会话压缩设置。
features.entry: submit(tx, draft) / whenIdle / afterRun / configure({ compaction })
features.behavior: 输入接纳与应用记录可在一个事务内完成；回答已提交后 afterRun 子任务仍可使会话保持忙碌，不能把 Submission.wait 等同于完全 idle。

features.title: 根入口与类型 · 支撑实现
features.purpose: Durable · 持久任务与文档的 root 文件尚未单独作语义解读，在此按实现目录完整列出。
features.behavior: 目录归属是索引依据；具体作用请结合原始注释、完整实现与双向引用阅读。

features.title: SSH 主机信任与 daemon 部署
features.purpose: 发现远端系统、部署按 SHA-256 命名的 daemon，并在启动前校验；也可在首个操作时惰性连接。
features.behavior: 主机指纹由用户带外确认；严格检查应用独立 known-hosts，禁用转发。首次操作失败后由下一操作重新尝试连接。

features.title: 远程文件、命令与连接
features.purpose: 通过分帧 stdio 协议连接远端 Rust daemon，为 Durable 工具提供远程 ExecutionEnv。
features.behavior: 远端执行文件和命令操作，Durable worker、存储与凭据留在本机；错误文本可能与本地环境不同。

features.title: 远端 PTY、窗口大小与前台进程
features.purpose: 通过 daemon 打开交互伪终端，接收原始字节、写入输入、调整尺寸并查询退出与前台程序。
features.behavior: 当前 Windows 不支持 PTY；Linux、macOS、Termux 使用相应平台实现。连接断开或关闭会结束所属程序与会话。

features.title: 根入口与类型 · 支撑实现
features.purpose: Env · 远程执行环境的 root 文件尚未单独作语义解读，在此按实现目录完整列出。
features.behavior: 目录归属是索引依据；具体作用请结合原始注释、完整实现与双向引用阅读。

features.title: 键盘、鼠标与输入缓存
features.purpose: 解析终端输入事件并映射到可配置动作。
features.behavior: 终端协议报告与普通输入需要分开处理。

features.title: 滚轮累计与平台修饰键
features.purpose: 处理高精度滚轮和平台修饰状态，避免小滚轮增量丢失或重复。
features.behavior: 终端协议与平台报告影响可用事件；备用屏 contain 会消耗剩余滚动量，防止边界滚动继续带动主区。

features.title: 路径、斜杠命令与模糊补全
features.purpose: 根据输入生成补全候选与模糊排序。
features.behavior: 补全逻辑与编辑器替换范围共同决定体验。

features.title: 撤销、Kill Ring 与词边界导航
features.purpose: 保存编辑撤销栈、剪切文本环与单词移动边界，供编辑组件复用。
features.behavior: 编辑历史属于输入状态，不等同于 Agent 会话树。

features.title: 布局节点、测量与滚动几何
features.purpose: 按可用列宽和行数测量布局，安排组件及滚动范围。
features.behavior: 终端列宽与文本字符数不同，测量结果服务于屏幕渲染。

features.title: 布局、滚动、输入与选择组件
features.purpose: 提供盒子、横纵布局、编辑器、列表、Markdown、图像和加载指示。
features.behavior: 每种组件的具体属性与方法在符号清单中可查。

features.title: 主屏、替代屏与差分渲染
features.purpose: 将组件行合成为终端输出并管理屏幕模式。
features.behavior: 渲染只处理展示，模型状态由上层传入。

features.title: 全屏搜索与匹配导航
features.purpose: 在全屏终端维护匹配与搜索高亮，支持定位当前渲染内容。
features.behavior: 检索的是终端呈现内容，源码、MCP 工具与会话存储检索属于其他功能。

features.title: Unicode 宽度、ANSI 与 LaTeX
features.purpose: 按终端显示列处理文本、链接、换行和公式。
features.behavior: 字符数量不等于终端列宽。

features.title: 颜色空间、样式与终端色值
features.purpose: 解析和转换颜色，组合文本样式并读取终端颜色。
features.behavior: 终端能力可能影响最终颜色显示。

features.title: 图像协议与能力探测
features.purpose: 处理 Kitty/iTerm2 图像与原生平台能力发现。
features.behavior: 终端不支持时使用对应回退路径。

features.title: 根入口与类型 · 支撑实现
features.purpose: TUI · 终端界面的 root 文件尚未单独作语义解读，在此按实现目录完整列出。
features.behavior: 目录归属是索引依据；具体作用请结合原始注释、完整实现与双向引用阅读。

features.title: Windows 平台桥接
features.purpose: 提供 Windows 原生平台和剪贴板实现及构建。
features.behavior: 二进制预构建仅列入资源清单，不解析为 TypeScript 符号。

features.title: macOS 平台桥接
features.purpose: 提供 macOS 原生平台能力与构建脚本。
features.behavior: Objective-C 代码保留全文，符号不由 TypeScript 解析。

features.title: Linux X11 平台桥接
features.purpose: 提供 Linux X11 剪贴板和工作线程适配。
features.behavior: 可用性取决于实际显示服务与平台条件。

features.title: 原生桥接头文件
features.purpose: 定义原生模块共享接口。
features.behavior: 属于平台实现支撑。

features.title: Chord v2 对象契约与宿主地址
features.purpose: 以 pi-schema 定义 params、members、variants 与版本。
features.behavior: remote 使用 hostAddress 决定宿主地址；提供远程对象的 host 必须有 address 和 principal。

features.title: Facet 声明、Host 激活与引用
features.purpose: 工厂只声明对象，Host 负责激活、失败重试、持有与释放。
features.entry: createHost / defineFacet / host.load / host.get / host.hold / host.root
features.behavior: get 等待 live 且状态已就绪；hold 立即给引用，最后释放与调用、job 等持有共同决定存活。

features.title: 持久文档、派生状态与原生资源
features.purpose: defineState 声明文档，self.state 取得状态，self.tx 在事务内修改。
features.behavior: self.open 管理原生资源；watchable 发布失败与恢复。旧版本的命名 cell 迁移接口不能直接复用。

features.title: 远程路由、链路与状态同步
features.purpose: 在浏览器、server、worker 间路由对象引用和调用。
features.behavior: 断链后引用进入 loading 并可重新绑定；已经发出的调用和远端副作用仍需按结果边界核对。调用响应排在其状态更新之后。

features.title: 插件重载与旧工作收尾
features.purpose: 插件变更逐宿主展开；受影响对象重新启动。
features.behavior: 采用 restart-only 重载；旧工作沿旧代码收尾，新对象重新激活，持久数据由 store 保存。不能沿用旧 cell version/migrate 的说明。

features.title: 注册表贡献与组合
features.purpose: 插件声明提供者与贡献，通过可观察组合值装配应用能力。
features.behavior: 注册表跟随生命周期与批次发布；Durable registryReader 可以读取注册表组合。

features.title: 按地址启动 worker 与基础代码快照
features.purpose: 按 host kind 和地址路由到进程，空闲退出并管理插件代码。
features.behavior: worker 基础代码在 server 启动时打包；新的 worker 仍使用该快照，基础代码变化需要重启 server。

features.title: 事务 JSON 增量与不可变应用
features.purpose: 计算候选变更，采用后发布新的权威值。
features.behavior: prepare 不改变权威值，adopt 才切换；传出后不可变是所有权约定。

features.title: 取消上下文与调用数据
features.purpose: 显式传递取消、截止时间和调用范围值。
features.behavior: 调用方负责提供上下文；上下文不是认证系统。

features.title: JSON 边界与带类型错误
features.purpose: 描述 JSON 值、失败与错误分类。
features.behavior: 在外部输入边界验证；同宿主的已类型化值按不可变约定传递。

features.title: WatchCall 与结束原因
features.purpose: 统一 tagged value/failed 通知、增量合并与永久结束。
features.behavior: 监听者接收 call 和 context；retired 是 value 通知字段，不是永久结束。JSON 增量超过 10000 个待处理操作后用根替换；NativeWatch 超过 100 个待处理值时合并。

features.title: 有界输出与进度节奏
features.purpose: 共享 OutputBuffer、boundOutput 和 Progress，控制流式输出窗口及提交频率。
features.behavior: ProgressClock 可注入 now/setTimer，当前默认 Date.now 和 setTimeout；定时回调再次检查时钟。节奏按提交起点计算，限制输出不代表回滚已经产生的操作。

features.title: 通用 SQLite、迁移与驱动
features.purpose: 提供数据库契约、原子迁移、前缀校验以及 Node / Cloudflare 驱动。
features.behavior: 从 Durable 迁入共享层；Durable 自身存储与 schema 迁移仍在 durable，版本从 1 连续递增。

features.title: 持久 Store、表与批量提交
features.purpose: 保存对象文档、表、事务与任务，供 Durable StoreStorage 复用。
features.behavior: 一批存储调用保留各提交的结果；复制是另外的实验 sync 层。

features.title: HTTP、应用与 Web/TUI 客户端
features.purpose: 提供应用装配、身份、设备配对、文件和界面插件基础能力。
features.behavior: Node 服务端、浏览器与终端入口隔离；应用负责具体工具授权与部署。

features.title: 实验性 Store 复制
features.purpose: 将 outbox 提交上传到远端槽位，在副本拉取并折叠快照。
features.behavior: 这是实验复制接口，不代表应用自动获得多写入者冲突处理。

features.title: 根入口与类型 · 支撑实现
features.purpose: Chord · 对象与热重载的 root 文件尚未单独作语义解读，在此按实现目录完整列出。
features.behavior: 目录归属是索引依据；具体作用请结合原始注释、完整实现与双向引用阅读。

features.title: jobs · 支撑实现
features.purpose: Chord · 对象与热重载的 jobs 文件尚未单独作语义解读，在此按实现目录完整列出。
features.behavior: 目录归属是索引依据；具体作用请结合原始注释、完整实现与双向引用阅读。

features.title: node · 支撑实现

symbols.name: AgentLink
symbols.comment: A script's call of a one-shot agent: its conversation, once the agent has one.

apps/p2/plugins/agent/activity.tsx.comment:
How the `agent` tool (a script's one-shot agent) shows in the chat: its label or what it was asked, and from the

script's call its conversation one tap away.

symbols.name: AgentRun
symbols.comment: The call's conversation, created once, so a rerun after a restart reattaches to it and its submissions.

symbols.name: createAgentExtension
symbols.signature: export function createAgentExtension(models: Models, access: () => ReadonlyMap<string, P2Tool>): Extension<P2Tool>
symbols.comment: `access` gives the worker's tools by name, with what they declare (`P2Tool`): which ones the agent may get.

apps/p2/plugins/agent/tool.ts.comment:
One-shot subagents for code mode scripts. `await tools.agent({ prompt, schema })` runs a fresh conversation and

resolves to its final answer, parsed as JSON and validated against `schema`. Nothing is reported to the main

conversation: only the script's return value reaches it.

apps/p2/plugins/agent/web.tsx.comment: The one-shot agents' web facet: how their calls show in the chat (activity.tsx).

apps/p2/plugins/agent/worker.ts.comment:
Code mode's one-shot `agent` tool, contributed unconditionally. Only scripts can call it (`callers: ["tools"]`), so

without code mode nothing reaches it, and its prompt section renders only while a conversation can call both

`codemode` and `agent`. Code mode stays independently removable: no import of its plugin. Its conversations are listed

with the subagents (one-shot entries of their document), which is where their sidebar metadata and read-only rule live.

symbols.name: artifactOf
symbols.comment: The version a call made, when its details are a complete, valid version (they come from the tool's result).

symbols.name: ArtifactResult
symbols.signature: function ArtifactResult({ tool, inline }: { tool: ToolView; inline: boolean })
symbols.comment: The artifact's card; in the chat, the artifact itself below it when the agent asked to show it inline.
inputs: { tool, inline }: { tool: ToolView; inline: boolean }

apps/p2/plugins/artifacts/activity.tsx.comment:
How the `artifact` tool shows in the chat: "Made <title>", and the version it made as a card that opens the viewer,

after the turn's answer; when the agent asked to show it inline, in place instead, with the artifact itself below it.

symbols.name: ArtifactList
symbols.comment: The complete per-conversation index, independent of compaction/reset and transcript paging.

symbols.name: MAX_ARTIFACT_PREVIEW
symbols.comment: Inline previews read at most this much of an artifact (the rest is a download).

symbols.name: ArtifactContent
symbols.comment:
An artifact's content for clients that cannot use the `/artifact` route (the TUI's worker has no cookie): text and
Markdown are shown inline, HTML and SVG as source. Same authority as the route: anyone who may view the session.
At most `MAX_ARTIFACT_PREVIEW` characters; `truncated` says there is more.

symbols.name: ArtifactSource
symbols.comment:
An artifact's whole source for the server's `/artifact` route (the session's worker, the server only: the route
authorizes the viewer, the worker owns the bytes). At most 2 MiB of UTF-8.

symbols.name: FrameMessage
symbols.signature: type FrameMessage = Diagnostic | { level: "size"; height: number };
symbols.comment: What a preview frame posts on the diagnostic channel: a diagnostic, or its content height (`store.ts`).

symbols.name: frameMessage
symbols.comment: A message from a preview frame (untrusted: the artifact's own script can post anything).

symbols.name: useFrameMessages
symbols.comment: Calls `receive` with each message the frame posts on the diagnostic channel.

symbols.name: useArtifactText
symbols.signature: function useArtifactText(url: string | undefined): { content?: string; error?: string }
symbols.comment: A text or Markdown artifact's content from its route: undefined while it loads, or the error.

symbols.name: ArtifactFrame
symbols.comment: The sandboxed frame of an HTML or SVG preview: an opaque origin, and the route's CSP sandbox on top.

symbols.name: ArtifactPanel
frameHeights
symbols.comment:
The heights inline frames last reported, by URL (versions are immutable), so a row the transcript mounts again
keeps its size instead of starting at `FRAME_HEIGHT`.

symbols.name: FRAME_HEIGHT
symbols.comment: A frame's height before it reports one.

symbols.name: InlineArtifact
symbols.signature: export function InlineArtifact({ sessionId, artifact }: { sessionId: string; artifact: ArtifactInfo })
symbols.comment:
An artifact version rendered at its tool call site, below the card (`inline: true`): Markdown and text as in the
viewer; HTML and SVG in the viewer's sandboxed frame, sized to the content height it reports after drawings were
scaled to its width (`store.ts`). CSS caps it at about 70vh: taller HTML scrolls inside the frame, an SVG scales
down to fit. Rendered for every viewer of the session (owner decision).
inputs: { sessionId, artifact }: { sessionId: string; artifact: ArtifactInfo }

symbols.name: ArtifactInfo
symbols.signature: export type ArtifactInfo = { name: string; title: string; type: ArtifactType; version: number };
symbols.output: { name: string; title: string; type: ArtifactType; version: number }

symbols.name: ArtifactInput
symbols.signature: export type ArtifactInput = { name: string; title: string; type: ArtifactType; content: string };
symbols.output: { name: string; title: string; type: ArtifactType; content: string }

symbols.name: DIAGNOSTIC_SCRIPT
symbols.comment:
The preview's diagnostics bridge: console errors and warnings, uncaught errors, CSP violations and lost WebGL

contexts, plus the document's content height (level "size", for inline previews sized to their content). Drawings fill

the frame's width: an SVG document with a viewBox (or an absolute width and height, made its viewBox) is set to

100% wide and high, so it scales with its aspect and reports viewBox height at its width; an HTML document whose

body is just a viewBox SVG or an image gets them 100% wide at height auto (zero specificity: any author rule wins).

HTML is measured without its scrollbar: a frame still too short shows one, and the narrower page would report a

taller height, which keeps the scrollbar once the frame grows to it.

symbols.name: instrumentArtifact
symbols.signature: export function instrumentArtifact(info: ArtifactInfo, content: string): string
symbols.comment: Add a diagnostics bridge without changing the immutable stored source.

symbols.name: record
symbols.signature: function record(value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown>

symbols.name: validName
symbols.signature: function validName(name: unknown): name is string

symbols.name: validVersion
symbols.signature: function validVersion(version: unknown): version is number

symbols.name: validTitle
symbols.signature: function validTitle(title: unknown): title is string

symbols.name: validType
symbols.signature: function validType(type: unknown): type is ArtifactType

symbols.name: MIME
symbols.comment: The type an artifact's bytes are stored with.

symbols.name: saveArtifact
symbols.comment:
Saves `input` as the next version of its artifact in the session's files (space `artifacts`, path = its name, Files
versions = artifact versions, never reused), written by the agent of conversation `ref`. Locators do not authorize
access; callers must authorize the session.

symbols.name: readArtifact
symbols.comment: Version `version` of artifact `name` of the session's files; a missing or invalid one is "Artifact not found".

symbols.name: SaveArtifact
symbols.signature: export type SaveArtifact = (input: ArtifactInput, holder: number, context: Context) => Promise<ArtifactInfo>;
symbols.comment: Saves the next version of an artifact for the agent of conversation `holder` (the session's files).
symbols.output: (input: ArtifactInput, holder: number, context: Context) => Promise<ArtifactInfo>

symbols.name: ArtifactDetails
symbols.signature: export type ArtifactDetails = ArtifactInfo & { inline?: true };
symbols.comment:
The tool's result details: the saved version, and `inline: true` when the call asked to show it at the call site
too (the transcripts render that version below the card). The index (`ArtifactDoc`) keeps only `ArtifactInfo`.

symbols.name: ArtifactDoc
symbols.comment:
Complete artifact index of one agent (on conversation 1 for the main agent, see `agentConversation`); reset and
compaction never rewind it.

symbols.name: createArtifactExtension
symbols.comment: The `artifact` tool, saving through `save`.

symbols.name: PREVIEW_LINES
symbols.comment: Collapsed cards show this many lines of a text or Markdown artifact; expanded ones all.

symbols.name: contentReader
symbols.comment: Reads artifact versions of `session` through one held `ArtifactContent`, until released.

symbols.name: ArtifactLines
symbols.comment:
One version of an artifact as lines at a width (Markdown rendered, text and HTML/SVG source), cached per width;
`load` reads a version and renders it once read.

symbols.name: ArtifactLines.cache
symbols.signature: private cache: { width: number; lines: string[] } | undefined;

symbols.name: ArtifactLines.load
symbols.comment: Reads `artifact` (a version) and shows it once read; the previous version stays shown meanwhile.

symbols.name: showArtifact
symbols.signature: function showArtifact(ctx: TuiContext, session: string, artifact: ArtifactInfo): void
symbols.comment: An artifact shown inline, over the chat.

symbols.name: pinArtifact
symbols.signature: function pinArtifact(ctx: TuiContext, session: string, conversation: number, artifact: ArtifactInfo): void
symbols.comment: An artifact pinned in the side panel: it shows each new version as the conversation's artifact list reports it.

apps/p2/plugins/artifacts/tui.ts.comment:
Artifacts in the TUI (p2-tui-port.md P11c), after the web's artifact card, picker and viewer. The card shows the

title, type and version; expanded, a text or Markdown artifact shows the content the call wrote. A call with

`inline: true` shows all of it at once (Markdown rendered); inline HTML and SVG keep the card line. `/artifacts` lists

the conversation's artifacts (`ArtifactList`): Enter shows one inline (`ArtifactContent`; Markdown rendered, HTML and

SVG as source; in the side panel, where it follows new versions, when the terminal is wide enough), Ctrl+B opens it in the browser (launcher `openUrl`; the browser needs its own sign-in) and Ctrl+S

downloads it (launcher `download`). The worker never fetches the `/artifact` route itself: it has no cookie.

symbols.name: viewer
symbols.signature: function viewer(overlay: string | undefined): ViewerItem | undefined
symbols.comment: Untrusted URL metadata is only a locator. HTTP routes authorize every content fetch.

symbols.name: CHAT_ENTRY
symbols.comment: Entry kind of a chat message: display-only, it carries no model message.

symbols.name: MENTION_ENTRY
symbols.comment: Entry kind of a mention: an input whose model message is the digest, and whose data is what the person wrote.

symbols.name: ReplyToSchema
symbols.comment:
The message a reply answers: an entry of the same conversation, with its author and the start of its text. The
worker derives author and excerpt from that entry; a client only names the entry. Pi's answers can be replied to.

symbols.name: ChatMessageSchema
symbols.comment:
A chat entry's data: a person's message (author stamped by the worker, attachments as the session's upload IDs),
perhaps answering another.

symbols.name: MentionSchema
symbols.comment: A mention entry's data: what the person wrote, and the IDs of the chat entries its digest passed on to Pi.

symbols.name: chatMessage
symbols.comment: Entries are history: read their data defensively, never assume this code wrote it.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_AGENT_NAME
symbols.comment:
The name people call the agent by in a conversation (chat mode's setting): one word, as it is spoken and mentioned
("Pi", "Claude"). Letters, digits, `_` and `-`, starting with a letter.

symbols.name: mentionToken
symbols.comment: The mention of the agent called `name`: `@` and the name in lower case ("@pi", "@claude").

symbols.name: escapeName
symbols.comment: The name as a regular expression, matched literally (a valid name holds no special character; `-` is literal).

symbols.name: mentionPattern
symbols.comment:
`@<name>` in any case, as a word of its own: with the default, "@pi", "@Pi," and "(@PI)" mention; "@pizza" and "me@pi"
do not.

symbols.name: spokenName
symbols.comment:
The agent's name spoken anywhere in an utterance, as speech recognition writes it (no "@"): a whole word in any case,
whatever punctuation surrounds it. With the default: "Hey Pi, …", "can Pi summarize this", "what do you think,
Pi?". Not "pie", "piano", "pip" or "Pi-hole"; and not "Pi's": a possessive or contraction talks about the agent more
often than to it ("Pi's answer was odd"), and is cheap to say again.

symbols.name: spokenMention
symbols.signature: export function spokenMention(text: string, name = DEFAULT_AGENT_NAME): string
symbols.comment:
A spoken message as chat mode reads it: one that names the agent gets its mention in front (what was said is kept
whole, for the context: "@pi can Pi summarize this"). One already holding the mention stays as it is.

symbols.name: ChatModeSetting
symbols.comment: One conversation's switch and agent name (worker-local), followed from its Durable document.

symbols.name: ChatMode
symbols.comment:
Chat mode of one conversation as a browser sees it: everyone reads it and the agent's name; only the owner switches
it and renames the agent.

apps/p2/plugins/chat-mode/contract.ts.comment:
Chat mode: the people viewing a conversation talk to each other in its transcript. The agent reads along only

when someone mentions it. Served by each session worker.

symbols.name: MAX_DIGEST_MESSAGES
symbols.comment: At most this many chat messages go into one mention; older ones are counted, not quoted.

symbols.name: MAX_DIGEST_FILES
symbols.comment: At most this many of their attachments are listed (the newest).

symbols.name: MAX_DIGEST_IMAGES
symbols.comment: Inline at most this many images per mention, the newest; the rest are listed by path.

symbols.name: EXCERPT_LENGTH
symbols.comment: At most this many characters of a replied-to message are quoted, whitespace collapsed.

symbols.name: speaker
symbols.signature: function speaker(author: Author, replyTo?: ReplyTo): string
symbols.comment: How a digest names a message's author: `Ann (guest, replying to Bob: "should we split…")`.

symbols.name: excerpt
symbols.comment: The start of a message: whitespace collapsed, cut at EXCERPT_LENGTH characters with an ellipsis.

symbols.name: quoteOf

symbols.comment:
Where a scan may stop: the lowest chat entry the latest placed mention passed on. Its digest took every chat message
not yet passed on, so older ones were passed on before, or dropped by the digest's cap. A mention that passed on
nothing bounds nothing: chat placed while it waited lies below it.

message placed while a mention waited in the queue is not covered by it and goes with the next one. The scan stops
at the lowest chat entry the latest mention passed on (see `boundaryOf`).

apps/p2/plugins/chat/outbox.ts.comment:
Messages sent from the composer, until the server has them: sending never waits for the connection. A message shows
at once as it will look (`Outgoing.item`), and the outbox sends its messages in order whenever a sender is connected
(the conversation's view is open and its chat object live), each with its own request ID: a retried send is admitted
once, so a send whose answer was lost to a broken connection is simply sent again. A message the server refuses goes
back to the composer (`Sender.restore`); one it accepted stays shown until the transcript shows it (`shown`).

One outbox per conversation, kept for the page's lifetime: switching conversations keeps unsent messages, and they
go out once their conversation is open again.

apps/p2/plugins/chat/session-start.ts.comment:
A new session's first messages, before the session exists: Send on the new-session screen shows them at once, as
sending in a conversation does (outbox.ts), and the session is created whenever the page is connected. Once it
exists, the messages move to its main conversation's outbox, which delivers them (uploads, template expansion,
retries), and the page opens the session.

One start per page, kept for the page's lifetime: messages sent while the session is being created join it. The page
chooses the session's ID at the first Send (`Sessions.create` takes it), so a creation whose answer was lost with
the connection is tried again with the same ID and answers the same session. A creation the server refuses (a
directory that does not exist, an unknown model) puts the messages back into the composer; a failure of the
connection is tried again, at most `GIVE_UP` times while connected.

the entry without a gap. One command at a time per conversation; the session neither moves nor clones while one runs.

symbols.name: RunningCalls
symbols.comment:
Problem: removing the plugin by a hot reload closes the sandbox while the Harness stays open. Durable stores no
outcome for a run the sandbox ended on its own (so a restart replays it), and the call then waits for its own
cancellation: nothing would ever settle it.
Solution: on removal (not on a worker stop, after which the next worker replays), each running call reports why in
its output, then is aborted through Durable (`abortTask`), which ends its script and nested calls bottom-up and
settles it with an error result. Only then is the sandbox closed.

destination (`LocationMoveDoc`); once the session's worker has nothing running (the turn ended, no subagent work), it

asks the server to move the session (`SessionMoves`, the same as the owner's Relocate). A refusal because work started

meanwhile is retried after the next commit; a destination that became invalid is recorded as the move's failure.

The record is Durable: a worker that stops first applies it after its next start.

connection (a crashed server, or an environment's connection whose daemon killed it) reconnects with backoff,

keeping its tools listed; a server's tool-list change refreshes its tools.

it enables (one process per session and location, or one for everybody) and its project's own servers (always at

that location), each with how it connects: a program on the p2 host or on an environment, or an HTTP server.

apps/p2/plugins/mcp/probe.ts.comment:
The loopback probe, a native of the manager: a listener on the p2 host's 127.0.0.1 that tells a sign-in page whether

its browser runs on the p2 host. The page (on p2's Radius or public origin) fetches `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/<nonce>`:

only a browser on this machine reaches this listener, and only this p2 knows the nonce, so another program or p2 on

the browser's machine cannot answer for it. A wrong answer costs nothing more than a sign-in to paste.

apps/p2/plugins/mcp/sign-in.ts.comment:
MCP OAuth sign-ins, a native of the manager: the auth provider every OAuth HTTP connection sends its tokens with, and

the sign-in flows, one per server at a time. A flow redirects the browser either to a loopback callback server on the

p2 host (the browser runs there) or to p2's own `/mcp/callback` route (the browser reaches p2 through Radius or a

public host); the final redirect URL pasted by the owner always completes it too. Flows live in memory: a restart

forgets them, the stored tokens stay.

symbols.name: windowsCommand
symbols.signature: export function windowsCommand(command: string, args: readonly string[]): WindowsCommand
symbols.comment:
`command` with `args` as the daemon starts it on Windows: directly for an `.exe` or `.com` path, else through
`cmd.exe /d /s /c`, which finds `npx.cmd` for `npx` through `PATHEXT` as a shell would.

The daemon quotes every argv element itself (libuv's rules) and has no verbatim mode, so a command line in an
argument would reach `cmd.exe` with its quotes escaped as `\"`, which `cmd.exe` does not understand. The command
line goes in an environment variable instead, and `cmd.exe` gets `%P2_MCP_COMMAND%`, which needs no quoting: it
expands the variable before it parses quotes and `^` escapes, so it reads the line as cross-spawn's verbatim one.

symbols.comment:

quote or the end doubled, quotes escaped, the whole quoted, then every meta character escaped with `^`.

The MCP plugin's worker facet: the worker object holding the server's `Mcp` view. It sets the locations the session's

conversations work at (the session's, active subagents' own), with the project `.pi/mcp.json` read at each through

its environment, as its leases, again whenever they may have changed and whenever the view (re)activates, and offers

the servers' tools as one Durable extension that follows the view's `servers` and the code mode switch: as in pi,

tools are for code mode scripts, and only without code mode does `tool_search` (installed by the worker's registry)

load them for the model. No MCP process or credential is ever in a worker.

apps/p2/plugins/ports/protocol.ts.comment:
Port forwards: HTTP services on this device (a dev server on port 5173, say)
that the owner opens through Radius. Each forward gets its own origin,
`https://fwd--<label>--<id>.rdtun.com`, next to the brain's own
`https://<label>.rdtun.com`. Radius authenticates the owner for it; the brain
relays its requests to `localhost:<port>`.

A public forward is also open to anyone, without signing in, at
`https://pub--<label>--<id>.rdtun.com`. The brain alone decides that: Radius
sends unauthenticated requests on, and the brain answers them only for
public forwards.

symbols.name: Forwards
symbols.comment:
The port forwards, kept in `forwards.json` of the data directory as
`{ "<id>": { "port", "name"?, "public"?, "session"? } }`.

The owner manages them in the Ports sheet; a session's agent opens and closes them through the `ports` tool
(`session` names the session that opened one). The agent may change or close any forward; a session's forwards
close when it is archived.

The server is the only reader and writer: the Radius relay client looks a forward up for every relayed request, so
the list lives in memory and every change is written through. A forward's ID is random and becomes part of its URL;
removing a forward and adding the same port again gives a new URL, so a removed forward's links stop working.

symbols.name: Forwards.#saving
symbols.comment: Writes run one at a time, each with the whole list as it is then.

symbols.name: Forwards.#radiusOrigin
symbols.comment: The brain's Radius origin: saved in radius.json, updated from relayed requests for its UI.

symbols.name: HOST_SUBPROTOCOLS
symbols.comment:
p2 as a Radius brain
===========================

The brain keeps one outbound WebSocket to its relay in Radius (relay protocol
v4, `radius/packages/gateway/src/servers/protocol.ts`). Radius multiplexes
every browser connection over it as a channel and tells the brain who opened
it. Each channel becomes a loopback request to this server, marked with the
relay secret so the server treats it as the owner on the brain's cortex origin
(see relay-access.ts). No port is exposed and nothing listens publicly.

The brain's Radius identity is separate from model providers: `radius.json`
in the data directory holds the gateway, a stable server ID, and an OAuth
credential from `npm run radius:login`.

Who may open a channel. The owner reaches everything the owner reaches
locally. Radius also admits people, in any organization, to the brain's UI
when the brain shared a session with their email (`reportShares`): Radius
verifies the email, and the brain passes such a user on as a Radius user (not
an owner), whom p2's sharing maps to the sessions shared with that email now.
A user without an email, service accounts, and everyone but the owner on
forward origins are refused. Browser cookies never reach the server through
the brain's UI channels.

Shares. Radius admits and lists a brain for the emails the brain reports with
`PUT /v1/servers/<id>/shares`, which replaces the whole set. The brain reports
whenever the set changes and after every connect, so a report lost while
offline is repaired by the next connection. Radius learns nothing else: not
which sessions, nor their titles.

Backpressure. Nothing may buffer without bound between a loopback source and
a slow browser; the relay itself cannot see a slow WebSocket reader.

- HTTP channels use the relay's credit flow control (`pi-server.host.v3`):
  response bodies stop at the window until the relay returns credit as the
  browser reads, and request bodies earn the relay credit as the loopback
  request takes them.
- WebSocket channels rely on the application acknowledging end to end (the
  terminal does; see shared/terminals.ts; chord links do too).
- Whatever the case, while more than CONGESTION_HIGH_BYTES are unsent on the
  socket to Radius, every loopback source on it is paused, so a slow uplink
  slows the server down instead of growing this process's memory.

Channel sockets (relay protocol v5). One socket to Radius is one TCP stream:
a 500 KiB transcript snapshot in one tab delays the echo of a terminal in
another by the time the snapshot takes to cross the uplink, and the pause
above stops every channel at once. A v5 relay therefore has the brain open
one socket per WebSocket channel (`/v1/servers/<id>/channels/<connection>`,
authenticated like the host socket), and the brain pipes it to the loopback
socket unchanged. Each direction pauses its source while its destination has
more than PIPE_HIGH_BYTES unsent, so a slow reader slows only its own
channel. HTTP channels stay on the host socket with credit flow control.

Port forwards (relay protocol v4). A channel whose `connection_open` names a
`forward` comes from that forward's own origin
(`fwd--<label>--<forward>.rdtun.com`, see shared/forwards.ts), not from the
brain's UI. It goes to `localhost:<port>` of the forward, never to this
server: it carries no relay secret, `Host` is the target's own, and `Origin`
and redirects to `localhost` are translated between the two origins. A
forward ID this server does not know answers 404 (HTTP) or closes the
channel. `stream` channels, end-to-end forwards whose TLS terminates in the
environment, are not supported yet and are closed at once.

Reconnecting. A network loss rarely closes the socket: packets just stop, and
TCP may take many minutes to notice (after a laptop sleeps, the socket can look
open indefinitely). The brain therefore watches for anything from the relay.
After HEARTBEAT_IDLE_MS of silence it sends a `ping`, which the relay answers
with `pong`; after HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_MS of silence it terminates the socket and
reconnects with backoff. The handshake has its own timeout, so a connection
attempt into a dead network fails instead of hanging. The relay keeps a lost
host until its own heartbeat expires (90 s by default) and refuses a second
one meanwhile with 409. A brain that noticed the loss first would stay
offline until then, up to 90 s, while browsers opened channels into the
dead socket and waited for them to time out. The brain therefore connects with
`?replace=1`: the relay fails the old host and its channels and takes the new
socket at once. Relays that predate the parameter ignore it and answer 409,
which the backoff retries until the old host expires.

Two p2 processes with the same `radius.json` share one server ID, so they
would replace each other in turn. The relay closes a replaced host with 1012
"Server host replaced", and that is always another process: this one gives up
its own socket before it reconnects. The brain then yields: it reconnects
without `replace`, gets 409 until the other process is gone, and replaces
again once it is connected. So the most recently started process wins.

Public forwards. Radius opens channels from a forward's public origin
(`pub--<label>--<forward>`) without a principal: nobody signed in. Such a
channel reaches only a forward the owner marked public; for any other
forward, and for the brain's own UI, it is refused like an unknown forward.

Client channels. A Pi client of the owner, the TUI launcher with `--radius`
(src/hosts/tui-radius.ts), connects to Radius with its own bearer credential
(`pi-server.client.v2`). Radius then opens a `ws` channel with the principal
but without a request or public origin: there is no browser request to
describe. The client's first message is its request instead, JSON
`{ type: "http" | "websocket", method, path, headers }`, and the brain makes
it a loopback request marked like the owner's browser requests, except
without a shell origin: no page frames a client. HTTP request bodies follow
as binary messages and a text end marker. The brain answers with one text
message `{ status, headers, origin }` (`origin`: what the server sees as this
client's origin), then for HTTP the response body as binary messages and a
close with 1000; for `websocket`, status 101 turns the channel into the piped
loopback socket. Only relays with channel sockets (v5) carry them.

Temporary: one channel per request. Radius limits new connections (120 a
minute per user, shared with this brain's reconnects), so the launcher polls
rarely. The proper form carries all of a client's requests and its chord link
over one channel (docs/p2-notes.md "TUI through Radius").

Offered newest first; v3 adds credit flow control for HTTP channels, v4 port forwards, v5 channel sockets.

symbols.name: RelayAccess
symbols.comment:
Distinguishes requests relayed through Radius from local and tunneled ones.

Problem: the relay client (brain.ts) serves relayed browsers by making
loopback requests to this server, which would otherwise look like the device
itself and receive localhost-only owner powers (minting owner tokens, the
automatic owner cookie, provider login).

The relay client marks its loopback requests with a per-process secret. A
marked request comes from a browser Radius authenticated on the cortex
origin, and is treated as remote, so every localhost-only path stays closed.
Without the user header it is the brain's owner. With it, it is a person the
owner shared sessions with by email: Radius vouches for their email, and
p2's sharing decides what they may reach, as for a guest cookie on a tunnel
host. Without the secret the marker headers mean nothing, so neither
browsers nor other local processes can claim them. Without the shell header
it is the owner's Pi client, the TUI launcher through Radius (brain.ts,
"Client channels").

symbols.name: Sessions
symbols.comment:
Sessions as a principal sees them. The owner lists and manages all; a guest sees its own session; a worker sees
and renames only its own session (its principal names it). The provider still serves 3, 4 and 5 (its `accepts`):
pages and TUIs loaded before a deploy keep working.

6, client-chosen IDs and lifecycle operations as jobs: `create` takes the new session's `id`, `clone` and `fork` the
copy's (`copy`), so a page navigates at once. `clone`, `fork`, `relocate` and `archive` answer once their effect is
visible (the copy's row, the archived row) or started (a move), and their long part runs as a job, shown in
`operations` (running, then gone or failed with its error) until `dismissOperation`. A `relocate` the worker
refuses (busy) is a failed operation.

The worker's `treeSelf`: the session's main conversation or its branches changed (a `/tree` switch or fork, a branch
renamed), or the worker started; the catalog entry follows, so clients open the main one and list the branches.

method answers once its visible effect committed and runs the rest as a job (`operations`). `move` is the agent's
relocation (`SessionMoves`): it waits for the job and answers why a busy worker refused (nothing recorded).

symbols.comment:

plugin's `location_move` once the main agent's turn has ended. Validates the destination (throws when it is not a
directory or its environment is not configured), then moves the catalog entry and the running worker in place.
`refused` is why a busy worker could not be fenced (nothing moved; try again once it is idle), else null.

with them before anyone sends to it.

history seeded into a fresh store.

apps/p2/plugins/sessions/tui.ts.comment:
The sessions screen: pi's `/resume` session selector (coding-agent interactive/components/session-selector.ts) on

p2's data, with the adaptations of p2-tui-port.md section 1.17:

- one line per session (activity marker, title, env:cwd in the "all" scope, age); Tab switches the current env:cwd /

all sessions; the marker is the web drawer's dot: working, a failed worker, else an unread answer (owner); the

chat showing a session's main conversation reads it through its latest answer, as the web does;

- local fuzzy filtering over title, env:cwd and ID; message hits come from `Search` (owner), in a separate

"Messages" group of literal matches; pi's phrases and `re:` are unsupported (the hint says so);

- sorts: threaded (sessions with their subagent conversations nested, `Subagents`), recent, relevance;

- pi's named filter is a pinned filter; delete means archive (confirmed), restored from the archived scope (Ctrl+A);

- rename and pin (owner). Selecting a subagent opens its conversation: the (session, conversation) identity.

`+ New session` asks for a working directory, Tab choosing the environment; `/new [env:]path` creates one directly;

`/cd [env:]path` relocates the viewed session (the web's Relocate); `/name`, `/session` live here and in the status

plugin. With projects (`projects.json`, owner) and an empty search, the list is grouped: each project's row (its

places probed in the background; Enter creates a session in the project at the first reachable place, or the one

picked with left/right) with its sessions below it, then "Other" ("+ New session" and the sessions of no project).

The grouped list shows every session; Tab's scope (current folder / all) applies to the flat lists. `/move` moves the

viewed session within its project (tui-move.ts).

symbols.name: GuestGrantSchema
symbols.comment: A guest's current principal: the sessions shared with it now (see `GuestPrincipal`).

symbols.name: Shares
symbols.comment:
Share links, guests and their grants (server, SQLite `shares.sqlite`). Host-internal. A guest holds one grant per
session shared with it; every change of its grants (share, join, removal, link reset, archive, restore) bumps its
revision and invalidates the objects of the older principal.

Sessions are shared two ways, into the same grants:

- Links, for browsers on loopback or a tunnel host. A session has at most one link per mode. Joining mints a cookie
  (the name is self-chosen); the same browser joining more links gains their sessions.
- By email, for people who reach the brain through Radius (only offered while it is connected to Radius). Radius
  verifies the email of whoever opens the brain, and admits only emails the brain reported (`emails`).

symbols.name: Sharing
symbols.comment:

`peopleUrl` is where those people open the session (the brain's page in Radius), or null while sharing with people
is unavailable: the brain is not connected to Radius, or does not know its address there yet.

symbols.name: SCHEMA_VERSION
symbols.comment:
Version 2 separates who a guest is (`guests`) from what was shared with them (`grants`, one per session), so that one
guest can hold several sessions, and adds guests the owner shared with by email. Version 1 had one guest per link.

symbols.name: TerminalPlacement
symbols.comment:
Terminals of a session, in the workspace panel (owner only). The programs run in the terminal host on the session's

machine (detached.ts); this view renders one with libghostty-vt into DOM rows, so text selection and

copying are the browser's own, and sends keys, text and pastes back. A reconnect attaches again and starts from the

host's snapshot.



Typing goes through a hidden textarea. Keys that type nothing (Enter, arrows, Ctrl+C) are encoded from keydown.

Text is taken from what changes in the textarea, not from keydown: on Android every key of an on-screen keyboard

arrives as keyCode 229 ("Unidentified"), and the keyboard composes words in the field, corrects them and deletes

from them. Example: Gboard types "teh" (sent as typed), then corrects it to "the ": the field goes from "teh" to

"the ", which sends two Backspaces and "he ". The field keeps what was typed since the last key that moved the

terminal's cursor some other way (Enter, arrows, a paste), so the keyboard's idea of the text matches the field. A

field kept empty by cancelling every insertion does not: the keyboard deletes and corrects text the field never

had, which changes nothing and sends nothing.



Touch: a long press on output text is the browser's own (word selection, handles, Copy); a long press on a blank

spot puts the textarea under the finger, so the browser offers Paste into it. Example: on "$ ls -la", a long press

on "ls" selects "ls"; one right of the prompt's end gets the Paste menu. While output is selected, rows are not

redrawn (`#held`): replacing a row's spans would drop the selection the moment the program printed.

Where terminals open: a tab of the workspace panel, or a panel below the chat. Kept per browser.

symbols.name: IDLE_EXIT_MS
symbols.comment:
The terminal host: owns the pi-env connections and the programs running in terminals, independent of the server and

the session workers, so terminals survive their restarts (detached.ts). A headless libghostty terminal

follows each one, so a browser that attaches later gets the current screen. It exits when it has had no terminals

and no connections for a while. One per data directory. It is its own program, started by path (not a facet built by

the plugin loader), so it and the files only it runs (daemon.ts, envs.ts, log-preload.ts) import p2's base code and

Chord directly.



The agent's terminal tool reaches the same terminals through calls with replies (`call`, see `HostCall`): each

terminal keeps its last MiB of output and a read cursor for it here, so reads continue where the last one ended,

also across server and worker restarts.

symbols.name: Client
symbols.comment:
Output flow control per viewer: `sent` and `acked` count output bytes (snapshots included) since it attached. A
viewer with more than `TERMINAL_OUTPUT_WINDOW` unacknowledged output after its latest snapshot (see `lag`) is
`behind`: it gets no more output, only the headless terminal follows the program. When its acknowledgements catch up
it gets a fresh snapshot instead of the bytes it missed, so a flood (`find /`) costs a slow viewer one screen, not the
whole stream, and nothing buffers without bound.

The snapshot itself never counts against the window, as chord lets one large frame exceed its window: a screen with
colored scrollback can be larger than the window, and counting it would mark the viewer behind as soon as it was sent,
so every catch-up would send it again, forever, without any new output.

apps/p2/plugins/voice/engine.ts.comment:
Voice mode in the browser, one voice room per conversation (p2's /voice/room, bridged to the speech service's

/room). The microphone goes to the room: each finished utterance becomes this person's message in the conversation,

and the others hear it. The owner's browser has the agent's new answers read aloud sentence by sentence (each with

a stable ID, `<answer>-<index>`, so the owner's other tabs do not say it twice); the room synthesizes them once and

everyone hears them. A tap on the orb while it speaks stops the speech (for the room when the owner taps, else for

this browser); a message while the agent works stops that run first, and "stop" stops it without a message.

Transcripts wait in order until the conversation accepted them (transcripts.ts), so a link that drops for a while

loses none.



The audio pipeline is pibot's (badlogic/pibot src/client at 2ef6b69), ported as a unit: its microphone constraints

(applied again after getUserMedia), a microphone AudioContext of its own, the playback stream with its voice chain

and reference tap (playback.ts), its input blocking (0 while speech starts, 500 ms after it ends or is cancelled), and

its barge-in detector and state transitions (barge-in.ts). Only the backend is p2's: the conversation instead of

pibot's server, and the room's speech instead of pibot's TTS frames.



Barge-in is pibot's detector, while the agent's speech plays (policy.ts): the microphone is buffered, not streamed;

sound the playback does not explain streams the speaker from a second before, while the agent goes on speaking.

Only words interrupt (interruption.ts): once the room's interim (or final) transcript holds a real word, the speech

is cut and the run stopped (outside chat mode), whether the agent spoke or only worked; a trigger the room never

hears as words is dropped. A transcript without words is never sent.



What happens is also logged to the server (POST /voice/log, batched): a phone's console is out of reach.

apps/p2/plugins/voice/interruption.ts.comment:
When the person talking interrupts the agent: only once the speech service heard real words. The barge-in

detector (barge-in.ts) and the service's VAD may both take noise (windshield wipers, a door) for speech, so neither

stops anything on its own:



- A barge-in trigger while the agent's speech plays only opens a candidate: the microphone (from a second before)

streams to the room while the agent goes on speaking. No `speech_start` from the room within CANDIDATE_START_MS:

the candidate is dropped (`dropStream`) and the microphone goes back to being buffered.

- Words decide: the first interim (or final) transcript with a real word (not empty, not a filler such as "um", not

the agent's own words picked up from the speaker) interrupts at once: the agent's speech is cut and its run is

stopped, as the Stop button would (in chat mode only when the words are for the agent, or a stop command; there

people talking with each other cut the agent's speech, never its work). This holds while the agent only works

too: the speaker no longer waits for the end of the utterance.

- A final without such words is dropped: never sent as a message, and nothing was interrupted.

- Utterances overlap on the wire: the next one's `speech_start` often arrives before the previous one's final (its

decode takes a moment; the service also splits speech at 30 s). So the state is kept per utterance, in order: a

final belongs to the oldest open one, interim transcripts to the newest. A final whose next utterance has already

started is held and sent joined with it: one dictation is one message, never stopping the run of its own first

half.



A service without interim transcripts interrupts at the final (after the utterance), by the same rule.

symbols.name: pcmInitialPrebufferSeconds
symbols.comment:
Speech output (ported from badlogic/pibot src/client/tools/speech.ts at 2ef6b69: its PCM stream). One stream per

spoken answer: PCM chunks are scheduled back to back on the playback AudioContext after a 0.4 s prebuffer, through

pibot's voice chain (high-pass 150 Hz, low-pass 7.2 kHz, +3.5 dB presence at 2.6 kHz, a compressor, gain 0.98) to the

output. The chain's output also feeds the barge-in reference (a script processor through a muted gain) and an

analyser for the orb's level. When the stream ends or is cancelled the microphone stays blocked for 500 ms (the

room's echo); a barge-in unblocks it at once.



Adapted: the AudioContext is this object's (created on first use, as pibot's), callbacks replace pibot's face and

RPC plumbing, finished audio may be pushed as an AudioBuffer too, and a watchdog ends a stream whose audio clock

stalled (a suspended context never ends its sources), and an underrun re-buffers (pibot scheduled every later chunk

20 ms ahead, so one late chunk made the rest of the answer choppy). Voice rooms add the other people's microphones:

each plays on its own schedule (16 kHz chunks, a jitter buffer that grows with each underrun), and the barge-in

reference is one bus that hears both Pi and the people (pibot's tap moved from the stream to that bus), so voices

from the speaker are not taken for yours.

symbols.name: humanPrebufferSeconds
symbols.comment: How far ahead a person's audio is scheduled when its stream starts: room relay jitter.

symbols.name: humanPrebufferStepSeconds
symbols.comment: Each underrun of a person's audio adds this much delay, up to the most: a jittery link settles on enough.

symbols.name: pcmRebufferSeconds
symbols.comment:
After an underrun of the agent's speech, the next chunk is scheduled this far ahead (more with each underrun, up to
the most), so the chunks after it join without gaps instead of each arriving just too late.

apps/p2/plugins/voice/server.ts.comment:
Voice mode (server): browsers reach the speech service (sts-server) only through p2, which signs it in and tells it

who is talking (the token never leaves the server). `voice.json` in the data dir names the service and its token;

without it voice mode is off. Each conversation is a voice room: the owner's browser has Pi's speech synthesized

once for everyone, each person's microphone becomes their own messages and is relayed to the others. The owner and

read/write guests of the session take part (a guest's grant is rechecked while its socket lives); only the owner

speaks for Pi or sets the voice. View-only guests get nothing.



The configuration is pushed, not asked for: VoiceService (contract.ts) publishes the service's engines and default

(the service's /voices), or null without a valid voice.json. While anyone holds it, the data dir is watched, and each

change of voice.json (written, replaced, removed) fetches the voices again, so the composer's button follows it live.



WS   /voice/room?session=…&conversation=…  bridged to the service's /room (room p2-<session>-<conversation>)

POST /voice/sample  { engine?, voice?, speed } -> audio/wav of a short sample (the owner's settings sheet)

POST /voice/log     { client, events: [{ t, message }] } -> 204; each event becomes a `[voice …]` line of the log

apps/p2/plugins/voice/transcripts.ts.comment:
What voice mode heard and has yet to deliver: each final transcript waits here until the conversation accepted it.

Sends go one at a time in the order spoken; a send that fails because the link is down (the reference is gone, a

ping timeout) is kept and tried again, through whatever reference the conversation has by then. Each transcript keeps

its request ID across attempts, so one the server already admitted is not placed twice.

Voice mode in the browser. In the composer only a microphone: on, it is an orb that shows what voice mode does

(listening, hearing you, the agent working, preparing speech, speaking) and pulses with the sound; a tap stops the

speech while an answer is read, else turns voice mode off. An error is a dot on the orb (its text in the orb's label

and in the settings). The settings are the owner's, in the sidebar's footer: the Voice sheet (engine, voice, speed,

kept in the conversation; this browser's last choice for conversations without one), with voice mode's state on top.

A read/write guest talks (its transcripts are its own messages) but hears nothing yet: the answers are read aloud only

in the owner's browser. View-only guests have no voice mode. Only when the server has a speech service (voice.json).

apps/p2/plugins/voice/worker.ts.comment:
Voice mode (worker): the owner's switch and voice, kept in a Durable document, and the prompt section voice mode

turns on. A read/write guest's microphone switch is not written there: the document is the owner's, and a guest

turning its microphone off must not turn voice mode off for anyone else. It counts while the guest's object lives

(objects are per grant; leaving, a revoked grant or the linger time ends it): the prompt section is on while the

owner's switch or any guest's is, since that guest talks by voice too.

symbols.name: Workspace.files
symbols.comment:
Every file below the root, for the name filter. In a repository: tracked and untracked files without ignored ones,
as Quick Open skips them. Elsewhere (or without git): a walk of the directory, skipping `.git` and `node_modules`
folders and not following symlinks. Private directories inside the root are left out either way.

The walk is breadth first with each directory's entries in name order (UTF-16 code units; byte order for names
without astral characters, as pi-env's `listDir` and `listFiles`), so a truncated walk keeps the same files on
every filesystem: shallow directories, and earlier names among siblings. Directory order (`openDirReader`) is
the filesystem's hash or creation order and would keep an arbitrary subset.

symbols.name: Workspace.search
symbols.comment:
Literal, smart-case (case-insensitive unless the text has capitals) search of text
files below `path`, tracked and untracked, skipping ignored files. Outside a
repository it searches the directory itself. Include/exclude globs relative to
`path` become case-insensitive glob pathspecs; a pattern also matches everything
below a folder it matches. Includes are alternatives; excludes apply to all.

apps/p2/src/api/v1/index.ts.comment:
p2's plugin API, version 1 (`@p2/app/v1`): what every facet kind may import (browser-safe). Plugins import p2 and

Chord v2 only through this API and its per-kind modules (`/node`, `/server`, `/worker`, `/tui`, `/web`), never through

relative paths into `src`: a plugin is built and reloaded on its own, and the API is the code its host provides.

p2's plugin API, version 1, for Node facets (`@p2/app/v1/node`: server and worker): configuration files, logs,

apps/p2/src/api/v1/server.ts.comment:
p2's plugin API, version 1, for server facets (`@p2/app/v1/server`): the server's locals and registries (routes,

authenticators, workers), HTTP helpers and pages, and Chord's process lock.

apps/p2/src/api/v1/tui.ts.comment:
p2's plugin API, version 1, for TUI facets (`@p2/app/v1/tui`): the TUI runtime, its context, commands and renderers,

the chat surface other facets use, the shared transcript model and pi's components as p2 copied them.

apps/p2/src/api/v1/web.ts.comment:
p2's plugin API, version 1, for web facets (`@p2/app/v1/web`): the browser runtime (objects as React hooks, slots,

sheets, navigation) and the shared components and stores of p2's page (chat, drawer, viewers, icons).

apps/p2/src/api/v1/worker.ts.comment:
p2's plugin API, version 1, for worker facets (`@p2/app/v1/worker`): the session worker's locals and registries (the

Harness, extensions, the worker process), Durable commit helpers, conversation stats and tool attribution.

symbols.comment:
Where a request came from. The server listens on loopback only. Local hosts are served over http; an allowed tunnel
host is https (the tunnel terminates TLS; app authentication gates access). Any other Host header is refused (DNS
rebinding), and forwarded requests never pass as local.

symbols.name: foreignBrowserRequest
symbols.comment:
Whether a browser sent this request for another site (Fetch Metadata): a cross-site or same-site (another local port)
page, link, form, fetch or WebSocket, or a frame or embed another site holds. Such a request never gets the loopback
owner: a page anywhere could otherwise frame the owner UI (clickjacking) or drive it. Requests without the headers
(the TUI, scripts, older browsers) are unaffected; the page's CSP `frame-ancestors` still refuses framing there.
