may authenticate. It cannot read anything back into the foreign page, and opens the app as usual. Only browsers set
`navigate` (a page's fetch cannot); frames say `iframe`/`frame`. Chrome on Android launches an installed app (WebAPK)
with `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site`, `Sec-Fetch-Dest: empty` and no cookies, so `empty` counts as a document too.

that relays it.

symbols.comment:
Stops an archived session's worker for good: its holders (a page's lingering conversation, say) wait suspended
instead of starting a worker the archived session refuses, which failed with an owner notice. `retry` (restore)
ends the suspension; so does the release of its last holder (a later hold is refused as archived).

symbols.comment: Stops every worker; their exits are no news to subscribers (the server's objects close next).

symbols.comment:
Runs `work` while the session's worker is stopped and its holders wait (suspended); then starts it if held and
waits for that start's outcome (running or failed), as callers read the worker's state next.

symbols.comment: Stops the session's worker; its holders start a new one (not waited for: the caller reports the stop).

symbols.comment: `step`, rejected as soon as the session's worker is no longer running (it exited while the step waits on it).

symbols.comment: Resolves once a start of `session`'s worker the retry began (its holders') is running or failed.

"Worker exited (signal): tail" in the notice and the status error too, as in v1. A lost link Chord recovers from
is only a log event.

symbols.name: SessionWorkers.#crashed
symbols.comment:
A running worker exited unasked (SIGKILL, OOM): as in v1 its holders start a new one, up to
`CRASH_RESTARTS` such restarts within `CRASH_WINDOW_MS`; a crash past that stays failed until Retry (no crash
loop). A worker that crashes while starting stays failed too.

symbols.comment: Every change of the workers' states, as `HostEvent`s.

apps/p2/src/hosts/session-workers.ts.comment:
The session workers on Chord v2's workers component: one forked worker per session, started on the first hold,

stopped when idle, its failure kept until a retry. On top: worker generations (in the worker principal and start

data), logs and owner notices, restarts after a crash (as v1), and the lifecycle steps of relocation and cloning,

serialized per session.

symbols.name: MAX_CLIENT_FRAME
symbols.comment: Largest frame a client may send. Uploads go over HTTP; a 1,000,000-character message fits.

symbols.name: MAX_UNSENT_BYTES
symbols.comment: Unsent data beyond the frame being sent: a client that stops reading is cut off instead of growing the server.

symbols.name: limitedSocket
symbols.comment:
The socket Chord's link sees for one client connection (Chord queues calls behind its own window).

- Errors (an oversized frame) terminate the socket instead of crashing the server.
- Output: before each send, data still buffered beyond the largest unfinished frame (one snapshot may itself be
  large) must stay under `MAX_UNSENT_BYTES`, or the socket is terminated; the client reconnects from snapshots.
  chord2's flow control normally keeps a reading client far below it; this catches clients that stop reading.

symbols.name: BridgeLink
symbols.comment:
The host's parent link, relayed by the launcher: its messages travel as `link` bridge messages to the launcher's
socket and back. Until `activate` (the launcher's first activation) what is sent waits. Chord closing it (its
heartbeat found the socket silent, a protocol error) posts `linkClosed`: the launcher terminates that socket, and
its reconnect brings a new link. Without it, a connection that died without a close (a laptop that slept while the
relay dropped it) kept the launcher's socket "open" and the TUI stuck on "Connecting conversation…".

symbols.name: configureFetch
symbols.comment:
Installs npm undici's fetch over HTTP/1.1, like the coding agent's dispatcher.

Node 26's bundled fetch negotiates HTTP/2, one shared session per origin. After that
session dies, it can keep handing new requests to it: every provider request to the
origin fails at once with `ERR_HTTP2_INVALID_SESSION` ("fetch failed") or hangs until the
process exits. Over HTTP/1.1 a failed connection is dropped and the next request opens another.
Call once per process, before any provider request.

symbols.name: Observer
symbols.comment:
Loads `load` whenever watched files may have changed. Watching is established before each load starts, so a change
made during a load is never missed: every change, `overflow` (lost events, reconnect) or explicit `reload()` bumps a
generation, and a load that finishes behind the current generation runs again. A load returns `true` to be read
once more shortly (content that may be half-written); it reports errors itself and keeps its last valid state.
While watching is impossible (an error, or offline), `fallbackMs` drives loads and new watch attempts.

symbols.name: originOf
symbols.signature: export async function originOf(api: ToolExecutionApi, context: Context): Promise<ConversationOrigin | undefined>
symbols.comment:
Who started the calling tool's turn: the owner, or nobody allowed (undefined). The turn is the conversation's current
run, a code mode script's nested calls included: it is the owner's only if every input the run placed so far is
(`entryOrigin`). A guest's message steered into the run takes it away for the rest of the run.

symbols.name: entryOrigin
symbols.signature: export function entryOrigin(entry: EntryRecord | undefined): ConversationOrigin | undefined
symbols.comment:
The origin an input entry records in its data: a person's input is the owner's when its author is the owner; what an
agent wrote (a subagent's task or report, a `team` or peer message, a one-shot agent's task) says `origin: "owner"`
when the turn that wrote it was the owner's. Anything else, a tool's plain input included, grants nothing.

symbols.name: answerOrigin
symbols.comment:
The origin of the run that ended with the answer `answer` of `conversationId`, read after it ended (a subagent's
report, when `pi.live.run` is gone): its inputs are the input entries after the previous run's final answer. The
owner's only if all are. Only a final answer (`stop`, `length`) bounds the scan: a retried model error appends an
`error` answer and an overflow compaction a head marker inside a run, and scanning past a failed or aborted run only
adds inputs, so the result can only be stricter. (An `onYield` continuation after a final answer would hide the
inputs before it; p2 installs no such hook.)

conversation (subagent tasks and reports, `team`, peer messages, one-shot agents) read it.

the start's outcome (running, or failed with its redacted error).

symbols.comment:
Clears the session's failure or suspension (a restore): its holders start a worker, a later hold does too. Nothing
is started when nobody holds it.

symbols.comment: Stops the session's worker; its holders start a new one (a restart, e.g. for a changed environment).

symbols.name: SessionWorkerControl.suspend
symbols.comment:
Stops an archived session's worker and starts none for its holders: they wait (suspended) until `retry` (restore)
or their release, instead of a start the archived session refuses.

symbols.comment: Every change of a worker's state (the dev supervisor's events).

symbols.name: SessionWorkerControl.observe
symbols.comment:

of `Hosts.workers`.

symbols.name: SessionLocation
symbols.comment:
Where the session works now. A worker starts at its spawn location (`SessionInit`) and follows `Sessions.relocate`
in place (`Harness.relocate`): plugins read `value` at each use instead of the spawn parameters, and subscribe to
reopen what they keep for a location (prompt files, workspace watches). Listeners run once the move is committed:
the Harness's environments and the conversations' agent cwds are already at the new location.

During a move the Harness's environments switch before the location is committed, so `value` may still name the
old location while `Harness.environments` already resolves on the new machine. Decide what depends on the machine
from the environment itself (`isLocalEnvironment`), and key what is kept for a location by `version`: it changes
when a move is committed, so anything opened before (also during the switch) is older and opened again.

cwd, fixed at spawn (a subagent spawned with a cwd: on the caller's environment). A contributor must not need the
Harness (it would wait for itself): it gets the opening Durable Harness, or a reader of its documents, as an
argument. Contributed by a facet (no runtime state), so it is there when the Harness opens.

Harness calls it, and every relocation, and moves the followers whose agent cwd differs to the session's cwd with
the root, in one commit, before it is live: nothing can run or resume in a stale cwd first.

symbols.name: Liveness
symbols.signature: export class Liveness implements Watchable<Readonly<Record<string, number>>> {
symbols.comment:
What keeps the worker process alive besides held references (Chord's own count): its Durable tasks, calls under way
(`call`), viewers plugins count themselves, and the relocation fence. A JSON watchable of those counts
(`workerMain`'s `busy`): the worker is idle when every count is zero.

symbols.name: Liveness.watch
symbols.comment: A watch of the counts (only `workerMain` watches): it gets the newest counts at each change.

symbols.name: Liveness.stopping
symbols.comment:
Whether the worker process is shutting down (set before its host closes). Disposal code tells a stop, after which
Durable resumes interrupted work in the next worker, from a plugin removed by a reload, whose work must end now.

symbols.name: Liveness.relocating
symbols.comment: Whether admissions are fenced for a relocation (`WorkerBoundary.prepare` accepted, not yet moved or cancelled).

symbols.name: Liveness.freeze
symbols.comment:
Fence new admissions before checking Durable state; a failed check releases the fence. The fence counts as an
active call, so the worker cannot stop idle between the server's prepare and its relocate.

symbols.name: Liveness.call
symbols.comment: Runs `fn` as one active call.

symbols.name: WorkerParts
symbols.comment: The worker process: its start data, liveness counters, and where the session works now (read `location`).

symbols.comment:
Runs `fn` in a root of the worker's own (`HOST`) under `context`: for code outside Chord calls (a Durable tool or
section passes its Durable context), or a method acting as the worker (`withoutAbortSignal(ctx)`).

symbols.signature: readonly copyFilesTo: (session: string, context: Context) => Promise<void>;
symbols.comment:
Copies this session's files (the kit's `Files`: its index and blobs) into the directory of the new session
`session`, which must not exist yet: a fork, whose worker waits while it copies. The session goes on meanwhile.

symbols.name: WorkerProcess
symbols.comment:
The worker process's natives, contributed by the core facet from the start: `self.registry(WorkerProcess).value`
(`.init.dataDir`, `.liveness.call(…)`, `.location.value`). Read `location`, not `init.values.session`, for the cwd.

symbols.name: RelocationCheck
symbols.comment:
Refusals of a move to `to` (from the session's current location), checked under the fence before anything moves. A

apps/p2/src/tui/theme/system-theme.ts.comment:
Copied unchanged from coding-agent src/modes/interactive/theme/system-theme.ts (p2-tui-port.md section 5.3).

The `system` theme: pi's colors derived from the terminal's own theme.

Every token belongs to a color family (its hue) and has contrast rules: it must reach a contrast level
on the background and on the panels it is drawn on. Hue and saturation come from the terminal's palette
color for the family's ANSI slot, or from the family's own hue when the terminal reports no palette.
Lightness comes from the rules alone. Colors are built in OKHSL, whose saturation is relative to the
sRGB gamut, and fade toward gray near black and white. A palette color never gains OKLCH chroma when it
moves to another lightness, so pastel palettes stay pastel.

A contrast level is a target-lightness curve: the OKLab lightness a token needs, given the lightness of
the surface below it. The curves were fitted to the reference theme design from the "Pi themes: system
and light/dark" review. On dark backgrounds they aim for nearly fixed lightness; on light backgrounds the
required difference grows as the background darkens.

Depending on what the terminal reports, the theme is generated in one of three tiers:
- background and palette: hues from the palette, lightness from the background;
- background only: the families' own hues, lightness from the background;
- nothing: ANSI palette indices and the default colors, which the terminal renders itself.

A turn's activity: what the agent did between a person's message and its answer. Derived from the transcript's

items: `chatItems` keeps each response's thinking and text in the transcript, in their order, and turns each run of

consecutive tool calls into an activity item (a wheel in the chat, its steps in a sheet). A turn's last text is its

answer, followed by the results meant for the person (artifacts, sent files, opened ports). A result its tool shows

in place (an inline artifact) comes right after its call instead, splitting the run of calls around it. How much of

that shows in the transcript, and how much goes on the wheels, is settings.json's `detail` (`Detail`).

symbols.name: firstVisibleBlocks
symbols.comment:
The first `count` blocks not entirely above `top`, with their tops: the scroll anchor that keeps a reader's place
while content above changes. Several candidates, because the top block can disappear (a tool result merging into its
call's card once an older page arrives). Blocks are stacked top to bottom, so a binary search finds the first one in
about log2(n) layout reads instead of one per block: reading every block's rectangle in a long session cost hundreds
of milliseconds, on every resize.

apps/p2/src/web/conversation-cache.ts.comment:
Conversations kept on the device (IndexedDB), so opening one shows it at once, before the connection is back: a
cold start (iOS discards a home-screen app in the background), a reload after an update. What was kept seeds the
conversation's transcript (`TranscriptStore.seed`); the live view is merged into it when it continues it, and
replaces it otherwise.

Only the owner's browser keeps conversations: a guest's share can end, and what it saw must not stay on its device.
Signing out, or the server saying this browser is no longer the owner, clears everything kept (`clearKept`).

Per conversation: the transcript's newest entries without a gap among them, up to `MAX_BYTES` (older ones page in
again from the server), with the documents but without the live state (a run, its queue: stale once kept), and the
measured row heights. The most recently used `MAX_CONVERSATIONS` stay.

symbols.name: DECIDE
symbols.comment:
A one-finger drag along one axis that a gesture takes over from the page, shared by the phone drawer's swipe

(drawer-swipe.ts) and the bottom sheets' (sheet-swipe.ts). Modeled on native drawers and sheets and the web gesture

code that gets close to them (Ionic's gestures, Framework7's swipe panels, MUI's SwipeableDrawer).



One touch is either the page's (a scroll, a selection) or the gesture's, never both. The browser holds back the

first moves of a touch (its touch slop) and then sends one cancelable touchmove; if nobody cancels it, the touch

scrolls and every later touchmove is uncancelable. So the axis is decided on the first move that is far enough to

measure: within MAX_ANGLE of the gesture's axis, and accepted by the gesture (`take`: its direction, what is under the

finger), the gesture owns the touch and cancels every move; otherwise the touch is left to the page for good. That

needs a non-passive touchmove listener; it returns at once for touches that are not candidates. Pointer events

cannot cancel a scroll, so they cannot guarantee this.



A gesture follows the finger 1:1 (`move`, the distance along the axis since it took the touch) and settles on

release (`end`, with the finger's velocity: measured over VELOCITY_WINDOW, so a finger that rested has none). A

second finger, `touchcancel`, the page being hidden mid-drag (the app switcher, a call: touchcancel may not come)

and `cancel()` end it without a velocity: it settles back.

Movement (px) before the axis is decided, for browsers that report moves inside their touch slop.

symbols.name: MAX_ANGLE
symbols.comment: Steepest angle (degrees from the gesture's axis) that still counts as the gesture.

symbols.name: VELOCITY_WINDOW
symbols.comment: Velocity is measured over this window (ms) before the release.

symbols.name: FLING
symbols.comment: px/ms; a release faster than this settles in the fling's direction regardless of the position.

symbols.name: SETTLE_EASING
symbols.comment: Settle easing (ease-out); its initial slope, so a settle starts at the finger's speed.

symbols.name: FASTEST
symbols.comment: Settle durations (ms): a slow release takes up to SLOWEST for the whole distance, a fling at least FASTEST.

symbols.name: settleDuration
symbols.signature: export function settleDuration(remaining: number, total: number, toward: number): number
symbols.comment:
How long a settle over `remaining` of `total` px takes, released at `toward` px/ms toward its destination: it
continues the finger's speed (capped), a slow or backward release takes a time in proportion to the distance.

symbols.name: useDrawerSwipe

apps/p2/src/web/drawer-swipe.ts.comment:
Swipe for the phone drawer, modeled on native drawers and the web gesture code that gets close to them (Ionic's

menu gesture, Framework7's swipe panels, MUI's SwipeableDrawer): a drag toward the inline end (rightward; leftward

in RTL) anywhere on the chat column drags the drawer open, a drag toward the inline start on the open drawer or

its scrim drags it closed. The drawer follows the finger 1:1; on release it settles by fling velocity, else by

position, with a duration that continues the finger's speed. Following the touch, deciding its axis, owning it and

measuring the release are shared with the sheets' swipe (drag-gesture.ts).



A touch that interrupts a fling gets no cancelable moves at all (Chromium), yet swiping the drawer open right after

flicking the transcript must work. style.css sets `touch-action: pan-y pinch-zoom` on the phone layout and its

vertical scrollers, so the browser does not scroll a mostly horizontal drag either way (the 35 degree limit is

stricter than its 45 degree split). Should the page scroll under such a drag anyway, the drawer gives the touch up

and settles back.



Left to the page: text fields, elements with `touch-action: none` (the terminal, resize handles: they handle their

own drags), horizontal scrollers that can still scroll in the drag's direction (a code block scrolled away from its

start), drags extending a text selection, and the workspace panel (full screen above the drawer on phones).

symbols.name: FACE
symbols.comment:
The Ticker's drum (ticker.tsx), with iOS's picker physics (UIScrollView; Apple's "Designing Fluid Interfaces", WWDC
2018): it follows the finger one to one. On release, the release velocity is projected to where iOS's deceleration
would stop it; the drum picks the item nearest that point and decays to it at the same rate, so the motion carries on
from the finger. A slow release settles quickly to the nearest item. Past the ends: the rubber band. Catching it
stops it.

It follows the newest item: a new one rolls in. While the reader scrolls it holds still, and once they have left it
alone for a few seconds it rolls to the newest item if new ones came in meanwhile. Positions are in items: 0 is the
oldest, `last` the newest.

Ported from Elanor's Ticker (not in its npm release yet); replace with Elanor's once it ships.

Height of an item (px), as `semantic.dimension.size.small`.

symbols.name: DRAG_RESISTANCE
symbols.comment:
Drag to close for bottom sheets (drawer.tsx), in place of Base UI's swipe (which closes at half the height or on any
light flick, with no resistance). Like iOS sheets and Vaul: the sheet follows the finger through a rubber band, light
at first and heavier the further it goes; on release it closes past a share of its height or on a clear flick, and
otherwise springs back. Dragging up gives only a little. A drag starts only where the content under the finger is
scrolled to its top; otherwise the content scrolls, and once it reaches the top the same finger takes over the sheet.

The sheet's offset is `--drawer-drag` on the popup and its progress towards closing `--drawer-drag-progress` on the
backdrop; `data-dragging` on both turns transitions off while the finger moves.

Ported from Elanor (not in its npm release yet); replace with Elanor's Drawer once it ships.

Rubber band of a drag down: offset = (1 - 1 / (distance * k / height + 1)) * height.

symbols.name: OVERPULL_RESISTANCE
symbols.comment: Rubber band of a drag up, past the resting place: much stiffer.

symbols.name: CLOSE_DISTANCE
symbols.comment: A release past this share of the height closes the sheet, or a flick down faster than this (px/ms).

symbols.name: SLOP
symbols.comment: Movement (px) before a touch is read as a drag or a scroll.

symbols.name: STILL
symbols.comment: Without a move this long (ms) before release, the finger was held still: no flick.

`@` and Tab file completion in the web composer (p2-tui-port.md section 8.4, P7c; a p2 addition, Pi Mobile has

none). The same rules as the TUI (src/runtime/completion.ts): `@` after a token boundary opens a popover of the

session's FileIndex matches; a Tab on a path-like token lists that directory. While the popover is open, Enter/Tab

apply, arrows move and Escape closes, ahead of send and stop. Keys during IME composition are ignored and the popover

never opens mid-composition. `@pi` (chat mode's agent mention) is never completed as a file; in chat mode a

synthetic "@pi — mention Pi" item comes first.

a history entry per step everywhere else. Desktop Back buttons never reach close

symbols.name: RETRY_INITIAL_MS
symbols.comment:
The browser's connection loop: keeps one socket to the server, replaces it when it ends, and notices dead ones early.

Retry delays after a failed or short-lived connection: 250 ms, doubling, at most 5 s.

symbols.name: STABLE_MS
symbols.comment: A connection that stayed open this long counted as working: the next retry starts again at the initial delay.

symbols.name: CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS
symbols.comment: A socket not open after this long is given up. Through Radius an upgrade may wait 15 s for the brain's side.

symbols.name: STALE_MS
symbols.comment: The server pings every 15 s: an open socket silent for longer than this is presumed dead.

symbols.name: WAKE_GRACE_MS
symbols.comment: After a wake, messages held while the page was frozen get this long to arrive before the socket is checked.

symbols.name: SocketEvents
symbols.comment: What the page tells the loop about one socket.

symbols.name: SocketEvents.received
symbols.comment: Any message: the server pings every 15 s, so silence means a dead connection.

symbols.signature: closed(code: number, reason: string, wasClean: boolean): void;

symbols.comment: The link over one socket: it ends when the socket closes, and closing it ends it at once.

symbols.comment: Runs `callback` after `ms`; returns a cancel function.

symbols.name: ReconnectEnvironment.online
symbols.comment: False when the device is known to be offline.

symbols.name: ReconnectEnvironment.onWake
symbols.comment:
`listener` runs when the page may have been away: back online, visible again, network changed, or restored.
Returns a function that removes it.

symbols.comment: Opens a socket and its link; the socket reports to `events`.

symbols.name: ReconnectOptions.canRetry
symbols.comment: Asked after every close; false stops reconnecting (an outdated page, a guest's ended share).

symbols.name: ReconnectOptions.silenceTimeoutMs
symbols.comment:
Replace an open socket after this long without a message, at any time, not only on wake. For sockets whose own
protocol has no timeout (the terminal's); chord links time out by themselves.

symbols.name: Attempt
openedAt
symbols.comment: When the socket opened; undefined while connecting.

symbols.name: keepConnected
symbols.signature: export function keepConnected(options: ReconnectOptions): { stop(): void }
symbols.comment:
Keeps the page connected until stopped:

- After a close it retries with backoff. A connection that stayed open STABLE_MS resets the backoff; one that opens
  and ends at once (an older server refusing the protocol, for instance) keeps backing off instead of looping.
- An attempt not open after CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS is given up: browsers have no handshake timeout.
- On wake (online, visible, network change, back/forward cache) a pending retry runs at once, and an open socket
  that has heard nothing for STALE_MS is replaced. After a network change the socket looks fine until the server's
  next ping is missing, so the check runs when that ping is overdue rather than only now.
- With `silenceTimeoutMs`, an open socket is also replaced whenever it stays silent that long. A check that runs
  late (a frozen or throttled page) first gives held messages WAKE_GRACE_MS to arrive.
- Every close is logged with its reason and close code: a 1006 that never opened is a refused handshake, one after
  opening a dropped connection.

symbols.name: browserEnvironment
symbols.comment:
The page's environment: wakes on `online`, visibility, network changes (where reported) and back/forward restores.
Logs go to the console under `name`.

symbols.name: RowFeatures
symbols.comment:
Height estimates for list rows never rendered, learned from the rows that were (after react-virtuoso, which sizes
unmeasured items from measured ones, and TanStack Virtual's advice to estimate roughly). No element sizes are
modeled: the stylesheet decides them, and the measurements carry them here.

Rows are grouped by kind (the caller's `features`: a person's message, an answer with tool calls, a tool card), and
per kind the height is fitted as a line over text length relative to the list's width (`text / width`, roughly the
number of lines times a font's character width): a one-line and a fifty-line answer differ more than any average
could cover. Parts whose height the caller knows exactly (images, sized from their headers) are added on top and left
out of the fit. A kind with no measurements yet takes the fit over all kinds, and nothing measured at all takes
`fallback`.

A row's first estimate is kept: later measurements of other rows must not move rows already placed by estimate (a
changed estimate below the reader moves what they look at).

symbols.name: SETTLE_MS
symbols.comment:
Whether the reader is moving a scroll area right now: a finger or the mouse is down on it, or the scroll it started
(a fling's momentum, the wheel's smooth scroll) is still running. While it is, the transcript must not write
`scrollTop`: iOS ignores a write under a finger and stops a fling's momentum on one, and a write cancels the wheel's
smooth scroll in desktop browsers. Corrections wait, held in the layout instead (see use-chat-scroll.ts), until the
scroll settles. Modeled on TanStack Virtual's iOS gesture tracking (`ios-gesture.ts`), applied on every platform.

After the input ends, a tail stays open while scroll events keep coming: momentum fires scroll events but no touch
events, so each one re-arms the tail, which closes `SETTLE_MS` after the last one. The slow end of a fling can move
less than a pixel per event, so a tail whose area still moved since the last event stays open.

apps/p2/src/web/sheet-swipe.ts.comment:
Swipe down to close a bottom sheet (phones; wide screens show sheets as dialogs), after native sheets: a drag that

starts on the sheet's top edge (its grip and header) and goes down moves the sheet with the finger and fades its

scrim; on release it closes on a downward fling or past CLOSE_AT of its height, else it settles back, with a duration

that continues the finger's speed. The sheet closes (its route) when the slide out ends, so it is seen leaving.

Following the touch, deciding its axis, owning it and measuring the release are shared with the drawer's swipe

(drag-gesture.ts).



Only the top edge: the sheet's content scrolls vertically, and a drag there stays a scroll. The grip and header take

no browser gestures (`touch-action: none` in style.css), so their moves are always cancelable.

symbols.name: TranscriptScroll.#glide
symbols.comment:
New messages at the bottom push the transcript up by their height at once; this lets it glide there instead, as
chat apps do: the messages are drawn `height` lower and move up to their place (a transform: no layout, no
scroll change), while the new rows fade in (`.row.arriving`). At most a viewport of it; none with reduced motion.

symbols.name: TranscriptScroll.#endGlide
symbols.comment:
The reader takes over: a running glide ends at once (the rows are where the layout has them). Positions read while
it ran would include its transform, which corrections would take for content moving.

symbols.name: TranscriptScroll.scrollerRef
TranscriptScroll.listRef
symbols.comment: The `.rows` element; its parent (`.messages`) is observed for changes around the rows (Earlier, Working).

symbols.name: TranscriptScroll.topRef
TranscriptScroll.bottomRef
TranscriptScroll.rowRef
symbols.comment: A rendered row (`data-row` is its key): measured whenever its size changes.

symbols.name: TranscriptScroll.dockRef
symbols.comment: The composer dock floats over the transcript's bottom: the transcript keeps room for it.

symbols.name: TranscriptScroll.unpin
symbols.comment: The reader scrolls up or touches the transcript: stop following the answer.

symbols.name: TranscriptScroll.toBottom
symbols.comment: Follow the answer again; the transcript scrolls down to it.

symbols.name: TranscriptScroll.reveal
symbols.comment: Scrolls entry `entryId` to the viewport's center and highlights it; false when it is not loaded here.

symbols.name: TranscriptScroll.#layoutTop
symbols.comment: Where the viewport's top is in the layout (rows' offsets).

symbols.name: TranscriptScroll.#updateRange
symbols.comment:
Rendering rows at an end of the range can move the scroll position (the browser's scroll anchoring shifted a real
transcript by a few pixels for one row), and with it the range: a change that drops exactly the rows the last one
added would bring that layout back, and the next change would add them again, every render. Such a change keeps
them: at each end the range takes the larger of the two. Adding rows is never held back, and the next change that
is not such a reversal applies as computed.

symbols.name: TranscriptScroll.spacers
symbols.signature: spacers(range: RowRange): { before: number; after: number }
symbols.comment:
The heights of the spacers standing for the rows before and after `range`. Rendered together with the rows: a
layout in between, with rows gone and the spacer not grown yet, would shorten the content for a moment, and at
the top edge the browser clamps the scroll position to that and keeps it (a jump).

symbols.name: TranscriptScroll.#applyHold
symbols.comment:
Translates the rows by the held correction (a transform changes no layout). Content it pushes past an edge is out
of reach until the hold is written, which happens near that edge (`#nearEdge`) or when the scroll settles.

symbols.name: TranscriptScroll.#captureAnchor
symbols.comment: The first rendered row whose bottom is below the viewport's top, and where its top is.

symbols.name: TranscriptScroll.#moved
symbols.signature: #moved(scroller: HTMLElement, element: Element, anchor: { screen: number; content: number }): number
symbols.comment:
How far the anchor moved by layout since it was captured. While the reader scrolls, its place in the content: the
browser scrolls on its own thread, so a place on screen read later can include scrolling no scroll event
reported yet, which would read as the layout moving the row. Otherwise its place on screen: nothing scrolls then
but the browser itself, which clamps the scroll position when content near an edge shrinks, and that clamp keeps
what the reader sees (compared in content, it would read as a move and be corrected twice).

symbols.name: TranscriptScroll.#contentTop
symbols.comment: Where `element` is in the scrolled content: its place on screen plus the scroll position, read together.

symbols.name: TranscriptScroll.#correct
symbols.comment: Moves content by `delta` under the reader: written when possible, else held as the rows' transform.

symbols.name: TranscriptScroll.#flushHold
symbols.comment: Writes a held correction: the spacer gets its height back and `scrollTop` moves with it, in one paint.

symbols.name: TranscriptScroll.#settled
symbols.comment: The reader's scroll ended.

symbols.name: TranscriptScroll.#sync
symbols.comment: After any layout change: place the spacers, then keep the anchor where it was (or the end, when pinned).

symbols.name: TranscriptScroll.#rowWidth
symbols.comment: The rows' width, for estimates (before the list is laid out, a guess that is never measured against).

symbols.name: TranscriptScroll.#measure
symbols.comment: Records a row's height; a row measured for the first time teaches the estimates.

symbols.name: TranscriptScroll.#scrolled
TranscriptScroll.#nearEdge
symbols.comment:
Whether a hold of `hold` would push content past the edge the viewport is within half a viewport of: a positive
hold translates the rows up (past the top), a negative one down (past the bottom). Such a hold is written even
while the reader scrolls: the scroll is about to stop at the edge anyway. Not while a finger is down (iOS ignores
the write) or the scroll bounces past the edge (the rubber band).

symbols.name: TranscriptScroll.#loadEarlier
symbols.comment:
Loads older history while the reader is within `PREFETCH` viewports of the loaded start; following the answer at
the bottom, while less than a viewport of history is above it, so there is always something to scroll back to.
(A turn's many tool calls are one row: a page of them can add next to no height, and without this a short
transcript would show only that row under "Earlier messages", with nothing to scroll.) A scroll asks for it; a
layout change (a page arrived) asks again only when the last page added to the loaded history, so a failing load
is not retried in a loop.

symbols.name: TranscriptScroll.#release
symbols.comment: The finger or mouse lifted at the bottom: follow the answer again.

symbols.name: TranscriptScroll.#steer
symbols.comment: One step of a reveal: moves the target toward the viewport's center until it stays there two frames.

apps/p2/src/web/use-chat-scroll.ts.comment:
The transcript's scroll controller: a virtual list that renders only the rows near the viewport, keeps the reader's
place while rows change size, follows the answer at the bottom (Pi Mobile's pinning), and reveals an entry anywhere
in the loaded history.

Problem: a row's real height is known only once it is rendered, and older history arrives in pages above the reader.
Every such change above the reader moves what they look at and has to be compensated. Changes below the reader (an
answer streaming in, tool calls arriving, the composer growing) move nothing: the scroll position counts from the
top. That is the common case while an agent works, and it needs no correction at all; a scroll position counted from
the bottom (a reversed column) inverts this and has to correct every change below the reader while they scroll,
which Chrome for Android, scrolling on its own thread, shows as jumps.

Solution: where the browser keeps the place itself (CSS scroll anchoring, `overflow-anchor`: Chrome, Firefox), it
does, also mid-fling and under a finger; the spacers are never anchors (a spacer below the rows moves down when rows
are rendered before it). Elsewhere (Safari) one anchor row, the first one visible, keeps its place on screen: written
to `scrollTop` when nobody scrolls; while the reader scrolls held as a transform of the rows (which changes no layout)
and written once the scroll settles, or right away near the edge it would push content past (after TanStack
Virtual's iOS handling).

Measured heights are kept per conversation (`keptSizes`), so the spacers are exact for rows shown before and only
rows never shown are estimated. Layout: `.rows` holds the top spacer, the rendered rows in normal flow, and the
bottom spacer; rows carry their own spacing (padding), so a row's measured border box is everything it adds.

symbols.name: RowLayout
symbols.comment:
The size model of a virtual list: where each row starts, from the rows' measured heights and an estimate for rows
never shown. Only the rows near the viewport are in the DOM; the rest are two spacers whose heights come from here.
Modeled on TanStack Virtual's measurement cache, reduced to one vertical lane of keyed rows.

Measured heights are kept by row key in a map the caller owns, so a list rendered again (switching back to a
conversation) starts from the heights it had, and its spacers are exact instead of estimated.

symbols.name: RowLayout.#offsets
symbols.comment: `offsets[i]` is where row `i` starts; `offsets[count]` is the total height. Rebuilt lazily after a change.

symbols.name: RowLayout.setRows
symbols.signature: setRows(keys: readonly string[], estimate: (index: number) => number): void
symbols.comment: Replaces the rows; `estimate` gives the height of a row that has never been measured.

symbols.name: RowLayout.invalidate
symbols.comment: Estimates changed (the list's width did): offsets are computed again.

symbols.name: RowLayout.measure
symbols.comment: Records a row's measured height; true when it changed.

symbols.name: RowLayout.measured
symbols.comment: Whether a row's height was measured (its offset below it is exact) rather than estimated.

symbols.name: RowLayout.offsetOf
symbols.comment: Where row `index` starts; `count` gives the total height.

symbols.name: RowLayout.rowAt
symbols.comment: The row at `offset`: the last one starting at or above it (0 above the list, the last row below it).

symbols.name: RowLayout.range
symbols.signature: range(top: number, bottom: number): { start: number; end: number } | undefined
symbols.comment: The rows overlapping `[top, bottom)`, at least one while there are rows; undefined for an empty list.

symbols.name: kept
symbols.comment: Measured row heights of recently shown lists, by list (a conversation), the most recently used last.

symbols.name: seedSizes
symbols.signature: export function seedSizes(key: string, sizes: Iterable<readonly [string, number]>): void
symbols.comment: Starts list `key` from heights measured before (kept on the device); heights it measured since stay.

symbols.name: keptSizes

symbols.name: declareToolChanges
symbols.signature: function declareToolChanges(context: AgentContext, pendingMessages: AgentMessage[]): AgentMessage[]
symbols.comment:
Declare tool loadout changes to the model.

`context.tools` is what the runtime can execute; the transcript's system messages declare
what the model may call. Before each request the difference becomes `toolsAdded` and
`toolsRemoved` on a system message. When a pending system message exists, its tool fields
are treated as intent and replaced with the delta between the committed transcript and
the executable set, so replay always yields exactly `context.tools`. Otherwise a new
system message is inserted before the first non-system pending message.

`context.systemPrompt` or `context.tools`.

- Must return an AssistantMessageEventStream.
- Failures must be encoded in the returned stream via protocol events and a

symbols.name: ToolExecutionMode

Configuration for how tool calls from a single assistant message are executed.

- "sequential": each tool call is prepared, executed, and finalized before the next one starts.
- "parallel": tool calls are prepared sequentially, then allowed tools execute concurrently.

- "one-at-a-time": drain and inject only the oldest queued message, leaving the rest queued for later drain points.

symbols.name: AfterToolCallResult
symbols.comment:
Partial override returned from `afterToolCall`.

Merge semantics are field-by-field:
- `content`: if provided, replaces the tool result content array in full
- `details`: if provided, replaces the tool result details value in full
- `isError`: if provided, replaces the tool result error flag
- `usage`: if provided, replaces the tool result usage
- `terminate`: if provided, replaces the early-termination hint
- `structuredContent`: if provided, replaces the structured content. If `content` is provided
  without it, the structured content is dropped, because it may no longer match the content.
  Return it along with `content` to keep it.

Other omitted fields keep the original executed tool result values.
There is no deep merge for `content`, `details`, or `usage`.

Contract: must not throw or reject. Return [] when no steering messages are available.

Called when the agent has no more tool calls and no steering messages.
If messages are returned, they're added to the context and the agent
continues with another turn.

Use this for follow-up messages that should wait until the agent finishes.

Contract: must not throw or reject. Return [] when no follow-up messages are available.

symbols.comment:
Tool execution mode.
- "sequential": execute tool calls one by one
- "parallel": preflight tool calls sequentially, then execute allowed tools concurrently;
  emit `tool_execution_end` in tool completion order after each tool is finalized,
  then emit tool-result message artifacts later in assistant source order

Default: "parallel"

symbols.signature: beforeToolCall?: (context: BeforeToolCallContext, signal?: AbortSignal) => Promise<BeforeToolCallResult | undefined>;
symbols.comment:
Called before a tool is executed, after arguments have been validated.

Return `{ block: true }` to prevent execution. The loop emits an error tool result instead.
A blocked result can also set `terminate: true` to participate in the batch early-termination rule.
The hook receives the agent abort signal and is responsible for honoring it.

symbols.name: AgentLoopConfig.afterToolCall
symbols.signature: afterToolCall?: (context: AfterToolCallContext, signal?: AbortSignal) => Promise<AfterToolCallResult | undefined>;
symbols.comment:
Called after a tool finishes executing, before `tool_execution_end` and tool-result message events are emitted.

Return an `AfterToolCallResult` to override parts of the executed tool result:
- `content` replaces the full content array
- `details` replaces the full details payload
- `isError` replaces the error flag
- `usage` replaces the tool result usage
- `terminate` replaces the early-termination hint

Any omitted fields keep their original values. No deep merge is performed.
The hook receives the agent abort signal and is responsible for honoring it.

symbols.name: ThreadParam
symbols.signature: type ThreadParam = { type: "create" } | { type: "continue"; previous_message_id: string };
symbols.comment:
Message threads: the server keeps the conversation of a thread, so a request can continue
from the previous reply and send only the new messages. pi still builds the full request;
`prepareThreadRequest()` compares it with the previous request of the session and sends
only the new part when nothing earlier changed.

symbols.name: ThreadedParams
symbols.comment: The pinned SDK types do not include the `thread` request field yet.

symbols.name: ThreadEntry.prefixCount
symbols.comment: Number of messages in the last full request as sent plus the converted reply.

symbols.comment: `hashThreadPrefix()` of the request's settings and those messages.

symbols.name: ThreadEntry.replyId
symbols.comment: Id of the reply to continue from.

symbols.name: threadState
symbols.comment: Per session: where the next request can continue, or "off" after the endpoint rejected threads.

symbols.name: NEW_THREAD_ERRORS
symbols.comment: Rejections of a `continue` that a new thread fixes: expired, raced, or a fixed setting changed.

symbols.name: setThreadState
symbols.signature: function setThreadState(sessionId: string, value: ThreadEntry | "off"): void
symbols.comment:
Sets a session's thread state, keeping at most `MAX_THREAD_STATE_ENTRIES` sessions.

State is normally freed by `cleanupSessionResources(sessionId)` when a session ends, as pi's
coding agent does. The cap bounds memory for library users that never call it, for example a
server passing a new `sessionId` per conversation. Dropping the least recently updated session
is cheap: its thread has most likely expired on the server already (after a few minutes idle),
and otherwise its next request just starts a new thread.

symbols.name: hashThreadPrefix
symbols.comment:
Hash of everything a `continue` builds on: the settings that must stay the same within a thread
and the messages the server already holds.

- Settings, as sent: the endpoint (a thread exists on one endpoint only), and the fixed request
  fields. A `continue` omits `system` and `tools` and the server keeps the thread's own, so only
  this check can notice a change to them, including their cache markers. The server rejects
  changes to the other fields with `thread_fingerprint_mismatch`; checking them here saves that
  rejected request. A fixed field missing here costs only that rejection, which also starts a
  new thread.
- Messages, normalized so messages that mean the same to the API hash the same.

symbols.name: AnthropicOptions.thinkingEnabled
symbols.comment:
Enable extended thinking.
For adaptive thinking models: the model decides when/how much to think.
For older models: uses budget-based thinking with thinkingBudgetTokens.
Default: undefined (thinking is omitted unless `streamSimple()` maps
a simple reasoning level to this option, or callers set it explicitly).

symbols.name: AnthropicOptions.thinkingBudgetTokens
symbols.comment:
Token budget for extended thinking (older models only).
Ignored for adaptive thinking models.
Default: 1024 when `thinkingEnabled` is true and no budget is provided.

symbols.name: AnthropicOptions.effort
symbols.comment:
Effort level for adaptive thinking models.
Controls how much thinking Claude allocates:
- "max": Always thinks with no constraints (Opus 4.6 only)
- "xhigh": Highest reasoning level (Opus 4.7+, Fable 5)
- "high": Always thinks, deep reasoning
- "medium": Moderate thinking, may skip for simple queries
- "low": Minimal thinking, skips for simple tasks
Ignored for older models.
Default: omitted unless `streamSimple()` maps a simple reasoning
level to this option.

symbols.name: AnthropicOptions.thinkingDisplay
symbols.comment:
Controls how thinking content is returned in API responses.
- "summarized": Thinking blocks contain summarized thinking text.
- "omitted": Thinking blocks return an empty thinking field; the encrypted
  signature still travels back for multi-turn continuity. Use for faster
  time-to-first-text-token when your UI does not surface thinking.

Note: Anthropic's API default for Claude Opus 4.7 and Claude Mythos Preview
is "omitted". We default to "summarized" here to keep behavior consistent
with older Claude 4 models. Set this explicitly to "omitted" to opt in.
Default: "summarized" when thinking is enabled.

symbols.name: AnthropicOptions.interleavedThinking
symbols.comment:
Whether to request the interleaved thinking beta header for non-adaptive
thinking models. Adaptive thinking models have interleaved thinking built in,
so the header is skipped for them regardless of this setting.
Default: true.

symbols.name: AnthropicOptions.toolChoice

Anthropic tool choice behavior. String values map to Anthropic's built-in
choices; `{ type: "tool", name }` forces a specific tool.
Default: omitted (Anthropic default behavior, currently equivalent to auto).

`fetch` is optional only because the published `Ai` type doesn't declare it yet — every real
binding has it at runtime. `aiGatewayLogId` is here to pin the type to the AI binding: it is

symbols.name: CLOUDFLARE_GATEWAY_BINDING_AUTH_SENTINEL
symbols.comment:
Placeholder value for auth headers on binding-routed requests. API implementations
require an API key or a recognized auth header (`authorization`, `x-api-key`,
`cf-aig-authorization`) before dispatch; binding calls are pre-authenticated, so pass
`cf-aig-authorization: Bearer ${CLOUDFLARE_GATEWAY_BINDING_AUTH_SENTINEL}` to satisfy
the check. The gateway ignores (and strips) `cf-aig-authorization` on binding-routed
requests. Pair it with `Authorization: null` / `x-api-key: null` so the SDKs' placeholder
auth headers never reach the gateway, which would treat a request-supplied auth header as a
BYOK provider key that overrides its stored keys — the same as it would over HTTPS.

symbols.name: createAiBindingFetch

packages/ai/src/api/cloudflare-ai-bindin.comment:
AI Gateway transport over the Workers AI binding.

pi's Cloudflare AI Gateway support speaks HTTPS
(`gateway.ai.cloudflare.com/v1/{account}/{gateway}/{provider}/...`, see `api/cloudflare.ts`),
which needs a Cloudflare API token even when the caller is a Worker in the gateway's own
account.

A Worker avoids that token by talking to the gateway through the AI binding's `fetch`
passthrough (`env.AI.fetch()`), which serves the gateway's provider passthrough at
`https://workers-binding.ai/ai-gateway/gateways/{gateway}/{provider}/{endpoint...}` — the same
shape as the HTTPS URL, minus the account id (the binding channel carries identity). Binding
calls are pre-authenticated in-account and return the provider's native wire format as a
regular (streaming) `Response`, so API implementations behave identically over either
transport.

A model whose `baseUrl` names that route therefore needs no translation: point it there and
pass {@link createAiBindingFetch} as the request `fetch`. Nothing is rewritten, buffered or
re-encoded — method, headers, query string and the body stream go to the binding as they
arrive, so every method, non-JSON body and streaming request body works.

The only thing this module adds over calling `env.AI.fetch()` yourself is a type: `Ai#fetch`
exists at runtime (`workerd/src/cloudflare/internal/ai-api.ts:158`) but
`@cloudflare/workers-types`' `Ai` class does not declare it yet, so calling it directly means
casting the binding at every call site. {@link AiBinding} takes the cast instead — declare
`fetch` optional, check it once at construction — so `env.AI` can be passed as-is. Once
workers-types declares `fetch`, the optional marker and the runtime check both go away.

symbols.name: transport
symbols.comment:
System One models on the Workers AI REST endpoint:
`POST /accounts/{account}/ai/run` with `{ model, input }`. The REST API wraps the model
output in Cloudflare's API envelope. Third-party models such as `typesafe/jev` add a run record:
`{ success, result: { state: "Completed", result: { answers, usage } } }`.
https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai/models/typesafe/jev/
Cloudflare-hosted models such as `@cf/cloudflare/clef` return the output directly:
`{ success, result: { model, answers, usage } }`.
https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/models/clef/

Clef models take images as an `images` list of data URLs. TypeSafe's models take them as
System One `assets`, without TypeSafe's opt-in header. The catalog sets `compat.imageInput`;
the model ID check only covers models without it.

Protocol note (Gemini / Vertex AI thought signatures):
- `thought: true` is the definitive marker for thinking content (thought summaries).
- `thoughtSignature` is an encrypted representation of the model's internal thought process

symbols.name: LABEL
symbols.comment:
Classification with a chat model served by llama.cpp's `llama-server`.

The model never generates an answer. Each question becomes one chat prompt
that lists the possible answers under single-token labels (letters for a
choice, `Yes`/`No` for a bool, digits for a score). The server evaluates the
prompt and returns the log-probabilities of its most likely next tokens; the
answer is the softmax over the label tokens among them.

Server endpoints used: `/tokenize` (label token IDs), `/apply-template` (the
model's own chat template, thinking disabled) and `/completion` with
`n_predict: 1` and pre-sampling `n_probs`. Pre-sampling log-probabilities are
a softmax over the full vocabulary, unaffected by sampler settings, so the
softmax over the label log-probabilities equals the softmax over the label
logits. The server returns only the top `n_probs` tokens, so a label missing
from the list is retried with a deeper list and then reported as an error.

In router mode every request carries the model ID in its `model` field;
single-model servers ignore it.

symbols.name: MIN_READOUT_DEPTH
symbols.comment: First `n_probs` depth is `max(MIN_READOUT_DEPTH, READOUT_DEPTH_PER_LABEL * labels)`.

symbols.name: READOUT_ESCALATION
symbols.comment: Deeper readouts tried when a label is missing. Only the response size grows.

symbols.name: UNDERFLOW_LOGPROB
symbols.comment: llama-server reports an underflowed probability as the lowest float instead of -Infinity.

The message is the state, every question of the request with its options,

symbols.name: LABEL
symbols.comment:
OpenAI's Decisions API: `POST /v1/decisions` with `{ model, input, questions }`.
https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/decisions

The state is sent as JSON text. With images, the input becomes one user message with the state
as `input_text` followed by `input_image` data URLs. Questions map to Decisions types:
`choice` to `choice`, `score` to `score`, and `bool` to `predicate`. Predicates have no

symbols.name: ConvertResponsesMessagesOptions.configurationUpdateEffort
symbols.comment:
Effort for the reply being generated. When set, the thinking level is sent as
configuration_update items instead of a changing reasoning.effort, which would invalidate the
prompt cache. Each item sets the effort from that point on: one goes before every earlier
reply with the level recorded on it (`providerThinkingLevel`), and one with this effort goes
at the end. Earlier input therefore never changes. OpenAI documents the item before user
messages only. After tool results it was verified on gpt-6-luna (October 2026) to be accepted
and to apply to the next reply.

symbols.name: getResponsesToolSupport
symbols.comment:
=============================================================================

Message conversion

=============================================================================

How a Responses transport expresses tool changes.

`additional_tools` items accumulate: a later item adds tools and replaces same-name
definitions from earlier items, but it cannot replace a top-level tool and cannot remove any
tool (verified with strict schemas on the OpenAI, Codex, and Copilot backends, October 2026).
Like Codex, every tool is therefore declared in `additional_tools` items, starting with one
at the head of the input, and removals are announced as text. Synthetic tool search can
only add tools. Without mid-conversation system messages there is nothing to anchor.

symbols.name: renderIncrementalToolsNotice
symbols.comment:
Precedes every additional_tools item after the first. Without it, models read the latest item as
the complete tool set once a removal was announced; Codex precedes its incremental tool batches
with the same guidance. Restating the tools that are still unavailable keeps smaller models
(gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-6-luna) from calling them again after later loads (verified October 2026).

packages/ai/src/api/pi-messages.ts.comment:
pi-messages API implementation.

Streams pi's own message protocol directly to a backend: the request is a
single POST of `{ model, context, options }` to `<baseUrl>/messages`, the
response is an SSE stream of serialized assistant-message events plus a
terminal `done`/`error` event. This is the wire protocol spoken by the
Radius gateway, but any backend implementing it can be used, e.g. via a
models.json custom provider with `"api": "pi-messages"`.

How a service takes images (`SystemOneCompat.imageInput`):
- `assets`: TypeSafe's `assets` map, `{ "<image-1>": { type: "image", format, data_base64 } }`,
  with the names placed before the state: `state: ["<image-1>", state]`. PNG and JPEG only.

  PNG, JPEG, and WebP, at most four.
- `state-image-urls`: OpenRouter's form, data URL parts placed before the state:
  `state: [{ type: "image_url", image_url: { url } }, state]`. OpenRouter accepts this for every
  model, and drops `assets` silently.

symbols.name: importOAuthModule
symbols.comment:
Loads an OAuth flow module through a variable specifier so bundlers cannot
follow the import into Node-only flow code (`node:http` callback servers,
`node:crypto` PKCE). The `.ts`/`.js` rewrite keeps the trick working from
both source and built output. The specifier is resolved against this
module's URL, not left relative: a bundler inlining this file (Chord's

packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/meta.ts.comment:
Meta Model API OAuth flow

RFC 8628 device authorization grant against https://auth.meta.com (JSON
responses). Meta splits identity from API access: the resulting identity
token is not accepted for inference, so it is exchanged for a Model API
key via the Muse Code key-mint endpoint (minted keys live about a day).
The identity token is stored as `refresh` and the minted key as `access`,
so the standard OAuth scheduler re-mints the key when it expires with no
bespoke renewal machinery. The identity token itself is not renewable
(auth.meta.com answers grant_type=refresh_token with 404 and issues no
refresh_token), so a 401/403 from mint means the session is dead and the
user must sign in again.

export async function refreshStoredOAuthCredential(
	credentials: CredentialStore,
	providerId: string,
	oauth: OAuthAuth,
	needsRefresh: (credential: OAuthCredential) => boolean,
	signal: AbortSignal,
): Promise<OAuthCredential | undefined>
symbols.comment:
Refresh a stored OAuth credential under the credential-store lock and persist
the result before the lock is released. `needsRefresh` is re-checked under
the lock, so concurrent callers and processes refresh only once.

`signal` cancels only the wait for the lock. Once a refresh starts, the
provider may already have rotated the refresh token, so the refresh and its
persistence ignore `signal` and are bounded only by a timeout. Otherwise a
cancelled caller could discard the only valid refresh token. Callers that
must return promptly on cancellation race this promise with their signal.

Resolves with the stored OAuth credential after the operation, or undefined
when the provider no longer has an OAuth credential.

symbols.name: CredentialStore
symbols.comment:
App-owned credential storage, keyed by `Provider.id`, one credential per
provider. `modify` is the only write path, so every mutation is a
serialized read-modify-write; `Models.getAuth()` runs OAuth refresh inside
`modify` so concurrent requests cannot double-refresh a rotated token. The
app persists a credential after login via
`modify(provider.id, async () => credential)`. Login/logout orchestration
is app-owned.

Error semantics: `read` resolves `undefined` for missing entries. Methods
reject only on storage failure; `Models` wraps such rejections in
`ModelsError` with code "auth". Best-effort stores that serve an in-memory
view and record persistence errors internally (like coding-agent's
AuthStorage) are valid implementations.

symbols.name: CredentialStore.modify
symbols.comment:
Serialized write — the only write path. `fn` sees the current credential
because correct writes (refresh, login-during-refresh) depend on it;
return the new credential, or undefined to leave the entry unchanged.
Mutual exclusion per provider id, cross-process too where the backing
store supports it (e.g. a file lock). Resolves with the post-write
credential. Rejections from `fn` propagate.

symbols.name: registerLazyBedrockProvider

Registers a bedrock loader with a literal dynamic import, for Node bundles
that split at dynamic imports (esbuild `splitting`, Chord's worker base):
the implementation and the AWS SDK land in a chunk loaded on the first
bedrock request, inside the bundle. Without it, pi-ai imports bedrock
through a variable specifier that bundlers cannot follow, so a bundle loads
it from pi-ai's own files. Browser bundles must not import this module.

symbols.name: registerLazyOAuthFlows

that split at dynamic imports (esbuild `splitting`, Chord's worker base):
each flow lands in a chunk loaded on its first use, inside the bundle.
Without it, pi-ai imports the flows through a variable specifier that
bundlers cannot follow, so a bundle loads them from pi-ai's own files.
Browser bundles must not import this module (the flows are Node-only).

symbols.name: Provider
symbols.signature: export interface Provider<TApi extends Api = Api> {
symbols.comment:
A provider is the concrete runtime unit. It owns id/name/base metadata,
auth methods, model listing, and the operations its models support
(streaming, image generation, classification).

`TApi` lets concrete provider factories declare which chat APIs their models
use (e.g. `openaiProvider(): Provider<"openai-responses" | "openai-completions">`),
giving typed chat model lists to direct factory users. Other model types use
their operation-specific API unions. Inside a `Models` collection providers
are held as `Provider<Api>`.

symbols.name: Provider.auth
symbols.comment:
Required: at least one of `apiKey`/`oauth`. Every provider has auth
semantics — even providers with only ambient credentials (env vars, AWS
profiles, ADC files) and keyless local servers provide `apiKey` auth
whose `resolve()` reports whether the provider is configured.
`Models.getAuth()` returns undefined when the provider is unconfigured.

symbols.name: Provider.getModels
symbols.comment:
Current known chat models, sync. Static providers return their catalog;
dynamic providers return the list as of the last `refreshModels()` (empty
before the first). Must not throw; `Models` treats a throwing
implementation as having no models.

symbols.name: Provider.getAllModels
symbols.comment:
Current known models of every type, sync, with the same contract as
`getModels()`. Providers with only chat models may omit it; `Models` then
uses `getModels()`. Model ids are unique within each type; one upstream
model may have separate entries for different operations.

symbols.name: Provider.refreshModels
symbols.comment:
Dynamic providers only: restore `context.stored` and optionally fetch a newer list using
the effective credential. Implementations retain their previous list on failure, publish
persistence and synchronous state changes through `context.publish()`, and honor the
shared abort signal for blocking work.

symbols.signature: filterModels?(models: readonly Model<TApi>[], credential: Credential | undefined): readonly Model<TApi>[];
symbols.comment:
Optional provider policy for credential-specific model availability.
`getModels()` remains the complete synchronous chat catalog; `Models.getAvailable()`
applies this filter after confirming that provider auth is configured.

symbols.name: Provider.filterAllModels
symbols.comment:
Optional credential-specific availability policy across every model type.
Without it, `Models.getAllAvailable()` applies `filterModels` to chat models
and keeps every other model.

symbols.name: Provider.stream

symbols.name: SystemMessage
symbols.comment:
System instructions and tool declarations at one point in the transcript.

The leading system message is the system prompt. Later system messages change it:
`content` adds instructions from that point on, `sections` replace or remove named
prompt sections, and `toolsAdded`/`toolsRemoved` change the tool set. Replaying
every system message in order yields the current prompt and tools. Providers that
accept system messages mid-conversation send each one in place; other providers
rebuild the leading system message from the replayed state.

symbols.name: SystemMessage.content
symbols.comment: Instruction text. On the leading message this is the base prompt; later, additional instructions.

symbols.name: SystemMessage.sections
symbols.comment:
Named, ordered prompt sections rendered verbatim after `content`. The leading message
declares them; later messages replace sections by name, and `null` removes one. Keep
each section self-delimiting (a tag, a heading) so the model can relate an update to
the original. Avoid integer-like names; JSON objects reorder those.

symbols.name: SystemMessage.toolsAdded
symbols.comment: Complete definitions of tools that become available at this point.

symbols.name: SystemMessage.toolsRemoved
symbols.comment: Tools that stop being available at this point.

symbols.name: AssistantMessageEvent
symbols.comment:
Event protocol for AssistantMessageEventStream.

Successful streams emit `start` before partial updates and terminate with
`done`. A stream may terminate directly with `error` when request setup fails
before generation starts; after `start`, failures also terminate with `error`.
Direct `streamSimple()` calls throw synchronously when request auth is missing.
Updates and `done` must never appear before `start`.

`partial` is the shared live response-so-far helper, not an event-time
snapshot. Text and thinking blocks are empty when their `*_start` event is
emitted and grow only through their corresponding `*_delta` events until the
authoritative `*_end`. Redacted thinking may be complete at start and emit no
deltas. Tool-call arguments at `toolcall_start` are provider-specific;
`toolcall_delta` carries subsequent JSON updates.

reason with a generic message (`openai`: `"Connection error."`). The real

`"fetch failed"` wraps `connect ECONNREFUSED ...`). Append the deepest

symbols.name: extractStatus
symbols.comment:
Probe the HTTP status, first numeric hit wins, in SDK-field order:
`statusCode` (Mistral) → `status` (`openai`, `@google/genai`) →
`$metadata.httpStatusCode` (Bedrock) → `$response.statusCode` (Bedrock).

symbols.name: extractBody
symbols.comment:
Probe the raw body reason, first usable hit wins, in SDK-field order:
`body` string (Mistral) → `error` parsed JSON body object (`openai` SDK's
`this.error`) → `$response.body` (Bedrock). Empty objects and unread response
streams are treated as no body so they do not surface as `"{}"` or serialized
stream internals. The chosen body is truncated to the cap.

symbols.name: isPlainNonEmptyObject
symbols.comment:
Only a PLAIN object counts as an HTTP body. SDK error fields can hold class
instances instead of parsed bodies — AWS SDK v3's `$response.body` is an
HTTP stream/response wrapper object, and stringifying one produced garbage
like `{"_events":...}` as the "body", which then REPLACED `error.message`
in the composed display string. `error.message` is where the SDK puts the
real deserialized exception text ("Input is too long...", schema validation
details, ...), so the one useful string was discarded for noise. A class
instance yields no body, `messageCarriesBody` stays true, and the real
message survives. Complements the `pipe` sniffing above: web
ReadableStreams (pipeTo/pipeThrough, no `pipe`) and non-stream SDK wrapper
classes fail the prototype check, while parsed JSON bodies (plain objects
by construction) still pass.

carries the body (Anthropic / `@google/genai` happy path) or no body/status
was extracted, the message is returned unchanged. Otherwise the status and
body are surfaced, with an optional provider prefix.

- no prefix: `"<status>: <body>"`
- prefix:    `"<prefix> (<status>): <body>"`

symbols.name: truncateErrorText
symbols.signature: export function truncateErrorText(text: string, maxChars: number): string

packages/ai/src/utils/error-body.ts.comment:
Shared normalization for provider HTTP error objects.



Endpoints behind a proxy / gateway may return a non-2xx response whose body

the provider SDK cannot fold into `error.message`. The SDK error object still

carries the HTTP status and the raw/parsed body, but under SDK-specific field

names. Provider catch blocks that read only `error.message` therefore drop

the body and surface opaque messages like `"403 status code (no body)"` or

collapse to `"Unknown: UnknownError"`.



`normalizeProviderError` probes the known SDK field shapes (Mistral,

`openai`, `@google/genai`, AWS Bedrock) and returns a struct each provider

composes into its display string. The `messageCarriesBody` flag captures the

Anthropic / `@google/genai` happy path where the SDK already folded the body

into the message, so providers can preserve it without double-printing.

symbols.name: OVERFLOW_PATTERNS
symbols.comment:
Regex patterns to detect context overflow errors from different providers.

These patterns match error messages returned when the input exceeds
the model's context window or the provider's request byte-size limit.

Provider-specific patterns (with example error messages):

- Anthropic: "prompt is too long: 213462 tokens > 200000 maximum"
- Anthropic: "413 {\"error\":{\"type\":\"request_too_large\",\"message\":\"Request exceeds the maximum size\"}}"
- OpenAI: "Your input exceeds the context window of this model"
- OpenAI/LiteLLM: "Requested token count exceeds the model's maximum context length of 131072 tokens"
- LiteLLM pre-call check: "litellm.ContextWindowExceededError: ... Context Window exceeded for given call."
- OpenAI-compatible: "Input length (265330) exceeds model's maximum context length (262144)."
- Google: "The input token count (1196265) exceeds the maximum number of tokens allowed (1048575)"
- xAI: "This model's maximum prompt length is 131072 but the request contains 537812 tokens"
- Groq: "Please reduce the length of the messages or completion"
- OpenRouter: "This endpoint's maximum context length is X tokens. However, you requested about Y tokens"
- OpenRouter/Poolside: "Input length X exceeds the maximum allowed input length of Y tokens."
- Together AI: "The input (X tokens) is longer than the model's context length (Y tokens)."
- llama.cpp: "the request exceeds the available context size, try increasing it"
- LM Studio: "tokens to keep from the initial prompt is greater than the context length"
- GitHub Copilot: "prompt token count of X exceeds the limit of Y"
- GitHub Copilot: 'github-copilot API error (413): {"message":"failed to parse request","code":""}'
- MiniMax: "invalid params, context window exceeds limit"
- Kimi For Coding: "Your request exceeded model token limit: X (requested: Y)"
- DS4: "Prompt has X tokens, but the configured context size is Y tokens"
- Cerebras: "400/413 status code (no body)"
- Mistral: "Prompt contains X tokens ... too large for model with Y maximum context length"
- z.ai: `{"code":"1261","message":"Prompt too long"}`, `{"code":"1261","message":"Prompt exceeds max length"}` (CN endpoint), or silent overflow via usage.input > contextWindow
- Xiaomi MiMo: Truncates input to fill contextWindow exactly, then returns finish_reason "length"
  with output=0 (no room left to generate). Detected via stopReason "length" + zero output +
  input filling the context window.
- DashScope/Qwen: "Range of input length should be [1, X]" (HTTP 400 invalid_parameter_error)
- Ollama: Some deployments truncate silently, others return errors like "prompt too long; exceeded max context length by X tokens"

symbols.name: NON_OVERFLOW_PATTERNS
symbols.comment:
Patterns that indicate non-overflow errors (e.g. rate limiting, server errors).
Error messages matching any of these are excluded from overflow detection
even if they also match an OVERFLOW_PATTERN.

Example: Bedrock formats throttling errors as "ThrottlingException: Too many tokens,
please wait before trying again." which would match the /too many tokens/i overflow
pattern without this exclusion.

symbols.name: isContextOverflow
symbols.signature: export function isContextOverflow(message: AssistantMessage, contextWindow?: number): boolean
symbols.comment:
Check if an assistant message represents a context overflow error.

This handles three cases:
1. Error-based overflow: Most providers return stopReason "error" with a
   specific error message pattern.
2. Silent overflow: Some providers accept overflow requests and return
   successfully. For these, we check if usage.input exceeds the context window.
3. Length-stop overflow: Xiaomi MiMo can return "length" with zero output when
   the input fills the context window.

## Reliability by Provider

**Reliable detection (returns error with detectable message):**
- Anthropic: "prompt is too long: X tokens > Y maximum" or "request_too_large"
- OpenAI (Completions & Responses): "exceeds the context window", "exceeds the model's maximum context length of X tokens", or "exceeds model's maximum context length (X)"
- Google Gemini: "input token count exceeds the maximum"
- xAI (Grok): "maximum prompt length is X but request contains Y"
- Groq: "reduce the length of the messages"
- GitHub Copilot: HTTP 413 "failed to parse request" (request byte-size overflow)
- Cerebras: 400/413 status code (no body)
- Mistral: "Prompt contains X tokens ... too large for model with Y maximum context length"
- OpenRouter (most backends): "maximum context length is X tokens"
- OpenRouter/Poolside: "Input length X exceeds the maximum allowed input length of Y tokens."
- Together AI: "The input (X tokens) is longer than the model's context length (Y tokens)."
- llama.cpp: "exceeds the available context size"
- LM Studio: "greater than the context length"
- Kimi For Coding: "exceeded model token limit: X (requested: Y)"
- DS4: "Prompt has X tokens, but the configured context size is Y tokens"
- DashScope/Qwen: "Range of input length should be [1, X]"
- z.ai: "Prompt too long"

**Unreliable detection:**
- z.ai: Sometimes accepts overflow silently (detectable via usage.input > contextWindow),
  sometimes returns rate limit errors. Pass contextWindow param to detect silent overflow.
- Xiaomi MiMo: Truncates input to fit contextWindow then returns stopReason "length" with
  output=0. Pass contextWindow param to detect via the "filled context + zero output" signal.
- Ollama: May truncate input silently for some setups, but may also return explicit
  overflow errors that match the patterns above. Silent truncation still cannot be
  detected here because we do not know the expected token count.

## Custom Providers

If you've added custom models via settings.json, this function may not detect
overflow errors from those providers. To add support:

1. Send a request that exceeds the model's context window
2. Check the errorMessage in the response
3. Create a regex pattern that matches the error
4. The pattern should be added to OVERFLOW_PATTERNS in this file, or
   check the errorMessage yourself before calling this function

@param message - The assistant message to check
@param contextWindow - Optional context window size for detecting silent overflow (z.ai)
@returns true if the message indicates a context overflow

symbols.name: retryAssistantCall
symbols.comment:
Run a single assistant-producing call with bounded retry on transient errors.

Behavior:
- A successful response is returned immediately. Aborts are terminal and never
  retried, but reported as unsuccessful if they happen after a retry was scheduled.
  Aborts during the backoff sleep are normalized to an aborted `AssistantMessage`
  too, so callers do not need to care when cancellation happened.
- A non-retryable error (per {@link isRetryableAssistantError}, including quota/
  billing exhaustion) is returned immediately so deterministic errors fail fast.
- Otherwise retries up to `maxRetries` times with exponential backoff, emitting
  `onRetryScheduled` before each sleep, `onRetryAttemptStart` after each sleep before
  the retried call starts, and `onRetryFinished` once at the end (whether the loop
  ends in success, exhausted retries, or an aborted backoff).

When `policy` is undefined or disabled, the first response is returned unchanged
(equivalent to calling `produce()` directly).

symbols.name: isRetryableAssistantError

Classifies whether a failed assistant message looks like a transient provider
or transport error, so callers can decide if the last assistant turn should be
restarted.

This does not implement retry policy. Callers should first handle context
overflow separately, then apply their own retry budget, backoff, and reporting
before restarting the assistant turn.

symbols.name: sanitizeSurrogates
symbols.comment:
Removes unpaired Unicode surrogate characters from a string.

Unpaired surrogates (high surrogates 0xD800-0xDBFF without matching low surrogates 0xDC00-0xDFFF,
or vice versa) cause JSON serialization errors in many API providers.

Valid emoji and other characters outside the Basic Multilingual Plane use properly paired
surrogates and will NOT be affected by this function.

@param text - The text to sanitize
@returns The sanitized text with unpaired surrogates removed

@example
Valid emoji (properly paired surrogates) are preserved
sanitizeSurrogates("Hello 🙈 World") // => "Hello 🙈 World"

Unpaired high surrogate is removed
const unpaired = String.fromCharCode(0xD83D); // high surrogate without low
sanitizeSurrogates(`Text ${unpaired} here`) // => "Text  here"
