packages/ai/src/utils/streaming-json.ts.comment:
Incremental, tolerant parsing of JSON text that arrives in pieces, such as streamed tool-call arguments.

`StreamingJsonParser.append()` reads each piece once, so a stream costs time and memory linear in its length, and
`snapshot()` returns the value of the text read so far. Snapshots are plain JSON values and never change once
returned: the parser copies the containers that are still open (the "open path") into every new snapshot and shares
completed containers and strings. The rules for incomplete text follow `parseStreamingJson()`:

- An unterminated string shows the characters read so far; an unterminated escape is held back until complete.
- An unterminated container shows the members and elements read so far.
- A member whose key or value has not started is omitted.
- An unterminated literal shows its value once it is a prefix of `true`, `false` or `null`; an unterminated number
  shows its value when the digits read so far form a number (an exponent without digits is ignored).

Malformed text is read leniently, the way `repairJson()` and `parseStreamingJson()` treat it: raw control characters
in strings are kept, an invalid escape such as `\d` stays literal text, missing commas and colons are tolerated,
values in invalid positions and unknown words are dropped, and text after the root value is ignored. The parser never
throws. Callers that need the exact value of the finished text parse it once, e.g. with `parseToolCallArguments()`.

Differences from `parseStreamingJson()` on incomplete text: trailing whitespace inside an unterminated string is
kept (it was trimmed), a string that contains a raw control character or an invalid escape stays visible while it
streams (it was dropped until the document was complete), and `NaN` and `Infinity` words are dropped.

`append()` also returns the changes the piece made, for a writer that keeps its own copy of the value and applies
them instead of re-assigning snapshots: `set` when a key, an array item or a finished value appears (a new string is
set once with its first text, a container empty), `append` when the piece extended an open string. Unterminated
numbers and literals are not reported until they end. A container nested more than 32 levels deep is reported as one
`set` of its whole value when it closes, so paths stay short.

Cost: copying the open path costs its member and element count. Each `append()` earns copy credit proportional to its
length plus a constant; `snapshot()` spends it and returns the previous snapshot while the open path costs more than
the credit. So a document that keeps a very large container open (thousands of elements) shows a preview that lags
a little behind the text, and no input makes the total work grow faster than the text.

symbols.name: TranscriptToolSupport
symbols.comment:
How a transport can express tool changes after the first request.

- `"none"`: only the top-level tool list exists; it always holds the current tools.
- `"additions"`: tools can be added at a later message, but not removed or redefined.
- `"changes"`: every tool, including the initial ones, is declared in place, and a later
  declaration under the same name replaces the earlier one. Removals are not expressible on
  the wire, so the transport announces them as text and the removed tools stay declared.

symbols.name: resolveTranscriptTools
symbols.signature: export function resolveTranscriptTools(messages: TranscriptMessages, support: TranscriptToolSupport): TranscriptTools
symbols.comment:
Split tool declarations between the top-level request field and in-place changes.

With `"changes"`, the top-level list stays empty and every system message, including the
leading one, declares its tools in place: an in-place declaration can replace an earlier
in-place one, but not a top-level one. With `"additions"`, a removal or redefinition cannot be
expressed in place, so the top-level list becomes the tool state after the last such change;
later additions stay anchored, and the cached prefix is invalidated once per removal instead
of on every later addition. With `"none"`, the top-level list is the current tool set.

symbols.name: Op
symbols.comment:
Tuples are the form — in memory, on the wire, on disk.

`r` is the ONLY op that replaces a whole value. `s`/`d`/`a`/`t` cannot target
the root: the type forbids it. `p` and `m` may, because a tracked value can
itself be an array. Operation shape is not canonical: an array may be emptied by either
a replacement or a root splice.

`Op` knows nothing about the path dictionary. Interning, id references and
omitted paths live in `WireOp` and exist only between `encode` and `decode`.

| readonly ["r", JsonValue]
	| readonly ["s", NonEmptyPath, JsonValue]
	| readonly ["d", NonEmptyPath]
	| readonly ["a", NonEmptyPath, string]
	| readonly ["t", NonEmptyPath, number]
	| readonly ["p", Path, number, number, JsonValue[]]
	/** Reorder an array in place: `new[i] = old[permutation[i]]`. */
	| readonly ["m", Path, number[]]

symbols.signature:
export type WireOp =
	| readonly ["r", JsonValue]
	| readonly ["s", PathRef<NonEmptyPath>, JsonValue]
	| readonly ["s", JsonValue]
	| readonly ["d", PathRef<NonEmptyPath>]
	| readonly ["d"]
	| readonly ["a", PathRef<NonEmptyPath>, string]
	| readonly ["a", string]
	| readonly ["t", PathRef<NonEmptyPath>, number]
	| readonly ["t", number]
	| readonly ["p", PathRef, number, number, JsonValue[]]
	| readonly ["p", number, number, JsonValue[]]
	| readonly ["m", PathRef, number[]]
	| readonly ["m", number[]]
	| readonly ["#", number, Path];
symbols.comment:
What crosses a boundary. Adds two compressions and nothing else:

  ["#", id, path]    defines an id, emitted on a path's SECOND use
  a numeric PathRef  references a previously defined id
  a shortened tuple  reuses the previous op's path; arity disambiguates

["r", value] carries no path, so it encodes to itself — which is why isBase
works unchanged on either vocabulary.

symbols.comment:
`text.slice(start, end)` as a string of its own. V8 represents a slice of 13 or more characters as a view that keeps
all of `text` alive, so an append op cut from a long, growing string would retain that whole string for as long as
the op lives: in a delta chain, a watch backlog, or a value built by applying the op. Appending a character and
slicing it off again makes V8 copy just the slice.

symbols.name: RESERVED_SEGMENTS
symbols.comment:
─── Path safety ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Segments that reach the prototype chain.

`JSON.parse` is safe on its own — it makes `__proto__` an own property. What is
not safe is `parent[key] = value`, which is exactly what an applier does, and
paths are data: `["s", ["__proto__", "isAdmin"], true]` pollutes
`Object.prototype` for the whole process.

Ops arrive from a facet, a plugin compartment, or a tool whose details may echo
model output, so none of it is trusted input.

symbols.name: assertIndexInRange
symbols.signature: function assertIndexInRange(parent: readonly unknown[], index: number): void
symbols.comment:
An index may address an existing element or append exactly one past the end.

This is not an arbitrary cap — it is what keeps the value a `JsonValue`. A
sparse array does not survive a JSON round trip: holes serialise to `null` and
return as real properties, so `arr[7] = x` on a length-3 array already produces
state a replica cannot match. Rejecting the write is more honest than silently
diverging.

It also removes the denial of service it would otherwise permit:
`["s", ["xs", 4294967290], 1]` allocates a 4.29-billion-entry array from one op.
Growth stays possible and stays proportional — the tracker already emits
`arr.length = n` as a splice of explicit nulls, whose op size grows with the
gap, so a large growth costs a large op rather than a small one.

Path interning and arity omission live between the tracker and a boundary;

symbols.name: State
PendingOps
symbols.comment:
Pending ops of one state for one consumer, in order and raw (never encoded while they wait). `r` drops everything
before it. A leaf op merges into the last pending leaf op on the same path (`a` + `a` joined, `s` replaces `s` or `a`,
`a` after a string `s` appends into it); any other op clears the leaf index. Leaf ops on different paths commute,
except after an ancestor primitive `s`, after which the descendant cannot be written until a structural op clears the
index. Past `MAX_PENDING_OPS` only "replace with the current value" stays pending.

Ops are only those of Delta's tracker, `diffRevisions()` and `appendText()`; received op arrays and tuples are never
mutated (they feed other consumers too), a merge makes a new tuple.

symbols.comment: Queue the ops of one commit.

symbols.comment:
Pending ops after folding; 1 once overflowed (the replacement the owner sends). One batch is counted as received,
so a single commit larger than `MAX_PENDING_OPS` counts in full until a second one arrives and overflows.

The key of a path in the leaf index. Injective, as merging two distinct paths would lose a write: `["a.b"]` and
`["a", "b"]` are different keys. A number and its string (`1`, `"1"`) may share one: within one index lifetime a
parent is either an array or an object, as changing it is a structural op that clears the index.

symbols.name: TrackerImpl
symbols.signature: class TrackerImpl<T extends object> implements Tracker<T> {
symbols.comment:
Open drafts are tracked so that adopting one change makes its open competitors stale at once. Prepared contexts need
no tracking: `prepare()` releases their overlay, and `adopt()` rejects them by revision.

The most recent open context is held strongly in `#open`: with one transaction at a time per tracker, the common case,
that is the only one, and it costs no `WeakRef` (each `WeakRef` target survives the scavenges of the current job, and
V8 then pretenures the context allocation site). A second `beginChange()` while one is open moves the older context
into `#competitors` through a `WeakRef`, so a draft the caller drops can be collected. A dropped draft that was never
settled stays held by `#open` until the tracker's next `beginChange()` or `adopt()`: at most one per tracker.

(several appends to the same key in one change join into one op) without comparing the old and new strings. A plain
assignment such as `draft[key] += text` gives the same op, but `prepare()` then has to check that the new string
extends the old one, which reads the whole string: O(length) per change. A plain assignment or deletion of the key in
the same change falls back to that check.

packages/chord/src/documents/keyed-slot..comment:
Keyed slots (slice 6a §1.2, §4, §10, §11): the documents of one keyed name on one object, by key. In memory, every

present document stays; persisted, a document is loaded on demand (a cold read is a job on the object's line, one

load in flight per key, shared) and leaves memory when unpinned and idle for the retention (`residency.ts`). A key

read through `at(key)` or a watch has its own source, which exists while the key is pinned.

symbols.name: Line
symbols.comment:
An object's line (§9): its transactions, cold loads, key pages and eviction sweeps run on it one at a time, in the

order they asked.

An object's line: `acquire()` resolves with the release once every earlier holder released; releasing twice is harmless.

`document` as `definition` reads it: a stored version newer than the code's, or the same version with another

code's (a failing `migrate` too, whatever it throws), never the store's.

loaded document (Durable's `LoadedDocument` fields), its loads with the version and fingerprint checks and the

checked `migrate`, and the writes one commit stages for a changed or retired document.

symbols.comment: How long an unpinned persisted keyed document stays in memory after its last read or write (slice 6a §10).

symbols.name: GRANULE_MS
symbols.comment: A touch moves an entry at most once per granule: a tenth of the retention, up to 1 s (Durable's rule).

symbols.comment: The idle persisted keyed documents of one object, oldest first, and the one timer evicting them.

symbols.comment: Runs a sweep on the object's line.

symbols.comment: The pending sweep: when it is due and its timer; stays set until its job runs on the line.
symbols.output: { readonly at: number; timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined } | undefined

symbols.name: Residency.touch
symbols.comment: A use of an unpinned `resident`: it becomes the newest idle one (once per granule), and a sweep is scheduled.

symbols.name: Residency.forget
symbols.comment: `resident` is pinned or left memory: it is no longer idle.

symbols.name: Residency.end
symbols.comment: The object ended: nothing is evicted any more, the timer is cleared.

symbols.name: Residency.#schedule
symbols.comment: Schedules the eviction of the oldest idle document when its retention expires.

symbols.name: Residency.#evictExpired
symbols.comment:
On the line: evicts the idle documents whose retention passed, oldest first, then schedules the next sweep. No
load in flight needs a pin against it: cold loads run on the line too, so a sweep never runs during one, and a
load installing an unpinned key touches it (it is then the newest idle one).

packages/chord/src/documents/residency.t.comment:
Residency of keyed documents (slice 6a §10, rule 23): which keyed documents are in memory, and the eviction of

persisted ones nobody pinned and nobody read or wrote for the retention. One idle structure and one timer per

object, Durable's (`Session.#touchDocument`): an insertion-ordered map whose oldest entry the timer waits for, a

touch moving an entry to the back at most once per granule (O(1) per touch, no timer per key).

Document slots (slice 6a §1.2): one per declared document name on its object, across the object's attempts. A slot

holds the documents' trackers, the version and definition its values are of, what is stored of persisted ones, and

the watches; each attempt's handles are thin views of it. This file: what every slot is, and the singleton's slot

failing the live object `broken` too (memory and disk disagree).

symbols.name: Transaction.#adopt
symbols.comment:
Adopts the changed documents (persisted ones with what the commit stored of them) and the staged changes in one
batch; nothing when nothing changed.

symbols.name: Transaction.discard
symbols.comment: Aborts every draft and prepared change.

symbols.name: Transaction.cut
symbols.comment:
Its token was sealed while it held the line: every draft is aborted, the line released, and every later use,
its commit included, throws `released`.

symbols.name: Transaction.settle
symbols.comment: Tells the staged changes how the transaction ended; runs once the object's line is free.

symbols.name: Transaction.#slotOf
symbols.comment: The slot behind a handle of this object, after the handle's version fence (R15).

symbols.name: Transaction.#handle
symbols.comment: The handle behind `table`, one of this object's tables (another object's is refused).

symbols.name: Transaction.#changes
symbols.comment: The writes to `table` in this transaction, made by the first.

symbols.name: Transaction.#refreshQueries
symbols.comment:
Stages the re-run of the live queries over the tables this transaction wrote (decision "Live queries over an
object's own tables"): read in the commit step after every table write staged so far (the callback's), published
in the commit's batch. None when no written table has a live query.

symbols.name: Transaction.#track
symbols.comment: Counts `read` as pending until the operation's promise settles (rule 3).

symbols.name: Transaction.#begin
symbols.comment: The entry's draft, begun on the current document (or a fresh `initial()`) by the first use.

symbols.name: checkFound
symbols.signature: function checkFound(found: FoundDocument, persisted: PersistedSlot, slot: DocumentSlot): void
symbols.comment: Throws, failing `slot`'s owner `broken`, when its definition cannot read the cold document `found` (R15).

packages/chord/src/documents/transaction.comment:
Transactions (§9, R12, R13): drafts of an object's documents, prepared and adopted in one batch, with Chord's own

staged changes (job runs, §15), fenced by the token they run under; they run on the object's line (`line.ts`).

symbols.name: ActivityCounts
symbols.comment: What `host.activity` counts.

symbols.name: references
symbols.comment: Holds arriving over links and served here.

symbols.name: calls
symbols.comment: Method calls running on this host, local and remote.

symbols.name: jobs
symbols.comment: Running jobs (slice 5).

symbols.name: lingering
symbols.comment: Objects kept live by their type's `linger` after their last reference.

symbols.name: Activity
symbols.comment:
`host.activity`. A count marks it changed; while it is watched or derived from, the first change of a microtask turn
schedules one publication, a batch that gives its watches the counts as they are then (`[["r", counts]]`: a slow
watch gets the newest counts) and marks derives over it. Its value is built from the counters when read or
published.

symbols.name: Activity.#value
symbols.comment: The counts as last read, until the next change.

symbols.name: Activity.count
symbols.signature: count(kind: keyof ActivityCounts, delta: number): void
symbols.comment:
Adds `delta` to the count of `kind`; published with the turn's other changes. Nothing is scheduled while nobody
watches or derives from it: a later watch or derive reads the counts as they are then.

packages/chord/src/host/activity.ts.comment:
Keep-alive counts (§3, R26): `host.activity`, a JSON watchable of the work keeping a host busy, for the app's

supervisor. Counters are kept where the work happens; their changes in one microtask turn are one publication.

symbols.name: StateMapping
symbols.comment: A state mapping as an accepts table holds it (checked by `checkAccepts`).

symbols.name: VersionMappings
symbols.comment: One older version's mappings, as `checkAccepts` checked them: remote state by variant, local state flat.

symbols.name: state
symbols.signature: readonly state?: { readonly [key: string]: StateMapping | { readonly [member: string]: StateMapping } };
symbols.output: { readonly [key: string]: StateMapping | { readonly [member: string]: StateMapping } }

symbols.name: AdaptedInstance
symbols.comment: What the mappings of one instance read: its provider, its variant, its own members, its host's batch and reports.

symbols.name: member
symbols.comment: The instance's state member `member` (`invalid/member` when its variant has none).

symbols.name: report
symbols.comment: Reports a mapping derive's failure (`derive_failed`).

symbols.name: MappedKey
symbols.signature: type MappedKey = { readonly derive: Derive; holders: number };
symbols.comment: A key's mapping derive, shared by the references holding the key at this version.

symbols.name: refusal
symbols.signature: export function refusal(served: Served, version: number, variant: string | undefined): ChordError | undefined
symbols.comment:
Why consumers of the older `version` cannot bind to `served`'s `variant`: a version it does not accept, or a member
of it the provider refuses (`contract_mismatch`); `undefined` when they can.

symbols.name: AdaptedMembers
symbols.comment: One instance's members as the consumers of one older version read them.

symbols.name: AdaptedMembers.#members
symbols.comment: The members read so far: a mapping derive, or the instance's member itself (unchanged).

symbols.name: AdaptedMembers.#derives
symbols.comment: The mapping derives it made (an unchanged member is the instance's own: it never detaches that one).

symbols.name: AdaptedMembers.#keys
symbols.comment: The keys held so far, by the instance's key document.

symbols.name: AdaptedMembers.member
symbols.comment:
State member `member` as this version reads it, made by the first use; `contract_mismatch` when the provider
refuses it or does not accept this version.

symbols.name: AdaptedMembers.key
symbols.signature: key(member: string, document: DeriveSource): { readonly source: DeriveSource; release(): void }
symbols.comment:
The document `document` at a key of keyed member `member` as this version reads it: the document itself when
unchanged, else a derive of it through the mapping, shared by its holders; `release` (once per call) lets the last
holder's go. `contract_mismatch` when the provider refuses the member.

symbols.name: AdaptedMembers.keyed
symbols.comment:
The provider's mapping of keyed member `member`'s documents to this version's shape (`undefined`: unchanged),
counted; throws `contract_mismatch` when the provider refuses it.

symbols.name: AdaptedMembers.detach
symbols.comment: Its instance ended, or the version's last reference left: its derives go (their watches end with `error`).

symbols.name: AdaptedMembers.#keyed
symbols.comment: The mapping of keyed member `member`, counted; `contract_mismatch` when refused.

symbols.name: AdaptedMembers.#make
symbols.comment:
What `member` is at this version: the instance's member itself (unchanged), or a derive through the mapping, of the
member when the current variant has it, else of the variant's whole current state (a removed member).

symbols.name: AdaptedMembers.#assertAccepted
symbols.comment: Throws `contract_mismatch` unless the provider accepts this version.

symbols.name: AdaptedMembers.#mappings
symbols.comment: This version's mappings in the provider's accepts table.

symbols.name: mappingsOf
symbols.signature: function mappingsOf(served: Served, version: number): VersionMappings | undefined
symbols.comment: `version`'s mappings in `served`'s accepts table.

symbols.name: stateMapping
symbols.comment: The mapping of state member `member` of `variant` in `mappings`; `undefined` when it is unchanged.

symbols.name: refused
symbols.signature: function refused(contract: Contract, version: number, member: string): ChordError
symbols.comment: The `contract_mismatch` of a member of `version` the provider refuses.

symbols.name: ended
symbols.comment: The `released` error its derives end with when its instance or version goes.

packages/chord/src/host/adapted.ts.comment:
Adapted members (Q10, §22, slice 7b §7; decision "References are the only indirection" (5)): one object instance's

shared mapping for the consumers of one older version its provider accepts. Per state member one derive of the

instance's member through `(current) => old` (a changed member), of its variant's whole state through `(state) => old`

(a removed member), or the member itself (unchanged), made on first use; per key of a keyed member one derive of the

key's document through the member's mapping, shared by the references holding it. One map and one diff per commit

per version, whatever the number of old references. Dropped when no reference of the version is left, gone with the

instance; references move to a new instance's mappings as to any new instance. A version the provider does not

accept, or a refused member, gives no member (`contract_mismatch`): its consumers wait unbound.

symbols.name: Self
symbols.signature:
export interface Self

extends RoutineDeclarations

{
symbols.comment:
What a factory declares with. Declarations (`state`, `derive`, `get`, `registry`, `writable`, `retryOn`, `open`,
`on`, `onLive`, `job`; `table`, `query` and `contribute` in `StoreSelf`) are valid only while it runs. `P` is the
app's principal type, which the ctx of routine calls and job runs carry.

symbols.name: Self.state
symbols.signature: state<D extends StateDefinition<JsonObject, boolean, false>>(definition: D): HandleOf<D>;
symbols.comment: This object's documents of `definition`, in memory for its life (across its attempts).

symbols.name: Self.derive
symbols.comment:
A value computed from `sources` (JSON watchables and native ones: a `writable`, a registry value, `ref.state`) by
the pure, synchronous `compute`; always JSON.

symbols.name: Self.get
symbols.signature: get<C extends Contract>(Type: C, params: ParamsOf<C>): Reference<C>;
symbols.comment: A reference to another object, live once this object is, released when it ends.

symbols.name: Self.registry
symbols.comment:
Registry `R`'s composed value as this plugin's version of `R` sees it: a declared dependency, as `get` is
(the attempt parks until it has a usable value: `failed { waiting }` while it has none, woken when it has). Read
`.value` at use; once live, a later failure of the registry keeps its last good value while every contribution it
was built from is still in the table.

symbols.name: Self.writable
symbols.comment:
An in-process value this attempt sets (`set`, identity compared): a contribution, a derive source and an `on`
source, never a state member; its watches end with the attempt, and `set` after its end throws `released`.

symbols.name: Self.retryOn
symbols.comment:
Wake signals: a new value of any of `sources` (registry values; constants never change) retries this object
while it is failed, as `ref.retry()` does, and once more at once if its current activation fails. Followed from
the factory's return until the next attempt's declaration or the object's end; failures wake nothing.

symbols.name: Self.open
symbols.comment:
A native, opened during activation after the references are live and the earlier natives are open, and closed
in reverse when the attempt ends. `open` gets a context aborted when the attempt is abandoned; `close` one aborted
at the close timeout. Throw `broken(error)` from `open` when retrying is pointless.
inputs: close: (value: T, reason: NativeCloseReason, context: Context) => void | Promise<void>

symbols.name: Self.tx
symbols.signature: tx<R>(fn: (tx: Tx) => R | Promise<R>, context: Context): Promise<R>;
symbols.comment: Runs `fn` as one transaction of this object (§9).

symbols.name: Self.follow
symbols.comment:
A source following another runtime's synchronous observer (Durable's views, slice 6b §3): `attach` runs during
activation once the natives opened (a rejection or `undefined` fails the activation `transient`), and the observer
is detached when the attempt ends. Its runtime failing fails this object `transient`; its `ended` is final, the
source keeping its last value. A state member, a derive source, an `on` source.

symbols.name: Self.job
symbols.signature: job<A, R, S>(definition: JobDefinition<A, R, S>, implementation: JobImplementation<A, R, S, P>): JobHandle<A, R, S>;
symbols.comment:
This object's job `definition` (§15), once per job name: `run` runs each started run outside transactions,
`finish` records its outcome in one. Starts are taken once the object is live.

symbols.signature:
export interface StoreSelf

extends Self

{
symbols.comment:
What the factory of a `local` type with empty params declares with: one object per host and type, so its data may
persist (P3). `P` as for `Self`.

symbols.name: StoreSelf.state
symbols.signature: state<D extends StateDefinition<JsonObject, boolean, boolean>>(definition: D): HandleOf<D>;
symbols.comment: This object's documents of `definition`: in memory for its life, or persisted in the host's store.

symbols.name: StoreSelf.table
symbols.signature: table<C extends Columns, K extends readonly string[]>(definition: TableDefinition<C, K>): Table<C, K>;
symbols.comment: This object's table `definition` in the host's store, once per table name.

symbols.name: StoreSelf.query
symbols.comment:
A live query (decision "Live queries over an object's own tables"): the rows of `q` (at most `limit`, in its
order) over `table`, a table this factory declared, as a JSON watchable (a state member, a derive source). Run
before the object goes live, and again in the commit step of every commit of this object that writes `table`
(one query per such commit, bounded by `limit`; not for tables written hundreds of times a second). A limit is
required (`invalid/args`).

symbols.name: StoreSelf.contribute
symbols.signature: contribute<C>(R: Registry<C, unknown>, value: Contribution<C>): void;
symbols.comment:
Contributes `value` to registry `R` from the moment this object is live until it ends, fails or restarts (R21: a
host-lifetime object): a plain value, or a Chord watchable of one (followed: its change recomposes). At most one
per registry.

symbols.name: NONE
symbols.comment: No declarations of a kind: the shared empty list.

symbols.name: Work
symbols.comment: Running work of one kind (calls, routine calls, job invocations), with the bookkeeping each runs once.

symbols.name: RoutineRun
symbols.signature: type RoutineRun = { readonly abort: AbortController; readonly calls: Work };
symbols.comment: Its routines once started: aborted when they stop (its seal, a reload's handover or restart), and their running calls.
symbols.output: { readonly abort: AbortController; readonly calls: Work }

symbols.signature: type Reloaded = { started: boolean; callsDrained: boolean; routinesStopped: boolean };

What a reload did to an attempt: `started` (a reload started it), `callsDrained` (a restart drains its calls: old
work runs on it until its seal, and its end's drain does not wait for them again), `routinesStopped` (its routines
stopped, and do not start late).
symbols.output: { started: boolean; callsDrained: boolean; routinesStopped: boolean }

symbols.name: writables

symbols.name: NotLive

symbols.output: { readonly trigger: TelemetryContext; readonly attempt: number }

symbols.name: Activated
symbols.comment:
How an attempt's activation ended, for its span: live, failed (a transient failure's next attempt at `retryAt`), or
ended (abandoned, its object gone).

symbols.name: notLive
symbols.signature: export function notLive(label: string, ms: number): ChordError

symbols.name: Attempt
symbols.signature: export class Attempt implements StoreSelf, KeyDeclarer, RegistryWaiter {
symbols.comment:
One attempt of an object. Activation: factory, documents hydrated (the object's slots), tables prepared and live
queries run, references bound, then parked until every dependency is live (no timer: the deadline paused), then its
own steps: natives opened one after another, followed sources attached, members checked, derives computed; bounded
by the host's `readyTimeout`. Ending: sealed at once (calls aborted, its transactions refused and the one holding the
line discarded, its job invocations cut off), then the drain, the closes in reverse, derives and live queries
detached; its object releases its references. Documents and job runs stay on the object.

symbols.name: Attempt.#served
symbols.comment: The type its object was served as when it was made: its provider's `accepts` map its older consumers.

symbols.name: Attempt.#adapted
symbols.comment: Its shared mappings for the consumers of older versions (Q10), by version; made by the first.

symbols.name: Attempt.#context
symbols.comment: The object's context: the natives' closes run under it.

symbols.name: Attempt.#abort
symbols.comment: Aborted when the attempt is abandoned or ends: openers, activation's waits and calls run under its signal.

symbols.name: Attempt.#opening
symbols.comment: The object's context under this attempt's signal, and its activation span while one is recorded.

symbols.name: Attempt.#activation
symbols.comment: Its activation span while it runs (none when the host records nothing); a parked attempt resumes in a new one.

symbols.name: Attempt.#parkedAt
symbols.comment: When it parked (`performance.now()`), while it is parked: `chord.park.duration` once it leaves.

symbols.name: Attempt.#token
symbols.comment: The seal token its handles and transactions carry (the seal fence).

symbols.name: Attempt.#routineRun
symbols.comment: Its routines once they started (most attempts have none).

symbols.name: Attempt.#declared
symbols.comment: The documents it declared, by name: "declared twice" is per attempt.

symbols.name: Attempt.#pins
symbols.comment: Its factory's `at(key)` pins: the object holds them from its factory's return to the next one's (rule 6).

symbols.name: Attempt.#isLive
symbols.comment: Set once it went live: its derives' failures are reported from then on (`derive_failed`).

symbols.name: Attempt.#members
symbols.comment: The checked implementation and, for a remote object, its variant, once activation checked them.

symbols.name: Attempt.#follows
symbols.comment: Its followed sources, attached in declaration order after the natives.

symbols.name: Attempt.#tables
symbols.comment: The tables it declared, by name.

symbols.name: Attempt.#queries
symbols.comment: Its live queries, run at activation (after the tables are prepared), detached at its end.

symbols.name: Attempt.#references
symbols.signature:
readonly #references: { readonly binding: Binding; readonly contract: Contract; readonly params: CheckedParams }[] =
		[];
symbols.comment: References this attempt declared with `self.get` (params checked), bound during activation.
symbols.output: { readonly binding: Binding; readonly contract: Contract; readonly params: CheckedParams }[]

symbols.name: Attempt.#dependencies
symbols.comment:
Its dependencies (`self.get` references and `self.registry` values) in declaration order: the parked cause and
`parked_long` name the first that blocks. Made by the first; let go after the dependency check (a live attempt
keeps none).

symbols.name: Attempt.#running
symbols.comment:
Running calls' handlers, routine calls and job runs, each with its bookkeeping (call counts, `ctx.get`
references): an ending attempt waits for them (the drain); the bookkeeping runs once, when its work settles or at
teardown for work stuck past the drain (decision "The seal fence" (4)). One map and one reaction per piece of work:
the call path costs no more than before the cleanups.

symbols.name: Attempt.#runs
symbols.comment:
Its running job invocations, as `#running`: the drain at its end waits for them (a restart's drain does not: they
are cut at its seal). Made by the first.

symbols.name: Attempt.#abandoned
symbols.comment: What activation returns once the attempt was abandoned: a timeout, a cycle through its object, or its end.

symbols.name: Attempt.#parked
symbols.comment: Its dependencies while it is parked on them (the dependency check); `undefined` otherwise.

symbols.name: Attempt.#moved
symbols.comment: A dependency changed since the last check: the parked attempt checks again (one check per batch of changes).

symbols.name: Attempt.#changed
symbols.comment: What a parked attempt waiting for a change waits on; resolved after the change's batch.

symbols.name: Attempt.#endedEarly
symbols.comment: A followed source's end while this attempt activated: it fails as it goes live (if its activation returned).

symbols.name: Attempt.#registryDeclarations
symbols.comment: Its registry reads, contributions, wake signals and writables, made by the first: most attempts have none.

symbols.name: Attempt.#check
symbols.comment:
Its first dependency check, for a reload (its report, its predecessor's references): waited for by someone, or
done with why it parked (`undefined`: it did not). Made by the first who asks or by the check.

symbols.name: Attempt.#reloaded
symbols.comment: What a reload did to it, made by the first such step (most attempts never meet one).

symbols.name: Attempt.activate
symbols.comment:
Activates once `ending` (the previous instance's) has finished; `readyTimeout` bounds both (an attempt abandoned
while it waits has opened nothing).

symbols.name: Attempt.activationSpan
symbols.comment: Its current (or last) activation span; `undefined` when the host records nothing.

symbols.name: Attempt.activated
symbols.comment:
Its activation's outcome, as its object took it: its span ends with it (a failure's error and a transient one's
backoff an event). An attempt still parked (its span ended `parked`) that fails or ends there records it in a short
span linked to the parked one, as its resumed steps would run in one (review L4).

symbols.name: Attempt.#startActivation
symbols.comment:
Starts an activation span on the host's adapter linked to `link` (none when it records nothing); the activation's
steps (its natives' opens, its references' holds) run under it.

symbols.name: Attempt.#parkedOn
symbols.comment: It parked showing `shown`: its activation span ends `parked` with the cause as an event.

symbols.name: Attempt.#parkEnded
symbols.comment: It leaves its parking (its dependencies live, or abandoned): its park's duration is recorded.

symbols.name: Attempt.abandon
symbols.comment: Abandons the activation with `outcome` (once): its waits stop and the openers' contexts are aborted.

symbols.name: Attempt.#followEnded
symbols.comment:
A followed runtime ended its observer (R4): `failed` fails this attempt `transient`, live or activating; `ended`
does only while it activates (it would go live over a source that ended). An activation that already returned
fails as it goes live.

symbols.name: Attempt.live
symbols.comment: The object went live: its jobs take starts and its routines start, in this turn; both stop when it is sealed.

symbols.name: Attempt.#startRoutines
symbols.comment: Starts its routines, unless it was sealed meanwhile.

symbols.name: Attempt.#stopRoutines
symbols.comment: Its routines stop with `reason` (or may not start any more: `#startRoutines` asks the abandonment too).

symbols.name: Attempt.stopRoutines
symbols.comment: Its routines stop (their ctx aborted); their running calls are waited for by the drain.

symbols.name: Attempt.beginDrain
symbols.comment:
A restart drains it: from now on it serves old work (calls caused by calls on old attempts, routed by its object)
until its seal, counted as the host's old work.

symbols.name: Attempt.draining
symbols.comment: Whether a restart drains it and it is not sealed yet: old work runs on it.

symbols.name: Attempt.drainCalls
symbols.comment:
Waits until no call or routine call runs on it, routed old work included (it joins while the drain runs), or until
`due` (`Date.now()` time; `drain_timeout` reported). Its end's drain then waits for them no more.

symbols.name: Attempt.served
symbols.comment: The type it was made with: its contract and provider (old work and its consumers use it by that contract).

symbols.name: Attempt.startedByReload
symbols.comment: A reload started it: once live, its object retries its blocked job runs (slice 7b §8).

symbols.name: Attempt.reloadStarted
symbols.comment: Whether a reload started it.

symbols.name: Attempt.#reload
symbols.comment: What a reload did to it, made by the first such step.

symbols.name: Attempt.declaresJob
symbols.comment: Whether its factory declared job `name`.

symbols.name: Attempt.opensNatives
symbols.comment: Whether its factory opens natives (`self.open`): a restart's contributions then leave at its seal (F-b).

symbols.name: Attempt.checked
symbols.comment:
Its first dependency check: why it parked (`parkedCause`), `undefined` when it went on (its dependencies live) or
its activation ended before (its predecessor's references are released once it is done).

symbols.name: Attempt.#settleCheck
symbols.comment: Its first dependency check is done: parked for `cause`, or not (once).

symbols.name: Attempt.isParked
symbols.comment: Whether it is parked on its dependencies (the dependency check runs).

symbols.name: Attempt.contributions
symbols.comment: Its contributions, resolved by its activation: in the registries' tables while its object is live.

symbols.name: Attempt.variant
symbols.comment: The variant a remote object's factory chose; `undefined` for a local object.

symbols.name: Attempt.stateMembers
symbols.comment: The state members, as Chord follows them.

symbols.name: Attempt.call
symbols.signature:
call(
		method: string,
		args: unknown,
		context: Context,
		caller: Caller,
		version: number,
		parent: TelemetryContext,
	): Promise<unknown>
symbols.comment:
Calls a method for `caller`, bound at `version`: a method outside the variant fails `invalid/member` first (for an
older version after its table's checks), then the arguments are checked against that version (L1) and, for an
older one (Q10), mapped forwards, the handler's result mapped back, or the provider's replacement of a removed
method run instead; a refused method fails `contract_mismatch`. The handler runs under a ctx aborted by the caller
and by this attempt's end, admitted to the drain before it runs. Either rejects the caller at once; the handler
runs on, its transactions refused, and the drain waits for it. Its `ctx.get` references are released when it
settles. Measured choices (fix round 2): one body for every version (with the shared part in a helper method, a
call over a link was about 10% slower in the links benchmark), and no `async` (a check's throw is returned as a
rejection; as an async function a local call allocated about 250 B more).

symbols.signature: #methodSpan(parent: TelemetryContext, method: string, acting: Caller, context: Context): OpenSpan<"chord.method">
symbols.comment: The `chord.method` span of a call of `method` acting as `acting`, under `parent`.

symbols.name: Attempt.#noMethod
symbols.comment: The `invalid/member` error of a method outside the variant.

symbols.name: Attempt.keyedMember
symbols.comment:
The keyed member `member`'s ultimate slot (slice 6a §12, rule 22: through re-exposures); an unknown one fails
`invalid/member`.

symbols.name: Attempt.keyedMembers
symbols.comment: The keyed members as checked: what each is (`KeyedBinding`), for the keys its object holds across attempts.

symbols.name: Attempt.memberAt
symbols.comment:
State member `member` as a consumer of `version` follows it: its own member at its version, else its shared mapping
for that version (`AdaptedMembers`); `invalid/member` outside the variant, `contract_mismatch` for a version or
member its provider refuses.

symbols.name: Attempt.keyMapping
symbols.signature: keyMapping(member: string, version: number): ((current: JsonValue) => JsonValue) | undefined
symbols.comment: How a consumer of `version` reads keyed member `member`'s documents: mapped when older (`undefined`: as they are).

symbols.name: Attempt.pinKey
symbols.signature: async pinKey(member: string, key: string, version: number, context: Context): Promise<PinnedKey>
symbols.comment:
Pins `key` of keyed member `member` on this instance, loaded (its own slot's document, or the re-exposed reference's
key), as a consumer of `version` reads it (mapped when older); `release` lets it go.

symbols.name: Attempt.dropVersion
symbols.comment: No consumer of `version` is left: its shared mapping goes.

symbols.name: Attempt.#adaptedAt
symbols.comment: Its mapping for `version`, made by the first use, reading this instance's own members and provider.

symbols.name: Attempt.member
symbols.comment: The state member `member`, as Chord follows it; one outside the variant fails `invalid/member`.

symbols.name: Attempt.seal
symbols.comment:
Ends the attempt at once (the seal fence): calls, openers and routines aborted with `error` (their callers
rejected with it), its transactions refused and the one holding the line discarded, its job invocations cut off
(an in-memory run ends `aborted` with `runs` as its reason: `reload` for a native restart, slice 7b §8); documents
stay readable.

symbols.name: Attempt.close
symbols.comment:
Tears a sealed attempt down: waits for its running handlers, routine calls and runs up to the host's
`closeTimeout` (the drain), then closes its natives in reverse with `reason`. Resolves with the closes that threw.

symbols.name: Attempt.#drained
symbols.comment:
The drain at its end, bounded by `closeTimeout`: its running calls (unless a restart's `drainCalls` waited for them
already), routine calls and job invocations.

symbols.name: Attempt.detach
symbols.comment:
Detaches its derives and live queries (once their object no longer needs them: reads throw `released`, their
watches end; no commit re-runs the queries), its followed sources (their observers detached, their watches ended)
and its writables (their watches ended).

symbols.name: Attempt.releaseReferences
symbols.comment: Releases its references and registry reads.

symbols.name: Attempt.#activate
symbols.comment: The activation steps; each catches its own failures with their kind (the table in slice 2's spec).

symbols.name: Attempt.#park
symbols.signature: async #park(dependencies: readonly Dependency[], deadline: Deadline): Promise<NotLive | undefined>
symbols.comment:
Parks while a dependency is not live (dependency model §3), with no timer: the deadline paused, `parked_long`'s
report the only clock. Checks at every change of a dependency (after its batch) and shows what it found on its
object; once all are live, the keys the factory pinned on them are loaded (a failed load parks it `waiting`
until the next change or a retry). Resolves `undefined` once all are live and pinned, else with how it ends:
abandoned, or broken (a cycle, an ended dependency).

symbols.name: Attempt.#unparked
symbols.comment: Its dependencies are live after it parked: its own steps run in a new activation span, linked to the parked one.

symbols.name: Attempt.#nextChange
symbols.comment:
Waits for the next change of a dependency (at once when one came during the check); `false` when the attempt was
abandoned meanwhile (its end, the only thing that stops the wait).

symbols.name: Attempt.#pinKeys
symbols.comment:
Loads the keys the factory pinned on its dependencies' keyed members (`at(key)`), each reference's named to `long`
as the blocker while they load (`failed` when they failed); `undefined` once all are, else what the parked attempt
shows for the first that failed to load (`waiting` on its reference).

symbols.name: Attempt.dependencyMoved
symbols.comment:
A dependency of this parked attempt changed (its state, its cause, its first outcome): it checks again after the
batch that changed it, once however many changed. A change while it checks or loads pinned keys is remembered
(`#moved`); one outside parking costs a flag.

symbols.name: Attempt.closed
symbols.comment: A registry it is parked on closed with its host: the parked attempt ends with `error`.

symbols.name: Attempt.#pinsKeys
symbols.comment: Whether its factory pinned keys on its dependencies' keyed members (`at(key)`), which load while it is parked.

symbols.name: Attempt.retryDependencies
symbols.comment:
`ref.retry()` on its parked object (`failed { waiting }`): passed on to every failed dependency (a broken or
transient one retries, a parked one passes it on, a request waiting in an index is left alone), as a step of
`walk`; then it checks again (a key that failed to load is loaded again).

symbols.name: Attempt.#ownSteps
symbols.comment:
The steps after the dependency check (its own: natives, followed sources, the member check, derives, the keys
references pin on its keyed members), under the deadline. A dependency that leaves `live` meanwhile changes
nothing (R18 after live).

symbols.name: Attempt.#resolveContributions
symbols.comment: Its declared contributions, as Chord follows them (its references are live now), by its plugin and type.

symbols.name: Attempt.#prepareTables
symbols.comment:
Brings the declared tables to their definitions before the references are bound (slice 6a §9): created fresh or
migrated eagerly, with the `readyTimeout` deadline paused meanwhile (resumed with the budget it had left).

symbols.name: Attempt.#declare
symbols.comment:
Runs the factory with declarations open; the member check establishes what it returned. A throwing factory
releases its pins.

symbols.name: Attempt.#assertPersistable
symbols.comment:
Persisted data needs a stable identity (P3: a `local` type with empty params, also checked by the types) and the
host's store; returns the store.

symbols.name: Attempt.#admit
symbols.signature: #admit(work: Work, running: Promise<unknown>, cleanup?: () => void): void
symbols.comment:
Adds `running` to `work` (its calls, routine calls or job invocations: the drain), with `cleanup` run once: when
it settles, or at teardown if it never does.

symbols.name: Attempt.#caller
symbols.comment: Whom this object's own work acts for: a remote object as its principal, a local one as the host; from this host.

symbols.name: Attempt.#inVariant
symbols.comment: ` (variant reader)` for a remote object, for errors.

symbols.name: pinned
symbols.signature: async function pinned(slot: KeyedSlot, key: string, context: Context): Promise<PinnedKey>
symbols.comment: Pins `key` on `slot` and loads it when it is not in memory; a failed load releases the pin.

packages/chord/src/host/attempt.ts.comment:
Attempts (§6, §13, §14, §15): one activation of an object, a fresh instance each time. It is the `self` its factory

declares with (handles to the object's documents and jobs, under its seal token); it runs the activation steps,

each failing with its own kind; it takes the live object's calls and starts its routines and jobs; and it ends with

its seal (slice 6a §1.3), the drain and the closes of its natives. A reload's restart drains it (decision "Reload

restarts every affected object; old work finishes on old code"): its routines stop, it serves old work under its

own contract, and it is sealed once that work settled.

symbols.name: FIRST_DELAY
symbols.comment:
Retry backoff per identity (§6): after a transient failure an identity waits 1 s, doubling up to 60 s. The entries

hold no object, so a failed object is collected after its last reference while its window still runs.

The delay after the first transient failure.

symbols.name: MAX_DELAY
symbols.comment: The longest delay.

symbols.name: nextDelay
symbols.signature: export function nextDelay(previous: number | undefined): number
symbols.comment:
The delay after a failure: 1 s after the first (no `previous` delay), then the previous one doubled, up to 60 s.
Identities, routines and job finishes back off alike.

symbols.name: Entry
symbols.signature: type Entry = { readonly delay: number; readonly until: number; timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined };
symbols.comment:
One identity's backoff: the delay of its last window, when that window ends (`Date.now()` time), and the timer ending
a window still running.
symbols.output: { readonly delay: number; readonly until: number; timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined }

symbols.name: Backoff
symbols.comment:
The host's backoff map. When a window ends, `due(identity)` runs: the host retries the identity's object, or
deletes the entry when there is none. An entry is deleted on success, on a broken failure, and when its window has
passed with nothing left to retry.

symbols.name: Backoff.failed
symbols.comment: Records a transient failure: a window of the previous delay doubled (1 s at first), then `due`.

symbols.name: Backoff.waiting
symbols.comment: Whether `identity` is inside a window: a new object for it waits for `due` before its first attempt.

symbols.name: Backoff.until
symbols.comment: When the window of `identity` ends, while one runs: a failed reference's `retryAt`.

symbols.name: Backoff.skip
symbols.comment: Ends the window at once (its object is retried now: `ref.retry()`, a wake); the delay stays for the next failure.

symbols.name: Backoff.ended
symbols.comment: Its object ended: an entry whose window has passed gets no outcome any more and goes.

symbols.name: Backoff.delete
symbols.comment: Forgets `identity` (success, a broken failure, or a window that passed with nothing to retry).

symbols.name: Backoff.clear
symbols.comment: Forgets every identity (the host closes).

packages/chord/src/host/backoff.ts.comment:
Retry backoff per identity (§6): after a transient failure an identity waits 1 s, doubling up to 60 s. The entries

hold no object, so a failed object is collected after its last reference while its window still runs.

symbols.name: FollowSource.#advance

The runtime ended its observer (R4); its attempt is told. `ended` is final: what came before reaches the watches

Followed sources (slice 6b D9, R4, §3): `self.follow(attach)`, a Chord source over a synchronous observer of another

runtime (Durable's `observeConversation`, `observeTaskGraph`, `observeDoc`). Attached during its attempt's

activation, detached at the attempt's end. Calls inside a running batch (Durable adopting in the store's commit step)

are marked in that batch, calls outside one are grouped into one batch on the next microtask, so a derive over two

views of one commit computes once with both changes.

symbols.name: principal
symbols.comment: Who this host acts as for its own requests; a host without one (a client) has none.

symbols.name: principalKey
symbols.comment: The key of a principal in identities; L1's canonical JSON by default. The same function on every host.

per span site.

Who a span was for (decision "Who a span was for"): the attributes its method and call spans record for a
principal, in place of the default `chord.principal` (its principal key, capped at 256 characters). Called for

symbols.name: onError

symbols.name: readyTimeout

symbols.name: reloadDrainTimeout

readiness) before it is sealed and anything still running is cut off (`released`); 5 s by default, at most

symbols.name: Host.load
symbols.signature:
load(facets: readonly PluginFacet

[], context: Context): Promise;
symbols.comment:
Runs every facet's setup and publishes what they declared in one batch (the types and registries served, the
registries composed once, the contributions); holds that waited for the publication are placed after that batch,
and a registry with contributions and no provider is reported (`registry_undeclared`). Then activates every
served type with empty params and resolves when each has had its first outcome (the start barrier, decision (a)):
live, failed by its own cause, parked with no blocker here still without its first outcome, or ended (failures go
to `onError`). A plugin whose setup throws or is refused at declaration (a name given twice, a type or registry
another plugin serves, a remote type here without principal or address, `checkAccepts`) is left out and reported
(`failed`); it never closes the host. A name that is no npm name throws before anything changes. Runs once.

symbols.name: Host.reload
symbols.signature:
reload(facets: readonly PluginFacet

[], context: Context, options?: ReloadOptions): Promise;
symbols.comment:
Reloads this host's plugins (slice 7b): `facets` is its complete new plugin set; a plugin in it and not loaded
is added, one loaded with another facet value is changed (the same facet object is unchanged: untouched), one
loaded and not in it is removed. Staging runs every new setup and every affected object's new factory against a
recording `self`, per plugin: a plugin whose new code fails there keeps its old code (an added one is left out),
and so does a changed plugin whose recorded requests would not bind because of it (the closure rule); both are
reported (`failed`); `options.failed` names plugins the caller passes as their loaded facet because their new
code failed before (a build, an evaluation): the same for the closure rule and the report. Then it commits in one
batch (types, registries, contributions; a publication waking the requests for the names it serves) and every
object of a changed or removed plugin takes its fate: restarted (its old attempt finishing old work first),
retried, or ended (its type removed). Resolves with the report once every fate started (retries checked their
dependencies; a restart reports what its readiness found at once; it does not wait for objects to go live).
Reloads run one after another. Throws before `load` resolved and for a name that is no npm name (before anything
changes); rejects `released/closed` after `close`; `context`'s abort before the commit rejects `aborted` and
changes nothing, after it only ends the wait (`aborted`, its `details.committed` naming what the commit applied:
`CommittedReload`).

symbols.name: Host.get
symbols.signature: get<C extends Contract>(Type: C, params: ParamsOf<C>, context: Context, options?: GetOptions): Promise<Reference<C>>;
symbols.comment:
A reference once its object is live (and hydrated). It acts as the host's principal and goes where its type's host
address puts it: here, over a route, or over the parent link (`Destination`). It waits while the reference is
`loading`, `failed { transient }` or `failed { waiting }` until its `readyTimeout`, then rejects with the last
cause and releases the reference; a broken failure rejects at once, and so does a get before `load` (`not_ready`).

symbols.name: Host.hold
symbols.signature: hold<C extends Contract>(Type: C, params: ParamsOf<C>, context: Context, options?: GetOptions): Held<C>;
symbols.comment:
A reference at once, following its object until released: loading, live, failed (retried as its object is) and
loading again while its link is down; it never rejects. Throws at once only for invalid params and before `load`
(`not_ready`). A type not served where it goes is `failed { waiting }` (bound when a publication serves it;
reported `unbound_long` after 5 s); a `hostAddress` or route that refuses fails it broken. Its `variant` is
`undefined` until its first binding.

accept(link: Link, options: LinkOptions

, context: Context): void;

A link from a child: this host serves its remote types over it, every hold and call arriving on it acting as
`principal`. `context` is the parent of the work arriving on it (its cancellation is dropped).

symbols.name: Host.connect

connect(link: Link, options: LinkOptions

, context: Context): void;

This host's parent link: remote types not served here and not routed are held over it, every such reference held
again on a new one; holds arriving on it may name whom they act for. Throws while the previous one is open; once
it closed (a drop), `connect` takes the next. `principal` is who the parent is.

symbols.name: Host.route
symbols.comment:
How this host reaches hosts of `Kind` (called before `load`, once per kind): `authorize` admits every hold routed
over it, `resolve` makes the link of an address, for a new hold, on `retry`, or once after a link that completed
its handshake dropped while held (no timer). A rejected `resolve`, or a link closed before its handshake, fails the
address's holders `failed { waiting }` (they stay on its path). `context` is the parent of the route's work (its
`resolve`s, the holds and calls on its links), aborted for it when this host closes. Returns the address controls.

symbols.name: Host.revoke
symbols.comment:
Revokes `revocation` (§4, R10, R11), synchronously: every remote object whose principal it revokes (`revokedBy`)
ends at once, whatever references remain (holders get `forbidden`, running calls are aborted, an activation is
abandoned); every child link whose principal it revokes closes (never the parent, never this host's own
principal); and every route link is sent `revoke`, which the host there applies with its own `revokedBy`. Nothing
is replayed to links made later.

principal it acts as (remote types) and its origin, the incarnation of the host it was made for (two tabs are two
origins). Changes in the batch where a reference binds or ends; a link drop is a departure.

symbols.name: Host.activity

calls running, running jobs and lingering objects; published at most once per microtask turn with changes.

has no value (`unavailable/undeclared` without a provider, a first `compose` that threw, a version not served

`not_ready` at once.

root(fn: (ctx: Ctx

) => Promise, context: Context, options?: RootOptions

Runs `fn` with a call context for code outside objects (a Durable tool, a CLI): the host's principal (or
`options.principal`; an explicit `undefined` runs anonymous), this host's incarnation, `context`'s telemetry and signal, `ctx.get`. When `fn` settles or

symbols.name: ChordHost.#stageReload
symbols.signature:
#stageReload(facets: readonly PluginFacet

[], before: readonly PluginFailure[], context: Context): ReloadPlan
symbols.comment:
Staging (slice 7b §2), synchronous (no request or arriving hold meets it half done), per plugin (decision "Per
plugin at startup and reload"): a pass stages the new code (`#stagePass`); a plugin whose new code fails there
(or failed `before`, passed as its loaded facet) keeps its old code (an added one is left out) and staging runs
again without it; then a changed plugin whose recorded requests would not bind because of such a plugin keeps its
old code too (`#closure`), until nothing more fails. Bounded by the number of plugins with new code.

symbols.name: ChordHost.#stagePass
symbols.signature: #stagePass( given: ReadonlyMap>, failed: ReadonlyMap, context: Context, ): StagingPass
symbols.comment:
One staging pass: the loaded entries of the plugins kept as they are (unchanged, or failed: their setups not run
again) first, then every other plugin's new code in the given order (one refused by a name the table has already
fails), then the new factory of every object of a changed or removed plugin whose type is still served (a throw
fails the plugin serving it). Its plan, or the plugins that failed.

symbols.name: ChordHost.#closure
symbols.signature:
#closure( plan: ReloadPlan

, recorded: readonly RecordedFactory[], failed: ReadonlyMap, ): Map
symbols.comment:
The closure rule: the changed plugins (new code applied) of `plan` with a recorded request that would not bind in
the staged table because of a plugin that failed in this reload: its name served there by such a plugin's old code,
or not served at all while some plugin failed (what a failed setup would have served is unknown). Requests to
another host are not checked (a rollout's rules). Each such plugin with the error it keeps its old code for.

symbols.name: ChordHost.#unboundRequest
symbols.signature: #unboundRequest(staged: Staged, request: Request, failed: ReadonlyMap<string, unknown>): string | undefined
symbols.comment:
Why `request` (of a new factory) would not bind in `staged` because of a plugin in `failed`; `undefined`
when it binds, is placed on another host, or does not bind for another reason (it waits as any request does).

symbols.name: ChordHost.#commit
symbols.comment:
The commit (slice 7b §3), one batch: the served types become the staged ones (an unchanged plugin's stay as
they were), the removed plugins' registry providers go and the reloaded ones' are replaced, their facet
contributions replaced by plugin, every changed registry composed once; a removed type's presence list goes.
Then each object takes its fate (`#startFates`), host-lifetime objects of new types start, and the publication
wakes the requests waiting for the names the reload serves.

symbols.name: ChordHost.#startFates
symbols.comment:
Starts `fates` and returns them in their order, for the report: the removals first (a dependent whose new code
still needs a removed provider then parks, decision 4), then the restarts and retries; then the restarts'
readiness and successors, once every object has its new served type (their requests bind against the new code).

symbols.name: ChordHost.#startFate
symbols.comment:
Starts one object's fate after the commit: a removed type's object ends, its holders waiting `not_served`; any
other restarts or retries on its new served type.

async #report(
		started: readonly StartedFate[],
		committed: CommittedReload,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<ReloadedObject[]>
symbols.comment:
The report, once every retry had its first dependency check (a parked one reports why); a restart reports at once
what its readiness found (its successor's own check follows the old attempt's end). `context`'s abort ends only
this wait (`aborted`, its `details` naming what the commit applied: `committed`).

symbols.name: ChordHost.#checked
symbols.comment:
Why a restarted or retried object's new attempt waits, for the report: what a restart's readiness found, at once
(its new attempt's own check follows the old attempt's end), also for a retry of an attempt that still waits for
an open old attempt; otherwise its new attempt's first dependency check.

Hosts (§3): `createHost`, loading facets and the start barrier, links to children, the parent (connected again after

a drop) and routes, the origins it relays holds for, getting and holding references as a principal, the heartbeat

(staging, the commit, each object's fate, the report; old work and its reload cycles), closing; one batch per host,

the backoff map and the endings new instances wait for.

Hosts for apps: creating a host, facets, factories, natives, references and the ctx of method handlers, routines and

Hosts for Chord's layers: what the remote sides of links use of a host, its objects and references (and old work

symbols.comment:
Resolves every derive's sources; errors name a derive by the member exposing it, else by its position. `report`
makes each derive's failure report, with the member exposing it when there is one (`derive_failed`).

symbols.comment:
A contribution of `contributor` at `version` to `record`, as Chord follows it: a Chord watchable (a source, a
constant, a document handle, a reference member, a native source: another registry's value too) is followed,
anything else is a plain value, whatever methods it has (registries carry natives).

symbols.name: contentOf
symbols.comment: What Chord follows behind a contribution: its JSON or native source when it is a Chord watchable.

packages/chord/src/host/members.ts.comment:
The member check (Q14): an implementation is one variant with exactly that variant's members, methods being

functions and state members JSON watchables; and the resolution of what Chord follows behind every derive's declared

sources (JSON and native) and every contribution to a registry (slice 8).



The rule for watches across attempts (decision "References are the only indirection"): consumers' watches and

derives over another object's member follow it through their reference's member (`reference-source.ts`) and keys

(`reference-keys.ts`), passed straight through to the instance's own document or derive. While the object points at

nothing they keep their last values (one `failed` call for a failure); when a new instance goes live they move by

name to its member (a key pinned there again), whether a document or a derive: one frame from the last value, and

every derive downstream recovers (decision "self healing"). A re-exposed member is the re-exposing object's

reference member: it holds with that object, its provider's source goes on. Holds over a link follow the live

instance's members and take a snapshot at each binding.

symbols.comment: Why a native closes: its object ended or its attempt failed (`end`), the host closes (`close`), a reload (slice 7).
symbols.output: { readonly kind: "end" } | { readonly kind: "close" } | { readonly kind: "reload" }

symbols.comment: The opened value: throws `not_ready` until its open resolved and `released` once its close started.

symbols.name: NativeOptions

symbols.name: Served
symbols.comment:
A type served on a host, by kind: its contract, factory (a remote one gets the object's principal) and argument
checks. Factories are plugin code: what they return is checked at activation.

symbols.name: factory
symbols.signature: readonly factory: (params: ParamsOf<Contract>, self: Self) => unknown;

symbols.name: hostLifetime

symbols.name: ServedType
plugin
symbols.comment: The plugin whose facet served it: its objects contribute to registries by it.

symbols.name: linger
symbols.comment: How long a live object stays live after its last reference, in milliseconds (`serve`'s `linger`, 0 by default).

symbols.name: traced
symbols.comment: Whether its calls start method spans (`serve`'s `untraced`: not).

symbols.name: Holder
symbols.comment: What holds an object: a reference's binding, or a hold arriving over a link.

symbols.name: Holder.dependent
symbols.comment: The object whose attempt declared the reference: it checks its dependencies again when this object changes.

symbols.name: Holder.caller
symbols.comment: Whom the reference acts for, with its origin's incarnation (`host.references`).

symbols.name: Holder.contract
symbols.signature: readonly contract: { readonly version: number; readonly fingerprint: string };
symbols.comment: The consumer's contract version and fingerprint (its request's): the provider binds it or it waits unbound.
symbols.output: { readonly version: number; readonly fingerprint: string }

symbols.name: Holder.listed
symbols.comment: Whether presence lists show it (§19): not a restart's readiness binding, which is no consumer of its own.

symbols.name: Holder.retarget
symbols.comment:
Inside a batch, before `moved`: what it follows of the object changed (`ChordObject.followed`): a reference moves its
members' subscriptions to the new instance, or keeps their last values; a hold over a link has nothing to do here.

symbols.name: Holder.following
symbols.comment: Whether `retarget` moves anything (a reference whose members or keys were used): it then runs in a batch.

symbols.name: Holder.moved
symbols.comment: The object's state (`state`) changed: an attempt started after a failure, it went live, or it failed.

symbols.name: Holder.end
symbols.comment: The object ended with `error`.

symbols.name: Holder.removed
symbols.comment:
The object ended because a reload removed its type (slice 7b §6): the holder's request is not ended; it waits
unbound with `removal.cause` (`not_served`) until a publication serves the name again.

symbols.name: Removal
symbols.comment:
What an object tells holders it leaves: why they wait (`not_served` after a removal, `contract_mismatch` after a
version refusal), its params (they place their requests again) and its context. A reference keeps its last values
meanwhile and moves its subscriptions to the next object of the identity that serves its version (one frame).

symbols.name: ReloadFate
symbols.comment: What a reload does to an object whose type is still served: a live one restarts, any other is retried.

symbols.name: ObjectState
symbols.comment:
Where an object stands. `waiting`: for its identity's backoff window before its first attempt. `activating` has what
its references show: `loading`, or `failed { waiting }` while its attempt is parked on a failed dependency. `failed`
has the state its references show.

symbols.name: Teardown
symbols.comment:
What an ended object still has to do once its previous teardowns finished (`previous`): drain and close its attempt;
then drop its documents and job runs (`end` alone).

symbols.name: Ending
symbols.comment: How an object ends: by an end (its last reference, revocation, the host closing) or by its type's removal.
symbols.output:
| { readonly kind: "end"; readonly error: ChordError }
	| { readonly kind: "removed"; readonly error: ChordError; readonly cause: FailureCause }

symbols.name: NO_DEPENDENCIES
symbols.comment: No dependencies waited for: the shared empty list.

symbols.name: NO_CONTRIBUTIONS
symbols.comment: No contributions leaving: the shared empty list.

symbols.name: ChordObject
symbols.comment:
One object. Each attempt is a fresh `Attempt`; the documents, the line, the job runs and the holders outlive it. An
attempt parked on its dependencies waits for them without a timer; a transient failure (its own) is retried after its
backoff window, or at once when a reference asks (`retry`); a broken one stays failed until a reference asks.
The object ends with its last reference, a live one after its type's `linger` (never, for a host-lifetime object),
or when the host closes.

symbols.name: ChordObject.kind
symbols.comment: An object on this host (a reference's target that is not held over a link).

symbols.name: ChordObject.served
symbols.comment: Its served type: replaced by a reload that restarts or retries it.

symbols.name: ChordObject.key
symbols.comment: Its params' identity key (empty for empty params).

symbols.name: ChordObject.principal
symbols.comment: The principal in a remote object's identity, which its factory gets; `undefined` for a local object.

symbols.name: ChordObject.label
symbols.comment: The object in errors, reports and cycles: its type, and its params key when it has params.

symbols.name: ChordObject.chain
symbols.comment:
The activation chain it was created for (Q5): the instance ids of the activations waiting for it, from the hold
that created it (a trusted link's) or the activation here that declared it; empty otherwise.

symbols.name: ChordObject.documents
symbols.comment: Its documents and line, across its attempts.

symbols.name: ChordObject.#context
symbols.comment: The context of every attempt: its creator's, without the creator's cancellation.

symbols.name: ChordObject.#trigger
symbols.comment:
What its next attempt's activation span links to: its first trigger (the span that created it, a hold's carrier),
then the last attempt's span (a retry's trigger).

symbols.name: ChordObject.#attempts
symbols.comment: Its attempts so far (the activation span's `attempt`).

symbols.name: ChordObject.#jobs
symbols.comment: Its job runs by job name, across its attempts.

symbols.name: ChordObject.#instance
symbols.comment: This instance's id (uuidv7), minted at its first attempt: a restarted object is a new instance (D4).

symbols.name: ChordObject.#holders
symbols.comment: References and holds of this object.

symbols.name: ChordObject.#waitingFor
symbols.comment: The dependencies its parked attempt waits for; their objects are followed to find cycles (Q5).

symbols.name: ChordObject.#firstOutcome
symbols.comment:
Its first outcome (decision (a)): live, failed, parked with no blocker here still without one, or ended; once.
The promise is made by the first who waits for it (the start barrier, for host-lifetime objects).

symbols.name: ChordObject.#lastFailure
symbols.comment: The error of the last failed attempt, or the last cause a parked attempt showed, until one goes live.

symbols.name: ChordObject.#lingering
symbols.comment: Ends the object when its type's `linger` passed after its last reference; cleared by a new one.

symbols.name: ChordObject.#runs
symbols.comment: Its running and finishing job runs: they keep it alive like references (D4), without being references.

symbols.name: ChordObject.#exposed
ChordObject.#following
symbols.comment:
Whether references still follow `#exposed`, which may still change: while it is live, while a restart keeps it
open for old work, or failed live until the commits admitted before it published (every member, its own and
re-exposed ones: audit A10); not once it stopped changing.

symbols.name: ChordObject.#flush
symbols.signature: #flush: { readonly deadline: number; readonly timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> } | undefined;
symbols.comment: The one timer storing its jobs' held state changes by their earliest deadline (D8), while one is held.
symbols.output: { readonly deadline: number; readonly timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> } | undefined

symbols.name: ChordObject.#wakes
symbols.comment: Its wake signals (`retryOn`), the last attempt's declaration; made by the first.

symbols.name: ChordObject.#old
symbols.comment:
A restart's old attempt while it is open (until it stopped changing): old work runs on it, and consumers whose
version it binds see it live (decision "Reload restarts every affected object", rules 2 and 5).

symbols.name: ChordObject.#kept
symbols.comment:
A restart's old attempt without natives whose contributions stay in the tables until its successor is live (F-c),
replaced there in one batch; they leave if the successor fails, parks on a failure or the object ends.

symbols.name: ChordObject.#readiness
symbols.comment: A restart's readiness, until its successor's first dependency check.

symbols.name: ChordObject.#showsReadiness
symbols.comment: A restart's successor that shows its readiness's failures, until the old attempt ended.

symbols.name: ChordObject.#startSuccessor
symbols.comment: Starts a restart's readiness and successor, once every fate of its reload started (`startSuccessor`).

symbols.name: ChordObject.#gateWaits
symbols.comment: The objects whose gate its activation's opener waits at now: its wait edges for reload cycles.

symbols.name: ChordObject.#liveQueries
symbols.comment: Its live queries by table, across its attempts; made by the first table it declares.

symbols.name: ChordObject.#changed
symbols.comment: Resolves at its next change of state, for calls waiting at the gate; made by the first one.
