symbols.name: RoutineDeclarations
symbols.signature:
export interface RoutineDeclarations

{
symbols.comment: What the declarations of an owner (`on`, `onLive`) take; part of the factory's `self` and the facet's.

symbols.name: RoutineDeclarations.on
symbols.signature: on(source: Watchable, fn: OnHandler>): void;
symbols.comment:
A routine over `source`: `fn` gets its current value first (ops `[["r", value]]`), then one call per change,
never overlapping: changes during a call fold into one next call (the newest value, the ops since the previous
call, `retired` when any of them was a retirement). After a call that threw, it is called again with the whole
newest value (`retired` again if the call that threw had it) after a backoff (1 s doubling to 60 s), or at once on
a change during the backoff. Ends with its source. A JSON watchable is one whose watch is Chord's shared `Watch`
(every Chord and Durable source).

symbols.name: RoutineDeclarations.on
symbols.signature: on(source: NativeWatchable, fn: OnNativeHandler>): void;
symbols.comment:
A routine over a native source (a registry value, `ref.state`): one whose watch is Chord's shared `NativeWatch`.
As above without ops: after a busy call, one call with the newest value.

symbols.name: RoutineDeclarations.onLive
symbols.comment:
A routine called once its owner is live. Returning ends it; a throw is reported and restarts it after a backoff
(1 s doubling to 60 s, reset after a run of a minute); the owner's end aborts its ctx.

symbols.comment: A declared routine: its kind and position in reports (`{ kind: "on", position: 2 }`), its source and its handler.

symbols.name: RoutinePosition

symbols.name: LONG_RUN

symbols.name: Routines.start
symbols.comment:
Starts every routine for `owner`, which went live; they stop when its context is aborted. A routine whose
synchronous start ends the owner (an `onLive` releasing its last reference) starts none of the later ones.

symbols.signature: async function live(owner: RoutineOwner, { at, fn }: Extract<Declaration, { kind: "onLive" }>): Promise<void>
symbols.comment:
Runs `onLive`'s handler until it returns or its owner ends; a throw is reported and the handler restarts after the
backoff.

symbols.name: call
symbols.comment:
Runs one routine call under its own ctx (its `ctx.get` references released when it settles) in its `chord.routine`
root span, linked to `trigger` (the span of the commit that changed its source, when known), admitted to the owner's
drain before the handler runs: a handler may end its own owner before its first await. Resolves with how it ended and
its span, still open (`callEnded`); never rejects.

symbols.name: callEnded
symbols.signature: function callEnded({ called, span }: CallEnd, owner: RoutineOwner, backoff: number | undefined): void
symbols.comment:
A routine call's span ends: `ok`, `aborted` (a cancel), or `error` with `routine_failed` and, when its routine calls
again after a backoff, a `chord.retry` event with that delay.

symbols.name: failed
symbols.signature: function failed(owner: RoutineOwner, routine: Position, error: unknown): void
symbols.comment: Reports a failed routine call or source.

symbols.name: OnState
symbols.comment:
Where an `on` routine stands. `starting`: taking its watch; `idle`: waiting for a change; `calling`: a call runs
(changes meanwhile wait, folded, for the next); `settling`: a call succeeded while changes arrived, and the next one
waits for one macrotask, so every value its watch still buffers (a native watch replays them one per microtask) is
taken first; `backoff`: the last call threw and its timer calls again, unless a change during the backoff calls
first; `ended`: its watch ended (the owner ended, or the source ended or failed).
symbols.output:
| { readonly kind: "starting" | "idle" | "calling" | "ended" }
	| { readonly kind: "settling" | "backoff"; readonly timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> }

symbols.name: Basis
symbols.comment:
What the next call's ops are relative to: `none` before the first call and after a throw (the handler may not have
applied what it got: the next call gets the whole value), `last` after a call that succeeded.

symbols.name: OnRoutine
symbols.comment:
One `on` routine. Its watch's listener never throws (a throwing listener would end the watch) and never waits: it
keeps the newest frame, folding JSON ops, and the routine makes one call at a time from it, the first call and the
retries after a throw through the same pending frame.

symbols.name: OnRoutine.#native
symbols.comment: A native source's watch yields values without ops; decided by its watch's class.

symbols.name: OnRoutine.#pending
symbols.comment: The newest value no call got yet.

symbols.name: OnRoutine.#ops
symbols.comment: The ops of the frames since the last call (JSON sources), folded.

symbols.name: OnRoutine.#retired
symbols.comment: One of the frames since the last call was a retirement (JSON sources).

symbols.name: OnRoutine.#last
symbols.comment: The value of the last call: a retry after a throw calls with it.

symbols.name: OnRoutine.#lastRetired
symbols.comment: The last call reported a retirement: a retry after a throw reports it again.

symbols.name: OnRoutine.#failed
symbols.comment: The source failed after its last value: no call until its next value (a retry waits too).

symbols.name: OnRoutine.#trigger
symbols.comment: The span of the commit that made the newest frame (a frame's context), linked from the next call's span.

symbols.name: OnRoutine.start
symbols.comment:
Takes the watch and calls with its value. On a failed Chord source it waits for its first good value instead (a
source that never had one is followed until it has). A source that cannot be watched otherwise is reported; an
owner or source that ended meanwhile ends the routine. Never rejects.

symbols.name: OnRoutine.#failing
symbols.signature: #failing(): { readonly kind: "failed" } | { readonly kind: "no_value"; readonly source: Source } | undefined
symbols.comment:
Whether the source is a Chord source failed now (`failed`), or a JSON one with no value yet (`no_value`, with the
source to follow); `undefined` otherwise (Durable's views tell their failures through their watches).
symbols.output: { readonly kind: "failed" } | { readonly kind: "no_value"; readonly source: Source } | undefined

symbols.name: OnRoutine.#firstValue
symbols.comment:
Follows `source`, failed with no value, until its first good value (`true`), or until it or the owner ends
(`false`): a subscriber of its own, since a watch has nothing to start at.

symbols.name: OnRoutine.#failure
symbols.comment:
The source failed: what was pending goes (a value a failure followed is stale), a pending retry or settle is
dropped, and the next call waits for the next value, as a whole value; a running call runs on.

symbols.name: OnRoutine.#frame
symbols.comment:
A frame of the watch: kept as the newest; it is called at once when nothing runs or waits, during a backoff too
(the backoff ends); while a call runs or settles it waits for the next call.

symbols.name: OnRoutine.#next
symbols.comment: Makes the next call from the pending frame, if there is one and the owner still runs; otherwise idles.

symbols.name: OnRoutine.#invocation
symbols.comment:
The handler's call with `value`: a native one with the value alone, a JSON one with the folded ops or the whole
value, and whether a retirement came since the last call.

symbols.name: OnRoutine.#called
symbols.comment:
A call settled. After a success the next frame's ops build on it, and changes that arrived during the call are
called after one macrotask (`settling`). After a throw (reported) the backoff always starts, also when changes
arrived during the call (a handler that changes its own source and throws would feed itself otherwise); its timer
calls with the newest value, or the last call's, as a whole value.

symbols.name: OnRoutine.#end
symbols.comment: The watch ended: the owner ended (aborted), or the source ended (no report) or failed (reported once).

packages/chord/src/host/routines.ts.comment:
Routines (§14): the standing behaviour an object or a facet declares, `self.on(source, fn)` and `self.onLive(fn)`.

They start once their owner went live and stop when it ends (their ctx aborted, the drain waits for running calls);

each call gets its own ctx and its own `chord.routine` root span; a call that throws is reported and called again

after a backoff.

symbols.signature: export function sleep(ms: number, context: Context): Promise<void>
symbols.comment:
Resolves after `ms` milliseconds; rejects with the abort reason once `context` is aborted, clearing its timer and
listener. Delays above the timer limit (2^31-1 ms) are chained timers.

symbols.name: untilAborted
symbols.comment: Resolves once `context` is aborted (never without an abort signal); leaves no listener behind.

packages/chord/src/host/sleep.ts.comment:
Waiting helpers for routines, jobs and handlers (§14): `sleep(ms, ctx)` and `untilAborted(ctx)`, which end with

their context, leaving no timer or listener behind. Portable: timers and `AbortSignal` only.

packages/chord/src/host/staging.ts.comment:
Staging (slice 7b §2; per plugin, decision "Per plugin at startup and reload"): each plugin's setup runs into a table of

its own (the types it serves with their providers, the registries it serves, its facet contributions) with `load`'s

checks, merged into the staged table beside the live one, where a type or registry another plugin serves already

fails the plugin; and an object's new factory run against a recording `self`, which keeps what the factory declares

(documents, tables, jobs, contributions, requests with their contract versions) and activates, binds and opens

nothing, so a reload decides which plugins keep their old code before its commit, and a restart knows the requests

its successor will make (its readiness).

`load` stages its facets the same way and publishes them.

The `unbound_long` report (decision "Mistakes that wait are reported at once" (c)): a request waiting unbound after

the host's publication (a type or registry not served here, not at its version, a registry whose first `compose`

threw) is reported once through `onError` after 5 s, naming what it waits for and why; it keeps waiting as before.

One clock per host, one timer armed for the earliest wait not reported yet: no timer per request.

packages/chord/src/host/unbound.ts.comment:
The unbound index (dependency model §1, §4): the requests a host decided cannot bind yet, by the name they wait for.

Before the host's first publication every hold arriving on its links, and a request made here while `load` runs the

setups (before `load` this host's own requests throw), waits here (`unpublished`); after it, those its check left

unbound (`not_served`, `version`): a reference made here, a hold that arrived over a link and was refused for a name.

A publication wakes the requests of the names it serves (`load`'s every one, a reload's those of its names); a

request leaves when it ends (released, settled, given up, its link or origin closed, revoked) or binds. A request

waiting with a cause (after the publication) is on the host's `UnboundClock` while it is indexed: reported after 5 s.

symbols.name: JobRecords.#runStates
symbols.comment: The run state documents of `state`, reporting their changes to `running` and their held deadlines.

symbols.name: JobRecords.check
symbols.comment:
Refuses a declaration of this job that its records cannot take (slice 7b §8): the same version with another
fingerprint (its args, result or state schema changed without a version bump), or a state document definition
the run documents refuse (`SlotDefinition.check`). A reload's staging checks it too.

symbols.name: JobRecords.redefine
symbols.comment:
Takes a new attempt's declaration `definition` (another version after a reload, `ChordObject.checkJob` refused
the same version with another fingerprint): new runs are of its version; the runs of others keep theirs, their
`running` entries show their args mapped forwards (or blocked); their state documents keep their version until
their run settles or moves to the new code.

symbols.name: JobRecords.undeclare
symbols.comment:
The latest live attempt does not declare the job (slice 7b §8): its runs not invoked and its finishing runs are
blocked `version` (kept, not invoked) until a reload declares it again or they are aborted; a running
invocation finishes and is blocked then.

symbols.name: JobRecords.retryBlocked
symbols.comment:
A reload brought new code (its attempt is live): blocked runs are retried, once: a `finish_failed` one finishes
again, a `version` one whose version the code now takes (its own, or an older one with an adapter) is invoked or
finished; the others stay blocked. A persisted run blocked at its load has its state document read first.

symbols.name: JobRecords.#readBlockedState
symbols.comment: Reads and decodes the state document of a persisted run blocked at its load, now that the code takes it.

symbols.name: JobRecords.#takes
symbols.comment:
Whether the current code takes `run`: of its version and fingerprint, or of an older version its `accepts` maps
forwards; a newer one (a rollback) or an older one without an adapter is not (`blocked { version }`).

symbols.name: JobRecords.argsOf
symbols.signature: argsOf(run: JobRun, definition: JobDefinition<unknown, unknown, unknown>): JsonValue
symbols.comment:
`run`'s args as the code of `definition` takes them (the current code's, or an invoking attempt's own): mapped
forwards once per run and version when older.

symbols.name: JobRecords.outcomeOf
symbols.comment:
`run`'s outcome as the current code's `finish` gets it: an older run's args and result mapped forwards (once per
run), its state document migrated to the current state definition.

symbols.name: JobRecords.name
symbols.comment: The job in errors: its object and its name.

symbols.name: JobRecords.outcome
symbols.comment: Waits for the outcome of the unsettled run `id`; a settled or unknown id rejects `gone`.

symbols.name: JobRecords.abort
symbols.signature: async abort(id: string, context: Context): Promise<"marked" | "terminal">
symbols.comment:
Aborts run `id` (D7, Durable's `abortTask`): a blocked run is dropped; a finishing one is only marked; any other
is marked (stored for a persisted job) in a transaction, its signal fired after the commit, outside the batch and
the line, and the abort joins its invocation. `"marked"`, or `"terminal"` when no unsettled run has that id.

symbols.name: JobRecords.stage
symbols.signature: stage(tx: Transaction, args: unknown, context: Context, options: StartOptions): Run<AnyOutcome>
symbols.comment: See `Job.stage`: the checks and the staged creation, against the object's runs.

symbols.name: JobRecords.change
symbols.comment:
Stages `change` in `tx`: in the job's staging, adopted in the commit step, and for a persisted job the run's record
written with it (rule 8: serialized now), and for a settled run its state document retired.

symbols.name: JobRecords.staging
symbols.comment: This job's changes in `tx`, made on the first.

symbols.name: JobRecords.load
symbols.comment:
A persisted job's runs, loaded once per object at its first activation (slice 6b §4.2), again only after a load
failed (design §9): each record read; a record of another version or fingerprint blocked (`version`) as stored,
its state document left undecoded; the others' state documents read and decoded, a run cut off while `running`
counted (`restarts + 1`; at the limit it ends `restart_limit`, reported `job_interrupted`), `stopped` and
`pending` ones made `pending` again. The runs and their activation changes are adopted in one commit, all before
anything runs; a failure leaves nothing loaded.

symbols.name: JobRecords.#restoreAll
symbols.comment: Stages the loaded runs in `tx`: each restored, then the activation changes (adopted after every restore).

symbols.name: JobRecords.attach
symbols.comment: `job`, of the attempt that went live, invokes and finishes the runs from now on; the waiting ones first.

symbols.name: JobRecords.detach
symbols.comment:
`job`'s attempt was sealed: its running invocations are cut off (`cut`), the runs it was finishing wait for the
next live attempt.

symbols.name: JobRecords.requeue
symbols.comment:
A run whose reservation its sealed attempt never committed waits for the next live attempt (dispatched now when one
is attached already: the sealed attempt was detached at its seal).

symbols.name: JobRecords.reserve
symbols.comment: Records `run` running before its `run` is invoked (a persisted run's reservation: a crash after it counts).

symbols.name: JobRecords.progressed
symbols.comment: A state change of a run with restarts counted resets them in its commit (progress, D6).

symbols.name: JobRecords.settled
symbols.comment:
A run's invocation settled: its outcome is recorded (phase `finishing`) in a transaction of the object behind the
state changes admitted before, so `outcome.state` has them; then it is finished on the live attempt.

symbols.name: JobRecords.cut
symbols.signature: cut(run: JobRun, error: ChordError, reason: CutReason): void
symbols.comment:
A running run whose attempt was sealed: its signal fires with `error`, its invocation is fenced (later state
changes refused, the open one discarded, its settling ignored). In memory it ends `failed { aborted }` with
`reason` (`reload` for a native restart, slice 7b §8), finished on the next live attempt; persisted it is stopped (R3), written back by the close writer and
resumed by the next live attempt as after a clean close.

symbols.name: JobRecords.record
symbols.signature: async record(run: JobRun, change: RecordChange): Promise<void>
symbols.comment:
Records `change` (a run's finish failure, its block, its drop) in a transaction of the object, if `run` is still
one of its runs there. The object's end ends it.

symbols.name: JobRecords.writeAtClose
symbols.comment:
The close writer (slice 6b §4.2, Durable's `writeAtClose`): one commit past the seal writing the runs a clean stop
cut off `stopped` and every held state change, straight to the store (the object's transactions are refused by
now). Its failure is the store's; the records stay as they were (a crash counts them).

symbols.name: JobRecords.flushHeld
symbols.comment: Stores every held state change whose deadline passed (`now`), in one transaction of the object (D8).

symbols.name: JobRecords.nextDeadline
symbols.comment: The earliest deadline of a held state change (`Infinity`: none).

symbols.name: JobRecords.stateOf
symbols.comment: The value of run `id`'s state document, `undefined` without one or once retired.

symbols.name: JobRecords.states
symbols.comment: The run state documents, for `ctx.state.change`; `undefined` without a state definition.

symbols.name: JobRecords.persisted
symbols.comment: Whether the job persists its runs.

symbols.name: JobRecords.end
symbols.comment:
The object ends: running runs' signals fire, every waiter rejects with `error`; blocked in-memory runs are
dropped (reported), persisted ones keep their records; nothing finishes. The records stay readable until `drop`.

symbols.name: JobRecords.drop
symbols.comment: Its object's documents are dropped: the runs, their state documents and `running`'s watches go.

symbols.name: JobRecords.report
symbols.comment: Reports a run's failure, drop or interruption to the host.

symbols.name: JobRecords.#store
symbols.comment: The store writes of `tx` (Chord's own documents of a persisted job).

symbols.name: JobRecords.#restored
symbols.comment:
The run a loaded record stands for and the change its activation writes (D6): a record of another version or
fingerprint blocked as stored (its state document only found, never decoded: slice 7 maps it); otherwise its state
document read and decoded (migrated), pinned while it is unsettled, a crash counted, at the limit its outcome,
marked resuming unless blocked or finishing.

symbols.name: JobRecords.#recordOutcome
symbols.comment: Records the outcome of `run` (with what its state holds, D8), then has it finished on the live attempt.

symbols.name: JobRecords.#outcome
symbols.comment: `run`'s outcome for `ended`, with its args and its state as it is now.

symbols.name: JobRecords.#need
symbols.comment: `run` needs a live attempt (to be invoked or finished): now, or once one attaches.

symbols.name: JobRecords.#dispatch
symbols.comment:
Invokes or finishes `run` on `job`, as its record stands: a finishing run is finished; a run not invoked yet is
invoked, unless it is marked aborted (it ends `aborted` without `run`) or resumes abandoned (`failed { aborted,
reason: "restart" }`).

symbols.name: JobRecords.#adopt
symbols.comment:
Adopts one record change, inside the commit step: the maps, the active count, `running`. A new run is counted for
its object here, before the commit's publication (a link closing while it sends may release the object's last
reference) and before any run of the same commit settles in `#committed`.

symbols.name: JobRecords.#committed
symbols.comment: The actions after a record change committed.

symbols.name: JobRecords.#stateChanged
symbols.comment: A run's state document changed by `ops`, inside the commit step: its entry is replaced.

symbols.name: JobRecords.#replaceEntry
symbols.comment: A run's record changed, inside the commit step: its entry is replaced.

symbols.name: JobRecords.#entryOf
symbols.comment:
`run`'s `running` entry: blocked, or with its state and its args as the current code takes them (an older run's
mapped; one the code does not take, or whose mapping throws, shows its own).

symbols.name: runAll
symbols.comment: Runs every adoption of `adopts`.

symbols.name: recordFields
symbols.comment: The record fields a change writes, its phase transitions included.

packages/chord/src/jobs/records.ts.comment:
A job's records on its object (§15, slice 6a §1.2, slice 6b §4): its runs by id and by key, the active count, the

run state documents, `running` and the runs waiting for a live attempt, across the object's attempts. Records and

state documents change only in transactions on the object's line (staged changes adopted in the commit step); a

persisted job's also in its object's store, in the same commits, loaded once per object, and written back stopped by

the close writer when a clean stop cuts its runs off. Across a reload (slice 7b §8) the records take the new

declaration's definition and every run keeps its version: an older one is mapped forwards through `accepts`, one

without an adapter (or newer, or of a job the code no longer declares) is blocked `version` until a reload brings

matching code.

symbols.name: HeldState
symbols.signature: type HeldState = { readonly pending: PendingOps; base: boolean; deadline: number };
symbols.comment:
A held state's ops, folded as they come (`PendingOps`: repeated writes of one leaf keep one op; past its bound only
"store a base" stays), whether a held change asked for a base, and when it must be stored at the latest.
symbols.output: { readonly pending: PendingOps; base: boolean; deadline: number }

symbols.name: RunStatesOwner
symbols.comment: What the run states tell their job: a document changed (`running` follows), a held change's deadline.

symbols.name: changed
symbols.signature: changed(id: string, ops: readonly Op[]): void;
symbols.comment: Run `id`'s document changed by `ops`, inside the commit step.

symbols.name: held
symbols.comment: A held change must be stored by `deadline` (`Date.now()` time).

symbols.name: DEFAULT_WITHIN_MS
symbols.comment: How long a deferred change is held at most by default (Durable's `progress.persistWithinMs`).

symbols.name: RunStates
symbols.signature: export class RunStates implements DocumentSlot, PersistedSlot {
symbols.comment: A run's state documents. Created with the run, retired with its record; never drafted while absent.

symbols.name: RunStates.persisted
symbols.comment: The store side when the job persists; `undefined` in memory.

symbols.name: RunStates.definition
symbols.comment: The definition new documents are of: the job's latest declaration's state.

symbols.name: RunStates.#older
symbols.comment:
The definitions of documents older than `definition` (runs started before a reload's new job version), by run id:
the old code keeps writing the version it knows; the document migrates once its run settles or moves to the new
code (slice 7b §8).

symbols.name: RunStates.constructor
symbols.signature:
constructor(
		definition: StateDefinition<JsonObject, false, boolean>,
		states: RunStatesOwner,
		persistence: Persistence | undefined,
	)

symbols.name: RunStates.redefine
symbols.comment:
Takes a reload's new job version's state `definition` for new documents (`SlotDefinition.check` refuses an older
version or a schema changed without a bump); the documents there are keep the version they are of.

symbols.name: RunStates.migrated
symbols.signature: migrated(id: string, context: Context): JsonObject | undefined
symbols.comment:
Run `id`'s document as the current definition reads it: migrated when it is of an older version (its run's
outcome on the new code; the document itself is retired with the run), `undefined` once retired.

symbols.name: RunStates.#definitionOf
symbols.comment: The definition run `key`'s document is of.

symbols.name: RunStates.value
symbols.comment: The value of run `id`'s document; `undefined` once retired.

symbols.name: RunStates.cold
symbols.comment: Pinned in memory while the run is unsettled: never cold.

symbols.signature:
stage(

		writes: StagedWrite[],

A change of run `key`'s document: a deferred one of a stored document is held (nothing written); an immediate
one stores what is held with its own ops, as one delta on the stored revision or a base.

symbols.name: RunStates.adopt
symbols.signature:
adopt(

		tracker: Tracker<JsonObject>,
		prepared: Prepared<JsonObject>,
		change: StoredChange | undefined,

symbols.name: RunStates.retire
symbols.comment: Retires run `key`'s document (its record's deletion): what is held goes with it.

symbols.name: RunStates.create
symbols.signature: create(id: string, value: JsonObject, stored: Stored | undefined): void
symbols.comment: Run `id`'s document with `value`, as its start created it or a load found it (`stored`: persisted).

symbols.name: RunStates.stageCreate
symbols.signature: stageCreate(id: string, value: JsonObject, writes: () => StagedWrite[]): () => void

Stages the creation of run `id`'s document with `value` into `writes` (its start); returns the adoption, which

symbols.name: RunStates.deadline

symbols.name: RunStates.heldIds

symbols.name: RunStates.stageHeld
symbols.signature: stageHeld(id: string, writes: StagedWrite[]): (() => void) | undefined

Stages what run `id`'s document holds into `writes` (a flush: its deadline, the outcome, the close writer), as one
delta on its stored revision or a base; returns the adoption, `undefined` when nothing is held.

symbols.name: RunStates.drop
symbols.comment: Drops every document (the object ended): what is held is lost, as a crash loses it.

symbols.name: RunStates.#settle
symbols.comment: What is stored of run `key`'s document after a commit stored it: nothing is held any more.

symbols.name: RunStates.#hold
symbols.signature: #hold(key: string, prepared: Prepared<JsonObject>, change: Extract<StoredChange, { kind: "held" }>): void

symbols.name: heldOps
symbols.comment:
What `held` stores, its queue left as it was (a commit may still be refused): its folded ops, or a base once a held
change asked for one or the queue overflowed. Taking and pushing back one batch keeps it by reference: no copy.

packages/chord/src/jobs/run-states.ts.comment:
A job's run state documents (§15, slice 6b §4.1, §4.3): one per run by its id, Chord's own slot apart from the

object's `self.state` slots. In memory, or persisted in the object's store (namespace `chord.job-states`), always in

memory while the run is unsettled (`ctx.state.value` reads it synchronously). A persisted run's deferred changes

(D8) are adopted and published at once and held, stored before the next change's own, at the outcome, at close or

when their deadline passes.

symbols.name: Run
symbols.comment: A started run as its caller holds it: its id and a wait for its outcome.

symbols.name: Run.outcome
symbols.comment:
Resolves with the outcome once `finish` committed (also without a `finish`); a blocked run keeps waiting, a dropped
one rejects `aborted`, the object's end rejects with its error; `context` ends only this wait, which then keeps
nothing of it. A rejection's error keeps its stack's receivers (the transaction that ended the run) until its
`stack` is read (V8).

symbols.name: AnyOutcome
symbols.signature: export type AnyOutcome = Outcome<JsonValue, unknown, JsonValue | undefined>;
symbols.comment: A run's outcome, as Chord keeps it whatever the job's types.

symbols.name: Phase
symbols.comment:
Where a run's record stands. A persisted run is `pending` from its start's commit until its reservation commit
(`running`, then its `run` starts), `stopped` once a clean stop cut it off; an in-memory run is `running` from its
start's commit. `finishing` once its outcome is recorded, `blocked` after five failed finishes or for another
version.

symbols.name: BlockedReason
symbols.comment:
Why a run is blocked: its `finish` failed five times in a row, or its version is not the code's (stored by another
job version or fingerprint, of a newer version or an older one without an adapter, or of a job the code no longer
declares, slice 7b §8).

symbols.name: Answer
symbols.comment: How a run settled for its waiters.
symbols.output:
| { readonly kind: "done"; readonly outcome: AnyOutcome }
	| { readonly kind: "failed"; readonly error: ChordError }

symbols.name: Waiter
symbols.signature: type Waiter = { readonly settle: (settled: Answer) => void };
symbols.comment: One wait for a run's outcome, removed when its context aborts.

symbols.name: JobRun
symbols.comment: One run: changed only by its job, inside its transactions' commit steps (records) and after them (actions).

symbols.name: JobRun.version
symbols.comment: The job version it was started with: it keeps it across reloads (slice 7b §8).

symbols.name: JobRun.fingerprint
symbols.comment: The fingerprint of its job version (a persisted run's record keeps it).

symbols.name: JobRun.mapped
symbols.signature: mapped: { readonly version: number; readonly args: JsonValue; outcome?: AnyOutcome } | undefined;
symbols.comment: Its args and outcome mapped forwards to the job's current version (once per run and version), when older.
symbols.output: { readonly version: number; readonly args: JsonValue; outcome?: AnyOutcome } | undefined

symbols.name: JobRun.blockedPhase
symbols.comment: A persisted run blocked for its version at its load: the phase its record had, resumed when unblocked.

symbols.name: JobRun.invocation
symbols.comment: Its current invocation, from its reservation (or its start in memory) on; a later one replaces it.

symbols.name: JobRun.restarts
symbols.comment: A persisted run's crashes in a row while running (D6); reset by a state change.

symbols.name: JobRun.finishFailures
symbols.comment: Failed finishes in a row (stored for a persisted run, so they count across a crash).

symbols.name: JobRun.abortMarked
symbols.comment: Set by `abort(id)` (stored for a persisted run, D7): a run not invoked yet ends `aborted` without `run`.

symbols.name: JobRun.resuming
symbols.comment: A persisted run cut off by a crash or a clean stop, to be resumed per its job's `resume` (no new start).

symbols.name: JobRun.trace
symbols.signature: readonly trace: { readonly [key: string]: string } | undefined;
symbols.comment:
The start's trace carrier, when the adapter propagates (stored for a persisted run): its run and finish spans are
children of it, in a new attempt and a new process too (a carrier, not the span: a settled span starts no
recorded children).

symbols.name: JobRun.outcome
symbols.comment: What it ended with, once recorded (finishing and blocked).

symbols.name: JobRun.entry
symbols.comment: Its entry in `running`, while its record exists; replaced when its record or state document changes.

symbols.name: JobRun.#waiters
symbols.comment: Its waiters: apart from the run, so a handle kept by a caller keeps only how the run settled.

symbols.signature:
constructor(

		version: number,
		fingerprint: string,
		key: string | undefined,

	)

symbols.name: JobRun.entryFor
symbols.signature: entryFor(state: JsonValue | undefined, args: JsonValue): JsonValue
symbols.comment:
Its `running` entry for its current record, `state` (the job's state document, `undefined` without one) and
`args` (mapped forwards for an older version): a pending or stopped run shows as `running` (it runs, or will run
again).

symbols.name: JobRun.begin
symbols.comment: A new invocation, the current one from now on (a run marked aborted is never invoked: it ends without one).

symbols.name: JobRun.invoked
symbols.comment: Whether its current invocation runs (or is reserved): it is not invoked again meanwhile.

symbols.name: JobRun.over
symbols.comment:
Resolves once its current invocation ended, at once when none runs (`abort` joins it; one a seal cut off is
fenced and is not waited for); `context` ends only the wait.

symbols.name: JobRun.resolve
symbols.comment: Its waiters get the outcome.

symbols.name: JobRun.reject
symbols.comment: Its waiters get `error`.

symbols.name: Invocation
symbols.comment:
One invocation of a run's `run`: its fence (`ctx.state.change` admitted while it runs, under its own seal token,
which its attempt's seal fences), its abort signal and the waits for its end. Captured by its ctx and its settling,
so a replaced invocation never acts for its successor.

symbols.name: Invocation.abort
symbols.comment: `run`'s abort signal: `abort(id)`, the attempt's seal, the object's end and `host.close` fire it.

symbols.name: Invocation.state
symbols.comment: `running` from its reservation until `run` settled or a seal cut it off.

symbols.name: Invocation.settle
symbols.comment: The fence closes: a change made later is refused.

symbols.name: Invocation.ended
symbols.comment: Nothing of it runs here any more (its `run` settled, or the object ended): every join resolves.

symbols.name: Invocation.over
symbols.comment: Resolves once it ended; `context` ends only the wait.

symbols.name: Waiters
symbols.comment: A run's waits for its outcome: each removed when its context aborts; late ones answered at once.

symbols.name: Waiters.#settled
symbols.comment: How the run settled, once it did.

symbols.name: Waiters.settle
symbols.comment: The run settled (once): every wait gets it.

symbols.name: Waiters.wait
symbols.comment: A wait for the outcome: at once once settled; otherwise until it settles or `context` aborts.

symbols.name: answer
symbols.comment: A settled run's answer to a wait.

symbols.name: Joins
symbols.comment: The waits for a run's invocation to be over: each removed when its context aborts, so a cancelled one keeps nothing.

symbols.name: Joins.end
symbols.comment: The invocation is over (once): every wait resolves.

symbols.name: Joins.wait
symbols.comment: A wait: at once when over; otherwise until it is or `context` aborts (rejecting with its reason).

packages/chord/src/jobs/run.ts.comment:
One run of a job (§15, slice 6b §4.1): its record (id, version, key, args, phase, restarts, finish failures, abort

mark, outcome), its current invocation (the fence of its seal token, its abort signal, the end an abort joins: one

per invocation, as a persisted run is invoked again after a seal, R3), its `running` entry and the `Run` handle its

callers wait on.

symbols.name: RunningEntry
symbols.comment:
One entry of `running`: a running or finishing run with its args (and state, when the job has a state document), or
a blocked run, which carries neither (it may be of another version than the code).

symbols.name: Running
symbols.comment:
The list behind `running`. Every change copies the list (O(unsettled runs)) and, while it is watched, records its
ops; the batch delivers them as one frame. Unwatched, no op is built.

symbols.name: Running.#label
symbols.comment: The job in errors.

symbols.name: Running.#list
symbols.comment: `undefined` once its object ended: reads throw `released`, and no ended run's args or state are kept.

symbols.name: Running.#ops
symbols.comment: The ops of the current batch's changes, kept only while watched.

symbols.name: Running.#listed
symbols.comment: Whether the current batch listed this source for a frame.

symbols.name: Running.add
symbols.comment: Appends the entry of a new run.

symbols.name: Running.replace
symbols.comment: Replaces a run's entry `before` by `after` (its record changed).

symbols.name: Running.stateChanged
symbols.signature: stateChanged(before: JsonValue, after: JsonValue, ops: readonly Op[]): void
symbols.comment: Replaces a run's entry `before` by `after`, whose state document changed by `ops`.

symbols.name: Running.remove
symbols.comment: Removes a run's entry.

symbols.name: Running.end
symbols.comment: Its object ended: every watch ends, and the list goes.

symbols.name: Running.#replaced
symbols.comment: Copies the list with `after` in the place of `before`; returns that place.

symbols.name: Running.#mark
symbols.comment:
Records that the list changed, in the batch running now: derives over it are marked; while watched it is listed
once per batch for a frame. Returns whether the change's ops are to be recorded (only while watched).

symbols.name: under
symbols.signature: function under(prefix: readonly [number, string], op: Op): Op
symbols.comment: `op` of a value at `prefix` inside a larger one: a replacement becomes a set there.

packages/chord/src/jobs/running.ts.comment:
A job's `running` (§15): a JSON watchable of its unsettled runs, one entry per run in start order, tagged by phase.

It is a source of its own (keyed state documents publish nothing): the job tells it each change in the commit step,

and a frame carries exactly the ops of those changes, a run's state ops re-pathed under its entry.

symbols.name: StoredJobError
symbols.comment: How a run failed, as stored: a thrown error in the wire format, an abort, the restart limit.

symbols.name: StoredOutcome
symbols.comment: A run's outcome as stored: its result, or how it failed.
symbols.output:
| { readonly kind: "done"; readonly result: JsonValue }
	| { readonly kind: "failed"; readonly error: StoredJobError }

symbols.name: StoredRun
symbols.comment: The record document of one unsettled persisted run.

symbols.name: RUN_RECORD
symbols.comment:

symbols.name: SHORT
symbols.comment: Up to this many UTF-16 units a string takes at most 126 bytes, so its length is one varint byte.

symbols.name: LONG
symbols.comment: From this many UTF-16 units a string is encoded in place (below it, encoding on its own and copying is cheaper).

symbols.name: LENGTH_SLOT
symbols.comment: The fixed length prefix of a long string: five varint bytes, up to 32 GiB (16 GiB for a part).

symbols.name: SPARE
symbols.comment: The room left after a large chunk for the fields that follow it.

symbols.name: Writer
symbols.comment: Writes a message into one growing buffer, right-sized at the end.

symbols.name: Writer.#buffer
symbols.comment: Large enough for most small messages (a state change, a call), small enough to zero cheaply.

symbols.name: Writer.varint
symbols.comment: An unsigned LEB128 varint of a safe integer.

symbols.name: Writer.string
symbols.comment: A length-prefixed UTF-8 string (`#text`).

symbols.name: Writer.part
symbols.comment:
A part: its text encoded in place, or its bytes (a part received) copied as they are, behind its length doubled,
plus one when deflated.

symbols.name: Writer.#text
symbols.comment:
Text behind its UTF-8 length times `scale` (2 for a part's prefix), encoded straight into the buffer where the
prefix is known in advance: a short text (its prefix fits one byte: at most 126 bytes, 42 UTF-16 units, divided
by `scale`) and a long one (a snapshot's JSON, behind a fixed five-byte prefix, a padded varint, which readers
accept). Others are encoded on their own and copied in. No text is encoded twice, and the largest value of a
message is never copied.

A state entry's failures and retirements: the failure count times two, plus one when retirements follow, so an
entry without retirements costs no byte more than its failures.

symbols.comment:
The message: a view of the buffer, or a right-sized copy when the spare room is meaningful (at least 64 bytes and
more than an eighth of the message), so a kept message keeps at most that much beyond itself. A large message
ends within its 4 KiB of room and is not copied.

symbols.comment: Grows the buffer to fit `bytes` more: doubled, or for a large chunk to its end plus room for the small fields after it.

symbols.comment: Reads a message's bytes; every read is bounds-checked, segments are views of the message.

symbols.name: Reader.varint

symbols.name: Reader.part
symbols.comment: A part as a view of the message, unparsed and not inflated.

symbols.name: Reader.end
symbols.comment: The message is consumed exactly.

packages/chord/src/link/binary.ts.comment:
The binary codec (2b): a kind byte (its high bit set when an origin follows as a varint, the next one when a trace

carrier follows as JSON, slice 9), then the kind's fields as

unsigned varints, length-prefixed UTF-8 strings, raw incarnation (16 bytes) and fingerprint (8 bytes), parts as

length-prefixed bytes whose prefix also says whether the part is deflated (decoded as views of the message, never

parsed or inflated here), and byte segments only beside payloads marked as carrying bytes. No outer length: links

deliver whole messages.

symbols.name: ChannelHandler
symbols.comment: What the owner of a channel handles.

symbols.name: ChannelHandler.opened
symbols.comment: The peer's `hello` arrived: the link is open.

symbols.name: ChannelHandler.message
symbols.comment:
A checked message after the handshake (never `hello`, `ping` or `pong`). A throw is a protocol error. A promise
(the message waits for an asynchronous inflate) holds every later message until it settles; a rejection is a
protocol error too.

symbols.name: ChannelHandler.closed
symbols.comment: The link closed, from either end; called once.

symbols.name: ChannelOptions
symbols.comment: What a channel is made with besides its link and handler.

symbols.name: incarnation
symbols.comment: This host's incarnation, sent in `hello`.

symbols.name: calls
symbols.comment: How many concurrent calls this side accepts, sent in `hello`.

symbols.name: trusted
symbols.comment: Skips the `MESSAGE` check (framing, the codec's decode and the owners' checks still run).

symbols.name: report
symbols.comment: Where protocol errors go.

symbols.name: metrics
symbols.comment: The host's instruments: the bytes of every encoded message sent and received (`chord.link.bytes`).

symbols.name: SENT
symbols.comment: `chord.link.bytes`' attributes, made once.

symbols.name: ChannelState
symbols.comment:
Where a channel stands: `greeting` until the peer's `hello`, with what this end sent meanwhile; `open` with the
peer's incarnation and call window.

symbols.name: Channel
symbols.comment:
One end of a link. It sends `hello { protocol, incarnation, calls }` first and nothing else until the peer's arrived
(its own messages wait). Every message is decoded by the link's codec and, unless the link is trusted, checked
against the message schema; a first message that is no `hello` of this codec, a second `hello`, another protocol
version, or a message failing a check closes the link and is reported. The heartbeat: every received message
stamps `lastReceived`; the host's timer calls `tick`, which pings a silent open link and closes a link silent for
too long (the handshake included); a `ping` is answered with `pong` at once. A message the handler handles
asynchronously holds the later ones, `ping` included, until it settles; they are handled in order then, and dropped
when the link closes meanwhile.

symbols.name: Channel.#lastReceived
symbols.comment: When the last message arrived (`Date.now()`), or the channel was made.

symbols.name: Channel.#pinged
symbols.comment: Whether a `ping` went out since the last received message.

symbols.name: Channel.#held
symbols.comment:
Messages received while one is handled asynchronously, in order, and the index of the next to handle; `undefined`
while none waits.

symbols.name: Channel.#waiting
symbols.comment: Whether a message is being handled asynchronously: the held ones wait.

symbols.name: Channel.#bytes
symbols.comment: Counts the bytes of the encoded messages (sizes the channel has).

symbols.name: Channel.constructor
symbols.signature: constructor(link: Link, handler: ChannelHandler, options: ChannelOptions, context: Context)

symbols.name: Channel.start
symbols.comment:
Sends `hello` and starts listening: messages that arrived already are handled now, and a link closed already
calls `closed` now; so the handler is complete before it starts.

symbols.name: Channel.peer
symbols.comment: The peer's incarnation, from its `hello`; empty before it arrived (nothing else can arrive before it).

symbols.name: Channel.peerCalls
symbols.comment: How many concurrent calls the peer accepts, from its `hello`; 0 before it arrived.

symbols.name: Channel.send
symbols.comment: Sends one message; before the handshake it waits, after the close it is dropped.

symbols.name: Channel.tick
symbols.signature: tick(now: number, paused: number, ping: number, close: number): void
symbols.comment:
The heartbeat, at `now`: a link silent for `close` ms (the handshake included) closes; an open one silent for
`ping` ms sends one `ping`. `paused` ms this process did not run before it are no silence: what the peer sent
meanwhile is still unread (timers run before I/O). The silence stays what it was before the pause, at least `ping`
ms, so a dead peer (a dropped TCP connection) is found `close - ping` ms later.

symbols.name: Channel.#handle
symbols.comment: Handles one received message; one the handler handles asynchronously holds the next until it settles.

symbols.name: Channel.#hold
symbols.comment: Holds later messages until `handling` settles, then handles them in order (each may hold again).

symbols.name: Channel.#release
symbols.comment:
The held message was handled: the ones behind it are handled in order, until one holds again (the handled ones are
dropped from the queue then).

symbols.name: Channel.#failed
symbols.comment: A protocol error: reported, and the link closes.

symbols.name: Channel.#decode
symbols.comment: A message from its bytes, checked against the message schema unless the link is trusted.

symbols.name: Channel.#greet
symbols.comment: The first message: the peer's `hello` in this link's codec and protocol version.

packages/chord/src/link/channel.ts.comment:
A host's end of a link (§3, §22, 2b): the handshake, the link's codec, the checks of every message (skipped on a

trusted link), the heartbeat, and messages handled in order while one waits for an asynchronous inflate; a protocol

error closes the link. The bytes of every message it encodes and receives are counted (`chord.link.bytes`).

symbols.name: wireError
symbols.comment: What crosses for a thrown value: a ChordError, a PluginError, or anything else as the plugin code `internal`.

symbols.name: errorFromWire
symbols.signature: export function errorFromWire(error: WireError): ChordError | PluginError
symbols.comment: The error a consumer rethrows. A malformed ChordError envelope throws (a protocol error).

packages/chord/src/link/errors.ts.comment: Errors on the wire: a ChordError's JSON or a plugin's code, message and details; never a stack or a cause.

packages/chord/src/link/index.ts.comment:
Links for apps: the link interface adapters implement, the in-memory pair, IPC and WebSocket links, the codecs a link

may use, its limits per part and the compressor a host may bring.

packages/chord/src/link/internal.ts.comment:
Links for Chord's layers: a host's end of a link (handshake, codec, checks, heartbeat and in-order handling), the

message type, parts with their limits and compression, and errors in messages.

symbols.name: IpcPort
symbols.comment:
The part of a Node IPC channel a link uses: a `ChildProcess` or the child's `process`. `send` returning `false` is
backpressure (the message is queued by Node), not a failure.

symbols.name: IpcPort.send
symbols.signature: send(message: Uint8Array, callback: (error: Error | null) => void): boolean;

symbols.name: ipcLink
symbols.comment:
A link over `port`: each message one `Uint8Array` (V8 serialization keeps it one). It listens from the moment it is
made and queues messages until its listener is set, so a child makes it before awaiting its start message; messages
that are no `Uint8Array` (the app's own, such as that start message) are not the link's and are skipped. A thrown
`send`, an error in its callback or `disconnect` closes the link once; its listeners are removed then.

symbols.name: IpcLink.#port
symbols.comment: The port while the link is open.

symbols.name: IpcLink.#onMessage
IpcLink.#onSent
IpcLink.#end
symbols.comment: Detaches from the port and closes this end.

packages/chord/src/link/ipc.ts.comment:
IPC links (§3): a link over a Node IPC channel, a forked child (`fork` with `serialization: "advanced"`) or

`process` in the child, typed structurally so Chord imports nothing from Node.

symbols.name: Link
symbols.comment:
Links (§3): an ordered, bidirectional channel of messages between two hosts, and the in-memory pair.

An ordered, bidirectional channel of `Uint8Array` messages between two hosts. Adapters only move bytes.

symbols.name: Link.send
symbols.comment: Sends one message; a no-op once closed.

symbols.name: Link.onMessage
symbols.comment:
Sets the one listener for incoming messages; messages that arrived earlier are delivered to it first. On a closed
link it is not kept.

symbols.name: Link.close
symbols.comment: Closes both ends; messages not delivered yet are dropped.

symbols.name: Link.onClose
symbols.comment: Sets the one listener for the close of either end; it runs at once when the link is closed already.

symbols.name: memoryLinkPair
symbols.comment: Two ends of one link: what one sends, the other receives asynchronously (a microtask later), in order.

symbols.name: LinkEnd
symbols.signature: export abstract class LinkEnd implements Link {
symbols.comment:
What every link end shares: the one message listener (messages that arrived before it are queued for it), the one
close listener, and closing once. Subclasses move the bytes: `deliver` what arrived, `ended` when the transport
closed, and implement `send` and `close`.

symbols.name: LinkEnd.#queued
symbols.comment: Messages that arrived before the listener was set.

symbols.name: LinkEnd.deliver
symbols.comment: A message arrived; dropped once closed.

symbols.name: LinkEnd.ended
symbols.comment: Closes this end (once): nothing is delivered any more, and nothing the listeners reach is kept.

symbols.name: MemoryLink
symbols.comment:
One end of a memory link. Closing it closes this end at once and the peer a microtask later, as a transport would.
Portable: `queueMicrotask` only.

packages/chord/src/link/link.ts.comment:
Links (§3): an ordered, bidirectional channel of messages between two hosts, and the in-memory pair.

An ordered, bidirectional channel of `Uint8Array` messages between two hosts. Adapters only move bytes.

symbols.name: id
symbols.comment: A link-local id, chosen by its origin: a counter, unique per link, direction and origin while in use.

symbols.name: origin
symbols.comment:
Whose work a message is (decision "Relay flow control per origin"): a relay's number for one downstream link (and
the origin that link's messages carried), never reused on a link; absent for the sender's own work. Holds, calls,
windows and acks are keyed by (origin, id), and replies carry the origin of what they answer.

symbols.name: index
symbols.comment: A name as an index into the hold's bound version (each variant's names sorted).

symbols.name: wireError
symbols.comment: An error that may come from plugin code: a ChordError's JSON (checked by L1), or a plugin's code and message.

symbols.name: failed
symbols.comment: The members of a hold that failed with this message (W1).

symbols.name: part
symbols.comment: A part's envelope: the codec built it, so any value passes (its content is the owner's to parse).

symbols.name: segments
symbols.comment:
The byte segments of a payload part whose method's schema has a `bytes()` leaf, referenced from its JSON by
`{"$bytes": i}`; absent for every other payload. Built by the codec, like the part.

symbols.name: NAME_LENGTH
symbols.comment:
The longest name a message carries (a type's, a host kind's): a relay records them in its spans unparsed, so a peer
cannot hand it an unbounded string (slice 9 review M1).

symbols.name: name
symbols.comment: A type's or a host kind's name.

symbols.name: address
symbols.comment: An address as a hold names it: its host kind and params, checked against the kind where it is routed.

symbols.name: principal
symbols.comment: A principal on a hold: JSON with a `kind`, honoured only on a parent link.

symbols.name: incarnation
symbols.comment: A uuidv7 as text.

symbols.name: CARRIER
symbols.comment: The most keys a trace carrier has, and the longest key or value (R5).

symbols.name: trace
symbols.comment:
The caller's trace carrier on a `hold` or `call` (R5, slice 9): an adapter's opaque string record, bounded, of
printable ASCII only (keys without spaces), as W3C's headers and Chord's adapters are; anything else fails this schema
as any malformed header does, so no control character becomes a stored trace or span id (review M2). The provider
extracts it with its own adapter (absent or unknown: the adapter's root).

symbols.name: CHAIN
symbols.comment: The longest activation chain a hold carries (Q5): a longer one keeps its last entries.

symbols.name: RETRY_HOPS
symbols.comment: A `retry`'s hop budget as the first host sends it (dependency model §3.7, audit A5): one less per host after it.

symbols.name: CAUSE_KINDS
symbols.comment: The kinds of a `failed` message's cause, in their codes' order (the binary codec's byte, the text codec's letter).

symbols.name: MESSAGE
symbols.comment: The protocol's messages, one tagged union. Parts are opaque here (the owners parse them).

symbols.name: Message
symbols.comment:
A protocol message. `args` absent: a method without arguments; `value` absent: `null`. A `state` entry's `retired`
list is read-only (the schema's type is mutable): entries without retirements share `NO_RETIRED`.
symbols.output:
| Exclude<WireMessage, WireState>
	| (Omit<WireState, "holds"> & { readonly holds: readonly StateEntry[] })

symbols.name: WireError
symbols.comment: An error as it crosses a link.

symbols.name: OriginMessage
symbols.signature: export type OriginMessage = Exclude<Message, { readonly kind: "hello" | "revoke" | "ping" | "pong" }>;
symbols.comment: A message that may carry an origin (every kind but `hello`, `revoke`, `ping` and `pong`).

symbols.name: ProviderMessage
symbols.comment: A message for a provider side: the direction from the consumer (`closed` is the link's).

symbols.name: ConsumerMessage
symbols.comment: A message for a consumer side: the direction from the provider.

symbols.comment: The `retired` list of a state entry without retirements, shared (no allocation per message).

symbols.name: WireAddress
symbols.comment: An address as a `hold` carries it.

symbols.name: FailedMember
symbols.comment: A member of a hold that failed, by index, as `bound` and `state` list it.

symbols.name: Codec
symbols.comment: How a link turns messages into bytes and back; both ends of a link use the same one.

symbols.name: Codec.decode
symbols.comment: Throws on bytes that are no message of this codec (a protocol error); the envelope is checked afterwards.

symbols.name: checkMessage
symbols.signature: export function checkMessage(message: unknown, context: Context): Message
symbols.comment:
Checks a decoded message's envelope with the compiled schema (the wire is a trust boundary, after any codec): kinds,
ids and indexes, lists and error shapes; not the parts. Throws on a mismatch (a protocol error). Counted in
`chord.link.checks`.

packages/chord/src/link/message.ts.comment:
Messages (§22, R1, R4, 2b): the one `Message` type every link carries, defined as a schema and checked after every

decode, and the codecs that turn it into bytes.

symbols.name: Part
symbols.signature: export type Part = string | Uint8Array | DeflatedPart;
symbols.comment:
A part (R1): a value as JSON text at its origin (and after a text decode), its UTF-8 bytes once a binary codec
received it (or at an origin that encoded it already), or those bytes deflated by an origin that compresses. Opaque
on the way: only the end that owns it opens and parses it, while handling its message (a malformed part is a protocol
error then), so a relay forwards it unparsed and still deflated.

symbols.name: Inflated
symbols.comment: What inflating a deflated part gave: its JSON bytes, more than the decoded limit, or data that is no raw deflate.

symbols.name: DeflatedPart
symbols.comment:
A JSON part deflated (raw deflate) by its origin. A host without a synchronous compressor inflates it before its
owner handles the message (`inflateAsync`) and keeps the outcome here for the owner to open.

symbols.name: DeflatedPart.inflated
symbols.comment: The asynchronous inflate's outcome; `undefined` until one ran.

symbols.name: Compression
symbols.comment:
A synchronous compressor (`createHost({ compression })`; `nodeCompression` for Node). `deflate` is raw deflate at
level 1. `inflate` gives at most `limit` bytes (`Infinity`: no limit; 0 allowed), `too_large` when the output would
be larger, `corrupt` for data that is no raw deflate stream.

symbols.name: PartLimits
symbols.comment: A link's limits per part as `accept`, `connect` and `resolve` take them, in bytes.

symbols.name: part
symbols.comment: A part's size on the wire.

symbols.name: decoded
symbols.comment: A part's size after inflating it.

symbols.name: Limits
symbols.signature: export type Limits = { readonly part: number; readonly decoded: number };
symbols.comment: A link's limits in force; `Infinity` for none.
symbols.output: { readonly part: number; readonly decoded: number }

symbols.name: UNTRUSTED
symbols.comment: The limits of untrusted links unless set (Q2); trusted links (IPC) have none.

symbols.name: linkLimits
symbols.signature: export function linkLimits(trusted: boolean, limits: PartLimits = {}): Limits
symbols.comment: The limits of a link: the ones set, the defaults of its trust for the others.

symbols.name: COMPRESS_ABOVE
symbols.comment: JSON parts above this many UTF-8 bytes are compressed at their origin (a protocol constant).

symbols.name: originPart
symbols.signature: export function originPart(json: string, compression: Compression | undefined, context: Context): Part
symbols.comment:
A JSON part at its origin: deflated when the host compresses, its UTF-8 bytes are above `COMPRESS_ABOVE` and
deflating made it smaller; otherwise the text, or its bytes once they were encoded (never encoded twice). Counts one
deflate (`chord.link.deflates`).

symbols.name: oversized
symbols.signature: export function oversized(part: Part, limit: number): ChordError | undefined
symbols.comment:
The `too_large/part` error of a part whose size on the wire (its UTF-8 bytes; a deflated part's deflated bytes) is
above `limit`; `undefined` within it. Nothing is parsed or inflated.

symbols.name: openPart
symbols.comment:
The JSON of a part its owner is about to parse: its size checked against `limits.part` first, then its decoded size
against `limits.decoded`, a deflated part inflated within it (synchronously with `compression`, or by the
asynchronous inflate that ran ahead of its owner). Throws `too_large/part` past a limit; throws a plain error for a
deflated part nothing inflated or that is no raw deflate stream (a protocol error). Counts one synchronous inflate

packages/chord/src/link/text.ts.comment:
The text codec (2b): one JSON tuple per message, Delta style (a short kind tag, positional fields, no field names),

and `describeMessage`, which prints any message in that form. A part's JSON text is spliced into the tuple as it is;

decoding parses the tuple and writes each part back as text (one parse per part per hop: a debugging codec). Byte

segments of a payload marked as carrying bytes follow the tuple after a newline (JSON text never contains a raw

one), their lengths the tuple's last field. A message with an origin is wrapped: `["@", origin, tuple]`. Every part

is tagged with its codec, so no JSON value is reserved: `[0, json]`, or `[1, base64]` for a part its origin deflated

(the text codec itself never compresses). A `hold`'s or `call`'s trace carrier is an optional element after its

other fields (slice 9); a `call`'s old-work flag (`old`) follows it as `true` (the carrier then `null` when absent).

leaf), its byte segments: each `Uint8Array` leaf becomes a segment, and an own key `$bytes`, reserved there, fails
`invalid/args`; otherwise plain JSON, where `$bytes` is ordinary data. `undefined` (a handler returning nothing) is
`null`.

`startServer` (slice 13 §1, §5; decisions "The app kit, point 1" to "point 5"): the server of an app built with the kit.

It lays out the data directory, opens the server's store, creates the server host, the HTTP component and one

The index of one host's files (Files v2, decision "Files v2"): four tables of the host's store and two documents.

`files` holds one row per version (its space, folder, path, version, blob, size, metadata), `folders` one row per

folder, `blobs` one row per blob on disk with its reference count, `paths` each path's highest version ever (kept

through removals: no number is used twice for a path); the `summary` document per space (counts, bytes, the newest

versions) is what an app mirrors to its server, the `usage` document the bytes on disk the caps count. Reads by id,

by path, by folder, by `ref` and by `key`; every change is one transaction, computed by its caller's turn (the

object runs one change at a time), so a version number, a key and a blob's count are decided once.

packages/chord/src/node/app/files.ts.comment:
Files (slice 13 §4; decision "Files v2"): the kit's file storage, one `Files` object per host (`self.get(Files, {})`),

its bytes in the host's `files/` and its index in the host's store (`files-index.ts`). Every file lives in a space

(`shared`, `artifacts`, `uploads`, …) at a path (`docs/report.md`); folders are index entries, and a move changes only

the index. Bytes never change: writing to a path adds a version (a new blob), `copy` shares a blob, and a blob goes

once no version references it. Small files in one call (`put`), large ones in chunks (design §23 "Chunked transfers":

`begin`, `append` at the stored offset, `uploaded` to resume after a drop, `finish`; unfinished uploads expire); a

`key` makes a write idempotent; reads by range; caps per host; a summary per space for an app's server index;

`FilesFolder` lists one folder live. Plugins never see a path on disk.

The owner (slice 13 §2, decision "The app kit, point 3: authentication"): no owner by loopback alone. At each start

the kit makes a one-time owner link (a random token, single use, valid 10 minutes, the previous one dropped); the

start script prints it. Its page reads the token from the URL's fragment (never sent to a server, so never in a

log) and posts it; the post consumes it and sets a browser session cookie for the owner. The owner token file

(mode 0600) carries a device session of the owner for command-line clients on the same machine.

packages/chord/src/node/app/pairing.ts.comment:
Device pairing (slice 13 §2, decision "The app kit, point 3" (c)): a command-line or terminal client on another

machine asks for a code (`POST /_chord/pair`, public) and polls with a secret it got with it; the owner opens

`/_chord/pair/<code>` in a signed-in browser and approves; the next poll returns a device session's token, once.

Codes are short, random, single use and expire after 10 minutes; the poll secret is kept only hashed. Asking is

public, so pairings anonymous clients start are capped: `maxPending` in all (100 by default) and `perAddress` per

client address (10). The trade: a party filling the caps locks pairing out for others for up to 10 minutes (behind a

tunnel every remote client has the tunnel's address), instead of growing the server's memory without bound; a

signed-in owner's pairings are not counted, so the owner can always pair.

Writes `text` to `path` with mode 0600 in one step: a temporary file of the same directory (made exclusively, 0600)
linked into place (`create`: refused when `path` exists, `"exists"` returned) or renamed over it (`replace`).

Secrets of the app kit (slice 13 §2): tokens from `crypto.randomBytes`, kept only as their SHA-256 hashes and

compared in constant time, and secret files (the cookie key, the owner token file) created with mode 0600 in one

step, so no other OS user and no half-written file ever reads them.

response sets it again with a fresh signed expiry, so a browser used within every 400 days stays signed in. Not when

authenticates.

packages/chord/src/node/app/sessions.ts.comment:
Sessions (slice 13 §2, decision "The app kit, point 3: authentication"): the kit's object on the server that issues

and revokes sessions, and its authenticator. A session is a principal behind a token `<id>.<secret>` (random); only

the secret's hash is kept. A browser carries its token in the kit's signed session cookie (`HttpOnly`,

`SameSite=Strict`), a command-line client in `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Browser and device sessions persist in

the server's store and expire after 400 days unused; ephemeral sessions (a pick-a-name login, a public route) live

in memory only (`EphemeralSessions`), at most `maxEphemeral` of them (past it the oldest ends), so a public login

costs the same whatever came before; each ends with its client's connection (its last link closed, a grace period

passed: the links endpoint's `opened` hook counts them), and none outlives the server's run.

symbols.name: TarEntry
symbols.signature: export type TarEntry = { readonly path: string; readonly size: number; readonly data: AsyncIterable<Uint8Array> };
symbols.comment:
A minimal ustar (POSIX tar) writer and reader for the kit's address archives (slice 13 §4): regular files and

directories, paths of at most 255 bytes, nothing else. The reader is a trust boundary: an archive may come from

anywhere, so it refuses every entry that is no regular file or directory, a path that is absolute, holds `..`, a

backslash or NUL, or names an empty segment, and a header whose checksum does not hold.

One entry to write: its path (`/`-separated, relative) and its bytes, as a size and the chunks that make it up.
symbols.output: { readonly path: string; readonly size: number; readonly data: AsyncIterable<Uint8Array> }

symbols.comment: One entry read: a regular file (its data, to be consumed before the next entry) or a directory.

| { readonly kind: "file"; readonly path: string; readonly size: number; readonly data: AsyncIterable<Uint8Array> }
	| { readonly kind: "directory"; readonly path: string }

A minimal ustar (POSIX tar) writer and reader for the kit's address archives (slice 13 §4): regular files and

directories, paths of at most 255 bytes, nothing else. The reader is a trust boundary: an archive may come from

anywhere, so it refuses every entry that is no regular file or directory, a path that is absolute, holds `..`, a

backslash or NUL, or names an empty segment, and a header whose checksum does not hold.

One entry to write: its path (`/`-separated, relative) and its bytes, as a size and the chunks that make it up.

symbols.name: Upload
symbols.comment: An upload under way: its owner's data, its file, the bytes accepted, its writes in flight, its first failed write, its end.

symbols.name: Finished

symbols.name: Uploads
symbols.comment:
The uploads under way of one `Files` object, in the directory `run` (this object's own, made on first use), at most
`max` at once: each holds a file handle until it ends, so a caller beginning uploads without end would exhaust the
process's descriptors. Each carries its owner's `T` (what the file becomes when it finishes).

symbols.comment: The bytes accepted by every upload under way (they count against the host's cap).

symbols.name: Uploads.find
symbols.comment: The id of the upload under way whose data `matches`, if any.

symbols.name: Uploads.begin
symbols.comment: A new upload carrying `data`: its id; `unavailable` (`busy`) while `max` are under way.

symbols.name: Uploads.append
symbols.signature:
async append(
		id: string,
		offset: number,
		bytes: Uint8Array,
		room: (adding: number, fileSize: number) => void,
	): Promise<void>
symbols.comment:
Writes `bytes` at `offset` of upload `id`, which must be where the accepted appends reached (else `invalid`, its
details the expected `{ offset }`); `room(adding, fileSize)` refuses what the caps do not allow, before anything
is accepted. A failed write ends the upload.

symbols.name: Uploads.expire
symbols.comment: Drops the uploads unwritten for `idleMs`, once their writes landed.

symbols.name: Uploads.close
symbols.comment: Drops every upload under way (their object ended).

symbols.comment: The upload `id` under way; else `invalid`.

symbols.name: Uploads.#discard
symbols.comment: Takes upload `id` out, closes its file once its writes landed and removes it.

symbols.name: Uploads.#end
symbols.comment: Closes `upload`'s file once its writes in flight landed; once, whoever ends it first.

symbols.name: failedUpload

packages/chord/src/node/app/uploads.ts.comment:
Chunked uploads of one `Files` object (slice 13 §4, design §23 "Chunked transfers"): each upload one file handle in

the run's directory, written at positions. An append is accepted at the offset the accepted appends reached, so a

writer may send several without waiting (the call window allows it): each write lands at its own position whatever

order the thread pool completes them in. `uploaded`, `finish` and expiry wait for an upload's writes in flight; a

failed write ends its upload.

packages/chord/src/node/app/users.ts.comment:
The users plugin (slice 13 §3, decision "The app kit, point 2: principals and users"): accounts keyed by the user's

id with a profile the app describes (a schema it passes in: a Slack-like profile or just a name), kept in the

server's store. User data never rides in the principal: a principal names the user, `Users` holds the rest.

An exported facet, not a plugin directory: it takes the app's schema as an argument (settings are arguments), and a

plugin directory could not import it (plugins import only the app's API). The app loads it in its root by

re-exporting it through its API (`export const users = defineUsers(Profile)` in `/v3/server`, a one-line plugin).

symbols.name: busy
symbols.comment: Extra keep-alive counts of the app (a record of numbers, all zero when idle).

symbols.name: principalAttributes

symbols.name: onError

symbols.name: WORKER_QUEUE
symbols.comment: How many finished spans a worker keeps while it cannot send (past it new ones are dropped).

symbols.name: WORKER_SEND_MS
symbols.comment: How often a worker sends what it recorded.

symbols.name: startWorker
symbols.signature:
export function startWorker

(options: WorkerOptions

): void
symbols.comment: Runs this process as a worker of the app: once the start message arrived, its host is up and its plugins loaded.

packages/chord/src/node/app/worker.ts.comment:
`startWorker` (slice 13 §1): a worker of an app built with the kit, in its entry module. `workerMain` plus the kit's

part: the worker's directory under its kind and address with its store, the host at the worker's address acting as

the principal the server gave it, connected to the server first, its plugins loaded with the kit's worker facets

(`WorkerInfo`, `Files`, `Translations` for a worker that renders final text); when the server has a telemetry store,

the host records in memory and sends its spans and metrics to the server every second (decision "The server is the

one place telemetry is stored").

symbols.comment:
Raw deflate at level 1 (`deflateRawSync`), and inflate bounded by `maxOutputLength` (`inflateRawSync`): past the
limit `too_large`, data that is no raw deflate stream `corrupt`.

packages/chord/src/node/compression.ts.comment:
Compression for Chord v2 hosts on Node (§22, slice 4b): the synchronous compressor `createHost({ compression })`

takes, over Node's zlib. Node-only, so it lives in `src/node`, outside the portable core (which imports no Node

module).

Responses (slice 10 §2, D5, R6; decision "The HTTP component's security baseline" (4), (6)): routes return

packages/chord/src/node/http/upgrades.ts.comment:
Upgraded connections (slice 10 §2, D6, Q6): the links endpoint (`host.accept` over a WebSocket with a per-socket

output cap) and plugin sockets (a `ws` WebSocket handed to the contribution's handler for its own protocol, in a scope

lasting until it closes, kept alive by a heartbeat). Each connection is kept with what admitted it: when that leaves

(its allowed host, its relay, its socket handler) it is terminated at once and its scope sealed (decision "Slice 10

fix round, allowed hosts only through contributions"); the component's close closes all (1001), terminating at its

timeout those that never acknowledge.

packages/chord/src/node/plugins/build.ts.comment:
Building (slice 7c §2, slice 12 §1-§4): one facet of one plugin as one script, by esbuild from cold. Its own files,

files of other plugins of its root imported by relative path (copies; decision "Contracts come from where the

plugin's code came from") and its npm `dependencies` (through their `exports`) are inlined; host packages, this

component, `chord.external` packages and Node builtins stay external, answered at evaluation by the `require` the

script takes. Every import is checked by the file it resolves to: a per-kind file only for its kind, the app's API

only at a listed version the kind provides, one version per facet, never Chord directly. The result is plain data,

the same value a worker or a page evaluates where it runs; a failed build is a result, never a throw.

symbols.name: ScopedCss
symbols.signature: export type ScopedCss = { readonly css: string; readonly classes: Readonly<Record<string, string>> };
symbols.comment: A CSS module scoped: its stylesheet with unique class names, and the mapping its import gives.
symbols.output: { readonly css: string; readonly classes: Readonly<Record<string, string>> }

symbols.name: SCOPED_CSS
symbols.comment: The namespace of a scoped stylesheet the facet's build imports.

symbols.name: scopeCssModule
symbols.signature: export async function scopeCssModule(plugin: string, dir: string, file: string, contents: string): Promise<ScopedCss>
symbols.comment:
Scopes the CSS module `file` of the plugin `plugin` (its directory `dir`) with `contents`: every class renamed
`chord_<hash of plugin and path>_<file>_<class>`. Throws esbuild's failure (a syntax error) for the build to report.

packages/chord/src/node/plugins/css-modu.comment:
CSS modules in plugin builds (slice 11 §4b, decision "Looks and themes"; fix round 1, Opus L1): a plugin's

`*.module.css` has its class names made unique to the file, the import giving the mapping, so twenty plugins'

`.card` never collide. esbuild's `local-css` loader names classes uniquely within one build only (and a minified

build names them `.a`, `.b`), while each facet is a build of its own; so each CSS module is scoped by a small build of

its own whose names start with a prefix of the plugin and the file, and the facet's build gets the scoped stylesheet

and the mapping. The mapping is esbuild's own (`composes` and escaped names as esbuild gives them); `url()` and

`@import` stay as written and resolve in the facet's build, relative to the module (an `@import`ed file is plain CSS,

its classes not scoped).

packages/chord/src/node/plugins/discover.comment:
Discovery (slice 7c §1, slice 12 §2, §4): the plugins under the app's roots, found by listing each root and reading

only `package.json` files. Each directory at a root's top is a package: the plugins its `chord.plugins` manifest

lists (decision "`chord.plugins` is a package's manifest of plugins"), else by convention itself when its top has

facet files, else its subfolders with a `package.json` (a checkout of several), else itself (contracts only). Files

named `<name>.<kind>.<ext>` at a root's top are single-file plugins grouped by name. Facet files are the ones named

after the app's facet kinds. Nothing parses or runs plugin code.

packages/chord/src/node/plugins/evaluate.comment:
Evaluating (slice 7c §3): a built script run with `vm.Script` in this context under a stable filename per (plugin,

kind, digest), given the `require` that answers its external imports: the host packages (one instance per process),

this component's `pluginFile` bound to the plugin's directory, and `chord.external` packages and Node builtins from

the plugin's own `node_modules`. No module map and no cache: an old facet's closures are collected once nothing holds

them.

packages/chord/src/node/plugins/index.ts.comment:
Chord v2's plugins component (`@earendil-works/chord/plugins`; slices 7c, 12): plugin directories and single-file

plugins found, built into scripts checked against the app's API, evaluated, loaded and reloaded per plugin, watched,

rolled out and installed, and a plugin tested alone. Node-only (`fs`, esbuild, `vm`); esbuild is an optional peer

dependency, imported only here.

symbols.comment: What `installPlugin` takes besides the source and the root.

symbols.comment: The app's facet kinds: a package whose top has a facet file is one plugin (`[]` by default).

	| { readonly npm: string; readonly version: string }

symbols.comment: The install's arguments: production dependencies only, no host peers, no scripts, no audit or funding notes.

symbols.name: installDependencies
symbols.comment:
Installs `plugin`'s `dependencies` into its own `node_modules` (`npm install --omit=dev --legacy-peer-deps
--ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund` in its real directory; git dependencies with a ref are npm's). Rejects with
the command's output when it fails, and when `context` aborts (the command is killed). A single-file plugin has
nothing to install.

symbols.name: installPlugin
symbols.comment:
Installs new plugins into `root` from `source`, then their dependencies: from git, a shallow clone of the ref into
`<root>/<repository name>`; from npm, the packed package extracted into `<root>/<name>`. The package's plugins are
its `chord.plugins` folders, else by convention (discovery's rules). Returns their names. Refused: a source option
(`-…`), an invalid name, an existing directory (no updating in place: install another ref, or delete and install), a
package discovery reports a problem in or finds no plugin in, a plugin name another plugin of `options.roots` has.
Only what this install created is removed on failure.
