refuses the install and a concurrent install of the same name loses here; returns what it created.
symbols.output: Promise<{ readonly target: string; readonly scope?: string }>

packages/chord/src/node/plugins/stack.ts.comment:
Stack traces of plugin scripts (slice 7c §3, decision Q1 (b)): `vm.Script` maps no positions through a source map, so

every evaluated script registers its map under its filename while something of its evaluation lives (its facet, or

the error it threw while evaluated), and `mapStack` rewrites an error's stack through them, for the app's reporters.

Nothing global: no `Error.prepareStackTrace`, no process-wide source-map switch. The registry is a module-level `Map`

keyed by filename, not a `WeakMap` keyed by an owner: `mapStack` starts from a stack's text, which names only the

filename. Its entries go with the last evaluation of their script (a `FinalizationRegistry` counts them down).

Testing a plugin alone (slice 12 §6, decision "Testing a plugin alone"): the plugin built as production builds it,

evaluated with the app's real API modules, loaded on an in-memory host (a `:memory:` SQLite store) beside stub facets

and a new reading of its metadata for its `package.json`, for discovery for a facet file at its top); a single-file
plugin's file dirties it (and asks for discovery when it is gone); elsewhere under a root (a directory or a
single-file plugin's file added or removed, a directory that is no plugin yet), discovery; every plugin whose
facets read the file is dirty too.

packages/chord/src/node/plugins/watcher..comment:
The watcher and its marks (slice 7c §5, slice 12 §4): `fs.watch` on every directory of the plugin roots and the app's

base code, `node_modules` and `.git` never watched (a directory appearing later gets its watch), marks what changed and

never applies it. A changed file dirties every plugin whose facets used it (a copied contract every user), whose

directory contains it or which is a single-file plugin of it; a changed `package.json` asks for an install (and for

its metadata to be read again); a plugin directory, a facet file or a single-file plugin's file added or removed asks

for discovery again; a file of base code asks the app to restart its hosts. The

marks are a JSON watchable; each mark records the generation of its latest change (generations only increase), so a

change during a build keeps its mark, however late an older build's rollout clears.

Throws esbuild's failure: the server does not start with a broken base.

last script) without waiting for clients; the files of the last few sets stay served for clients that still load

them.

`WebScripts` showing the current set, and the page through the app's own template; everything as `Http`

contributions of the surface's facet, which the app puts among the server's core facets. The app keeps its HTML,

CSS, components and themes.

symbols.comment:
The launcher's prompt on the real terminal, `columns` wide: `ask` shows `lines` (the question last) and resolves
with the user's answer, yes or no; `write` writes to the terminal past the output filter (the launcher's own
sequences).

symbols.signature: export function promptLines(lines: readonly string[], columns: number): string[]
symbols.comment: The prompt's rows for `lines` at `columns` wide: control characters removed, each line wrapped, never cut.

symbols.signature: export function wrap(line: string, width: number): string[]
symbols.comment:
`line` with control characters removed, in rows of at most `width` columns, counting every character but printable
ASCII as two (wide characters never push text past the edge, where the next row would cover it).

symbols.name: SHOWN_ROWS
symbols.comment: How many rows of a copied text the prompt shows before "and N more characters".

symbols.name: act
symbols.comment:
Does the sandbox's `request` (`copy`, `open`) once the user confirmed it: whether it was done. Throws (the request
refused) for text it will not copy and URLs it will not open. `opener` opens a URL (the platform's by default).

symbols.name: MAX_ATTACHMENT
symbols.comment: The largest file the sandbox may be given: 16 MiB.

symbols.name: attach
symbols.comment:
Reads the file at `path` (as the sandbox gave it; `~/` the home directory) for the sandbox once the user confirmed
it: its name and bytes, or `null` when declined. Refused at once: a path with control, format or unusual whitespace
characters, and on Windows a UNC, device or `//host` path or a reserved device name. Nothing on the machine is looked
at before the user's yes (Opus E9: on Windows a lookup of `\\host\share` alone sends the user's credentials): the
prompt shows the path resolved by its text (`~`, `.` and `..`); after the yes its links are resolved, and a path
that leads elsewhere is asked about again, showing where; what is opened must be the file confirmed (its device and
inode as when the last prompt was shown). Then it is opened without blocking (a FIFO waits for no
writer: Opus E12) and read only when it is a regular file of at most `MAX_ATTACHMENT` bytes; one refusal for anything
else (no hint what is there).
symbols.output: Promise<{ readonly name: string; readonly bytes: Uint8Array } | null>

symbols.signature: function attachable(path: string, platform: NodeJS.Platform): boolean
symbols.comment:
Whether `path` may be shown and, once confirmed, opened on `platform`: no character that hides or moves what the
prompt shows (controls, format characters such as bidirectional and zero-width ones, whitespace but single spaces
between words: Opus E5), and on Windows no UNC, device or `//host` path and no reserved device name (Opus E9).

symbols.comment: The prompt's lines for the file at `file`: its name, its directory, then `question`.

symbols.comment:
The command and arguments opening `url` on `platform`, as the coding agent opens a browser (`open-browser.ts`): never
a shell (on Windows not `cmd /c start`, whose parsing runs what follows a `&`): `rundll32
url.dll,FileProtocolHandler <url>` on Windows, `open` on macOS, `xdg-open` elsewhere, the URL one argument.

symbols.name: platformOpener
symbols.comment: Opens `url` with the platform's opener (`openerCommand`), detached, best effort: a missing opener is no crash.

packages/chord/src/node/tui/actions.ts.comment:
The launcher's actions (slice 11 §4; fix rounds 1 to 4: Fable's H1, H2, M1, L4, L6 and Opus's M1, M3, L2, L3, E5,

E6, E9, E12, R1): what the sandbox may ask of the machine, each confirmed by the user on the launcher's own prompt

before it touches it. Every line the prompt shows is wrapped to the terminal's width, never cut. Copying writes the

text to the terminal's clipboard (OSC 52, which the output filter refuses to sandboxed code) and shows it first (up

to five rows, then how many more characters); text with control characters (a newline and a tab aside) or

bidirectional controls is refused. Opening a URL (http or https, no user info) names its host first and runs the

platform's opener without a shell (as the coding agent's `open-browser.ts`). Attaching refuses a path with control,

format or unusual whitespace characters (and on Windows UNC and device paths), shows the path resolved by its text

(its name on its own line) without looking at the machine, after the user's yes resolves its links and asks again

when they lead elsewhere, and reads the very file confirmed (its device and inode), a regular file of at most 16 MiB,

exactly at the size its open handle has.

symbols.comment:
The terminal's output filter (slice 11 §4; p2's `tui-filter.ts`): the only path from the sandbox to the real

terminal. A frame's text and the escape sequences a terminal UI needs to draw pass (cursor moves, erasing, colours,

the alternate screen, bracketed paste, synchronized output, mouse reporting); every other sequence is dropped, so

sandboxed code cannot set the clipboard (OSC 52), retitle or reconfigure the terminal, or smuggle a sequence across

frames: an unterminated one ends with its frame.

The longest frame the sandbox may write.

sandboxed code cannot set the clipboard (OSC 52), retitle or reconfigure the terminal, or smuggle a sequence across

The longest frame the sandbox may write.

packages/chord/src/node/tui/launcher.ts.comment:
`startTerminal` (slice 11 §4, decision "Slice 11, P8"): the trusted launcher of a terminal client. It signs in with

its token (given, from a file, or by pairing), downloads the terminal kind's base bundle and plugin scripts, and

runs them in the sandbox, always. It keeps the credentials, the real terminal and the user's choices: the sandbox

gets input and resizes, its frames pass the output filter, its Chord link is a socket the launcher opens and relays,

its plugin script fetches go only to the terminal surface's files, and its actions on the machine (copy, open a URL,

attach a file) are confirmed by the launcher's own prompt. A new base bundle on the server starts a new sandbox.

Nothing the sandbox sends can end the launcher (fix round 2, Opus E3): its messages are checked (`pipe.ts`), a send

on a socket not yet open is dropped, every buffer and the requests in flight are bounded, a signal cannot open the

launcher's inspector, and however the launcher's process ends the terminal is given back (fix round 3, Opus E8,

E10, E11). During a prompt Ctrl-C ends the client: its keys are the launcher's; and three Ctrl-C within a second

always end it (Opus R2).

packages/chord/src/node/tui/pipe.ts.comment:
The launcher's end of the sandbox's pipes (slice 11 §4; fix round 2: the sandbox a child process): messages as

plain length-prefixed binary frames, not Node's IPC. A frame is a 4-byte big-endian length, then the payload: a

4-byte big-endian header length, the header (the message as JSON, its body field left out), and the body (the raw

bytes of `bytes`, or the UTF-8 text of `data`). The sandbox's bootstrap has the same codec (`sandbox.ts`). What the

sandbox sends is untrusted: each frame is bounded, and each message checked here before the launcher acts on it.

symbols.name: MAX_BUNDLE
symbols.comment: The largest base bundle a sandbox runs: 8 MiB.

symbols.name: SANDBOX_BUILTINS
symbols.comment:
The builtins code in the sandbox may `require`, each computation in memory without I/O, descriptors or machine
details: bytes and text (`buffer`, `string_decoder`, `punycode`, `querystring`), events and streams in memory
(`events`, `stream` and its submodules), formatting and type checks (`util`, `util/types`), URL and path strings
(`url`, `path`), timers, assertions, hashing and randomness (`crypto`: no keys from files, no network) and compression
in memory (`zlib`). Not `fs`, `tty`, `net`, `dgram`, `dns`, `http`, `https`, `http2`, `tls`, `child_process`,
`cluster`, `worker_threads`, `sqlite`, `inspector`, `vm`, `v8`, `os`, `module`, `process`, `perf_hooks`, `wasi`,
`repl`, `readline`, `trace_events` or anything else.

symbols.name: SANDBOX_PROCESS
symbols.comment:
The sandbox's `process`: a frozen plain object in place of Node's (no event emitter, so no prototype shared with
Node's internals leads back to the real one). Its properties, each harmless: which Node it is (`arch`, `platform`,
`version`, `versions`, `release`), time (`nextTick`, `hrtime`, `uptime`), ending the sandbox (`exit`), the permission
checks (`permission`), the allowed builtins (`getBuiltinModule`), fixed values (`env` empty, `argv`, `argv0`,
`execArgv`, `execPath`, `title`, `cwd` `/`), `stdout` (to the terminal through the bridge) and `stderr` (dropped),
and listener calls that keep nothing (`on`, `once`, `off`, `addListener`, `removeListener`, `removeAllListeners`,
`emit`, `emitWarning`, `listenerCount`, `listeners`). Not `binding`, `_linkedBinding`, `dlopen`, `_rawDebug`, `kill`,
`execve`, `chdir`, `abort`, `reallyExit`, `stdin`, `openStdin`, `report`, `pid`, `ppid`, `config`, the user and group
calls, `loadEnvFile`, `moduleLoadList`, resource and handle listings or any other.

symbols.name: sandboxFlags

The child's Node flags for its script `script`: the permission model allowing only reading that file, no SQLite, a
96 MiB heap. Exported for the tests of the operating system's layer alone.

symbols.name: MAX_UNREAD
symbols.comment: The most bytes waiting for the sandbox to read them before it counts as stuck: 64 MiB.

symbols.name: BOOTSTRAP
symbols.comment:
The trusted bootstrap (strict CommonJS, the child's main script). Before any downloaded code runs it keeps its own
references to what it uses (so code that changes shared prototypes later cannot steer it), closes the file system's
functions, shadows the real `process`'s listener calls, puts the substitute `process` in place, removes the module
globals and leaves the bridge on `globalThis`; then it waits for the launcher's start frame and evaluates the base
bundle through its own `require`. Frames as in `pipe.ts`.

packages/chord/src/node/tui/sandbox.ts.comment:
The terminal's sandbox (slice 11 §4, decision "Slice 11, P8"; fix round 2: a child process, as the owner decided

after the worker thread was escaped through its shared realm): a Node child process of the launcher's binary.

- The operating system's side: its stdin, stdout and stderr are pipes to the launcher (never the terminal: no

descriptor of the child is a TTY), its environment empty, its directory a private one holding only the bootstrap;

Node's permission model with nothing allowed but reading the bootstrap (no other file read, no write, no network,

no child processes, no workers, no addons, no inspector, no WASI) and `node:sqlite` removed

(`--no-experimental-sqlite`: SQLite opens files past the permission model). An escape from the JavaScript layer

reaches no terminal, no file, no socket, no launcher memory or token.

- The JavaScript side, a second layer: downloaded code (the base bundle, a CommonJS script; the plugins' registered

scripts) is only evaluated by the bootstrap (`vm.Script` with no dynamic import callback, so `import()` throws),

with a `require` answering the allowed builtins only (`SANDBOX_BUILTINS`); `process` is a substitute with

`SANDBOX_PROCESS` only. The bootstrap keeps its own references to what it uses before any downloaded code runs.

Messages go both ways as length-prefixed binary frames (`pipe.ts`). Known gaps, each needing the JavaScript layer

broken first unless noted: the child may signal processes of the same user (Node has no permission for signals; the

launcher ignores SIGUSR1, which would open its inspector), read machine details (`os`), learn whether any path exists

(`require.resolve` fails one way for a file that exists, another for one that does not: Opus E13), and allocate

memory outside its heap (no limit without a shell's `ulimit`; only the child dies). Needs Node 26.5.1 or later.

packages/chord/src/node/workers/base.ts.comment:
The worker base (decision "Workers start from the base code the server booted with"): a worker kind's entry and the

base code it imports, bundled once by esbuild when the workers component is created, as the surfaces build their base

bundles at start. Every worker of the kind is forked from this snapshot, so an edit of the app's source while the

server runs reaches workers only through a restart of the server. Packages installed under `node_modules` (native

addons, packages reading their own files) and Node builtins stay external: Node loads them at each fork from where

the build resolved them. Everything else, the app's files and workspace packages linked into `node_modules`, is

inlined. The bundle is split at each dynamic `import()` esbuild can follow: the entry module and the chunks it imports

statically load at each fork, a lazily imported module (pi-ai's provider APIs and the packages they import) only when

the worker imports it. Every file is an ES module with an inline source map, in one private temporary directory.

forked worker never loads esbuild.

it, and the other remove the new holder's file.

packages/chord/src/node/workers/lock.ts.comment:
Process locks (slice 10 §3): one live worker per address. A lock is a listening socket the

kernel owns for the holder's lifetime (an abstract socket on Linux and Android, a named pipe on Windows, a socket file

elsewhere), so there is no race between two would-be holders; a socket file a crashed holder left fails closed for a

taker (the error names it: a takeover would race another taker), and only the one process that starts the holders of

a name clears it (decision "Stale lock files are cleared by the starter"). A child finding the lock held waits

without polling: it connects to the holder's socket, which the holder never answers, and tries again when that

connection closes (the holder exited).

packages/chord/src/node/workers/workers..comment:
The workers component (slice 10 §3, §4; decision "Slice 10's points"): a forked worker process per address of one

host kind, started on demand by the route it owns, stopped when idle, never restarted by itself (R2): a crash, a

`fatal` or a failed start leaves the address failed until `retry` or a rollout. A running worker's lost link is a

stop its holders start a new worker after, once a minute (decision "A lost worker link is recovered from").

Per address, a child's events are recorded on that child as they happen; starts and stops run one after another.

Every worker is forked from the kind's worker base, bundled when the component is created (decision "Workers start

from the base code the server booted with").

packages/chord/src/react/hooks.ts.comment:
React bindings (slice 11 §3, decision "Slice 11, P7"; p2's `useObject`, `useReadable`, `useRegistry`): a host in

context, references held for a component's life, watchables read with `useSyncExternalStore`, page state kept for

(design §21): its releases are plain releases, presence is the app's. A component of a reloaded plugin is a new

function and remounts, its `useState` starting over; what must survive is page state (decision "Tutorial gaps" (1)).

Registries for apps: tokens, what a provider serves them with, the table `compose` gets and its helpers, and the

symbols.signature: serve(version: number, provider: RegistryProvider<unknown, unknown>): void
symbols.comment:
Serves the registry with `provider` at `version` (the defining plugin's facet, checked by `checkProvider` when

symbols.name: RegistryRecord.unserve
symbols.comment:
A reload removed the defining plugin, inside a batch: no provider serves it; its readers' values fail
`unavailable/undeclared` (a reader parked on it waits `not_served`), its contributions stay in the table.

symbols.name: RegistryRecord.composeServed

symbols.name: RegistryRecord.reportUndeclared
symbols.comment:
After a publication's batch, or a batch where an object's contributions entered: with contributions and no
provider, reports `registry_undeclared` naming the contributing plugins, unless the same ones were reported since
a provider last served it.

symbols.name: RegistryRecord.add
symbols.comment: Adds a live contributor's contribution, inside a batch: the table changes.

symbols.name: RegistryRecord.remove
symbols.comment: Removes an ending contributor's contribution, inside a batch: the table changes.

symbols.name: RegistryRecord.contributionChanged
symbols.comment: A followed contribution changed, inside a batch: the table is marked, composed when read or followed.

symbols.name: RegistryRecord.start
symbols.comment:
The current composition, composed now when the table changed: the value, or `compose`'s failure with the last
good one; `unavailable/undeclared` while no provider serves it. A read while it composes is a cycle.

symbols.name: RegistryRecord.composedFrom
symbols.comment: The contributions the current good composition was built from; `undefined` while there is none.

symbols.name: RegistryRecord.inTable
symbols.comment:
Whether every contribution of `from` (what a composition, or a mapping of it, was built from) is still in the
table (decision 5: one that left may have closed the native its entry held).

symbols.name: RegistryRecord.valueAdapter

symbols.name: RegistryRecord.adapt
symbols.comment: Runs an adapter of the provider as a pure compute, counted.

symbols.name: RegistryRecord.reportContribution
symbols.comment: Reports a contribution left out (`contribution_failed`, `contribution_refused`; the caller keeps the episode).

symbols.name: RegistryRecord.failed
symbols.comment: Reports a throw of `compose` or of a value adapter (`registry_failed`; the caller keeps the episode).

symbols.name: RegistryRecord.close
symbols.comment:
The host closed: the contributions stop following their sources, the values end (a value kept by a reader still
reads the last composition).

symbols.name: RegistryRecord.#invalidate
symbols.comment:
The table changed: every version's value is marked and listed (each lists itself once per batch); while it is
not composed since an earlier change, only listed (its dependents are marked already).

symbols.comment:
Builds the table and composes it, unless it is the last one composed, entry for entry (`compose` is pure). A
throw is a failure episode: reported once, the last good composition kept while every contribution it was built
from is still in the table (decision 5: one whose contributor ended may hold a closed native); conflicts are
reported once per episode, as their message and plugins.

symbols.name: RegistryRecord.#build
