packages/chord/src/registries/record.ts.comment:
A registry on a host (slice 8 §1): its provider (replaced or removed by a reload, slice 7b §3), its contributions in table order (`contribution.ts`), the table

and its lazy composition (marked when the table changes, composed when read or followed, in the batch's

deliveries), the reports of conflicts and failures (once per episode) and of contributions nobody serves, and the

values its readers follow by version.

symbols.name: Registry
symbols.comment:
A registry token: its name (as type names, `[a-z0-9@/._~-]`), the version the bundling plugin was built against, the
contribution type `C` and the composed value type `V`. Shared: every contributor and reader bundles its own copy.

symbols.name: "~types"
symbols.comment: Type only: `C` in, `V` out.

symbols.name: RegistryEntry
symbols.comment: One contribution in a registry's table: its plugin, its object type for an object contributor, its version.

symbols.name: type
symbols.comment: The contributing object's type; absent for a facet.

symbols.name: version
symbols.comment: The registry version its contributor was built against (an older one adapted to `C`).

symbols.name: RegistryTable
symbols.comment: A registry's table: one entry per live contributor, sorted by plugin name, then type (a facet's first).

symbols.name: RegistryConflict
symbols.signature: export type RegistryConflict = { readonly message: string; readonly plugins: readonly string[] };
symbols.comment: A conflict `compose` resolved with its fallback: reported as `registry_conflict`, once per conflict episode.
symbols.output: { readonly message: string; readonly plugins: readonly string[] }

symbols.name: ComposeContext
symbols.comment: What `compose` gets besides the table.

symbols.name: report
symbols.comment: Reports a conflict `compose` resolved (the first by plugin name wins, for example).

symbols.name: RegistryAccepts
symbols.comment:
Adapters of older versions, by version, the provider's code: `contribution` maps an older contribution to `C` (once
per contribution value), `value` maps the composed value back for a reader of that version (once per composition).
A plugin annotates the old contribution's type (`(old: HttpV1) => upgrade(old)`).

symbols.name: RegistryProvider
symbols.comment: What the defining plugin's facet serves a registry with (`host.serve(R, provider)`).

symbols.name: compose
symbols.signature: readonly compose: (table: RegistryTable<C>, context: ComposeContext) => V;
symbols.comment:
Composes the table: pure and synchronous, always a value (a fallback built in), conflicts reported. Runs when the
table changed and someone reads or follows the value; a throw is the owner's bug (`registry_failed`, the last
good composition stays).

symbols.name: Contribution
symbols.signature: export type Contribution<C> = C | Watchable<C> | NativeWatchable<C>;
symbols.comment: What a contributor contributes: a plain value, or a Chord watchable of one (followed: its change recomposes).

symbols.name: RegistryValue
symbols.comment:
A registry's composed value as a reader of one version sees it (`self.registry`, `host.registry`): a native
watchable; `.value` is the last good composition (a later throwing `compose` keeps it), a watch gets each new one.

symbols.name: RegistryValue.observe
symbols.comment:
A synchronous observer of its compositions (as Durable's `observeXXX`): `advance` runs inside the batch that
composed, so it only records; an attached observer counts as watching, so the composition runs for it.

symbols.name: defineRegistry
symbols.signature: export function defineRegistry<C, V>(name: string, options: { readonly version: number }): Registry<C, V>
symbols.comment: Declares a registry token: `name` and the `version` this plugin is built against.

packages/chord/src/registries/registry.t.comment:
Registry tokens (design §17, slice 8 D1): `defineRegistry`, shared by every plugin as a contract is (identity and

types only), and what the defining plugin's facet serves it with (`compose`, `accepts`); the table `compose` gets and

the composed value readers follow.

symbols.name: RegistryWaiter
symbols.comment: Who waits for a registry's value (a parked attempt, a `host.registry`): told when it may have changed.

symbols.name: RegistryWaiter.dependencyMoved
symbols.comment: The value may have changed (inside its batch: it only records).

symbols.name: RegistryWaiter.closed
symbols.comment: The value closed with its host: the wait ends with `error` (`released/closed`).

symbols.name: sameError
symbols.signature: function sameError(a: unknown, b: unknown): boolean
symbols.comment: Whether two failures say the same: the same error, or ChordErrors alike (a version mismatch is made per read).

symbols.name: Mapped
symbols.comment:
The last good mapping for an older version, the composition it was made from, and the contributions that composition
was built from (kept only while all are in the table, decision 5).

symbols.name: map
symbols.comment: The adapter it was made with: a reload's provider brings another, which maps again.

symbols.name: MapFailure
symbols.signature: type MapFailure = { readonly from: unknown; readonly map: (current: never) => unknown; readonly error: unknown };
symbols.comment: A failed mapping of composition `from` by `map`, until another composition or adapter maps.
symbols.output: { readonly from: unknown; readonly map: (current: never) => unknown; readonly error: unknown }

symbols.name: Registered
symbols.comment:
Where a value's registry stands for it: on the host, or closed with the host (its last start kept, the record let
go, so a value an app keeps keeps no closed host).
symbols.output:
| { readonly kind: "open"; readonly record: RegistryRecord }
	| { readonly kind: "closed"; readonly last: NativeStart<unknown> }

symbols.name: RegistryValueSource
symbols.comment: One version's view of a registry's composed value.

symbols.name: RegistryValueSource.#readers
symbols.comment: Its readers, each a token of its own (one object may read twice), until released.

symbols.name: RegistryValueSource.#waiters
symbols.signature: readonly #waiters = new Set<{ readonly waiter: RegistryWaiter }>();
symbols.comment: Its waiters, each a token of its own, until released.

symbols.name: RegistryValueSource.#told
symbols.signature: #told: { readonly kind: "usable" } | { readonly kind: "failed"; readonly error: unknown } | undefined;
symbols.comment:
What its waiters were last told: usable (a value, or a failure with a last good one), or the error it has none
for; a change wakes them.
symbols.output: { readonly kind: "usable" } | { readonly kind: "failed"; readonly error: unknown } | undefined

symbols.name: RegistryValueSource.constructor
symbols.signature: constructor(record: RegistryRecord, version: number, batch: Batch)

symbols.name: RegistryValueSource.value
symbols.comment: The composition (or its mapping) at its last good value; throws the failure when there is none.

symbols.name: RegistryValueSource.start
symbols.comment:
Its composition (mapped for an older version), composed now if its table changed; a change of whether it is
usable, or of its failure while it is not, wakes its waiters.

symbols.name: RegistryValueSource.current
symbols.comment: Its composition (or mapping) now; throws while it is failed, though `.value` keeps the last good one.

symbols.name: RegistryValueSource.watched
symbols.comment: Followed while someone watches or observes it, and while waiters wait on it.

symbols.name: RegistryValueSource.read
symbols.comment: Registers a reader (an attempt that declared it) until the returned release: its mapping is kept meanwhile.

symbols.name: RegistryValueSource.wait
symbols.comment:
Registers `waiter` (a parked attempt's object, a waiting `host.registry`) until the returned release: it is told
of every change of whether this value is usable (inside the batch that made it: it only records).

symbols.name: RegistryValueSource.recomposed
symbols.comment: The registry's table changed (inside a batch): its dependents are marked, its followers get the next frame.

symbols.name: RegistryValueSource.relisted
symbols.comment:
The registry's table changed again while not composed since (inside a batch): its dependents are marked already
(none read it meanwhile, or it would be composed); its followers get the next frame. Marking stops here, so a
cycle of registries through their values ends.

symbols.name: RegistryValueSource.close
symbols.comment: The host closed: its watches and observers end, its readers and mapping go; it keeps its last start only.

symbols.name: RegistryValueSource.unfollowed
symbols.comment: Nobody follows it: without readers, its mapping goes (computed again on the next read).

symbols.name: RegistryValueSource.#tell
symbols.comment:
Wakes the waiters when `start` says something else than they were told (by usability, then by the error); while
it is not usable, the wait is on its host's clock (`record.clock`).

symbols.name: RegistryValueSource.#mappedStart
symbols.signature:
#mappedStart(
		record: RegistryRecord,
		current: NativeStart<unknown>,
		map: (current: never) => unknown,
	): NativeStart<unknown>
symbols.comment:
The composition `current` mapped back with `map`, once per composition; a throwing mapping fails this version
only (reported once per episode), keeping its last good mapping; a composition mapped before heals it.

packages/chord/src/registries/value.ts.comment:
Registry values (slice 8 §1 "Reading", S2, S3): a registry's composed value as the readers of one version see it, a

native source. The provider's version reads the composition itself; an older one reads it mapped back with

`accepts[old].value`, once per composition, kept only while someone reads or follows it; a version the provider

cannot serve fails `contract_mismatch`. Its readers (attempts that declared it) keep the mapping; its waiters

(attempts parked on it, a waiting `host.registry`) are woken at every change of whether it is usable, and of its

failure while it is not (dependency model §9); waited for while it is not, it is on the host's `UnboundClock`.

symbols.name: QueuedCall
symbols.signature: export type QueuedCall = { readonly hold: number; readonly send: () => void };
symbols.comment:
The call window (§3, decision log "Flow control: an ack-clocked window"): at most the peer's N calls in flight on a

link from this host; further calls wait in one FIFO queue, sent in order as replies free slots.

A call waiting for a slot: its hold (a rebind or release takes it out) and what sends it.
symbols.output: { readonly hold: number; readonly send: () => void }

symbols.name: CallWindow
symbols.signature: export class CallWindow<C extends QueuedCall = QueuedCall> {
symbols.comment:
The calls of one link's consumer side. `limit` is the peer's N from its `hello` (0 before it, so every call waits).
A relay forwards its downstream calls at once, so only this host's own calls are counted here.

symbols.name: CallWindow.submit
symbols.comment: Sends `call` now when a slot is free and nothing waits, otherwise queues it behind the earlier calls.

symbols.name: CallWindow.opened
symbols.comment: The peer's window arrived with its `hello`: waiting calls go out.

symbols.name: CallWindow.freed
symbols.comment: A call in flight ended (its reply, its abort sent, its hold released or gone): its slot is free.

symbols.name: CallWindow.remove
symbols.comment: Takes a waiting call out (its caller cancelled); nothing happens for one that is not waiting.

symbols.name: CallWindow.removeHold
symbols.comment: Takes every waiting call of `hold` out and returns them (its hold rebinds or was released).

symbols.name: CallWindow.clear
symbols.comment: Takes every waiting call out and returns them (the link closed).

symbols.name: CallWindow.#drain
symbols.comment: Sends waiting calls in order while slots are free.

packages/chord/src/remote/calls.ts.comment:
The call window (§3, decision log "Flow control: an ack-clocked window"): at most the peer's N calls in flight on a

link from this host; further calls wait in one FIFO queue, sent in order as replies free slots.

A call waiting for a slot: its hold (a rebind or release takes it out) and what sends it.

symbols.name: Reply
symbols.comment: A reply to a call.

symbols.name: OutgoingCall
symbols.comment:
A call through this side: waiting for a slot of the call window (no id yet), then in flight under its id until its
reply, its abort, its hold's release or `gone`, or the link's close.

symbols.name: method
symbols.comment: The method's index in the bound variant and its arguments' part.

symbols.name: trace
symbols.comment: The caller's trace carrier (its `chord.call` span's), when its adapter propagates.

symbols.name: old
symbols.comment: Whether the caller is old work of a reload here (`call.old`: the provider routes it to open old attempts).

symbols.name: ConsumerSide
symbols.comment:
The consumer side of one link. Ids are its own counters, from 0; a reply naming an id this side gave up is ignored
(Q1). When the link closes, every call rejects `unavailable` (never resent) and its path tells every holder.

symbols.name: ConsumerSide.attach
symbols.signature: attach(holder: RemoteObject, chain: string[] | undefined, trace: TelemetryCarrier | undefined): number
symbols.comment:
Holds `holder` on this link and returns its new id: its first hold, or a re-hold on a new link; `chain`: the
activation chain it is held for, if any (Q5); `trace`: this hold's carrier, if any.

symbols.name: ConsumerSide.call
symbols.signature: call(hold: number, method: number, data: MethodData, args: unknown, context: Context): Promise<unknown>
symbols.comment:
Calls method `method` (an index into the bound variant) on hold `hold` with `args`: left out for a method without
arguments, with byte segments when its argument schema has a `bytes()` leaf, deflated above the threshold except on
the parent link; with the carrier of `context`'s span when its adapter propagates. The result is parsed here. The
caller's cancellation rejects it at once and sends `abort` when it is in flight.

symbols.name: ConsumerSide.release
symbols.comment: Hold `hold` was released: the provider is told, its calls fail with `error`.

symbols.name: ConsumerSide.retry
symbols.comment: `ref.retry()` on a failed hold, with `hops` left of its budget: the provider is asked for an attempt now.

symbols.name: ConsumerSide.forget
symbols.comment: Drops hold `hold` from the tables; its calls, in flight and waiting, fail with `error` and free their slots.

symbols.name: ConsumerSide.opened
symbols.comment: The peer's `hello` arrived: calls go out within its window.

symbols.name: ConsumerSide.message
symbols.comment:
Handles one message from the provider: this host's own, or (with an origin) one for a relayed hold. A `bound`,
`state` or `result` with deflated parts to inflate asynchronously returns that promise and is handled after it.

symbols.name: ConsumerSide.closed
symbols.comment: The link closed: calls in flight and waiting reject `unavailable` (never resent, §7); the tables are dropped.

symbols.name: ConsumerSide.#send
symbols.comment: Sends a call that got its slot, with the next id.

symbols.name: ConsumerSide.#cancel
symbols.comment:
Cancels `call`: a waiting one leaves the window and nothing is sent; one in flight sends `abort` and frees its
slot. Settling the caller is the caller's.

symbols.name: ConsumerSide.#deflated
symbols.comment:
The deflated parts of this side's own holds in `entries` that wait for an asynchronous inflate, each with the
link's decoded limit; `undefined` when none does (nothing allocated). Entries of holds this side gave up are not
inflated (Q1).

symbols.name: ConsumerSide.#bound
symbols.comment:
One `bound` message: every entry prepared first (one that does not fit closes the link before anything changed)
and applied in one batch; then the references go live, and the message is acknowledged. An entry with a part past
the link's limits fails only its hold (`too_large/part`); the others apply.

symbols.name: ConsumerSide.#state
symbols.comment: One `state` message, as `#bound` does it.

symbols.name: ConsumerSide.#adopt
symbols.comment: Applies prepared entries in one batch of this host, so no watch or derive sees half a provider commit (W1).

symbols.name: ConsumerSide.#loading
symbols.comment:
`loading`: the hold's object, or its relay's upstream, starts over; its calls still waiting for a slot reject
`unavailable` (they may name a method of the old variant), its calls in flight wait for their reply (a provider's
`loading` keeps them; a relay's upstream drop answered them before).

symbols.name: ConsumerSide.#failed
symbols.comment:
`failed`: its holder fails; its calls still waiting for a slot reject with the cause (a bound hold is unbound by it,
slice 7b; its calls in flight are rejected by the provider).

symbols.name: ConsumerSide.#gone
symbols.comment:
`gone`: one for a hold this side gave up is ignored (Q1); the holder ends, which forgets its hold here and fails
its calls.

symbols.name: ConsumerSide.#reply
symbols.comment:
A reply: its call settles with the parsed result or the error. A result past the link's limits rejects the call
`too_large/part`. A malformed part rejects the call `unavailable` and throws (a protocol error: the link closes).
A result to inflate asynchronously is inflated first (for a call still waiting), then handled again.

symbols.name: ConsumerSide.#failCalls
symbols.comment: Fails `hold`'s calls in flight and waiting with `error`; each in-flight one frees its slot.

packages/chord/src/remote/consumer.ts.comment:
The consumer side of a link (§7, §22, W1): the holds this host's own remote references sent on it, by this side's

ids, the calls through them within the peer's call window, and each `bound` and `state` message applied to their

replicas as one batch, then acknowledged. Messages with an origin answer holds this host relays: they go to that

origin's provider side. On a host without a compressor, the deflated parts of this host's own holds and calls are

inflated asynchronously first, and the message is handled once they are.

symbols.name: HoldMessage
symbols.comment: A `hold` message.

symbols.name: HoldRequest
symbols.comment:
What a `hold` message asks for. Whom it acts for is not part of it: a host takes that from the message once, as its
link allows (`ProviderSide`), and names it again only on a route link (`actingFor`). Its `chain` and `limit` are the
ones this host honours, sent on as they are when it relays the hold.

symbols.name: Followed
symbols.comment:
A state member a bound hold follows: its index in the bound version, its source and subscription (which feeds this
record), its own encoder (R1, path interning) and the ops waiting for a slot of the window.

symbols.name: source
symbols.comment: Its source (subscribed when it changes, a constant's never).

symbols.name: HoldState
symbols.comment:
Where a hold stands: `unplaced` in the unbound index until the host's publication places it; `pending` until its
object is live (the activation, parking and retries; `told`: the failure its consumer was told, so the next attempt
is announced with `loading` and a call that crossed the failure on the wire gets it); `binding` while its object is live and its `bound` waits for a slot;
`bound` with the object's variant and the members it follows. A `pending` hold unbound with `loading` and the
`binding` after it keep the names it was bound with, `previous`: its consumer's calls sent by those names (before it
learnt of the `loading`) wait at its object's gate and are answered by name, design §22; only contract data, so the
old instance and its sources go meanwhile.

symbols.name: variant
symbols.comment: The bound variant's data at the hold's version.

symbols.name: names
symbols.comment: The bound version's names of the variant, which the wire's indexes point into.

symbols.name: followed
symbols.comment: The members it follows, in the order they were subscribed.

symbols.name: instance
symbols.comment: The instance it was bound to: it follows it on while it still changes (a restart's open old attempt).

symbols.name: previous
symbols.signature: readonly previous?: BoundNames & { readonly until: number };
symbols.comment:
A rebinding's names before it (`until`: its `bound`, this host's own message number): calls its consumer sent
before it applied that `bound` carry their indexes, so they are decoded by them until its `ack`.

symbols.name: Bound
symbols.comment: A bound hold's state.

symbols.name: BoundNames
symbols.signature: type BoundNames = { readonly variant: VariantData; readonly names: VariantNames };
symbols.comment: What calls need of a binding: its variant's data at the hold's version and the names the wire's indexes point into.
symbols.output: { readonly variant: VariantData; readonly names: VariantNames }

symbols.name: Hold
symbols.signature: export class Hold implements Holder, UnboundRequest {
symbols.comment:
One hold served here: a reference to its object acting as its caller (the hold's principal). While pending, each
failure of its object is sent as `failed` (with the rest of its backoff window) and the next attempt as `loading`; a
hold that cannot be taken holds nothing: `failed { waiting }` (not served, another version) until a publication
re-runs its start, `failed { broken }` (invalid params, a cycle) until a `retry` does. Once live it binds when its
link's window has a slot, then sends a part per batch that changed its members (or keeps their ops pending while the
window is full), and `gone` when its object ends. It counts as one of the host's references from its arrival to its
end, bound or not.

symbols.name: Hold.dependent
symbols.comment: A hold is declared by no object on this host.

symbols.name: Hold.listed
symbols.comment: Presence lists show every hold.

symbols.name: Hold.caller
symbols.comment: Whom the hold acts for: its calls run as it, with its origin's incarnation.

symbols.name: Hold.limits
symbols.comment: The limits per part of its params and its calls' arguments: its link's, the decoded one smaller when stamped (Q2).

symbols.name: Hold.#request
symbols.comment: What it asks for (its params owned), once it started: it is placed again after a reload left it unbound.

symbols.name: Hold.#object
symbols.comment: The held object, from its binding until the hold is released.

symbols.name: Hold.#changes
symbols.comment: The members the current batch changed, with their ops, in order.

symbols.name: Hold.#failed
symbols.comment: The members that failed since the last message that carried this hold.

symbols.name: Hold.#retired
symbols.comment: The members whose document was retired since the last message that carried this hold (ORed while it waits).

symbols.name: Hold.#counted
symbols.comment: Whether the hold counts as one of the host's references (`host.activity`): from its arrival until it ends.

symbols.name: Hold.constructor
symbols.signature: constructor(id: number, provider: ProviderSide, caller: Caller, limits: Limits)

symbols.name: Hold.bound
symbols.comment: Whether the hold is bound: its members' changes are sent.

symbols.name: Hold.callable
symbols.comment:
Whether calls on it reach its object: bound, or by the names it was bound with while it rebinds (after a `loading`
unbind: its fresh `bound` not sent yet).

symbols.name: Hold.refusal
symbols.comment:
What a call it does not take is refused with: the failure its consumer was told (refused, or failed while pending:
the call crossed that `failed` on the wire, and its consumer shows that cause), else `not_ready` (not bound yet).

symbols.name: Hold.#names
symbols.comment:
The names its calls are decoded by: its binding's (its previous ones until its consumer acknowledged the `bound`
that brought them: another variant's indexes name other methods), or the ones it was bound with while it rebinds.

symbols.name: Hold.principal
symbols.comment: Whom it acts for (the unbound index's revocation).

symbols.name: Hold.contract
symbols.comment: Its consumer's contract version and fingerprint (its request's): the provider binds them or it waits.

symbols.name: Hold.unbound
symbols.comment: Whether the hold holds no object: before the publication, or refused (revocation ends it, §4).

symbols.name: Hold.start
symbols.comment:
Admits the hold: before the host's publication it waits in the unbound index, placed by the publication.
Then its params within the link's part limit (`too_large/part`), then relayed (it is replaced by a relayed hold),
or served here, its params opened and parsed (a malformed part is a protocol error), its object taken and followed
(`moved`) in the turn it arrived. A hold that cannot be served here waits refused (`#refuse`).

symbols.name: Hold.wake
symbols.comment:
Woken by the unbound index (out of it already): before the publication, placed now; refused `waiting`, its start
runs again, announced with `loading` (then `bound` or `failed`).

symbols.name: Hold.moved
symbols.comment:
The object's state changed, or the hold took it: a pending hold binds once its object shows it live (when a slot
is free), sends each failure, and announces the attempt after a failure with `loading`. A bound hold (or one whose
`bound` waits for a slot) whose object no longer shows it live goes back to pending (slice 7b §6).

symbols.name: Hold.#shown
symbols.comment:
What its object shows to its version and fingerprint: `live` also while a restart's open old attempt binds them
(decision "Reload restarts every affected object", rule 5).

symbols.name: Hold.#memberFailed
symbols.comment: Member `followed` failed with `error`: its failure waits to be sent, replacing one still waiting.

symbols.name: Hold.#memberHealed
symbols.comment: Member `index` has a value again: a failure of it still waiting to be sent (rare) is not sent.

symbols.name: Hold.#unbind
symbols.comment:
Its object no longer shows it live (a restart, a live failure): no longer subscribed or waiting for a slot,
pending again. With `error` (a failure, sent by `#pending`, which a consumer applies to a bound hold as a rebinding
too, model §5) its calls in flight are rejected. Without (`loading`, which tells the consumer it rebinds) they stay,
and calls by the names it was bound with keep arriving (sent before its consumer learnt of the `loading`): each gets
exactly one answer from what it waits on, the instance it already runs on (its result, or `released` at the seal)
or its object's gate (the new instance's result, its failure, `park_timeout`, its end), design §22.

symbols.name: Hold.retry
symbols.signature: retry({ hops }: Extract<Message, { readonly kind: "retry" }>): void
symbols.comment:
A `retry` message with `hops` left of its budget: the object is asked for an attempt now (it ignores this unless
failed; parked, it passes it on, to other hosts with one hop less); a refused hold is started again (a route's
`authorize` may admit it now).

symbols.name: Hold.#pending
symbols.comment: The pending hold's part of `moved`: binds once live, sends each failure, announces the next attempt.

symbols.name: Hold.#restart
symbols.comment: Starts a refused hold again, announced with `loading`.

symbols.name: Hold.call
symbols.signature: call(method: string, args: unknown, parent: TelemetryContext, context: Context): Promise<unknown>
symbols.comment: Calls a method of the held object as the hold's caller, its span under `parent` (the call's carrier, extracted).

symbols.name: Hold.method
symbols.signature: method(index: number): { readonly name: string; readonly resultBytes: boolean }
symbols.comment:
The method at `index` of the bound variant (while it rebinds, of the names its consumer still has: its object answers
by name) and whether its result carries byte segments (its schema has a `bytes()` leaf). Throws on an index outside
the variant (a protocol error); a hold that is not callable has none.
symbols.output: { readonly name: string; readonly resultBytes: boolean }

symbols.name: Hold.boundEntry
symbols.comment:
The hold's binding, sent when a slot is free. The snapshot of every member, as a value or failed, and the
subscription are taken in this synchronous step (race 2), so each member's next ops continue exactly from it.
Names travel as indexes into the bound version (2b). Counts one encode (`chord.link.encodes`).

symbols.name: Hold.entry
symbols.comment:
This batch's entry of the `state` message: the members it changed with their ops, each encoded once with its
member's encoder, and the members that failed; resets both. Counts one encode per hold (`chord.link.encodes`).

symbols.name: Hold.queue
symbols.comment: The window is full: this batch's ops join the members' pending queues (raw, never mutated).

symbols.name: Hold.pendingEntry
symbols.comment:
The entry of a freed slot's `state` message: each member's pending ops encoded once, or `[["r", value]]` after an
overflow, all reflecting the latest commit; and the members that failed meanwhile. Counts one encode per hold.

symbols.name: Hold.release
symbols.comment: The consumer released the hold, or its link closed: its waits stop and its object loses this reference.

symbols.name: Hold.drop
symbols.comment: Ends the hold without releasing its object (the host closes and ends its objects itself).

symbols.name: Hold.end
symbols.comment:
The object ended while held (revocation; a reload, slice 7b), or the hold was revoked (or its host closed) while it
held no object: the hold sends `gone` with `error`.

symbols.name: Hold.#bindTo
symbols.comment:
The binding: its variant and names at the hold's version, with no member followed yet, and the names its consumer
still has (a rebinding's) until it acknowledged this `bound`, the next of this host's own messages.

symbols.name: Hold.retarget
symbols.comment: A hold over a link follows its object's instances in `moved` (a fresh `bound` for a new one).

symbols.name: Hold.following
symbols.comment: It moves nothing in `retarget`.

symbols.name: Hold.removed
symbols.comment:
Its object left it (slice 7b §6): its type was removed (`not_served`) or its provider no longer binds the hold's
version (`version`): no longer subscribed, its calls in flight rejected, it waits refused with `removal.cause` in
the host's index (a publication starts it again) and the consumer is sent `failed`, which unbinds a bound hold.

symbols.name: Hold.#follow
symbols.signature: #follow(state: Bound, index: number, source: DeriveSource): void
symbols.comment:
Follows member `index` from its snapshot on (a failed one too: it may recover in this hold): its own encoder and
pending queue, and a subscription feeding its calls into this hold's batch. Failures fold per member: a failure
drops what was pending for it and replaces a failure not sent yet (one at most per member, however long the
consumer stalls); the value after it (a root replacement) replaces the failure. A retirement waits for a value.

symbols.name: Hold.#take
symbols.comment: Takes the current batch's changes; the hold is untouched again.

symbols.name: Hold.#entry
symbols.comment: A state entry with `members` and the failures and retirements since the last one; counts one encode.

symbols.name: Hold.#refuse
symbols.comment:
Refuses the hold with `cause`, holding nothing: it keeps `request`, indexed under its type while `waiting` (a
publication starts it again), for a `retry` otherwise.

symbols.name: unfollow
symbols.comment: Stops following every member of a bound hold.

symbols.name: owned
symbols.comment: `request` with its params owned, not a view of the message they came in (which the link's buffers may hold).

symbols.name: ActingFor
symbols.comment: A `hold` message's fields naming whom it acts for.

symbols.name: actingFor
symbols.signature: export function actingFor(link: HostLink, { principal, incarnation }: Caller): ActingFor
symbols.comment:
The fields of a `hold` message naming whom it acts for (`caller`): sent only on a route link, whose child honours
them (§4); none elsewhere.

packages/chord/src/remote/hold.ts.comment:
A hold arriving on a link and served here (§7, §22, W1): where it goes once the host published (waiting in the

unbound index until then), why it is unbound (refused: kept in the index while it waits for a name, dependency

model §1), the object it keeps, the notices of its object's failures and new attempts, the snapshot and subscription

taken in one synchronous step when a slot of the window is free, and the ops of its members per batch (sent at

once, or pending while the window is full), each member with its own Delta encoder. Across a reload a bound hold is

kept while its object shows it live (a restart's open old attempt that binds its version, decision "Reload restarts

every affected object"), then unbound (`loading` or `failed`, then a fresh `bound`; a `loading` one keeps its calls

in flight and takes more by its old names); a version no longer bound or a removed type leaves it waiting unbound. A

hold of an older version follows its object's adapted members (Q10).

symbols.name: LinkRole
symbols.comment:
How a link was made: `parent` by `connect` (holds arriving on it may name whom they act for), `child` by `accept`,
`route` by a route's `resolve`.

symbols.name: HostLinkOptions
symbols.comment: What a link is made with.

symbols.name: principal
symbols.comment: The peer, as this host stamps it.

symbols.name: trusted
symbols.comment: Skips the message schema check (framing and the owners' checks still run).

symbols.name: CALLS
symbols.comment: How many concurrent calls a host accepts on each of its links, announced in `hello`.

symbols.name: HostLink
symbols.comment:
A link of a host, both directions over one channel. Closing it, from either end, ends both sides: the provider sides
release the peer's holds, the consumer side's holds go loading until their path's next link.

symbols.name: HostLink.trusted
symbols.comment: Whether the link is trusted: activation chains on holds arriving on it are honoured (Q5).

symbols.name: HostLink.limits
symbols.comment: The limits per part of what arrives on this link (Q2).

symbols.name: HostLink.context
symbols.comment: The parent of the work arriving on this link.

symbols.name: HostLink.#providers
HostLink.#closing
symbols.comment: Aborted when the link closes: stops its asynchronous inflates at once.

symbols.name: HostLink.constructor
symbols.signature: constructor(host: AnyHost, link: Link, options: HostLinkOptions, context: Context)

symbols.name: HostLink.peer
symbols.comment: The peer's incarnation, from its `hello`.

symbols.name: HostLink.greeted
symbols.comment: Whether the peer's `hello` arrived (it may have arrived while the link was made).

symbols.name: HostLink.open
symbols.comment: Whether the link is open; one closed already when made is not kept.

symbols.name: HostLink.tick
symbols.signature: tick(now: number, paused: number, ping: number, close: number): void
symbols.comment: The heartbeat (see `Channel.tick`).

symbols.name: HostLink.part
symbols.comment: A JSON part this host originates on this link: deflated above the threshold when the host compresses.

symbols.name: HostLink.openPart
symbols.signature: openPart(part: Part, limits: Limits, context: Context): string | Uint8Array
symbols.comment: The JSON of a part arriving on this link, where it is owned, within `limits`. Throws as `openPart` does.

symbols.name: HostLink.inflates
symbols.signature: inflates(part: Part | undefined, limits: Limits): part is DeflatedPart
symbols.comment:
Whether `part` waits for an asynchronous inflate before its owner can open it: deflated, not inflated yet, on a
host without a synchronous compressor, and within the wire limit (past it, opening refuses it uninflated).

symbols.name: HostLink.inflate
symbols.signature: async inflate(parts: readonly (readonly [DeflatedPart, number])[], handle: () => void): Promise<void>
symbols.comment:
Inflates `parts` (deflated parts an owner admitted, each with its decoded limit) one after another with the web
`DecompressionStream`, then lets the owner handle its message again (`handle`); the channel holds the link's later
messages until then. A link closed meanwhile stops the inflate at once and drops the message (race 13).

symbols.name: HostLink.message
symbols.comment:
A message from the peer, to its side. One whose owner first waits for an asynchronous inflate returns its promise:
the channel holds later messages until it settled.

symbols.name: HostLink.drop
symbols.comment: `provider` holds nothing any more: it goes (its relay's upstream links are told `closed`).

symbols.name: HostLink.revokeUnbound
symbols.signature: revokeUnbound(revoked: (principal: Principal) => boolean, error: ChordError): void
symbols.comment: Ends the holds on this link that hold nothing and act for a principal `revoked` names (§4).

symbols.name: HostLink.#hold
symbols.comment: A `hold` goes to its origin's provider side, made for the origin's first.

packages/chord/src/remote/host-link.ts.comment:
One link of a host (§3, §22): its channel, its role, the peer's principal, its limits per part, and both sides: a

provider side per origin (holds and calls the peer sent, its own or a relay's for one of its downstream links) and

the consumer side (holds and calls this host sent). Message kinds are directional, so each goes to its side; a

revocation is honoured from the parent only. Parts are made and opened here, with the host's compressor, or inflated

asynchronously for their owner when the host has none.

packages/chord/src/remote/internal.ts.comment:
Remote objects for Chord's layers: a host's links (both sides of each), the paths its upstream holds take, and the

objects of its remote references.

symbols.name: Upstream
symbols.comment: What a path holds on its links: one of this host's remote references, or a hold it relays.

symbols.name: PathEvent
symbols.comment:
What changed on a path without a link, for its route: a holder attached, its link dropped (its holders went
loading), its last holder left.

symbols.name: Path
symbols.comment:
The parent link or one route address: its current link and its holders, held on that link and again on every next
one. `changed` runs when it gets a holder without a link, loses its link or its last holder (a route decides whether
to resolve), saying which.

symbols.name: Path.#linked
symbols.comment: Whether it ever had a link: a host never connected to a parent has no parent path to wait on.

symbols.name: Path.link
symbols.comment: The current link while one is open.

symbols.name: Path.linked
symbols.comment: Whether it had a link once (it may be down now: its holders wait for the next).

symbols.name: Path.held
symbols.comment: Whether anything is held over this path.

symbols.name: Path.attach
symbols.comment: Holds `holder` over this path: on the current link now, and on every next one.

symbols.name: Path.detach
symbols.comment: `holder` was released or ended; no later link holds it.

symbols.name: Path.connected
symbols.comment: `link` is the path's link now: every holder is held on it.

symbols.name: Path.disconnected
symbols.comment: `link` closed (its sides ended their calls already): every holder goes loading until the next link.

symbols.name: Path.unreachable
symbols.comment: Its address cannot be reached for now (a route's `resolve` failed, a suspension): every holder fails waiting.

symbols.name: Path.holders
symbols.comment: Every holder, for the host's close.

packages/chord/src/remote/path.ts.comment:
Paths (§3 recovery): where this host's upstream holds go, the parent link or a route address's link, across links.

Each new link of a path holds every holder of the path again; when it drops, every holder is told.

symbols.name: RunningCall
symbols.comment:
A call being handled: on a hold served here, with whether its result carries byte segments and the abort of its
handler's context; or relayed, its reply forwarded from upstream.

symbols.name: Sender
symbols.comment: Who sent a `bound` or `state` message in flight: this host, or the upstream link a relay forwarded it from.

symbols.name: Relay
symbols.signature: type Relay = { readonly origin: number; readonly links: Set<HostLink> };
symbols.comment: A relaying origin: its number on upstream links, and the open upstream links it relayed holds to.
symbols.output: { readonly origin: number; readonly links: Set<HostLink> }

symbols.name: WINDOW
symbols.comment:
At most this many of this host's own `bound` and `state` messages unacknowledged per origin; past it only the waiting
state a call's answer sends first.

symbols.name: ProviderSide
symbols.comment:
The provider side of one origin on a link. Ids are the origin's; a message naming an id this side does not know is
ignored (Q1), one reusing a live id is a protocol error, and so are more concurrent calls than this side announced.
This host's own `bound` and `state` messages go through the window: locally served holds wait while it is full
(their ops in their members' pending queues, their bindings for the next slot); a call's answer, its own or a
relayed one, sends the waiting state first. A relay forwards upstream messages at once (each upstream host keeps its
own window for the origin it sees), so a slow consumer stalls only its origin.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.origin
symbols.comment: Whose work this side serves: 0 for the peer's own, a relay's number for one of its downstream links.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.#sent
symbols.comment: The sender of each `bound` and `state` message in flight, in order: the consumer acknowledges in order.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.#inFlight
symbols.comment: This host's own messages in flight.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.#ownSent
symbols.comment: How many of this host's own `bound` and `state` messages it sent, and how many its consumer acknowledged.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.#touched
symbols.comment: The holds the current batch touched, in order; its flush sends or queues them.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.#waiting
symbols.comment: Holds whose ops wait in their pending queues for a slot.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.#binding
symbols.comment: Holds waiting for a slot to send their first binding.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.#bindingTurn
symbols.comment: The waiting bindings take the next slot: the last one went to waiting state while they waited.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.#relay
symbols.comment: Set once a hold of this origin is relayed.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.#waitingSince
symbols.comment: When state began waiting for a slot (`performance.now()`), while some waits: `chord.backpressure.wait`.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.constructor
symbols.signature: constructor(link: HostLink, origin: number, limit: number)

symbols.name: ProviderSide.message
symbols.comment: Handles one message of this origin; a call whose arguments wait for an asynchronous inflate returns its promise.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.closed
symbols.comment:
The link closed, or the origin did (`closed`): every hold is released (relayed ones by one `closed` to each
upstream link) and every call aborted.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.send
symbols.comment: Sends `message` on the link with this origin.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.revokeUnbound
symbols.signature: revokeUnbound(revoked: (principal: Principal) => boolean, error: ChordError): void
symbols.comment:
Ends with `error` every hold of this origin that acts for a principal `revoked` names and holds nothing: served
here but unbound (before the publication, refused), or relayed and waiting for its route's link.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.relayed
symbols.comment: A pending hold turned out to be relayed: it takes the hold's place in the table.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.relayTo
symbols.comment: This origin's number on upstream links (one per host, never reused), with `link` as one it relays to.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.forward
symbols.comment:
A message from upstream link `from` for this origin's relayed holds, forwarded with this origin: `bound` and
`state` join the window's senders (their `ack` goes back to `from`), a reply ends its call (after this host's own
waiting state: `reply`), `gone` forgets its hold. A link answers only for what was relayed over it: an entry, a
notice or a reply naming a hold (or a call) this origin did not relay over `from` is dropped (Q1); a `bound` or
`state` left without entries is acknowledged to `from` at once. Parts travel unchecked and unparsed: the end that
parses a part checks it against its own link's limits.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.unlinked
symbols.comment: An upstream link closed: nothing more is relayed to it, nor accepted from it.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.upstreamDropped
symbols.comment:
The upstream link of relayed hold `hold` dropped with `error`: its calls in flight fail, the hold goes loading
downstream, and its path's next link holds it again.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.forget
symbols.signature: forget(hold: Hold | RelayedHold, error?: ChordError): void
symbols.comment:
Forgets a hold (released, refused or gone) and every call on it; local calls are aborted with `error` (its
object's end for a gone hold, `released` otherwise).

symbols.name: ProviderSide.reply
symbols.signature: reply(id: number, reply: Extract<OriginMessage, { readonly kind: "result" | "error" }>): void
symbols.comment:
A call ended with `reply` (a result or an error, its own or forwarded from upstream): its slot is free; nothing is
sent for one already gone. The state waiting for a slot goes first, past the window if it is full (decision "A
call's answer follows its state"): when the call settles at the consumer, every change this host committed before
answering is applied there.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.#settle
symbols.comment:
Drops this side from its link once it holds nothing: no holds, no calls, nothing in flight. Its origin's next hold
makes a new one (origins are never reused), so a long-lived link keeps records only for live work.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.bind
symbols.comment: A hold's object is live: its `bound` goes now when a slot is free, else with the next free slot's bindings.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.unbind
symbols.comment: A hold stopped waiting for a slot: it was forgotten.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.unbound
symbols.comment:
A served hold left its object's binding with `error` (a failure, a removal or a version no longer bound; slice 7b
§6, model §5): as `unbind`, and its calls in flight rejected with `error` (each slot freed once). A hold unbinding
with `loading` keeps them (`unbind` alone).

symbols.name: ProviderSide.touched
symbols.comment: A hold's members changed in the current batch; its flush sends or queues it.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.#relayedOver
symbols.signature: #relayedOver<E extends { readonly hold: number }>(entries: readonly E[], from: HostLink): readonly E[]
symbols.comment:
`entries` whose holds this origin relayed over `from`, in one pass: the same array when all are, else a copy made
at the first one that is not.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.#relayedHold
symbols.comment: The hold `id` of this origin when it is relayed over `from`.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.#hold
symbols.comment:
A hold message: a protocol error for a live id or compressed params (params are never compressed), otherwise
admitted (`Hold.start`, placed once the host published). Its activation chain is kept only from a trusted link (Q5); its
decoded limit is the link's, or the smaller one a parent stamped (Q2), and travels with it when it is relayed.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.#caller
symbols.comment:
Whom a hold acts for: on a parent link the hold's own principal and incarnation when it names them, everywhere
else the link's principal and the peer's incarnation (a child cannot claim to be someone else).

symbols.name: ProviderSide.#call
symbols.comment:
A call: one on a hold this side does not know is ignored (Q1), more than this side's N at once and compressed
arguments from a child (clients never compress) are protocol errors. On a relayed hold it is forwarded, its
arguments checked against this link's part limit first (the bytes are here). On a served hold that is not callable
(not bound yet, nor rebinding by the names its consumer still has after a `loading`) it is
refused `not_ready`; its method is an index into the bound variant (one outside it is a protocol error) and its
arguments are opened and parsed here within the hold's limits (past one the call fails `too_large/part`; a
malformed part is a protocol error), absent ones `null`. Arguments this host must inflate asynchronously are
inflated first, then the call is handled again.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.#run
symbols.signature:
#run(
		id: number,
		call: Extract<RunningCall, { readonly kind: "served" }>,
		method: string,
		args: unknown,
		parent: TelemetryContext,
		scope: Context,
	): Promise<unknown>
symbols.comment:
Runs a call under `scope` (the link's context, marked when it is another host's old work) and sends its result
(absent when `null`) or error, unless it was aborted, released or gone meanwhile. A result that cannot be encoded
is sent as its error. Returns the handler's settling.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.#refuse
symbols.comment: Answers call `id` with `error` before it was admitted: it took no slot.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.#ack
symbols.comment:
An `ack` answers the oldest message in flight: this host's own frees a slot, a relayed one is acknowledged to its
upstream link (closed meanwhile: nothing to do). An ack crossing nothing in flight is ignored.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.nextOwn
symbols.comment: The number the next of this host's own `bound` and `state` messages gets (counted from 1).

symbols.name: ProviderSide.acknowledged
symbols.comment:
Whether its consumer acknowledged this host's own message number `own`, so applied it: a call it sent after that
arrives after the `ack` (one direction keeps its order).

symbols.name: ProviderSide.#flush
symbols.comment:
The end of a batch: while a slot is free and nothing waits, one `state` message with an entry per touched hold;
otherwise each touched hold's ops join its pending queues until a slot frees.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.#free
symbols.comment: Whether this host's next message goes out now: a slot is free and nothing waits for one.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.#slotFreed
symbols.comment:
A slot may be free: while there is room, the waiting state goes out as one message and the waiting bindings as
one `bound`, taking turns when both wait (state first), so neither a hold that keeps changing nor a stream of new
holds starves the other.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.#sendWaiting
symbols.comment:
The waiting state as one `state` message, taking a slot: a freed one, or one past the window before an answer.
Waiting bindings take the next slot.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.#result
symbols.signature:
#result(
		id: number,
		result: unknown,
		bytes: boolean,
		context: Context,
	): Extract<OriginMessage, { readonly kind: "result" }>
symbols.comment:
A call's result message, its part deflated above the threshold when this host compresses; with byte segments when
its method's result schema has a `bytes()` leaf.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.#waited
symbols.comment: The waiting state went out (or its holds left): how long it waited for its slot is recorded.

symbols.name: ProviderSide.#sendOwn
symbols.comment: Sends one of this host's own `bound` or `state` messages, taking a slot.

packages/chord/src/remote/provider.ts.comment:
The provider side of one origin on a link (§3, §22, W1; decision "Relay flow control per origin"): the holds the

peer sent for that origin, served here or relayed, by their ids; the calls on them, at most this side's N at once;

and the window: at most K unacknowledged `bound` and `state` messages of this host's own, with what waits meanwhile

(a call's answer sends the waiting state first, past the window), and the sender of every message in flight, so each

`ack` reaches the host that sent its message. A served call's method runs under the call's carrier (slice 9).

symbols.name: RelayedHold
symbols.comment:
One relayed hold: `id` on its downstream origin, and the same id upstream on its path's current link (none while
the path has no link). It keeps its `hold` message to hold again on the next link. Calls, `abort`, `retry` and
`release` go upstream at once; what comes back is forwarded by its downstream origin (`ProviderSide.forward`). Two
downstream holds are two upstream holds, each with its own encoders (R1).

symbols.name: RelayedHold.#request
symbols.comment:
What the upstream hold asks for, with the chain and decoded limit this host honoured; its params owned, not a view
of the message they came in.

symbols.name: RelayedHold.caller
symbols.comment: Whom the hold acts for, sent on route links.

symbols.name: RelayedHold.#upstream
symbols.signature: #upstream: { readonly link: HostLink; readonly origin: number } | undefined;
symbols.comment: The upstream link while the path has one, and the downstream origin's number on it.
symbols.output: { readonly link: HostLink; readonly origin: number } | undefined

symbols.name: RelayedHold.#relaying
symbols.comment: Its `chord.relay` span until it is first held upstream (or dropped); none when this host records nothing.

symbols.name: RelayedHold.#trace
symbols.comment:
The carrier of its first upstream hold: the relay span's, or the arriving one as it came when this host records
nothing; a re-hold's span links to it.

symbols.name: RelayedHold.#holds
symbols.comment: How many times it was held upstream.

symbols.name: RelayedHold.constructor
symbols.signature: constructor(id: number, downstream: ProviderSide, request: HoldRequest, caller: Caller, path: Path)

symbols.name: RelayedHold.span
symbols.comment: Its `chord.relay` span until it is held upstream (a route's resolve links to it); none when not recorded.

symbols.name: RelayedHold.start
symbols.comment: Takes the pending hold's place downstream and holds upstream (now, or when the path has a link).

symbols.name: RelayedHold.heldOn
symbols.comment: Whether it is held on `link` now: only that link answers for it.

symbols.name: RelayedHold.attach
symbols.comment: Holds on `link`, the path's link now: its kept `hold` message, with whom it acts for on a route link.

symbols.name: RelayedHold.#holdTrace
symbols.comment:
The carrier of this upstream hold: the first one's; a re-hold after an upstream drop is a fresh `chord.relay` root
linked to the first (none when this host records nothing), never the first's again (review L1).

symbols.name: RelayedHold.#attributes
symbols.signature: #attributes(member: string): { "chord.host": string; type: string; member: string; "upstream.kind": string }
symbols.comment:
A relay span's attributes: its host's `chord.host` (the downstream link's host), and names from the wire, bounded
by the message schema (untrusted links) and capped here.
symbols.output: { "chord.host": string; type: string; member: string; "upstream.kind": string }

symbols.name: RelayedHold.dropped
symbols.comment: The upstream link dropped: downstream its calls fail and the hold goes loading until the path's next link.

symbols.name: RelayedHold.unreachable
symbols.comment: Its path's address cannot be reached for now: downstream it fails `waiting` with `error` until the next link.

symbols.name: RelayedHold.waiting
symbols.comment:
Whether it waits for its path's link (a route still resolving, or a dropped link's next): a revocation ends it then,
since the link it is held on next gets no past `revoke` (§4).

symbols.name: RelayedHold.revoked
symbols.comment: Revoked while it waited for its path's link: forgotten, and `gone` with `error` downstream.

symbols.name: RelayedHold.lost
symbols.comment: `gone` from upstream: the hold is forgotten (the downstream origin forwards the message).

symbols.name: RelayedHold.call
symbols.signature: call(message: Extract<Message, { readonly kind: "call" }>): OpenSpan<"chord.relay"> | undefined
symbols.comment:
A call from downstream (registered there under its id), forwarded upstream at once; its reply comes back by the
origin. Without an upstream link it is answered `unavailable` at once (it crossed the `loading` notice).

symbols.name: RelayedHold.abort
symbols.comment: A downstream `abort` of call `id`, forwarded.

symbols.name: RelayedHold.retry
symbols.comment: A downstream `retry`, forwarded with its hop budget as it is (a relay visits no object).

symbols.name: RelayedHold.release
symbols.comment: Released downstream: released upstream (its calls with it) and no later link holds it.

symbols.name: RelayedHold.drop
symbols.comment: No later link holds it (gone, or its downstream origin closed, which `closed` tells the upstream links).

symbols.name: RelayedHold.#relayed
symbols.comment: It was held upstream, failed or dropped first: its `chord.relay` span ends with `outcome`.

symbols.name: relayEnded
symbols.comment:
A relayed call's `chord.relay` span ends with its `reply` forwarded downstream (`ok`, or the error's: `aborted` for
a cancel), or `aborted` without one (an abort, a release, a closed link).

symbols.name: unmarked
symbols.signature: function unmarked(message: Extract<Message, { readonly kind: "call" }>): Extract<Message, { readonly kind: "call" }>
symbols.comment: `message` without its old-work flag (`call.old`), as a relay forwards it from a link that is not trusted.

packages/chord/src/remote/relay.ts.comment:
Relayed holds (§4, §22, R1; decision "Relay flow control per origin"): a hold that arrived on one link (downstream)

and that this host neither serves nor parses, held again on its path's link (upstream) with the same id under its

downstream origin's number there; messages are forwarded between the two with the origin rewritten and parts

untouched. Forwarding a hold or a call is a `chord.relay` span under the arriving carrier, whose own carrier goes

upstream (slice 9).

symbols.name: Bound
symbols.comment: The last binding: its variant, methods, the bound version's names (the wire's indexes) and a replica per member.

symbols.name: RemoteObject
symbols.comment:
One remote reference's object, owned by its host across the links of its path. It is `loading` until a link's hold
of it is bound, and again whenever that link drops or its relay's upstream starts over; each link holds it with its
own id. Two references are two holds, each member of each with its own Delta decoder.

symbols.name: RemoteObject.label
symbols.comment: The object in errors: its type, and its params key when it has params.

symbols.name: RemoteObject.request
symbols.comment: What its holds ask for: the params as a part (checked by L1 when the reference was made), the address.

symbols.name: RemoteObject.caller
symbols.comment: Whom its reference acts for: named on route links (`actingFor`).

symbols.name: RemoteObject.#params
symbols.comment: Its params, for placing it anew (`retry` after a part past the limits).

symbols.name: RemoteObject.#path
symbols.comment: Its path: the parent's or a route address's; the host's `unplaced` one after a part past the limits.

symbols.name: RemoteObject.#dependent
symbols.comment: The object whose activation declared the reference (`self.get`): its holds carry its chain while it activates.

symbols.name: RemoteObject.#bound
symbols.comment: The last binding, kept while loading or failed: members keep their last values and watches.

symbols.name: RemoteObject.#hold
symbols.signature: #hold: { readonly side: ConsumerSide; readonly id: number } | undefined;
symbols.comment: The hold on the path's link while one is open: that link's consumer side and this hold's id on it.
symbols.output: { readonly side: ConsumerSide; readonly id: number } | undefined

symbols.name: RemoteObject.#holding
symbols.comment: Its current `chord.hold` span until its hold's `bound` or failure; none when nothing records.

symbols.name: RemoteObject.#firstHold
symbols.comment: The carrier of its first hold's span: a re-hold's span links to it.

symbols.name: RemoteObject.#holds
symbols.comment: How many times it was held (on the links of its path).

symbols.name: RemoteObject.constructor
symbols.signature:
constructor(
		host: AnyHost,
		contract: Contract,
		{ params, key }: CheckedParams,
		address: WireAddress,
		caller: Caller,
		path: Path,
		dependent: ChordObject | undefined,
		holder: TelemetryContext,
	)

symbols.name: RemoteObject.stateFor
symbols.comment: Over a link the provider decides what each version sees: its state as it is.

symbols.name: RemoteObject.span
symbols.comment: Its `chord.hold` span until its first `bound` or failure (a route's resolve links to it); none when not recorded.

symbols.name: RemoteObject.blocksFirstPass
symbols.comment: An object over a link is no blocker of this host's first pass.

symbols.name: RemoteObject.lastFailure
symbols.comment: The error of the last `failed`, until `bound`.

symbols.name: RemoteObject.variant
symbols.comment: The variant last bound; `undefined` before the first binding.

symbols.name: RemoteObject.hydrated
symbols.comment: Whether its state members have values: bound once.

symbols.name: RemoteObject.hold
symbols.comment: Its one reference bound to it.

symbols.name: RemoteObject.unhold
symbols.comment: The reference was released: the current link's provider is told and the reference's sent calls rejected.

symbols.name: RemoteObject.attach
symbols.comment:
Holds on `link`, the path's link now (a first hold, or a re-hold on a new link), with the activation chain of its
dependent while that activates (Q5).

symbols.name: RemoteObject.#holdTrace
symbols.comment:
The carrier of this hold: the first one's span's (a child of its holder's span); a re-hold on a later link (a
reconnect, days later for a page kept open) is a fresh `chord.hold` root of this host's adapter linked to the first,
so nothing keeps adding children under a span long ended (review L1).

symbols.name: RemoteObject.unreachable
symbols.comment:
Its path's address cannot be reached for now (a route's `resolve` failed, a suspension): `failed { waiting }` with
`error`, still on the path, bound by its next link.

symbols.name: RemoteObject.dropped
symbols.comment: The link dropped: loading until a new link's hold is bound (`#startOver`).

symbols.name: RemoteObject.call
symbols.signature: async call(method: string, args: unknown, context: Context): Promise<unknown>
symbols.comment:
Calls a method of the bound variant over the link; one outside it fails `invalid/member`. Only a live object is
called: bound on an open link.

symbols.name: RemoteObject.member
symbols.comment:
The replica of `member`; `not_ready` before the first binding, `invalid/member` for a member no binding had (one
a later variant lacks reads its `invalid/member` failure).

symbols.name: RemoteObject.followed
symbols.comment:
What its reference follows of `member` (a consumer over a link binds at its own version, mapped at the provider):
the replica while live, a member the bound variant lacks (`invalid/member`); while loading or failed nothing, the
replica (kept until the next binding) giving its last value (rule 5).

symbols.name: RemoteObject.attachable
symbols.comment: Its binding while live (its replicas change); `undefined` while loading or failed.

symbols.name: RemoteObject.instance
symbols.comment: Keyed members are only in local contracts: no instance to pin a key on.

symbols.name: RemoteObject.keyedMapping
symbols.comment: Keyed members are only in local contracts (`keyedMember`).

symbols.name: RemoteObject.pinKey
symbols.comment: Keyed members are only in local contracts (`keyedMember`).

symbols.name: RemoteObject.keyedMember
symbols.comment: Keyed members are only in local contracts, whose objects are never held over a link (slice 6a §12).

symbols.name: RemoteObject.activationId
symbols.comment: An object over a link activates on another host: it is in no chain here (Q5).

symbols.name: RemoteObject.pathTo
symbols.comment: An object over a link waits for nothing on this host: no chain of waits (its holds carry the chain, Q5).

symbols.name: RemoteObject.retry
symbols.comment:
`ref.retry()`, as a step of `walk`: a failed object's provider is asked for an attempt with the walk's hop budget,
none left: nothing is sent (a hold it refused is started there again; a parked object there passes it on with one
hop less). One that failed for a part past the link's limits is placed anew and held with a new id, now or on its
path's next link (a `hostAddress` that throws fails it broken again).

symbols.name: RemoteObject.#place
symbols.comment: Places a reference whose part was past the limits anew, on its path now (a throwing `hostAddress` fails it).

symbols.name: RemoteObject.tooLarge
symbols.comment:
A part of its snapshot or of a state change was past the link's limits (`too_large/part`): the hold is released
at the provider, and the reference fails broken with `error`, final: no link holds it again (a reconnect
included) until `retry`.

symbols.name: RemoteObject.#fail
symbols.comment: Fails broken with `error`: no automatic retry.

symbols.name: RemoteObject.prepareBound
symbols.comment:
Prepares one entry of a `bound` message (a first binding, a re-hold; a live hold is bound again): the
variant and every state member once, as a value or as failed. Returns what applies it inside the batch of the
whole message: a member it had gets the snapshot as one frame `[["r", value]]` and a fresh decoder, a member
outside the new variant fails (its replica stays, for a later binding that has it again), a new one gets its first
value. Throws on a snapshot that
does not fit (a protocol error), and `too_large/part` for a value past the link's limits, before anything changed.
`wentLive` follows the batch.

symbols.name: RemoteObject.wentLive
symbols.comment: After a `bound` message's batch: the reference goes live (its parked calls are sent, a parked dependent goes on).

symbols.name: RemoteObject.failed
symbols.comment:
`failed`: the provider's object failed and no attempt runs (`retryIn`: the rest of its backoff window), or the hold
is unbound there or its object parked on a failed dependency (`waiting`), each new cause a new message. On a bound
hold it unbinds it (slice 7b, model §5): the members keep their last values until the next `bound`.

symbols.name: RemoteObject.loading
symbols.comment:
`loading`: the provider's object started a new attempt after a failure, or its relay's upstream link dropped
(`#startOver`).

symbols.name: RemoteObject.prepare
symbols.signature: prepare({ hold: id, members, failed, retired }: StateEntry, link: HostLink): () => void
symbols.comment:
Decodes and applies one entry of a state message (its members by index, each with its ops), without changing
anything yet: returns what adopts it into the replicas, run inside the batch that applies the whole message.
Throws on an entry that does not fit (a protocol error), and `too_large/part` for ops past the link's limits.
inputs: { hold: id, members, failed, retired }: StateEntry

symbols.name: RemoteObject.revoke
symbols.comment:
Its principal was revoked on this host (`host.revoke`): released at its provider if it is held there, then ended
with `error` as `lost` does; no later link holds it.

symbols.name: RemoteObject.lost
symbols.comment: `gone`, or the host closes: the reference ends, its calls reject with `error`.

symbols.name: RemoteObject.#end
symbols.comment: Ends the object: detached from its path, waits rejected, replicas ended; keeps nothing of its reference.

symbols.name: RemoteObject.#held
symbols.comment: Its first `bound` or failure (or its end before either): its `chord.hold` span ends with `outcome`.

symbols.name: RemoteObject.#startOver
symbols.comment:
Loading again until the next binding; the members keep their last values. A drop while it is loading already
changes nothing: a dependent parked on it goes on waiting for the next link's binding (a drop is not a dependency
failure).

symbols.name: RemoteObject.#move
symbols.comment: Moves to `state` and tells the reference: its members follow what it shows now (in a batch), then its state.

packages/chord/src/remote/remote-object..comment:
An object held over a link (§7): what one remote reference is bound to on the consumer, across the links of its path

(the parent, or a route address). Its state, the replicas of its last bound variant (kept while its link is down),

its hold on the path's current link and calls through it: its hold in a `chord.hold` span until bound, each call in a

`chord.call` span, their carriers on the wire (slice 9).

symbols.name: ReplicaState
symbols.comment:
Where a replica stands: a value, a failed member (reads throw; the provider's member failed, or a newly bound variant
lacks it, and either may come back; `last` is its last good value, `undefined` when it had none), or ended with its
reference.

symbols.name: MemberSnapshot
symbols.comment: A member as a snapshot has it: a value, or failed.
symbols.output:
| { readonly kind: "value"; readonly value: JsonValue }
	| { readonly kind: "failed"; readonly error: unknown }

symbols.name: Replica
symbols.comment: One state member of a hold, as the consumer reads and watches it; changed only inside the consumer's batch.

symbols.name: Replica.#decoder
symbols.comment: The member's decoder, started with the snapshot as the provider's encoder was; a new one per snapshot.

symbols.name: Replica.#ops
symbols.comment: The ops of the current batch's frame, and whether the provider's document was retired in it.

symbols.name: Replica.#retiredWhileFailed
symbols.comment: A retirement that reached it while failed: its next value carries the flag.

symbols.name: Replica.start
symbols.comment: Its value, or while failed its failure and last good value.

symbols.name: Replica.decode
symbols.signature: decode(wire: unknown): { readonly value: JsonValue; readonly ops: readonly Op[] }
symbols.comment:
The value `wire` (this member's wire ops from one state part) makes, and its ops; changes nothing yet. Throws on
ops that do not fit (a protocol error): an ended member's, and a failed member's other than its recovery, which
the provider sends as `[["r", value]]`.
symbols.output: { readonly value: JsonValue; readonly ops: readonly Op[] }

symbols.name: Replica.adopt
symbols.signature: adopt(value: JsonValue, ops: readonly Op[], retired: boolean): void
symbols.comment:
Adopts the member's new value, the ops that made it and whether the provider's document was retired, in the
current batch (one adoption per member and batch).

symbols.name: Replica.retireAlone
symbols.comment:
The provider's document was retired with no ops for this member (a derive whose value stayed, rule 21), in the
current batch: the flag alone; while failed it waits for the next value (a failed member's value is never read).

symbols.name: Replica.reset
symbols.comment:
A re-hold's snapshot of the member, in the batch that applies it, with a fresh decoder (the provider's encoder
starts anew with it): a value is one frame `[["r", value]]`, a failed member fails.

symbols.name: Replica.fail
symbols.comment:
The provider's member failed, in the batch that applies it: reads throw `error`, watches get one failure call and
stay open, derives over it fail; its recovery is `[["r", value]]`.

symbols.name: Replica.vanish
symbols.comment:
The member is not in a newly bound variant, in the batch that binds it: as a failure (`fail`) with `error`; a later
binding of a variant that has it brings it back (`reset`), as on the provider's host.

symbols.name: Replica.end
symbols.comment: Its reference ended (outside a batch): reads throw `error`, watches end `ended`.

packages/chord/src/remote/replica.ts.comment:
Replicas (§7, §22): a state member of a remote reference on the consumer, built from the snapshot and then changed

by the provider's ops, decoded with the member's own Delta decoder and applied without validation or copy

(`applyImmutable` shares structure); replaced by the snapshot of each re-hold.

symbols.name: DurableObjectSqlValue
symbols.signature: type DurableObjectSqlValue = ArrayBuffer | string | number | null;
symbols.comment: Values a Durable Object SQL binding accepts and returns.

symbols.name: DurableObjectSqliteStorage
symbols.comment:

symbols.name: SqliteExecutor
symbols.comment:
Asynchronous SQL operations shared by a database and its transaction handles.

`exec` runs SQL text without bindings and may contain several statements. `run`, `get`, and `all`
execute one statement with positional bindings. `runCounted` runs one like `run` and resolves with the rows it
inserted, updated or deleted, as SQLite's `changes()` counts them (index writes and rows changed by triggers do not
count); it may cost a statement more than `run`, so callers that need no count use `run`. Adapters may cache
prepared statements by SQL text, so callers pass values as bindings instead of interpolating them.

symbols.name: SqliteDatabase
symbols.comment:
Minimal portable SQLite database facade.

All operations are asynchronous so adapters may execute outside the caller's runtime.

`transaction` passes the callback a transaction handle. All work in the transaction
must use that handle; the handle is invalid after the callback settles. Adapters must
queue unrelated operations and other transactions until the transaction finishes. The
returned promise settles after commit or rollback. Calling the database itself (including
`transaction` or `close`) from inside a callback therefore waits for that transaction and
never settles.

When the callback rejects, the adapter must roll the transaction back before rejecting
with that same error. If rollback fails, it must reject with a different error (for
example an `AggregateError`) so callers cannot mistake the callback error for a
guaranteed rollback.

The allocator: `value` is the next id it gives. An id raised to `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` is accepted, the value
stays there, and every later `mint` throws: no id past the safe range (it would stop counting exactly and repeat).

symbols.comment: Takes the next id; throws "ID space is exhausted" once saturated (Durable's message).

document ids), synchronous, raised by explicit ids, saturating at `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`.

The first id the allocator gives: id 1 is Durable's root conversation.

The applier (slice 6a §13, slice 6b §1.6): recorded writes applied as they were recorded, inside a backend

transaction, checked against the store's own records (a trust boundary: archives, a replica's batches). One code

path for import, bootstrap and batch apply, for every write kind; a recorded count the store does not reproduce

stops applying (`Diverged`, S17).

diverged, or when the first commit does not follow its `lastSeq` or one does not follow the one before; a write the
store's records refuse rolls the whole batch back (`invalid/args`); a recorded count the store does not reproduce
rolls it back and marks the store diverged, so every later batch is refused. Commits written to the store's outbox
too when it has one.

boundary), `lastSeq` and the allocator set from the last commit. Internal: the sync layer's entry point.

revisions in seq order; `end` with the count of the parts between.

packages/chord/src/store/export.ts.comment:
`store.export(ctx)` (slice 6a §13, rule 26): the store's state after its `lastSeq` as archive parts, read page by

page with plain reads while the export holds the commit queue (no commit can interleave, no long read transaction).

The queue is taken at the first `next()` and given back when the iteration ends, throws, is closed or `ctx` aborts;

an abort while the consumer is suspended gives it back at once and drops the pages and records the export held, and

an abort while it waits for the queue ends the wait. Closing the store ends it too (`released`).

packages/chord/src/store/import.ts.comment:
`importStore(backend, parts, ctx, { outbox? })` (slice 6a §13, rules 12, 24, 25): a store made from an archive, a

trust boundary. Every part is checked against the archive schema, its place in the archive's order and its content

(names, rows against their table's recorded columns, ids and seqs, lifetimes at one address never overlapping,

revisions in seq order from a base, versions, duplicates, the `end` count, the manifest); everything is applied in

one backend transaction with the applier, so a refused import leaves the backend as it was. An input that stalls is

cancelled by `ctx`.

The re-run of live queries in one commit: `write` reads them in the commit step after the commit's own writes (the
last write of the last phase), and `adopt` publishes their rows in the commit's batch; a refused step adopts nothing.
A transaction stages it as its own change (`Staged`).

symbols.comment: The staged write that reads the queries; it writes nothing and records nothing in the outbox.

symbols.name: QueryRefresh.adopt

symbols.name: LiveQuery
symbols.comment:
A live query: the rows of `query` (at most `limit`, in its order) over its object's table `handle`, as a JSON source
(a state member, a derive source, an `on` source). Its statement is compiled once; each run decodes only the rows
whose stored columns changed and keeps the others the same objects, so its frame, the diff from the rows its watches
had, compares unchanged rows by identity (a window shifted by one row: one insert and one removal, not a comparison
of every row with every other).

symbols.name: LiveQuery.#byKey
symbols.comment: The last adopted rows by key, with the stored rows they were decoded from (the next run reuses unchanged ones).

symbols.name: LiveQuery.#framed
symbols.comment: The rows this query's watches have, kept from its adoption to its frame in the batch; `undefined`: not listed.

symbols.name: LiveQuery.#adopted
symbols.comment: Commits adopted so far: an activation run that a commit overtook keeps the commit's newer rows.

symbols.name: LiveQuery.#failing
symbols.comment: Set from a failed run until the next good one: a failure episode is reported once.

symbols.name: LiveQuery.load
symbols.comment:
The first run, before its object goes live (activation, after its tables are prepared): a failure throws and fails
the activation. Rows a commit adopted meanwhile are newer and stay.

symbols.name: LiveQuery.rerun
symbols.signature: async rerun(step: Step, context: Context): Promise<QueryRun>
symbols.comment: A run inside the commit step `step`, after its writes: the rows, or the failure; it never throws.

symbols.name: LiveQuery.adopt
symbols.comment:
Takes a commit's run, inside its batch: listed for a frame when watched, its dependents marked. A failed run makes
the query a failed member (as a throwing derive): its watches get one failure call, the owner a report per
failure episode; the next good run replaces the value whole.

symbols.name: LiveQuery.deliver
symbols.comment: Delivers the frame: the diff from the rows its watches had, or one failure call when they had rows.

packages/chord/src/store/live-query.ts.comment:
Live queries (decision "Live queries over an object's own tables"): `self.query(table, q, limit)`, a JSON watchable

of a query's rows over a table of the object itself. Run once before the object goes live, then again inside the

commit step of every commit of the object that wrote the table (after its writes, so it sees them) and published in

that commit's batch as the diff from the previous rows (W1). Only the object writes its tables, so its commits are

the exact invalidation; a commit writing no table with a live query runs none.
