pi-ai model access used by generation, compaction, hooks and tools: a `Models`, or a function returning the current
one, called at each use, so a host can replace its model configuration without reopening the Harness.

symbols.name: identity
symbols.comment:
How model requests identify the app to providers, merged field by field over `DEFAULT_HARNESS_IDENTITY`
(`{ attribution: PI_ATTRIBUTION }`, provider attribution to pi). It applies to every request through the Harness's
models, including hooks and tools, and overrides the identity the `Models` was created with; a request's own
`identity` overrides it. Pass `{ attribution: null }` to send no attribution headers.

symbols.name: settings
symbols.comment: Run settings, or a function returning the current ones; read at each use either way.

symbols.name: env
symbols.signature: readonly env?: (target: EnvTarget, context: Context) => ExecutionEnv | undefined | Promise<ExecutionEnv | undefined>;
symbols.comment: Builds a conversation's environment at each use. Never called on the Session line; may be async.
symbols.output: (target: EnvTarget, context: Context) => ExecutionEnv | undefined | Promise<ExecutionEnv | undefined>

symbols.name: conversationCreated
symbols.signature: readonly conversationCreated?: (tx: Tx, conversation: ConversationRecord) => void | Promise<void>;
symbols.comment:
Runs in every commit that creates or forks a conversation, raw `tx.createConversation()` included, after the
built-in `pi.*` documents and before the conveniences apply `agent` and run `init`. A fork already has its copies.
Table reads throw `ReadAfterWrite`, as in `init`; a throw fails the creating commit.

symbols.name: now
symbols.comment:
The Harness clock, epoch milliseconds; default `Date.now`. Sleeping tasks store deadlines on it, so every process
that opens the same storage must use the same clock.

symbols.name: setTimer
symbols.comment:
Arms the timers of the Session, the scheduler, and its tasks: pacing progress commits, freeing idle memory
(`background`), and, without `onWake`, resuming sleeping tasks; and the timers of `TaskRuntime.setTimer()`. The
Node.js environment, file watcher, and image worker keep their own timers. Default `setTimeout`, with background
timers unreferenced, or declined in Cloudflare Workers and where they cannot be unreferenced. Tests can pass fake
timers; a host can keep timers off a process that should hibernate.

symbols.name: onWake
symbols.comment:
Wakes the process for sleeping tasks instead of a `setTimer` timer. Without it, while scheduling runs, a timer that
keeps the process alive resumes sleeping tasks when they are due. With it, the Harness arms no timer for them: it
calls `onWake` after open and whenever `Harness.wake()` changes, and the host arms its own wakeup, such as a
Durable Object alarm, and calls `resume()` when it fires. Called in a microtask the Session line never waits for,
after the commit that changed the value was adopted, so a host arms a recovery wakeup before calls that can start
work. It may call `wake()` and `resume()`, and must not block. A throw is reported, and the value is offered again
at the next change.

symbols.name: onReport
symbols.comment:
Receives failures that do not fail the calling operation, such as a throwing hook or listener, a task that faulted,
and the error that fails the Session, once: one `Report`, the `error` and what happened (`kind` and the fields of
its `ReportInfo`). A host can tell a failed Session (`storage_failed`, often a platform reset) from a faulted task
(`task_faulted`). Its own throw or rejection is dropped.

symbols.name: readOnly
symbols.comment:
Open for reading only, as a viewer of a session that another process drives, for example a synced copy on a device
that only shows it. Open recovers nothing: a `running` task stays as committed. Every commit with writes rejects
with `ReadOnlySession` before it reaches Storage, and so does `resume()` and every call that enables scheduling;
the Harness stays usable for reads and watches. `wake()` is always inactive, and `onWake` is never called. Reopen
without it to write.

symbols.name: Wake
symbols.signature: export type Wake = { readonly active: boolean; readonly at?: number };
symbols.comment:
When a Session next needs a running process (`Harness.wake()`). `active`: some task can run now or is running, or a
reconcile pass such as open's recovery has not landed yet, so a process that dies must be woken again soon, for
example by a recovery alarm. `at`: the earliest sleep not yet due,
when there is one. Neither: nothing needs a process until new work is submitted. Tasks blocked on a missing or
unmigratable definition, `completing` tasks, and waits on live tasks do not count; the work they wait for does.
symbols.output: { readonly active: boolean; readonly at?: number }

symbols.name: TaskInspection
symbols.comment: Live task and what the scheduler would do with it under the current registry.

symbols.name: state
HarnessInspection
symbols.comment: Point-in-time view of live work: unfinished tasks and submissions, read on the Session line.

symbols.name: submissions
symbols.comment: Queued and placed submissions, in ID order.

symbols.name: ContextView
symbols.comment: Raw active transcript and derived model context.

symbols.name: head
symbols.comment: Newest applicable head marker, if any.

symbols.name: entries
symbols.comment: Raw active entries: the head marker followed by non-head entries from its head through the tail.

symbols.name: contributions
symbols.comment: Per entry of `entries`, its model messages after edits and excluded stop reasons, before tool result ordering.

symbols.name: messages
symbols.comment: Model context for the next provider request.

symbols.name: Conversation
symbols.comment: Stateless handle for one conversation, bound to the Harness that returned it. Compare handles by `id`.

symbols.name: Conversation.agent
symbols.comment: Resolved with the current registry snapshot and settings.

symbols.name: Conversation.configure
symbols.comment: `configure()` in its own commit.

symbols.name: Conversation.submit
symbols.comment:
Durably admit user input, a passive entry write, or a continue. A busy conversation, or one with queued items,
queues input and writes that affect model context in `pi.inbox`; `whenBusy: "reject"` rejects input with
`ConversationBusy` instead and writes nothing. An idle conversation rejects `whenIdle: "reject"` input with
`ConversationIdle` and writes nothing. A write of only `kind` and `data` (no `model`, `head`, or `edits`)
is appended at once, even mid-run, as it changes nothing the model sees. A continue starts a run on the context as
it is, after placing queued items; a busy conversation rejects it with `ConversationBusy`, as it never queues.

symbols.name: Conversation.submit
symbols.comment:
Admit a submission inside the caller's commit `tx` (`Harness.commit()`, `Conversation.commit()`, a task's
`runtime.commit()`), with the same rules, and return its ID: the admission is stored with that commit, or not at all
when the callback throws later or the commit fails. Call it before the commit's first table write (`appendEntry()`,
`createTask()`, `createSubmission()`, another admission): otherwise it throws `ReadAfterWrite`, on every path.
Documents may be read and written before and after it. A rejection (`ConversationBusy`, `ConversationIdle`) throws
before any write, so the callback may catch it. Do not call `Submission` or other Harness reads inside the callback:
they wait for the commit holding the line. Its `pi.durable.submit` span covers the admission only, so its `result`
is provisional. Throws for a transaction of another Session.

symbols.name: Conversation.reset
symbols.signature: reset(handoff: string | undefined, context: Context): Promise<void>;
symbols.comment:
Admit a write of a `pi.reset` entry that starts a new context, carrying `handoff` as a user message when given.
Resolves after admission; while busy, it is placed at the next boundary.

symbols.name: Conversation.compact
symbols.signature: compact(instructions: string | undefined, context: Context): Promise<TaskId<CompactionResult>>;
symbols.comment:
Admit a manual compaction task and return its ID. It summarizes while the conversation keeps working and places its
summary through a write submission: at once when idle, otherwise at the next boundary (spec §8.7).

symbols.signature: commit<T>(change: (tx: Tx) => T | Promise<T>, context: Context, options?: CommitOptions): Promise<T>;
symbols.comment: Session commit whose `tx.createTask()` defaults to this conversation; `options` as for `Session.commit()`.

symbols.name: Conversation.context
symbols.signature: context(context: Context, options?: { readonly at?: EntryId }): Promise<ContextView>;
symbols.comment:
Committed raw active transcript and model context. With `at`, the context as of that visible entry: the same view
`fork(at)` would start with, without creating a conversation.

symbols.name: Conversation.entries
symbols.comment: Fork-aware history of this conversation, newest first unless `query.order` is `ascending`.

symbols.name: Conversation.fork
symbols.signature: fork(at: EntryId, options: ConversationCreateOptions, context: Context): Promise<Conversation>;

symbols.name: Conversation.abort
symbols.comment:
Withdraw queued inputs (queued writes stay), mark every live non-background task of the ordinary ownership scope,
signal them, and resolve once the scope is idle. Background subtrees survive unless `background` is set.

symbols.name: Conversation.waitForIdle
symbols.comment:
Resolve when the ordinary ownership scope has no live non-background task: this conversation and the conversations
owned, transitively, by its non-background tasks.

symbols.name: Conversation.watch
symbols.comment:
The structural view (spec §9.3) as a serialized watch; commits made while its listener runs arrive folded. Its
`entries` are a window over the transcript, as `window` says: the newest 50 by default, then appends, dropping the
oldest past 100. Built on the same mount as `Harness.observeConversation()`.

symbols.name: Harness
symbols.comment: Durable agent harness over one Session.

symbols.name: Harness.resume
symbols.comment:
Enable task scheduling. Idempotent; throws after close, and `ReadOnlySession` on a read-only Harness. Calls that
ask for progress enable it too: `Conversation.submit()`, `Conversation.compact()`, `Conversation.abort()`,
`Submission.wait()`, `waitForTask()`, `Harness.waitForIdle()`, and `Conversation.waitForIdle()`. Read-only viewers
never do.

symbols.name: Harness.wake
symbols.comment:
When this Session next needs a running process, from the scheduler's memory: `active` while some task can run now
or is running, `at` for the earliest sleep. Answers also while scheduling is paused. A host that wakes the
process itself, such as a Durable Object alarm, arms from it and calls `resume()` when woken; see
`HarnessOptions.onWake`.

symbols.name: Harness.root
symbols.comment: Return the reserved root conversation, creating it with `agent` and `init` in one commit when absent.
inputs: options?: { readonly agent?: AgentChange; readonly init?: ConversationInit }

symbols.signature: getTask<R>(id: TaskId<R>, context: Context): Promise<TaskRecord<JsonValue, JsonValue, R> | undefined>;

symbols.name: Harness.inspect
symbols.comment: Live tasks and unsettled submissions. Writes nothing and runs no task code.

symbols.name: Harness.submission
symbols.signature: submission(id: SubmissionId, context: Context): Promise<Submission | undefined>;
symbols.comment: Reacquire a submission, for example after reopen.

symbols.name: Harness.abortSubmission
symbols.comment: `not_found` for an unknown submission or one of another conversation than `conversationId`.

symbols.name: Harness.abortTask
symbols.comment:
Commit the abort mark, signal and join an active run invocation, and schedule the abort invocation. A task whose
definition cannot take it settles as `orphaned` instead.

symbols.name: Harness.waitForTask
symbols.comment: Resolve with the terminal receipt; cancelling `context` cancels only this wait.

symbols.name: Harness.waitForIdle
symbols.comment: Resolve when the ordinary ownership scope of every ownerless conversation has no live non-background task.

symbols.name: Harness.usage
symbols.comment: Session total: every conversation's `pi.usage` summed.

symbols.name: Harness.watchTaskGraph
symbols.comment:
Every live task with its owner edge, status, and owned conversations (spec §9.4), as a serialized watch; commits
made while its listener runs arrive folded.

symbols.name: Harness.observeConversation
symbols.comment:
Attach a synchronous `Observer` to a conversation's structural view (spec §9.3), atomically on the Session line,
for adapters: `advance` gets each next revision with its operations as memory adopts the commit, inside Storage's
`adopt` for a stored one and before it is stored for a deferred one, so it only records it. `window` as for
`Conversation.watch()`; each observer has its own. `context` governs only the attachment.

symbols.name: Harness.observeTaskGraph
symbols.comment:
Attach a synchronous `Observer` to the task graph (spec §9.4), as `observeConversation()` does to a view. A
`blocked` reason that changes without a commit (a registry change, a failed migration) advances it on the Session
line outside any commit and `adopt`, with the background context.

Session line, so reads see what is committed when they run; a hook rerun after a crash may see more.

symbols.signature: afterTools(assistant: EntryId, results: readonly EntryId[], api: HookApi, context: Context): void | Promise<void>;

symbols.name: GenerationHooks.afterRun
symbols.signature: afterRun(run: RunSummary, api: HookApi, context: Context): HookResult<{ readonly tasks: readonly RunEndTask[] }>;
symbols.comment:
After a run answered, its answer committed and its inputs settled `done`: a final answer, or a `terminate` round;
not when an `onYield` continuation is taken, and never after a failure or an abort. The requested tasks of every
hook are created together as children of the generation, which keeps the run, and the conversation busy, until
they are terminal; then queued items are placed and the run ends (spec §8.3). A crash before they are created asks
again; once created, never again for this run.

symbols.name: RunSummary
symbols.comment: How a run ended, for `afterRun` hooks. Read the run's history with `api.entries({ minEntryId: first, maxEntryId: last })`.

symbols.comment: A final answer, or a tool round whose every call asked to `terminate`.

symbols.name: first
symbols.comment:
The run's first entry (`LiveRun.first`): the first one the boundary that started it placed, for a continue the failed
run's it continues, otherwise its first tool-calling answer; the answer itself for a run that has none of these.

symbols.name: answer
symbols.comment: The answer, or the terminating round's tool-calling answer, whose results follow it.

symbols.name: last
symbols.comment: The run's last entry: the answer; for a `terminate` round its newest result, or the reset of its handoff.

symbols.signature: readonly parent?: { readonly taskId: TaskId; readonly callId: string };

symbols.name: ToolHooks
symbols.comment: Hooks of the built-in tool task, for model-issued and nested calls.

symbols.name: ToolHooks.beforeTool
symbols.comment: Before intent; the first `block` wins, otherwise `arguments` replace the call's arguments. A throw blocks.
symbols.output: HookResult<{ readonly arguments?: JsonObject; readonly block?: string }>

symbols.name: ToolHooks.afterTool
symbols.comment:
Before the result is committed; replaces the result. Runs on every result the tool task writes: an executed
call's, and the error results the Harness writes itself, told apart by their diagnostic code: a tool that does not
resolve (`tool_unavailable`), invalid arguments (`invalid_arguments`, with `call.arguments` as the model sent
them), a block (`blocked`), and, rebuilt from the call's partial output, an interruption (`interrupted`), the
restart limit (`restart_limit`), and an abort (`aborted`, `abandoned`). Once the task was cut off more than
`settings.restartLimit` times the hooks no longer run, since they may be what cuts it off, nor in the last attempt
the scheduler gives an abort handler (restarts at the limit minus one). A result's `structuredOutput` is dropped
when the Harness wrote it (a nested call a hook turns into a success gets the bounded output as a schema-less tool's
does), and its `control` applies only to a call that completes (not to an interrupted, cut-off, or aborted one).
An abort's hooks run inside the abort handler, which cannot be aborted: a slow hook delays `Conversation.abort()`.

symbols.name: CompactionHooks
symbols.comment: Hooks of the built-in compaction task.

symbols.name: CompactionHooks.beforeCompact
symbols.comment:
After range selection, before summarizing; the first decision wins. `entries` are the active entries the summary
replaces, the head marker first, and `messages` their model context, the summarizer's source; `firstKept` is the
first entry kept verbatim.
symbols.output: HookResult<{ readonly decline: true } | { readonly summary: string }>

symbols.name: createPhotonImages
symbols.comment:
An `ImageProcessor` on Photon (Rust compiled to WebAssembly), for `createCodingTools({ images })`. `wasm` is
Photon's `photon_rs_bg.wasm` as bytes or as a compiled module: `@earendil-works/pi-durable/images/node` reads it from
the installed package, `@earendil-works/pi-durable/images/cloudflare` imports it as a Workers module. Elsewhere, such
as a browser, fetch the file and pass its bytes. Photon loads once per process; later calls reuse the first `wasm`.

An image already upright, in a format providers take inline, and within the limits is returned as it is, once it
decodes. Otherwise it is turned upright by its EXIF orientation, scaled to the
maximum width and height, and encoded as PNG or JPEG at falling qualities (JPEG first for JPEG sources), then at
smaller dimensions, 3/4 at a time, until the base64 fits. Formats providers do not take inline (BMP) become PNG.

The work runs on the calling thread: about a second and a half for a 12-megapixel photo. Decoding takes the image's
RGBA size in WebAssembly memory, which does not shrink again; leave the processor out on memory-constrained hosts.

symbols.comment:
BM25 tool search for code mode's `searchTools()` and the `tool_search` tool, a copy of the coding agent's tool search
ranking: durable keeps its own copy of what it needs from the coding agent.

A tool as the ranker sees it: its name, its text, and the text of its namespace.

symbols.comment: Name, description, and instructions of the tool's namespace.

symbols.name: rankDocuments
symbols.signature: export function rankDocuments(query: string, documents: readonly SearchDocument[], limit: number): string[]
symbols.comment:
Okapi BM25 (k1 1.2, b 0.75) over `text`, with the name and the namespace as separate fields: the names of the best
matches, best first; ties keep document order.
- A tool that matches more of the query's terms, in any field, ranks above one that matches fewer, whatever their
  scores: for `screenshot window`, a tool whose description has both words beats `window` whose name has one.
- A query term in the name scores more than any number of mentions in the text.
- A tool whose whole local name (after the last `__`) is in the query gets a bonus worth one more match of every
  query term, so among tools matching as many terms, `peekaboo app` finds `mcp__peekaboo__app` over tools that
  only mention the words.
- A query that is exactly a tool's name, or its name after a `__`, ranks that tool first, before coverage.

Only `text` is length-normalized, so a long name or long namespace instructions do not lower a tool's score.

symbols.name: NAME_WEIGHT
symbols.comment:
A query term in the name counts this many times its IDF. The text part of a term is at most `K1 + 1` (2.2) times
its IDF and about 1 for a single mention, so a name match beats any number of mentions in the text.

symbols.name: NAMESPACE_WEIGHT
symbols.comment:
A query term in the namespace text counts this many times its IDF. Every tool of the namespace shares it, so it helps
find the namespace but not the tool in it.

symbols.name: IndexedDocument
symbols.comment: A document split into the fields the ranker weighs differently.

symbols.name: nameTerms
symbols.comment: Terms of the name: `mcp`, `app`, `thread`, `read` for `mcp__app__thread_read`.

symbols.name: localNameTerms
symbols.comment: Terms of the name after its last `__`, the part models say: `thread`, `read`.

symbols.name: tokenize

symbols.name: stem

symbols.name: CachedStorage
symbols.comment:
Storage that serves hot record reads from memory: conversations, tasks, and written submissions, each table bounded
by a count, the least recently used record leaving first, except live tasks, which are kept until they end, and the
ended tasks a task waits on, kept until it moved on from its wait: a task's record is read again at each of its state
changes, a waiter reads the outcomes of what it waited on once it resumes (`runtime.outcomes()`), and both are
bounded by live work, which the scheduler keeps in memory too. Without that, a burst of more tasks than the count
would make each of those reads a Storage read on the line. Every commit goes through it, and one process owns a
Storage, so it applies each batch as it is published and never goes stale: `commit()`'s batches when the Session publishes
them (`published()`), not at their durability receipts. A read
result is kept only when no commit published since the read started wrote its record, as the read may not observe
that commit; versions are kept only for records with a read in flight. Cached values are frozen and shared. Entries,
scans, and documents pass through: the Session keeps documents and the newest entry per conversation itself, and
context ranges hold the entries a run reads.

Not for a read-only Session: another process writes its Storage.

symbols.name: ConversationTails
symbols.comment:
The newest entry ID and newest head marker per conversation, for the Session that owns its Storage: every entry is
written by one of its commits, so `apply` keeps both current, and a value read from Storage stays valid until the
next entry of that conversation. Read only on the Session line after touching the conversation's appends, so no
commit that appends to it is unpublished and a value read from Storage can be kept. The newest entry visible from a conversation is its own newest, or for a fork without entries
of its own the parent's entry at the fork point: IDs grow, so a conversation's own new entry is always the newest.
Each map is bounded by a count, the least recently used conversation leaving first. Kept markers are frozen: entry
records are immutable (`Tx.appendEntry()`).

symbols.name: SessionImpl
symbols.comment:
Session kernel: one mutation line, the loaded document tracker cache, and committed publication.

The cache is bounded by use: a document with no watch attached leaves it once it was not read or
written for the retention period, and the next access loads it from Storage. Eviction runs as a job on the mutation
line, so no transaction ever holds a tracker that leaves.

Only committed state is observable. A deferred commit (`CommitPersistence`) is committed in memory first: it is
adopted and shown to the Session's own observers, and its changes wait, folded per document and pinned in the cache,
for the first commit that reads or writes the document, the document's deadline, a drop of its tracker, or close,
which store them.

Group commit: the line runs one job at a time, a commit's callback and settlement; a commit with writes then joins
the writer's pending batch (logical admission, `Writer`) and the line goes on. The writer stores every commit admitted
while no call is in flight in one `commit()` call, off the line, and publishes them one by one, in line order, a
macrotask apart: the read caches, adoption, telemetry events, the Session's own observers, and one microtask later
`observeCommits()` observers, before every wait the commit resolves and every abort it queues. Host listeners and
watch listeners have no order. A deferred commit is published when the commits before it are. A job's every read
touches its key (`touch()`); while an unpublished commit writes that key, the job waits for its publication, so no
job observes state that is not stored. Outcomes are delivered in line order (`#enqueue()`).

Storage failures are final. Every Storage call goes through one guard: the first error a Storage method throws, other
than for a cancelled caller, fails the Session, as does a commit it cannot adopt. That call gets the error; every later
call and every Storage call still underway gets `SessionFailed`; close listeners run at once with the error, and the
Session then closes itself, Storage included, and `closed` settles. Nothing retries: transient errors are the
Storage's to retry. Reopening recovers from what was committed.

symbols.name: SessionImpl.observeCommits
symbols.comment:

`advance` runs one microtask after the commit's publication, which follows its storage call, in line order, before
every wait the commit resolves and every abort it queues (in no order with watch listeners); it must not block or
call Session operations. A throw is reported, detaches it, and ends it `listener_error`; `end` gets the Session's
close after its last publication.

follows memory. A throw leaves that state behind, so it fails the Session instead of being reported. They run at
the commit's publication, synchronously, so they call no Storage method, run no task code, and contain every host
callback; the waits they resolve and the aborts they queue run after host observers.

Hold a deferred commit (`Transaction.holdable()`): adopt it in memory, queue its changes per document, pinned, by

symbols.name: SessionImpl.#storeHolds
symbols.signature: async #storeHolds(select: () => readonly Hold[], context: Context): Promise<void>
symbols.comment:
Store the held changes `select` returns in one storage transaction, through the writer, from a job on the line. A
barrier: they are selected once every commit admitted before is published. Memory already has them, so only
`observeCommits()` observers see it, published as the writer publishes it. A failure fails the Session, as every
Storage failure does.

symbols.name: SessionImpl.#release
symbols.comment: After their store: forget `holds`, unpin their documents, and move the timer to the next deadline.

symbols.name: SessionImpl.#armHoldTimer
symbols.comment:
Keep a foreground timer (Workers refuse background ones) for the earliest deadline of the held documents. When it
fires, every held document is stored, in one storage transaction: a deadline is the latest time, and the others
cost little more in the same transaction. Once fired, it stays until its job ran.

symbols.name: SessionImpl.#publish

#publish(
		seq: Seq,
		writes: readonly StorageWrite[],
		documents: AdoptedDocuments,
		context: Context,
	): { readonly error: unknown } | undefined
symbols.comment:
At publication: publish a stored commit. Its telemetry events first, then the dispatch to `observeCommits()`
observers, queued before the waits and aborts the observers wake, then the Session's own observers. Never throws:
returns the first error of an own observer, which fails the Session once its storage call settled.

symbols.name: SessionImpl.#notifyHosts
symbols.comment:
At publication: call the `observeCommits()` observers with `publication` one microtask from now, and, queued
before the Session's own observers run, before the waits they resolve and the aborts they queue. The observers are
those attached when it runs; their guards report a throw.

symbols.name: SessionImpl.#attachDocument
symbols.signature:
async #attachDocument<A extends object>(
		definition: AnyDocToken["definition"],
		resolved: { readonly id: string; readonly address: DocumentAddress },
		context: Context,
		attach: (loaded: LoadedDocument) => A,
		cancel: (attached: A) => void,
	): Promise<A | undefined>
symbols.comment:
On the line, as one job: load the document at `resolved` and `attach` to it, so the attachment sees every commit
after the value it starts from; `undefined` when absent. Cancelling `context` meanwhile rejects, after `cancel`
undid an attachment made.
inputs: resolved: { readonly id: string; readonly address: DocumentAddress }

symbols.name: SessionImpl.#observeDocument
symbols.signature:
#observeDocument<O extends Observer<Readonly<JsonObject>>>(
		definition: AnyDocToken["definition"],
		loaded: LoadedDocument,
		create: (value: Readonly<JsonObject>, detach: () => void, report: (error: unknown) => void) => O,
		ownerEnded: (observer: O) => void,
	): O
symbols.comment:
Follow the address of the incarnation `loaded`, after checking the definition, with the observer `create` makes
from its value, the idempotent detach, and the report of a listener error; returns that observer. It gets each
committed change there, a retirement as a `retired` change with the last value it was given and no ops (a change
in the retiring commit is not published), and a later incarnation as a root replacement. When the commit makes the
owner task of a task document terminal, no later commit can change the address: after its changes the commit
subscription and the pin go, and `ownerEnded` tells the observer, which stays subscribed to the Session's close
until it ends (its detach drops that). `end` gets the Session's close. The current incarnation is pinned in the
cache. The detach runs before `end`; once it ran, nothing more of the commit underway reaches the observer or pins
anything for it. `create` and `ownerEnded` are module functions where they can be, so a watch keeps no closure of
its caller.
inputs: create: (value: Readonly<JsonObject>, detach: () => void, report: (error: unknown) => void) => O

symbols.name: SessionImpl.#enqueue
symbols.comment:
Run `job` on the line, after the jobs before it, and deliver its outcome in line order: once the jobs before it
have theirs, and once its commit, if it admitted one, is published. With `exempt`, a job that admitted no commit and
waited at no gate is delivered as soon as it has its outcome: it is equivalent to having run before every
unpublished commit. A job
whose outcome comes after the one a failure is gets `SessionFailed` instead. At most `MAX_OUTSTANDING` jobs wait
for their delivery; beyond it the line waits.

symbols.name: SessionImpl.#poisoned
symbols.comment: Whether job `index` comes after the failure's boundary without an outcome of its own: it gets `SessionFailed`.

symbols.name: SessionImpl.#ended
symbols.comment: The job's outcome settled: run what waited for it (`onJobEnd()`).

symbols.name: SessionImpl.#maintain
symbols.comment: Run a job of the Session's own upkeep on the line: no outcome to deliver, so no fence and no `SessionFailed`.

symbols.name: SessionImpl.#publishing

symbols.comment: Job `index` has its outcome: let the line go on past `MAX_OUTSTANDING`.

symbols.name: GuardedStorage
symbols.comment:
The Session's Storage behind its failure guard; every component of the Session reads and writes through it. Before a
call, a failed Session gets `SessionFailed` without reaching the backend. A call that throws fails the Session and
rethrows the backend's error, unless it is a `StorageRequestError` or a read whose caller's context was aborted:
neither says the Storage is broken.

symbols.name: GuardedStorage.close
symbols.comment:
Close the backend once every call underway has settled, so none outlives it or fails after `closed` settles. New
calls are refused from here on: a paged read must not start its next page while the backend closes.

symbols.name: GuardedStorage.#call

symbols.comment:
Run one backend call under the guard. `read` is a read's context; `commit()` and `mintId()` pass none, so nothing
exempts their errors: once a batch is admitted, whether it committed is unknown. A call still underway when another
fails the Session ends with `SessionFailed` too, whatever it returns: nothing it read or wrote is used.

symbols.name: Writer
symbols.comment:
The writer of one Session. The line admits each commit as a part once its callback and settlement succeeded; the
writer sends every part admitted while no call is in flight as one `commit()` call, off the line, and publishes
the parts of a call one by one, in line order, with a macrotask between two, so the continuations of the waits one
resolves start before the next is published. Held commits are parts without writes, published when the parts before
them are.

Each part registers the keys it writes; until it is published, it is the newest unpublished writer of each, and a
job that touches one waits for its gate. A key leaves when its newest writer is published, so the map holds one entry
per key with an unpublished writer.

symbols.comment: The newest admitted part that is not yet published, whose gate opens after every earlier one's.

symbols.name: Writer.admit
symbols.comment: Admit a part: register its keys, queue it, and send it at once unless a call is in flight.

symbols.name: Writer.gate
symbols.comment: The gate of the newest unpublished writer of `key`, or `undefined` when it has none.

symbols.name: Writer.drained
symbols.comment: Opens once every part admitted so far is published or never will be.

symbols.name: Writer.unpublished
symbols.comment: Keys with an unpublished writer, for tests that bound memory.

symbols.name: Writer.#flush
symbols.comment:
Send and publish `parts`, then what was admitted meanwhile. Never rejects: a throw the writer did not expect fails
the Session and settles the parts (`#abandon()`), so no outcome or gate is stranded.

symbols.name: Writer.#send
symbols.comment: Store `parts` in one call, then publish them in order; settles every one of them.

symbols.name: Writer.#publish
symbols.signature:
async #publish(
		parts: readonly Admitted[],
		seqs: readonly (Seq | undefined)[],
		result: CommitResult | undefined,
		rejected: { readonly error: unknown } | undefined,
	): Promise<void>
symbols.comment:
Publish the received parts and held ones in order, a macrotask apart, and settle every part (group commit §3.4). A
refusal, a rejection, or a part whose adoption or own observer throws fails the Session once the parts before it
are published and the host observers got the last one; the parts after it are not published, and reject with
`SessionFailed`. What the failure decides (the outcomes, and the gates of the parts it concerns) is settled only
once the Session failed, so no job waiting at such a gate, and no later outcome, goes on as if it had not.

symbols.name: Writer.#abandon
symbols.comment:
A throw the writer itself did not expect while sending or publishing `parts` (a bug): fail the Session at the first
of them and settle every one not settled yet, so no outcome, gate, or close waits on it forever.

symbols.name: Writer.#failed
symbols.comment: `SessionFailed` with the Session's failure, or with `error` until the Session records it.

symbols.name: Writer.#unpublish
symbols.comment: Settle a part that will never be published: discard it, reject it with `error`, and open its gate.

symbols.name: Writer.#unregister
symbols.comment: Drop the keys a part is still the newest writer of: it is published, or never will be.

symbols.name: Writer.#open
symbols.comment: Open a part's gate: the jobs waiting for it go on. The newest part's opens `drained()` too.

symbols.name: hop
symbols.comment:
Yield to the event loop once: `setImmediate` where there is one, otherwise a `MessageChannel` message (Workers,
browsers). Microtasks queued before it, such as wait continuations, run first.

against the state the earlier ones left, and the first one refused ends the batch: the transaction commits the ones

batches costs a few statements per fork.

symbols.name: StoreStorage

Durable's `Storage` on Chord's store (slice 6b D1, D2, §2): its records as declared tables under an owner name, its
documents in the store's documents engine, its ids from the store's one allocator, each commit call as one series
of the store's commit queue (one backend transaction, one seq per batch), published in the host's batch. Several may share a store under distinct owner names
(claims); the app owns the store, and `close` leaves it open.

symbols.name: ReportInfo
symbols.comment:
What a report to `HarnessOptions.onReport` is about, by `kind` (`Report` adds the error). `extension`, where present,
names the extension whose code failed, when known; for a task's own code, the one that installed the definition the
task ran.
- `storage_failed`: the error failed the Session, which closes: a Storage error, often a platform reset.
- `task_faulted`: the task ended `faulted`: its phase threw (`reason: "threw"`), or its abort handler was cut off
  `settings.restartLimit` times (`reason: "restart_limit"`), as was a phase of a task of an extension's kind.
- `task_interrupted`: crashes ended the task: it ended itself after being cut off `settings.restartLimit` times in a
  row (`reason: "restart_limit"`; a tool call, a compaction, a generation), or a generation's run ended because the
  host kept stopping while the model answered (`reason: "interrupted"`). `restarts` is the task's count when it ended.
- `migration_failed`: the task's stored state could not be migrated; it is blocked until the registry changes.
- `task_outdated`: a running task keeps running under its old definition, which was uninstalled (`missing_task`)
  or replaced by one that cannot take over its state: older than the task (`task_too_old`), or newer without a
  `migrate` (`migration_failed`).
- `task_error`: the task's own `runtime.report()`, or a failure in running it.
- `extension_error`: a hook, a section, a wrapper, or a tool's invalid structured output; with the task that ran it,
  or, outside a task, the conversation whose agent was resolved.
- `host_error`: a host callback threw; with the task that called it, if one did.
- `listener_error`: a commit, close, watch, view, or document listener threw.

`Harness.observeConversation()`, `Harness.observeTaskGraph()`), with the shapes of Chord's watch: `advance` gets a
`WatchCall`, `end` a `WatchEnd`. `advance` gets every change, unfolded, as memory adopts it: for a stored commit at its
publication once Storage stored it, for a deferred one before it is stored. A view or the graph gets at most one call
per commit, a document observer one per change at its address (two for a commit that retires and recreates it); the
task graph also advances outside any commit's publication, on the Session line, when a registry change or a failed
migration changes a
`blocked` reason. Durable's failures are final, so every call is a `value` call; a failure ends the observer. Calls
may come before the attaching promise resolves; their ops apply from `Observation.value`. `advance` must only record
the call, synchronously and quickly, never await, call the Session, or throw. A throw is reported as
`listener_error`, detaches the observer, and ends it `listener_error` with the error. `end` is called once: `ended`
when the observed scope's owner ends (a task document's task, after its retirement change, inside that commit's
`adopt`), `failed` with "session closed" when the Session closes (an adapter follows the next Session) or with the
error that failed the Session; never after `detach()`.

symbols.name: CommitPersistence
symbols.comment:
When a commit reaches Storage. `immediate`, the default: before `commit()` resolves. `deferred`: when every write of
the commit changes an existing conversation document with `history: "latest"` and `fork: "initial"` (no creation,
migration, or retirement), the Session adopts it in memory, shows it to watches and views, and resolves, but stores it
later: with the next commit that reads (`tx.doc()`) or writes that document, before the document leaves memory or
retires, at `close()`, and at the latest about `withinMs` after the commit (default `settings.progress.persistWithinMs`,
1,000 ms; `Infinity` waits for one of the others). A commit that writes anything else is immediate. A crash loses what
is held, so only state whose loss is acceptable, such as streamed progress, should be deferred, and nothing durable may
depend on it without reading it in a commit.
symbols.output:
| { readonly kind: "immediate" }
	| { readonly kind: "deferred"; readonly withinMs?: number }

symbols.comment:
Run one atomic transaction on the Session mutation line. Inside the callback read only through `tx`: `snapshot()`, `watchDoc()`, `getTask()`, and the other Session and runtime reads may queue on the line the callback holds, and then never resolve.
`options.persistence` may defer storing it (`CommitPersistence`). The callback may run while an earlier commit is
being stored: at its first read or write of what an unpublished commit wrote, it waits until that commit is stored
and published; code before that runs early, so act on what it computes only once the commit resolves. Resolves
once the commit is stored and published, after every earlier commit's outcome.

symbols.name: Session.observeCommits
symbols.comment:
Observe stored commits, each with exactly what it stored, except that a document the commit retires is published
as its retirement only; a commit held in memory is published when it is stored (`CommitPublication`). Commits are
published in line order once Storage stored them, a macrotask apart; a publication queues one dispatch, which runs
a microtask later, before every wait the commit resolves and every abort it queues, and calls the observers
attached by then; a commit published while none was attached has no dispatch. There is no order relative to watch listeners. `advance` runs synchronously and must not block or
call Session APIs; a throw is reported as `listener_error`, detaches the observer, and ends it `listener_error`.
`end` is called once, when the Session closes (`ended`, after its last publication) or fails (`failed`), never
after `detach()`. Attaches synchronously; the observation has no `value`: commits are events, not a state, and the
Session does not know Storage's newest `seq` before its own first commit.

symbols.name: Storage
symbols.comment:
Atomic persistence boundary for Session records.

Storage trusts the owning Session to supply semantically valid records, references,
ancestry, and transitions. Implementations enforce atomicity, global ID ownership,
immutable conversation/entry creation, document record consistency, and detached values;
Session serializes commits.

An error a method throws is final: it fails the Session, which nothing retries, so retry transient failures inside
the method. Two errors of a read fail only that read: a `StorageRequestError` for an invalid request (an unknown
conversation, a foreign or malformed cursor, history a document does not keep), which must have no durable effect, and a
rejection because its caller's context was aborted. Any error from `commit()` or `mintId()` is fatal.

symbols.name: Storage.commit
symbols.comment:
Persist `batches` in order, each as one ordinary atomic commit with its own seq, checked against the state the
earlier ones left, in as few round trips as the backend can. Every batch has at least one write: a commit without
writes never reaches Storage, so the Session never sends an empty batch. Stops at the first batch Durable's own checks refuse
(global IDs, document actions, copy resolution): the batches before it are durable, it and the ones after are not.
Calls `receive(index, seq)` once per durable batch, in order, synchronously, after all of them are durable and
before the next commit starts. Resolves with the number of durable batches and the refusal, if any. Rejects for an
unknown outcome (connection lost, statement or commit failed); `receive` calls made before the rejection still
stand. `receive` is a durability receipt, not publication: the Session publishes later. Once it resolved, later
reads through this storage observe the stored batches.

symbols.name: Storage.publishing
symbols.comment:
Optional. Run `publish`, the Session's publication of one stored or held commit (its cache write-through,
adoption, and observers), inside this storage's own scope, such as a store's attached host batch, so what the
publication marks lands together. Call `publish` exactly once, now or soon after; the Session publishes the next
commit only once it ran. Without it, the Session publishes directly.

symbols.name: Subagent
symbols.comment:
─── Product code ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Each subagent is its own conversation with its own transcript, so it remembers earlier messages. The main

conversation keeps a small document that maps subagent names to their conversations. Documents are durable state

next to a transcript, changed in commits like entries.

symbols.name: reported
symbols.comment: Answers already reported to the main agent: several messages can end in one answer, reported once.

symbols.name: Anchor
symbols.comment:
Every task and conversation has an owner, and that decides what an abort or an idle wait reaches: aborting a task

aborts what it owns, and waiting for a conversation to be idle waits for its work. A subagent must outlive the main

agent's turns, so its conversation is owned by an anchor: a background task that finishes at once. A background task

is a boundary: the main agent's Esc and idle waits stop there, but `abort({ background: true })` still reaches past

it, so a host can stop everything.

symbols.name: ReporterInput
symbols.signature: type ReporterInput = { name: string; conversationId: ConversationId; message: string; followUp: boolean };
symbols.comment:
A reporter delivers one message to a subagent and reports the answer to the main agent. It is a background task

too, so the main agent's Esc and idle waits leave it alone. Tasks are durable: each phase ends with a saved

checkpoint, and after a restart the task continues from the last one. Request IDs make a repeated submission return

the first one, so the subagent gets the message once and the main agent gets the report once.
symbols.output: { name: string; conversationId: ConversationId; message: string; followUp: boolean }

symbols.name: sshConnection
symbols.comment:
A `Connection` to the target that does nothing until its first request. Each start detects the remote system (the
first time), verifies the daemon and deploys it if it is missing or changed, then starts it over `ssh`. A failure
(no network, an untrusted or changed host key) fails the requests waiting for that start with code `spawn_error`
and the `ssh` diagnostics as message; the next request tries again. `remote()` is the detected system, once known.

symbols.name: connectSsh
symbols.comment:
Detect the remote system and deploy the daemon now, then return a `Connection` that starts it over `ssh`, like
`sshConnection`. Failures reject here: host keys must already be trusted (`scanHostKey`, `acceptHostKey`), otherwise
this rejects with `HostKeyUnknownError`.

symbols.name: createMcpAuthProvider
symbols.comment:
Auth provider for MCP connections: sends the stored access token and refreshes it when it is about
to expire or after a 401. Throws `McpOAuthAuthorizationRequiredError` when the user has to sign in,
including when the server asks for more scope (`insufficient_scope`). `onChallenge` receives the
server's `WWW-Authenticate` challenge so sign-in can use its resource metadata URL and scope.
`settings` is only called when a refresh is needed, so a secret that fails to resolve fails the
refresh instead of the whole connection setup.

Many servers rotate refresh tokens, so two refreshes with the same refresh token lose the grant.
Requests in this process share one refresh, and other processes are kept out by the store's
refresh lock, held from reading the tokens to saving new ones. Tokens that changed meanwhile
(another process refreshed them, or the user signed in) are used without refreshing.

symbols.name: redirectUrl
symbols.comment:
A redirect URI the application signs in with, such as its https callback route. Refreshing tokens
from a sign-in with a Client ID Metadata Document needs a redirect URI the documents list; a
refresh never redirects, so any listed one works. Default: the loopback redirect URI of `settings`.

symbols.name: refreshStoredTokens
symbols.comment:
Refresh the tokens of `state` with the stored client (or the document it signed in with), or report
`REDIRECT` when that is not possible. `options.redirectUrl` is a redirect URI the application signs in
with, tried before the loopback ones of the settings and the stored client. Never registers a client or
prepares an authorization request, so a pending sign-in stays usable. Call while holding the store's
refresh lock. Not cancellable: a refresh the server answered may have rotated the refresh token, so its
answer must be saved.
inputs: options: { fetch?: McpFetch; challenge?: OAuthChallenge; redirectUrl?: string } = {}

Auth provider for `StreamableHttpTransport`. After a 401 it refreshes the tokens, or throws
`McpOAuthAuthorizationRequiredError` when the user has to authorize (again). Concurrent 401s share
one refresh, and a request whose token was already replaced is just retried: with rotating refresh
tokens, a second refresh with the old refresh token would fail and discard the new grant.

symbols.name: startMcpSignIn
symbols.signature: export async function startMcpSignIn(options: McpSignInOptions): Promise<McpSignInStart>
symbols.comment:
First half of a sign-in. Without a step-up (`insufficient_scope`), it first tries to refresh the stored
tokens with the stored client, whatever `redirectUrl` is (`authorized`). The refresh takes the store's
refresh lock, so never call this while holding it; when another process holds the lock for the whole
wait (`McpRefreshLockBusyError`), the refresh is skipped, and any other failure of the lock fails the
sign-in. Otherwise it prepares the browser step (`redirect`): a fresh `state`, and a stored client that
cannot use `redirectUrl` is dropped with its tokens. Requests to the authorization server are
time-limited.

symbols.name: refreshBeforeSignIn
symbols.comment:
Refresh the stored tokens, unless `cimd` is to replace a registered client. The refresh uses
`redirectUrl` when the tokens came from a Client ID Metadata Document whose documents list it.

the server answered must save its tokens.

symbols.name: completeMcpSignIn
symbols.comment:
Second half of a sign-in: exchanges the authorization code of `response` and saves the tokens. Pass
the options given to `startMcpSignIn`, including its `redirectUrl` (not `authorization.redirectUrl`).
Fails when the response carries another `state`, when another sign-in started with the store since, or
when the exchange would use another redirect URI than the authorization request (the options changed).
A redirect URL the user pasted goes through `responseFromRedirectUrl` first, which checks its path.

packages/mcp/src/oauth/sign-in.ts.comment:
Sign-in to an OAuth-protected MCP server, in two halves so an application can complete it in another
request with the same state store: `startMcpSignIn` refreshes the stored tokens when it can, or else
prepares the browser step and returns the authorization URL; `completeMcpSignIn` exchanges the
authorization code. The code arrives through a loopback callback server (`loopback.ts`), the
application's own https callback route, or a redirect URL the user pastes.

packages/schema/src/coerce.ts.comment:
Coercion: turns a loosely typed value (a model's tool call arguments, form input, query strings) into the value a

schema most likely meant, before it is checked. Only validators compiled with `{ coerce: true }` have it, and they

build it on their first coerce() or parse(); the check path never runs it.



Three passes, in this order:

1. Optional nulls: a `null` in an optional property whose schema rejects null is dropped, as if omitted.

2. Conversion rules ported from TypeBox 1.3.27's Value.Convert (MIT), keyed on JSON Schema structure (`$ref`, `const`,

`enum`, `anyOf`/`oneOf`, `allOf`, `type`, `items`/`prefixItems`, `properties`/`patternProperties`) instead of

TypeBox's kind marks: `null` becomes "null" for a string, `"3.5"` becomes 3 for an integer, a single value becomes

a one-item array, and a union takes the first branch whose conversion passes.

3. Primitive coercion by `type` (also type arrays), as in Ajv's `coerceTypes`: what pass 2 left, for example a type

array `["integer", "null"]`, or `""` for `null`.

A value that cannot be coerced is left as it is; the check then reports it.



Every pass is copy-on-write: an object or array is copied only when one of its members changes, so an unchanged

value comes back as the same reference and the input is never modified. All passes walk the same keywords for

members: `properties`, then `patternProperties`, then `additionalProperties` for keys neither names; tuple items by

`prefixItems` (or a draft-7 `items` array), the rest by `items`. Draft 7's `additionalItems` is not coerced.

packages/schema/src/compiler.ts.comment:
The compiler: a schema to one check closure, built once. Keywords group by the type they constrain, so a value

is classified once per schema, and the common shapes (closed objects, arrays of one item schema, tagged unions,

leaf schemas) get one specialized closure each.

packages/schema/src/explain.ts.comment:
Errors of a failed value: a walk over the schema that reports each failing keyword at the value it failed on.

It runs only for values that failed the check, using the compiler's checks for subschemas.

the Bidi Rule applies to every label in the domain.

symbols.name: NormalizeHostname
symbols.comment:
------------------------------------------------------------------

NormalizeHostname



Normalizes a hostname for label validation. Maps fullwidth

codepoints to their ASCII equivalent (e.g. 'ａ' U+FF41 maps to

'a'), then normalizes for NFC such that equivalent codepoint

sequences can be uniformly compared. It also removes codepoints

that IDNA mapping ignores, and converts full stop variants to

ASCII '.' so the hostname can be split into labels.

------------------------------------------------------------------

symbols.name: ExceedsMaxALabelLength
symbols.comment:
------------------------------------------------------------------

ExceedsMaxALabelLength



RFC 5890 §2.3.2.1: an A-label (the ACE-encoded form of a label,

"xn--" + punycode) must not exceed 63 octets. Only labels

containing non-ASCII characters need checking - a pure-ASCII label

has no "xn--" prefix and is used as-is, so its punycode-encoded

length is irrelevant. The ASCII check is a cheap short-circuit that

avoids running the punycode encoder on labels that don't need it.

------------------------------------------------------------------

symbols.name: HasInvalidHyphens
symbols.comment:
------------------------------------------------------------------

HasInvalidHyphens



RFC 5891 §4.2.3.2: label must not start or end with a hyphen, and

must not have hyphens in the 3rd and 4th codepoint positions (the

ACE prefix reservation, e.g. "xn--"). Operates on `chars` (the

per-codepoint string array) rather than raw string indices so

supplementary-plane characters earlier in the label don't throw

off the codepoint-position count.

------------------------------------------------------------------

symbols.name: NarrowIpvFuture
symbols.comment:
------------------------------------------------------------------

NarrowIpvFuture



Substitutes an IPvFuture address with a standard IPv6 loopback

address ([::1]). We do this because the native URL.canParse

(WHATWG standard) rejects IPvFuture literals, which are

otherwise valid in RFC 3987. Because regex substitution can

be expensive on large strings, this operation is strictly

limited to inputs under a defined length threshold.



(review-optimization)



------------------------------------------------------------------

packages/schema/src/typebox-static.ts.comment:
The static types of TypeBox-built schemas, read from the type shapes TypeBox 1.x declares (`'~kind'`, `'~optional'`,

`'~readonly'`, `'~unsafe'`) without importing TypeBox, so `Static` also types tool arguments of TypeBox schemas.

Only the common kinds are mapped; every other kind (Intersect, Cyclic, Ref, ...) is `unknown`. Tuples are plain

tuples: an element marked `Type.Optional`, `Type.Rest` or `Type.Readonly` is typed by its schema alone (`[string]`

where TypeBox gives `[string?]`), unlike TypeBox; tuples of tool and API schemas are fixed pairs, typed exactly.

Now as milliseconds since the epoch, rounded to the microsecond: `performance.now()` (monotonic, sub-millisecond)
plus an anchor to the wall clock. While the two agree within 10 ms, times in one process keep their order and
spacing to the microsecond; past that the clock follows `Date.now()` again, at whole milliseconds. Every adapter
of this package and Chord's SQLite store stamp span starts with it, so their times agree.

symbols.name: Editor.computeVerticalMoveColumn
symbols.comment:
Compute the target visual column for vertical cursor movement.
Implements the sticky column decision table:

| P | S | T | U | Scenario                                             | Set Preferred | Move To     |
|---|---|---|---| ---------------------------------------------------- |---------------|-------------|
| 0 | * | 0 | - | Start nav, target fits                               | null          | current     |
| 0 | * | 1 | - | Start nav, target shorter                            | current       | target end  |
| 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | Clamped, target fits preferred                       | null          | preferred   |
| 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | Clamped, target longer but still can't fit preferred | keep          | target end  |
| 1 | 0 | 1 | - | Clamped, target even shorter                         | keep          | target end  |
| 1 | 1 | 0 | - | Rewrapped, target fits current                       | null          | current     |
| 1 | 1 | 1 | - | Rewrapped, target shorter than current               | current       | target end  |

Where:
- P = preferred col is set
- S = cursor in middle of source line (not clamped to end)
- T = target line shorter than current visual col
- U = target line shorter than preferred col

Keyboard input handling for terminal applications.

Supports both legacy terminal sequences and Kitty keyboard protocol.
See: https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/keyboard-protocol/
Reference: https://github.com/sst/opentui/blob/7da92b4088aebfe27b9f691c04163a48821e49fd/packages/core/src/lib/parse.keypress.ts

Symbol keys are also supported, however some ctrl+symbol combos
overlap with ASCII codes, e.g. ctrl+[ = ESC.
See: https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/keyboard-protocol/#legacy-ctrl-mapping-of-ascii-keys
Those can still be * used for ctrl+shift combos

- matchesKey(data, keyId) - Check if input matches a key identifier
- parseKey(data) - Parse input and return the key identifier
- Key - Helper object for creating typed key identifiers
- setKittyProtocolActive(active) - Set global Kitty protocol state

packages/tui/src/stdin-buffer.ts.comment:
StdinBuffer buffers input and emits complete sequences.

This is necessary because stdin data events can arrive in partial chunks,
especially for escape sequences like mouse events. Without buffering,
partial sequences can be misinterpreted as regular keypresses.

For example, the mouse SGR sequence `\x1b[<35;20;5m` might arrive as:
- Event 1: `\x1b`
- Event 2: `[<35`
- Event 3: `;20;5m`

The buffer accumulates these until a complete sequence is detected.
Call the `process()` method to feed input data.

Based on code from OpenTUI (https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui)
MIT License - Copyright (c) 2025 opentui

symbols.name: ProcessTerminal.setupStdinBuffer
symbols.comment:
Set up StdinBuffer to split batched input into individual sequences.
This ensures components receive single events, making matchesKey/isKeyRelease work correctly.

Also watches for Kitty protocol response and enables it when detected.
This is done here (after stdinBuffer parsing) rather than on raw stdin
to handle the case where the response arrives split across multiple events.

symbols.name: ProcessTerminal.queryAndEnableKittyProtocol
symbols.comment:
Query terminal for Kitty keyboard protocol support and enable it if available.

Kitty's progressive enhancement detection requires requesting the desired
flags before querying them. The trailing DA query is a sentinel supported by
terminals that do not know Kitty keyboard protocol; receiving DA before a
Kitty response enables modifyOtherKeys fallback without a startup timeout.

The requested flags are:
- 1 = disambiguate escape codes
- 2 = report event types (press/repeat/release)
- 4 = report alternate keys (shifted key, base layout key)

The OSC 7501 program status query shares the DA sentinel: a terminal that supports it replies
before DA. `PI_PROGRAM_STATUS=1` or `0` skips the query.

(e.g. \x1b[Z for Shift+Tab). Without this, libuv's ReadConsoleInputW

scripts/check-entry-graphs.mjs.comment:
Entry points are cost contracts.

A package's `exports` map is the only place that says which modules are public, and one stray
`export *` can silently make a narrow entry drag an entire barrel: importing a 1-file pure
function through a barrel costs ~37 MB of evaluated module graph, and nothing fails until someone
measures a process. This walks the value-import graph of every declared entry point and enforces a
budget per entry, so that regression fails at commit time instead.

Only value imports count. `import type` / `export type` are erased before Node sees them.

scripts/check-model-catalog-compat.mjs.comment:
Checks that released pi versions can use the model catalog we are about to publish.



Problem: pi.dev serves each published catalog to every released pi at or above

MINIMUM_PI_VERSION. Released clients use it right away, without updating pi.

If the catalog needs code they don't have, they break.



Example: a catalog moved the kimi-coding models from anthropic-messages to

openai-completions. pi 1.2.0's kimi-coding provider only implements

anthropic-messages, so 1.2.0 sent requests to the wrong API and they failed.



Check: build the model list a released client would end up with (its built-in

models, overlaid by the new catalog), and compile the release's pi-ai source

against it. pi-ai's types tie each provider to the APIs it implements, so a

model with an API its provider lacks is a type error.



Only the latest release on npm is checked. If it is older than

MINIMUM_PI_VERSION, no released pi receives the catalog, and the check is skipped.



Usage: node scripts/check-model-catalog-compat.mjs [--catalog <file>]

--catalog <file>  catalog to check (default: .artifacts/model-catalog/models.all.json,

written by `npm run generate:model-catalog`)

Model catalog protocol shared by pi and pi.dev.

the same pair of pull requests and keep them byte for byte identical:

clients receive the legacy chat-only variant.

scripts/release.mjs.comment:
Release script for pi-mono

Usage:
  node scripts/release.mjs <major|minor|patch>
  node scripts/release.mjs <x.y.z>

Steps:
1. Check for uncommitted changes
2. Verify every public workspace package is registered on npm,
   pin the newest model catalog for Nix, and build with it
3. Bump version via npm run version:xxx or set an explicit version
4. Update CHANGELOG.md files: [Unreleased] -> [version] - date
5. Regenerate release artifacts
6. Run checks and tests
7. Commit and tag the release
8. Add new [Unreleased] section to changelogs
9. Commit next-cycle changelog updates
10. Push main and the tag to trigger CI publication and verified pi.dev announcement

boundaries.title: 普通 CLI 的计划模式和子智能体
boundaries.text: 根 README 明确说明未作为默认功能提供，仓库附带可加载扩展示例。
boundaries.impact: 列入“其他”的示例；Durable 的相应原语单独标为实验。

boundaries.title: 内置权限系统
boundaries.text: Pi 以启动用户和进程的权限运行，不内置完整的文件／进程／网络／凭据访问审批系统。
boundaries.impact: 工具 allowlist、项目 trust、审批扩展示例不能等同于系统沙箱。

boundaries.title: 项目信任保护范围
boundaries.text: 主要控制项目配置和资源加载；sessionDir 在信任前读取，AGENTS 等上下文文件也不以信任为前提。
boundaries.impact: 不能把“拒绝信任”理解为“目录内内容完全不会影响模型”。

boundaries.title: 技能 allowed-tools 字段
boundaries.text: 文档列为实验性元数据；Pi 不因此获得一套通用安全隔离机制。
boundaries.impact: 技能是指导与资源包，不是强制权限执行环境。

boundaries.title: 默认工具集合
boundaries.text: 普通 CLI 默认 read、bash、edit、write；其他内置工具按设置启用。MCP 可激活 codemode／tool_search。
boundaries.impact: “仓库内置”与“当前会话默认可调用”分别标注。

boundaries.title: SDK 内置扩展
boundaries.text: SDK 不自动加载 CLI 的 MCP、Codemode、tool_search，需显式加入工厂并完成绑定。
boundaries.impact: CLI 可用并不代表最小 SDK 示例自动具备全部能力。

boundaries.title: MCP 完整度
boundaries.text: 当前集成支持工具与资源，但不渲染 MCP Apps；独立 MCP README 将 sampling、tasks、旧 SSE 等排除在初始核心之外。
boundaries.impact: 不把“支持 MCP”写成“支持 MCP 的全部规范和应用 UI”。

boundaries.title: 图像生成保存行为
boundaries.text: 模型接口返回图像内容；Codemode 的 `image()` 会另存临时文件。models.md 中“生成图不落盘”与 codemode.md 的表述层级不同且容易混淆。
boundaries.impact: 清单将生成接口和 image 输出／临时保存分开，不承诺永久资产库。

boundaries.title: 模型硬输入限制
boundaries.text: 目录可以声明 request bytes 或每请求图片数，但文档明确 Pi 尚不据此重写或拒绝全部历史。
boundaries.impact: 图片缩放支持不等于所有元数据限制均被运行时强制执行。

boundaries.title: 分类和图像模型
boundaries.text: 不出现在普通聊天 `/model` 选择器，须通过 Codemode／扩展／库的专用接口使用。
boundaries.impact: 不把这些模型列成可直接替代聊天 Agent 的模型。

boundaries.title: 自动重试
boundaries.text: 模型暂时错误、MCP 重连和 Chord 断链是不同机制，Chord 在途请求断链后无法保证是否已执行。
boundaries.impact: 不承诺工具副作用自动重放，重试需由业务决定。

boundaries.title: 普通会话分叉
boundaries.text: 分叉保存对话分支，不自动恢复 Git 工作目录。
boundaries.impact: 代码恢复另见 git-checkpoint 示例。

boundaries.title: Durable 存储锁
boundaries.text: Durable 仍要求单进程拥有存储；新 Chord node 提供独立 processLock，须宿主显式集成。
boundaries.impact: 旧 experimental 宿主已删除，不能把其目录锁视为当前 CLI 能力。

boundaries.title: 外部生态
boundaries.text: Slack／聊天自动化指向独立 pi-chat 仓库；会话发布到 Hugging Face 使用外部工具。
boundaries.impact: 不作为本仓库内置业务模块。

boundaries.title: 其他代理常见功能
boundaries.text: 普通内置工具清单未提供通用浏览器自动化、专用网页搜索、语音转写、邮件客户端或定时任务调度模块。
boundaries.impact: 可借 Shell、MCP、技能或扩展实现，但不能将可扩展性写成现成功能。

boundaries.title: Chord 热重载边界
boundaries.text: 当前仅协调直接子宿主，commit 决策未持久化，重连不能续接旧 holds；loader 不回收旧模块且不隔离插件。
boundaries.impact: 跨进程能力已实现，但不承诺崩溃下原子集群升级、无限层级重载或沙箱。

boundaries.title: Chord 数据所有权
boundaries.text: track、replicatedState 和 replace 接管可信不可变 JSON，发布值并未冻结。
boundaries.impact: 消费者不得修改共享对象，跨可变信任边界须复制或序列化。

boundaries.title: PTY 平台范围
boundaries.text: Env 的远程文件／exec 与交互 PTY 有各自平台范围；历史工作台另有 Windows x64 ConPTY 实现，当前 checkout 不包含。
boundaries.impact: 不把工作台终端支持外推为 Env Windows PTY 支持；需宿主显式启用并校验原生资源。

boundaries.title: 历史工作台身份与 CLI 权限
boundaries.text: 旧 HTTP 宿主实现逐请求身份、工作区授权和来源校验，默认回环监听；原生 CLI 没有相同的 HTTP 身份入口。
boundaries.impact: 进程 worker、路径校验和工具上限不等于 OS 沙箱。

boundaries.title: 历史工作台草稿与真实执行
boundaries.text: 旧浏览器字段、fixture、保存回执、真实模型/daemon/Docker 操作是不同状态。
boundaries.impact: 按 capabilities 与运行证据判断，不以表单存在推断完整运行支持。

boundaries.title: 历史工作台两套设置
boundaries.text: 旧 /api/config 管理模块配置及 revisionVector；/api/settings 桥接原生白名单设置。
boundaries.impact: 两套 null、覆盖和信任规则不同，不互换；原生设置保存影响之后的 runtime 创建。

boundaries.title: 版本与持久化迁移
boundaries.text: Durable 1.4.0 引入的 SQLite schema v2 不能被 1.3.0 或更早版本打开；JSONL 旧版不能恢复 sleeping 任务。
boundaries.impact: 升级需对照当前源码和备份，还需检查 1.4.0 之后的 Unreleased Storage.commit / Watch 契约。
